articles.title: Popcorn Studio AI secures $1 million to expand AI-powered filmmaking platform
articles.text: UAE-based creative technology startup Popcorn Studio AI has secured a $1 million pre-seed funding package, led by Emirati entrepreneur and investor Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, to support product development and international expansion. Founded in 2026 by Egyptian entrepreneurs Shady Essam and Mohamed Hedar, Popcorn Studio AI operates an AI-powered video production platform that enables filmmakers, content creators, agencies and brands to produce cinematic content through an integrated workflow. The platform offers AI tools for scriptwriting, character development, scene generation, voiceovers, lip-syncing and post-production, with a particular focus on Arabic-language content and regional dialects. The funding will support the development of Popcorn's AI technology, expansion of its product suite and growth across the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, alongside international partnerships. Popcorn Studio AI has also announced an AI filmmaking competition associated with the El Gouna Film Festival, featuring a $70,000 prize pool to support emerging filmmakers. Press release: Popcorn Studio AI, the Dubai-based artificial intelligence platform transforming how films and video content are created, has announced a $1 million funding package, marking a significant milestone in its mission to reshape the future of creative production. The funding, led by Emirati serial entrepreneur and investor Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, will support Popcorn's next phase of growth, including continued AI technology development, international expansion, and the evolution of its creative platform. Founded by Egyptian entrepreneurs Shady Essam and Mohamed Hedar, Popcorn Studio AI is challenging one of the creative industry's longest-standing limitations: the belief that producing high-quality cinematic content requires substantial budgets, large production teams, and complex technical workflows. Popcorn is building a future where a compelling idea, rather than access to expensive production infrastructure, determines what can be brought to life. From an Idea to a Film. Without the Traditional Barriers. Unlike conventional AI video generators that require creators to navigate multiple tools, complex prompts, and disconnected production workflows, Popcorn brings the creative process together within one integrated platform. Through its specialised AI studios, creators, filmmakers, agencies, and brands can develop concepts, build characters, generate cinematic scenes, create commercial videos, and produce multilingual content using advanced generative AI models. A defining strength of the platform is its focus on Arabic-language content — including native Arabic lip-sync capabilities and support for regional dialects — addressing a major gap in the global AI video landscape. Built in Dubai with international ambitions, Popcorn combines advanced AI technology with a deep understanding of regional culture, language, and storytelling. Its vision extends beyond making video production faster or more affordable. The company aims to establish an entirely new creative infrastructure where filmmakers can experiment more freely, brands can produce content at scale, and emerging storytellers can bring ambitious ideas to the screen. A New Chapter for AI-Powered Filmmaking Popcorn's growth comes at a time when artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the economics of the global creative industry. What once required weeks of planning, expensive equipment, physical locations, and large production crews can increasingly be developed through AI-powered creative workflows. Yet the company's founders believe the greatest opportunity is not simply automation but creative empowerment. "Technology has always changed how stories are told. Cinema evolved from silent films to sound, from film reels to digital cameras, and now we're entering the next chapter with artificial intelligence," said Shady Essam, Co-Founder and CEO of Popcorn Studio AI. "Our ambition isn't to replace filmmakers. It's to remove the barriers between imagination and execution. We want to make it possible for anyone with a powerful story to create something extraordinary, regardless of their budget, location, or technical background." The company's momentum has also extended into the filmmaking community, with Popcorn announcing an AI filmmaking competition connected to the El Gouna Film Festival, featuring a $70,000 prize pool. The initiative reflects Popcorn's commitment to supporting emerging filmmakers and accelerating the adoption of AI-powered storytelling across the region. Strategic Investment to Accelerate Global Ambitions For Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, the investment reflects a conviction that the MENA region is positioned to lead the next chapter of AI-driven content creation — and that Popcorn has the team and the technology to make that happen. "POPCORN Studio AI represents exactly the kind of bold, regionally rooted technology I look for. The content market across the Middle East and North Africa is enormous, and AI is still in its earliest stages here. Shady and Mohamed have the vision, the execution capability, and a product that's already resonating. I am proud to back them at this stage." — Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, Investor With this funding in place, Popcorn Studio AI is focused on expanding its product suite, scaling its user base across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt, and building the partnerships that will bring AI-powered filmmaking to a new generation of creators worldwide.

articles.title: Hackers vulneraron OpenCode: hicieron compras de hasta USD 1.700 en cuentas de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google
articles.text:
Un ataque informático contra OpenCode, una herramienta de programación con inteligencia artificial de código abierto, dejó expuestas las claves de acceso de un grupo de usuarios y les generó cargos no autorizados de hasta USD 1.700 en sus cuentas de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google.
La compañía confirmó en la red social X que un atacante entró a un sistema antiguo que estaba en proceso de dar de baja y accedió a las claves que el 1,4% de los usuarios de OpenCode Console, su plataforma paga, habían guardado para conectar modelos de otros proveedores.
Esas claves funcionan como una contraseña digital: permiten que una aplicación use los servicios de IA de una empresa en nombre del usuario y le cobre a su cuenta. Según The Hacker News, la primera exposición posible ocurrió la madrugada del 17 de octubre de 2026.
OpenCode, que compite con herramientas como Claude Code y Cursor entre desarrolladores, notificó por correo a los afectados esa misma mañana y aclaró que quienes no recibieron el aviso no fueron alcanzados por la brecha.
Facturas que llegaron antes que el aviso de OpenCode
Varios desarrolladores se enteraron del problema por sus propias facturas antes del comunicado oficial. En Reddit y en X, usuarios publicaron alertas de gasto y cargos que no habían generado.
Uno de ellos, identificado como Colin Parsons, escribió que le cobraron USD 281 en su cuenta de OpenAI y USD 168 en la de Anthropic. Otro usuario, Preston Zeller, calculó sus pérdidas en USD 1.700, mientras que un tercero reportó más de USD 700 en consumo de OpenAI antes de desconectar su clave.
Anthropic revocó las claves de Claude que consideró comprometidas, OpenAI dijo que trabajó con OpenCode para restablecer el acceso de los usuarios y reembolsar los créditos consumidos durante el ataque y Google, suspendió proyectos que detectó con actividad de uso indebido.
Dax Raad, cofundador de OpenCode, aclaró que la brecha afectó únicamente a Console, el servicio alojado en los servidores de la empresa y no a la aplicación de código abierto que se instala en la computadora del usuario: “esas claves nunca nos llegan a nosotros”, escribió.
La compañía vinculó el episodio con un “ataque de destilación a gran escala”: una técnica que consiste en usar las respuestas de un modelo de IA costoso para entrenar, sin autorización, un modelo propio más barato. Algunos especialistas en seguridad cuestionaron esa explicación y plantearon que podría tratarse de una brecha común cuyo destino final todavía no está probado.
Los propios filtros de seguridad frenaron la respuesta
Raad relató que, mientras su equipo investigaba el ataque, los modelos de IA que usaban para analizar el código malicioso se negaban a procesarlo porque activaba sus propios filtros de seguridad. “Fue bastante frustrante”, escribió en X.
El problema se resolvió cuando OpenCode obtuvo acceso al programa Daybreak Blue de OpenAI, que habilita modelos menos restrictivos para tareas defensivas de ciberseguridad a usuarios verificados.
David Sacks, copresidente del Consejo de Asesores en Ciencia y Tecnología del presidente de Estados Unidos, comentó el caso en X: “OpenCode, como antes Hugging Face, chocó con el mismo muro en medio de un ataque: los modelos de IA más avanzados se negaron a analizar los mismos códigos maliciosos que hacían falta para defenderse porque activaban los filtros de seguridad”.
En julio pasado, la plataforma Hugging Face había enfrentado una situación similar cuando los modelos comerciales de IA se negaron a analizar los registros de una intrusión que, luego reveló OpenAI, habían ejecutado sus propios modelos durante una prueba con medidas de seguridad reducidas.
Raad dijo que los atacantes intentaron ingresar a los sistemas de OpenCode de forma ininterrumpida durante 48 horas, lo que obligó al equipo a mantener agentes de IA defensivos activos todo el tiempo. La compañía aún no reveló cómo lograron el acceso inicial ni la extensión total del robo de datos, y pidió a los usuarios afectados revocar y reemplazar sus claves directamente en cada proveedor.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Plex2Shell Flaws to Install Crypto Miners and Linux Proxy Backdoor
articles.text:
Threat actors have begun to exploit a chain of vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server to deploy cryptocurrency miners and reverse proxy software, a day after a proof-of-concept (PoC) went public.
According to a researcher who goes by the online alias boredhackerblog, the exploitation activity involves chaining four different vulnerabilities, collectively called Plex2Shell.
The vulnerabilities are below -
- CVE-2026-96652 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) stemming via the "/player/timeline" endpoint by taking advantage of the fact that the "protocol" parameter is inserted into a programmatically-constructed player URL with no validation, allowing an attacker to force the Plex server to POST to a destination of their choice.
- CVE-2026-96654 (CVSS score: 6.9) - An improper neutralization of URL values included in the "searchOne" endpoint that could allow an attacker to call other plugins' functions and supply their own parameters to obtain the owner's admin token.
- CVE-2026-96655 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An SSRF vulnerability that allows an authenticated user (i.e., the owner token) to request arbitrary internal or external addresses (e.g., an attacker-hosted carrier video carrying the malicious ELF payload) via the '/video/:/transcode/universal' path parameter.
- CVE-2026-96656 (CVSS score: 8.6) - An external control of file name or path vulnerability that writes the ELF shared object to an attacker-chosen path in the Codecs directory and execute it.
Put differently, the vulnerabilities can be combined together in this order to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on susceptible Plex Media Server instances.
The vulnerabilities, along with CVE-2026-96651 (CVSS score: 7.1), were disclosed to Plex on July 27, 2026, by security researcher Zach Main, and were patched in Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 released on August 3, 2026.
In-the-wild exploitation attempts targeting the flaws have since been recorded a day after technical details of the Plex2Shell chain went public on October 16, 2026. The attacks make use of a shell script to retrieve and deploy a miner payload ("x12345") hosted on a remote server ("217.60.194[.]116") using wget or curl.
The attack efforts have been observed from the following IP addresses -
- 91.92.40[.]202
- 176.65.139[.]228
- 45.194.92[.]222
- 176.65.139[.]228
| The Plex2Shell chain \| Source: Zach Main | 
Furthermore, the vulnerabilities have been exploited to deliver an artifact named "myawesomeproxy," which, according to VirusTotal, is a stealthy Linux backdoor and reverse proxy. Running the program displays the below message, per boredhackerblog -
Running this software on any of your devices makes you agree to the potential external use of your internet traffic.
Also deployed concurrently is an XMRig miner process identified as "mylovelyminer" with its mining server pointing to "ota.proxystream[.]st." Notably, another subdomain associated with the same domain, "global.relay.proxystream[.]st," was flagged by Bitsight in August 2026 in connection with the AISURU DDoS and proxyware botnet.
Posts on Reddit indicate that multiple Plex users have had their instances compromised with the same "mylovelyminer" payload. That said, it's not known at this stage if it stems from the exploitation of Plex2Shell flaws.
The development comes more than a month after Plex urged users to update their instances to the latest version following the release of an update that addressed multiple unspecified security flaws.
It's unclear if the aforementioned vulnerabilities were part of this alert. The Hacker News has contacted Plex for comment and we will update the story if we hear back. In light of active exploitation, users are advised to keep their Plex installations up-to-date for optimal protection.

articles.title: OVHcloud : un pirate a glissé un logiciel espion dans plusieurs versions de son outil en ligne de commande officiel
articles.text:
Hier, si vous avez installé l’outil en ligne de commande d’OVHcloud depuis GitHub entre 14h47 et 16h21, alors vous avez récupéré un programme conçu pour fouiller votre disque à la recherche de secrets. Et effacer l’exécutable ne vous protège pas, il faut changer toutes les clés stockées sur la machine.
Six semaines après avoir décroché la qualification SecNumCloud pour son cloud public, OVHcloud a subi une attaque par la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Le pirate n’est jamais entré dans ses centres de données. Il a piégé ovhcloud, l’outil avec lequel développeurs et administrateurs pilotent leurs serveurs depuis un terminal, et les utilisateurs ont récupéré le fichier vérolé sur les pages officielles du projet. « La version CLI de 14h47 a été compromise par un hacker », a prévenu Octave Klaba, fondateur d’OVHcloud, sur son compte X. Cinq versions, de la 0.11.0 à la 0.15.0, sont concernées, mais la méthode d’installation compte davantage que le numéro de version pour savoir si vous êtes exposé.
Des fichiers remplacés des semaines après leur publication
Le pirate n’a touché ni au code source ni à la chaîne de compilation. Octave Klaba évoque le compte GitHub « d’un des développeurs ». D’après la chronologie reconstituée par OpenSourceMalware, ce compte appartient à un contributeur de la documentation d’OVHcloud, doté des droits d’écriture sur le dépôt de l’outil. En 25 minutes, le pirate a supprimé puis remplacé les archives de cinq versions publiées entre avril et septembre. Il a ensuite changé le fichier checksums.txt, avec lequel l’utilisateur contrôle l’intégrité d’un téléchargement, pour que les empreintes collent aux binaires piégés. L’attaquant a profité de deux faiblesses. Tout compte doté des droits d’écriture pouvait modifier les fichiers d’une version publiée, et aucune empreinte n’était contrôlée lors de l’installation par le script officiel.
Un client d’OVHcloud avait heureusement fixé, dans sa chaîne d’intégration, l’empreinte SHA-256 de l’archive Linux pour processeurs ARM, et il a vu ses compilations échouer dès le remplacement du fichier. Il a alerté OVHcloud par un signalement public sur le dépôt. Les équipes d’OVHcloud ont effacé les fichiers à 16h21, puis publié une version 0.16.0 signée, dont les fichiers ne peuvent plus être modifiés. « Cette version est immuable, donc les fichiers qui y sont attachés sont fiables », a écrit l’un des mainteneurs de l’outil dans la discussion.
Selon OpenSourceMalware, le pirate contrôlait le compte du contributeur depuis au moins le 5 mars. Ce jour-là, quatre de ses dépôts personnels ont reçu un chargeur écrit en caractères Unicode invisibles. Le portefeuille Solana qui le pilote apparaît dans les listes d’indicateurs de GlassWorm. Repérés en octobre 2025 dans des extensions de l’éditeur VS Code, ces pirates volent les identifiants des développeurs puis réutilisent ces accès pour piéger d’autres logiciels. Les auteurs du ver Miasma, dont l’arsenal complet traîne en libre accès sur GitHub depuis juin, avaient rebondi vers d’autres projets avec les identifiants volés après avoir infecté des paquets npm publiés sous le compte de Red Hat. Les chercheurs ne peuvent toutefois pas prouver que le pirate de mars a lui aussi remplacé les fichiers en octobre.
- money_offRemboursement 30 jours
- securityCertificat SSL inclus
- install_desktopCompatible WordPress
Les installations concernées et les clés à changer
Si vous avez installé ou mis à jour l’outil entre 14h47 et 16h21 avec le script officiel ou avec Homebrew, vous êtes concerné. Vous êtes tout autant exposé si vous avez récupéré l’archive à la main sur GitHub à ces horaires, ou si vos chaînes d’intégration l’ont fait à votre place. D’après OpenSourceMalware, les développeurs qui ont compilé l’outil à partir du code source ou avec la commande go install n’ont rien à craindre, et l’image Docker d’OVHcloud, fabriquée en interne, n’a pas été touchée. Une installation antérieure à 14h47, sans mise à jour l’après-midi, ne pose pas de problème.
Un doute sur l’exécutable installé sur votre machine ? La commande ovhcloud version affiche le numéro de la version, par exemple v0.15.0, sur un fichier officiel, contrairement au fichier vérolé. Si Go est installé sur votre poste, la commande go version -m appliquée au fichier fait apparaître la mention « dirty » sur la copie piégée.
« La qualité du binaire est médiocre mais il peut aller jusqu’au bout », a averti Octave Klaba, qui demande aux personnes concernées de changer tous les secrets stockés sur leur disque. OpenSourceMalware cite en particulier vos clés d’API OVHcloud, le fichier de configuration ovh.conf, vos clés SSH et vos accès Kubernetes. Changez-les depuis un autre ordinateur, avant de supprimer l’exécutable et d’installer la version 0.16.0. Dans une PME, un développeur garde parfois sur son ordinateur les clés de tous les serveurs de production, et le pirate qui les a copiées peut encore s’en servir tant que vous ne les avez pas révoquées.
OVHcloud a promis un post-mortem détaillé sous quelques jours. Le client à l’origine de l’alerte attend de savoir si le compte piraté pouvait aussi pousser du code ou créer des étiquettes de version sur le dépôt.

articles.title: Tactful AI attracts fresh investment from Hatem Dowidar ahead of 2027 Series A
articles.text: Egypt-based AI startup Tactful AI has secured an undisclosed investment from Hatem Dowidar, former Group CEO of e&, as part of an extension to its pre-Series A round , initially announced in February 2026 and co-led by Foras AI and M Empire. Founded in 2016 by Mohamed Elmasry and Mohamed Hassan, Tactful AI develops an agentic AI-powered customer experience platform that enables businesses to manage customer interactions, automate workflows and analyse conversations across multiple channels. The company is preparing to introduce next-generation agentic AI technology that will allow enterprises to build and modify customer experience workflows in hours rather than months while maintaining human oversight and approval processes. The investment comes as Tactful AI, which operates teams in Cairo and Cambridge, UK, prepares to launch its next-generation platform and pursue a Series A funding round in 2027. Press release: Tactful AI, a startup specialising in agentic AI-driven customer experience (CX) infrastructure, announced that Hatem Dowidar, former Group CEO of e&, has joined its investor roster through a direct investment in the company's Pre-Series A extension round. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. The move comes as Tactful AI prepares to roll out its next leap in Agentic AI technology—a shift expected to serve as a crucial inflection point for enterprise capability, operational agility, and proactive market responsiveness. Dowidar brings a quarter-century track record in telecommunications and technology. He served as Group CEO of e& from 2020 through March 2026, having joined the company as Chief Operating Officer in 2015. Prior to e&, Dowidar spent 16 years in executive leadership roles at Vodafone, including CEO of Vodafone Egypt. Commenting on the investment, Mohamed Elmasry, Co-founder and CEO of Tactful AI, said: "Hatem Dowidar spent over 25 years leading major tech powerhouses serving millions of customers across the Middle East and Africa. Very few leaders share his depth of understanding and strategic clarity regarding what large enterprises require before trusting new, customer-facing technologies. His support and trust come at a pivotal moment as we take our boldest step yet toward defining a new era of agentic AI-driven customer experience." Hatem Dowidar added: "Enterprises across the region are actively seeking practical, reliable solutions to integrate AI into their customer operations safely and at scale. Tactful has successfully deployed this infrastructure in live production environments. Seeing the capabilities of their next-generation technology convinced me that this team has everything it takes to set the industry benchmark, both regionally and globally." While most current AI applications remain limited to answering routine queries, Tactful AI’s next-generation technology bridges this gap by addressing a core enterprise challenge: building, modifying, and evolving end-to-end CX workflows directly within the enterprise. This approach compresses development cycles from months to hours while maintaining human-in-the-loop oversight and sign-offs at every step. The company plans to reveal further technical details in the coming months. The upcoming technology builds on a unified infrastructure already proven in live production, driving rapid growth. The platform seamlessly integrates engagement, orchestration, governance, analytics, advanced automation, and agentic AI. This technical momentum is reflected in the company's financial performance since January 2025: Tactful AI recorded an 11.7x increase in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) and a 32x surge in monthly customer conversations processed through the platform. Its client portfolio includes Elaraby Group, Raneen, 2B, Lucky One, Erada Finance, and Simplex. This extension follows Tactful AI’s initial Pre-Series A round announced in February 2026, co-led by Foras AI and M Empire. The company aims to build on this investor momentum as it prepares for a Series A funding round in 2027.

articles.title: Una contraseña guardada en un dispositivo personal detonó el masivo hackeo a las licencias de Florida
articles.text:
Una sola contraseña guardada en un dispositivo electrónico personal desató el masivo hackeo a la base de datos de licencias de conducir de Florida (DAVID). La investigación confirmó que un criminal cibernético obtuvo las credenciales que un empleado policial conservaba fuera de los sistemas protegidos de la institución, usándolas para infiltrar los registros de licencias, vehículos e imágenes de documentos de residentes.
Tras el ataque ocurrido el 4 de septiembre, el Departamento de Seguridad Vial y Vehículos Motorizados de Florida (FLHSMV) comenzó a notificar tardíamente a las víctimas con un mes y medio de demora.
Un fallo de seguridad en una sola clave de policía expuso la base de datos de licencias
La investigación del propio FLHSMV determinó que el acceso no autorizado se produjo a través de las credenciales de un solo empleado del Departamento de Policía de Plant City, un suburbio cercano a Tampa. Ese empleado había guardado sus datos de acceso en un dispositivo electrónico personal, fuera de los sistemas protegidos de la policía.
Un criminal consiguió esas credenciales y las utilizó para ingresar a DAVID, la base de datos estatal que reúne licencias de conducir e información de vehículos y que usan agencias autorizadas en todo el país. El organismo atribuyó el ataque a “una organización criminal cibernética internacional”, sin identificarla formalmente.
El medio especializado en ciberseguridad BleepingComputer vinculó el episodio con el grupo ShinyHunters, que semanas atrás había publicado en un foro de la web oscura una captura de una supuesta licencia de conducir de Jeffrey Epstein, el financista fallecido y condenado por delitos sexuales, como prueba del robo. Según Ars Technica, ShinyHunters llegó a exigir un pago para no filtrar la base completa, con un plazo límite fijado para el 11 de septiembre.
Poco después de esa publicación, el grupo eliminó toda mención a Florida de su mensaje original, un movimiento que un investigador de la empresa de monitoreo de amenazas Flashpoint interpretó como un indicio de que el estado negociaba con los atacantes para evitar la difusión de los datos.
Qué información quedó expuesta
Según el propio FLHSMV, los datos que pudieron verse comprometidos incluyen licencias de conducir, información de vehículos, imágenes de documentos y otra información personal. La agencia no precisó cuántos registros fueron afectados en total.
ShinyHunters había reclamado haber sustraído más de 200.000 registros de conductores, de acuerdo con BleepingComputer, aunque el organismo estatal no confirmó esa cifra en ninguna de sus comunicaciones públicas.
El departamento ofrece un año de monitoreo de crédito gratuito a través de Sontiq, una empresa de TransUnion, para quienes reciban la carta de notificación. El problema, admitió la propia agencia, es que no cuenta con datos de contacto actualizados de muchos antiguos residentes de Florida cuya información seguía almacenada en el sistema.
Quienes sospechen que pudieron verse afectados, aunque ya no vivan en el estado, pueden escribir a la casilla customerinquiry@flhsmv.gov (dirección de correo electrónico) para confirmar si sus datos formaron parte del robo. La agencia también recomendó revisar periódicamente los resúmenes bancarios y considerar congelar el acceso al crédito ante las tres principales agencias calificadoras.
Un patrón que se repite
El episodio de Plant City ilustra lo que los especialistas en seguridad informática llaman “TI en la sombra”: el uso de dispositivos personales no autorizados para acceder a sistemas sensibles, fuera del control de los departamentos de tecnología. Un profesor de ciberseguridad consultado por la cadena WCTV explicó que esos equipos son mucho más fáciles de vulnerar que las computadoras institucionales.
FLHSMV aclaró que la investigación continúa junto con el Servicio Digital de Florida y el Departamento de Aplicación de la Ley del estado, y que difundirá nueva información cuando lo considere oportuno. Mientras tanto, las cartas de notificación seguirán llegando a quienes la agencia pueda localizar entre los residentes actuales y pasados del estado.

articles.title: Popular WordPress SEO Plugin Rank Math PRO Hijacked to Deliver Self-Restoring Backdoor
articles.text:
Copies of Rank Math PRO, the paid version of the Rank Math SEO plugin for WordPress, that were downloaded from rankmath.com or delivered as updates between 20:02 UTC on October 15 and 07:12 UTC on October 16 contained malware, Rank Math said in a security notice published on October 16.
Any site that installed and activated one of those copies should be treated as compromised, and the malware can recreate its hidden backdoor whenever someone visits the site.
Rank Math has removed the affected files and released a clean version, 3.0.124. Installing it replaces the plugin but does not remove files, administrator accounts, or scheduled tasks the malware may already have placed elsewhere on the server, Wordfence said in an advisory on October 17.
Who Is Affected
The version number does not show whether a copy is affected. Rank Math's changelog dates 3.0.123 to October 7, more than a week before the window opened, and the notice limits the incident to copies downloaded or installed through an update during the window.
A copy of 3.0.123 obtained before 20:02 UTC on October 15 is outside it.
The notice sorts sites into three cases:
- You installed and activated 3.0.123 during the window: treat the site as compromised, even if it has since been updated to 3.0.124, and follow the recovery steps below.
- You installed it but never activated it: delete the plugin files, install 3.0.124 from your Rank Math account, and run a security scan.
- You downloaded it but never installed or activated it: nothing in this incident alone indicates the site was compromised.
Rank Math has emailed some users about the incident and told anyone unsure whether the files were installed or activated to contact its support team.
The notice applies only to the PRO plugin, which customers download and update from rankmath.com rather than WordPress.org. The free Rank Math SEO plugin on WordPress.org, which lists more than 4 million active installations and was last updated on October 6, is not named in it.
What the Malware Does
What is known about the malware comes from Rank Math's notice. Neither it nor Wordfence's advisory includes an analysis of the code, and neither names who is behind it.
Deleting suspicious files before stopping what recreates the backdoor may not resolve the problem, which is why the cleanup order below matters. The attacker may also have left PHP backdoor files in other plugins' folders, in theme folders, and in the must-use plugins directory, created administrator accounts, added a fake WordPress core file, changed .htaccess so that .cache files run as PHP, and added scheduled tasks and SSH keys.
Any password, database credential, API key, or other secret the site could reach may have been exposed, and owners should assume it was.
Wordfence assigned the incident CVE-2026-111862 and rates it 9.8 out of 10, with the researcher listed as unknown.
Patchstack classifies it as a backdoor and says that, because the attack was on Rank Math's own systems, "a rule is not possible for mitigation."
How to Recover
Rank Math's preferred recovery is a restore. Where a backup of the site and its database from before 20:02 UTC on October 15 exists, restore it, run a security scan, change every password and credential, and only then install 3.0.124 from your Rank Math account.
Where no clean backup exists, the manual cleanup runs in a fixed order, and three actions come before anything else is touched:
- Delete the entire rank-math-pro plugin folder using the hosting file manager or FTP. "Deactivating the plugin alone is not sufficient," the notice says.
- In the wp_options table, delete any entry whose option_name is _uf6qdn2hmm, t8krdk990phb or _np5pvf754c.
- Block outgoing connections to rank1cdn[.]com if the hosting provider or firewall allows it.
Only then does the search for other changes begin, in these places:
- Files: PHP files in wp-content/mu-plugins/, in other plugins' folders, in the inc/, includes/ and lib/ folders of non-default themes, in Rank Math's own includes/ folder, and in uploads/.
- Code: PHP that uses base64_decode with XOR loops, the key xmmqhn, proc_open, or PHP-FPM socket code.
- File: wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php, which is not a WordPress core file.
- Accounts: administrator usernames beginning wpsupport_, or accounts with email addresses ending @wp-mail[.]net.
- Server: .htaccess rules that let .cache files run as PHP, .cache files containing PHP code, entries tagged #ms6v46 in the web server user's crontab, WordPress scheduled events, SSH authorized_keys files, other users' crontabs, running processes, and any location outside the site where the web server can write.
Wordfence adds a caution: "Their absence does not, by itself, prove that a website is clean."
Credentials are changed in every case, even after a restore from backup. The list covers WordPress passwords, the database username and password in wp-config.php, the security keys and salts in the same file, payment gateway, SMTP and other API keys, hosting control panel, FTP, SFTP and SSH access, secrets held in environment variables, and two-factor authentication for administrators.
The cleanup ends with a security scan, wp core verify-checksums for WordPress core, and wp plugin verify-checksums --all, with the caution that checksums may not exist for premium plugins.
WordPress.org publishes none for this one. The Hacker News checked its plugin-checksums service on October 19 and found no file for the PRO plugin under either of its names, while the service does publish one for the free plugin. The fallback notice provides a clean copy from the official source.
The clean 3.0.124 goes on last, downloaded by logging in at rankmath.com directly. Some customers may be unable to log in and may need to reset their account password, the notice says, without saying why, and Rank Math will never send login or download links by email.
What Rank Math Has Not Said
Rank Math, part of the Swedish hosting group group.one, has not said how the malicious files entered its download and update system, how many customers received one, whether automatic updates delivered them, or what the clean and tainted packages' hashes are. Its only statement about the future is that the team is taking steps to reduce the risk of similar incidents.
Registry records show the domain Rank Math tells owners to block, rank1cdn[.]com, was registered at 19:31 UTC on October 14, about a day before the window opened.
A Pattern This Year
This is at least the third time this year that a premium WordPress plugin's vendor-run update channel has delivered backdoored builds. In April, Nextend's update system served a backdoored Smart Slider 3 Pro for about six hours.
In June, ShapedPlugin's Pro plugins were found to have been backdoored in its update channel, and one package that had shipped clean was later "tampered with under the same version number," the trap Rank Math's customers now face.
Attackers also altered scripts served from Awesome Motive's CDN in June and poisoned BdThemes' API feed in August. Nothing published links the attackers behind any of those incidents to this one.

articles.title: Dès mars 2027, Yahoo vous laissera choisir entre publicité ciblée et abonnement payant
articles.text:
Si votre adresse mail se termine par @yahoo.fr, Yahoo vous demandera bientôt de choisir entre la publicité ciblée et un abonnement à 2,49 euros par mois. L’abonnement réduira le nombre d’annonces sans les faire disparaître, et refuser les deux formules revient à quitter Yahoo Mail.
Pay or consent, c’est ainsi que Yahoo ! a choisi de vous faire choisir, dès l’an prochain. Yahoo appliquera ce changement dans toute l’Union européenne le 18 mars 2027, sept semaines après le Royaume-Uni, où l’échéance est fixée au 28 janvier. L’entreprise explique sur sa page d’aide consacrée au changement que la publicité finance de longue date la gratuité de ses services, et vous ne ferez qu’un seul choix pour Yahoo Mail, Yahoo Actualités, Yahoo Sport, Yahoo Finance et la page d’accueil. Les moins de 18 ans et les abonnés à Yahoo Mail Plus n’auront rien à choisir. Si vous laissez passer la date limite, vos mails ne disparaîtront pas, mais il faudra choisir à la connexion suivante afin de garder l’accès. Avant de payer, mieux vaut savoir ce que ces 2,49 euros changent vraiment, et pourquoi Yahoo peut les réclamer alors que Meta a dû reculer.
2,49 euros pour des publicités moins nombreuses et non ciblées
Le tarif de l’abonnement sans ciblage publicitaire couvre d’un coup tous les services du groupe. Yahoo cessera alors d’exploiter vos données personnelles pour choisir les annonces et ne les transmettra plus à ses partenaires publicitaires. « Vous verrez également moins de publicités sur Yahoo », promet l’entreprise, sans chiffrer cette baisse. Yahoo continuera d’afficher des contenus sponsorisés et des liens d’affiliation, simplement sans tenir compte de votre profil.
Yahoo vend par ailleurs 2,60 euros par mois son offre Yahoo Mail Pro, avec une boîte de réception sans publicité d’après sa fiche contractuelle. Pour onze centimes de plus, vous gagnez donc une messagerie sans annonces, mais l’offre ne porte que sur Yahoo Mail, sans Yahoo Actualités ni Yahoo Finance. L’entreprise cite Mail Plus parmi les abonnements qui dispensent de choisir, sans préciser le sort de Mail Pro.
Si aucune formule ne vous convient, Yahoo propose un assistant de migration gratuit. L’entreprise transférera mails, dossiers, contacts et agenda directement vers un compte Gmail, Outlook ou AOL, et passera par le protocole IMAP pour les autres messageries. Votre adresse en @yahoo ne vous suivra pas, et Yahoo redirigera les nouveaux messages vers la nouvelle pendant sept mois, gratuitement, avant de cesser tout transfert. Le temps de choisir une nouvelle boîte mail gratuite et de prévenir votre banque ou les administrations, ces sept mois ne seront pas de trop.
Yahoo n’est pas soumis aux règles du DMA imposées à Meta
La CNIL a rendu publique en janvier 2024 une amende de 10 millions d’euros contre Yahoo, qui avertissait les utilisateurs de Yahoo Mail décidés à retirer leur consentement aux cookies qu’ils perdraient l’accès à leur messagerie, et le Conseil d’État a confirmé cette sanction en octobre 2025. Aux yeux de l’autorité, lier un service aux cookies publicitaires est légal, à condition que l’utilisateur qui refuse ne subisse aucun préjudice, et une adresse mail est « un élément de la vie privée de son utilisateur ». Avec l’abonnement à 2,49 euros, Yahoo offre aux réfractaires au ciblage une solution payante qu’il ne proposait pas à l’époque.
Meta a dû aller plus loin. Les contrôleurs d’accès désignés par le DMA, dont la maison mère de Facebook, doivent proposer une alternative gratuite quand un utilisateur refuse le croisement de ses données. Bruxelles a obtenu de Meta une option gratuite aux publicités moins personnalisées, proposée depuis janvier 2026, après une amende de 200 millions d’euros en avril 2025. La Commission n’a pas désigné Yahoo contrôleur d’accès, et l’entreprise n’est donc pas tenue de suivre la voie imposée à Meta, note Next.
Les autorités européennes de protection des données gardent malgré tout un œil sur ces formules. Le Comité européen de la protection des données a estimé en avril 2024, dans un avis relayé par la CNIL, qu’un simple choix entre consentement et paiement ne permettait pas, dans la plupart des cas, un consentement valable sur les grandes plateformes en ligne, et il a fortement invité celles-ci à ajouter une option gratuite sans publicité comportementale. Les Britanniques pourront trancher dès décembre 2026, et Yahoo évoque un choix anticipé dans d’autres régions, sans les nommer.

articles.title: Trump’s Russian diesel deal opens the door to nuclear-powered data centers
articles.text:
US, Russia to collaborate on nuclear-powered data centers as part of a 'joint project' on small-scale power plants
Russia and the US discuss small nuclear reactor deal
- Russia and the US discuss nuclear-powered data centers despite continuing sanctions
- Putin's envoy expects further economic agreements following the Russian diesel deal
- Small nuclear reactors emerge as a potential focus of US-Russia cooperation
Russia and the United States are discussing several joint projects, including data centers powered by small nuclear reactors, following a recent diesel supply agreement.
Kirill Dmitriev, an investment envoy of President Vladimir Putin, disclosed the talks on Friday at the Russian Energy Week conference in Moscow.
There are no details on locations, financing, timelines or participating companies, but further initiatives are expected to be announced soon.
Sanctions stand between the two governments
Dmitriev, who heads the Russian Direct Investment Fund, has long pushed for deals on minerals and energy and takes part in peace negotiations.
He said American sanctions create serious obstacles and called the Graham Act, which Trump signed in September, a "misguided" law.
The legislation seeks to cut Moscow's income from energy sales using tariffs and penalties, yet Dmitriev said both governments are considering other economic cooperation.
"There are so many layers of sanctions piled on top of one another that everyone has become confused; it's difficult now to figure out how to navigate a way out of this situation," Dmitriev said.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"Brainstorming sessions are already under way regarding how to lift these sanctions - that is exactly what the United States is currently working on."
Diesel deal – the starting point
Trump recently announced a diesel arrangement that would bring Russian fuel to American and global buyers and lower prices before November's midterm elections.
The arrangement requires lifting certain penalties Trump himself placed on Russian crude, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has sharply condemned it.
Washington's Treasury Department asked the Russian sovereign fund to help settle complicated payment questions tied to the diesel deal.
Dmitriev said the Russian Direct Investment Fund will ensure payments are efficient, though he supplied no figures on the value of the diesel deal.
The Kremlin has complained that Washington made any new agreements dependent on a peace deal for Ukraine, which remains out of reach.
Despite Zelenskiy’s opposition to the Diesel deal, Washington is focused on moving on with the deal — abandoning the Ukraine clause approach.
“The ice has, in fact, begun to break. We are effectively implementing projects with the United States of America at this very moment...” Dmitriev added.
Russia says its cooperation with Washington will continue until its “special military operation” in Ukraine ends.
The transcontinental country has a decent base for small nuclear reactors as it already controls two 35 MW small reactors commissioned in 2020.
President Vladimir Putin said Russia plans to build 38 nuclear power units over two decades to expand the computing capacity that artificial intelligence requires.
With reactors running and designs underway, Russia brings the technology to the table, and the open question is which projects both sides choose.
Via Reuters

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: 98 Zero-Days, Rogue AI Agents, $100M Crypto Theft, 700 Supermarkets Hit and More
articles.text:
The worst problems don't always come with a warning. Sometimes they arrive through a service everyone trusts, a device someone bought, or a system nobody thought to check. By the time something looks wrong, the damage may already be done.
This week had plenty of that. Trusted connections became a problem. Hardware wasn't as safe as it looked. Old bugs found new victims, and some systems were left so exposed that breaking in barely required any effort. Even AI agents crossed lines they weren't supposed to.
Some attacks were clever. Others were painfully simple. The full recap shows just how much can go wrong, and how little it sometimes takes.
⚡ Threat of the Week
ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup Following Unauthorized Access — ConnectWise disabled seven ConnectWise application identities as it continues its investigation into an incident in which unknown threat actors obtained unauthorized access to the application identities and compromised Microsoft 365 tenants. The IT management software provider said it took the action on October 17, 2026, at 07:00 UTC, adding it has also suspended Cloud Backup service by revoking certificates used for affected application connections across all users.
New Priorities for Critical Infrastructure: A Nation-State Threat Roundtable
Replace legacy DB tools with a modern platform that connects to every major database from one interface and eliminates locally stored credentials. Available for download as a free desktop app or as part of KeeperPAM.
Learn More ➝
🔔 Top News
- BeyondTrust Remote Support Flaw Exploited as 0-Day — The China-nexus cyber espionage group tracked as Armory Castle (previously UNC5221 or Warp Panda) exploited a newly disclosed security flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) as a zero-day in late August 2026. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS score: 9.3), is a case of improper origin validation in an internal messaging component that could be exploited by a remote attacker to perform file operations on an affected appliance. According to Google-owned Mandiant, the attack involved the deployment of a lightweight PHP web shell codenamed SAWFLY for interactive remote access and a tunneling program called BARECLAW to route traffic through the device. Only a small number of organizations are assessed to be impacted.
- Microsoft Disrupts 3 Phishing Kits Linked to Over 1 Billion Scam Messages — Microsoft says it has dismantled a criminal marketplace that sold three phishing kits, namely CoGUI (aka NX or FA), Haozi (aka Phoenix), and Iron Man System, that were responsible for sending over 1 billion malicious messages to more than 75,000 organizations worldwide. Redmond said it took down Yam Store (aka Storm-3119), a coordinated underground network that offered commercial phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) toolkits that allowed other threat actors to readily purchase and deploy phishing pages and steal data and credentials. The kits were also capable of advanced evasion, such as geofencing, fake CAPTCHA gates, IP address blocklists and allowlists, and anti-detection configurations. Yam Store functioned as an initial access broker, peddling not just phishing kits but also infrastructure built on compromised or fraudulently obtained Microsoft and Google cloud environments.
- Ledger Finds Unauthorized Hardware Implants — Cryptocurrency hardware maker Ledger temporarily paused sales of its products via CryptoBilis and other third-party resellers in Southeast Asia and Germany after a backdoor embedded into a handful of wallets led to the theft of an estimated $100 million in cryptocurrency. The implants are said to be an advanced version of a backdoor that hardware hacker Joe Grand found earlier this year and notified Ledger in March 2026. It's not clear how this occurred, but signs point to a compromise of Ledger's supply chain. One of the victims of the incident is a fraudster who engaged in a task scam and lost more than $4.8 million. "In this task scam, people were paid to fake sales and reviews of real items," Chainalysis said. "Then a 'negative balance' appeared, and they were told to add their own money in order to get paid. On Sep 22, the person behind the scam moved the proceeds into three separate Ledger addresses. On Oct 9, thieves emptied all three. One transfer each, into the same wallet." According to cybersecurity journalist Kim Zetter, Trezor wallet devices sold by third-party non-authorized sellers have also been found to contain implants that generated pre-determined seed phrases so as to allow the attackers to guess them easily and gain access to the accounts.
- Pwn2Own Ireland Demos 98 0-Days — The Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 hacking contest saw white-hat hackers exploiting 98 zero-day flaws, earning them a collective $1,262,000 in rewards. Ikotas Labs came first with 42.5 Master of Pwn points and $361,000 in cash after discovering 12 unique bugs. Xint and Team ZyGoat secured second and third spots. Ikotas Labs, Xint, and Mobile Hacking Lab broke into Google's Pixel 10, earning them $150,000, $300,000, and $112,500, respectively. Vendors are expected to patch the zero-days disclosed during the competition within 90 days before the details are publicly disclosed.
- OpenAI Disclosed New Misalignment Cases — OpenAI said internal models hacked more websites, bypassed browsing restrictions, and used cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn't otherwise access, in the latest set of disclosures where its agents carried out unethical and likely illegal acts. In all, the company reported seven new incidents. The development came as the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it received "multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers" whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, accessed personal data from Indian organizations. The agents found their way in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles. CERT-In did not name the providers or affected organizations.
- OpenAI Engineer Charged — The U.S. Department of Justice charged an OpenAI engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, with attempting to intercept oral communications after allegedly planting a recording device in an executive conference room. Prosecutors claimed company security staff found a second device in his bag. CCTV footage placed the defendant near the conference room on several dates. Alfozan allegedly had no authority to access or participate in meetings held in the room, which is often reserved for the highest-level discussions. In a subsequent filing, federal prosecutors revealed that Alfozan had booked a one-way ticket from San Francisco to Saudi Arabia with his wife and a third family member before his arrest on October 9, 2026.
- Attacks on French Refrigeration Systems — Cyber attacks on Danfoss- and Copeland-managed refrigeration systems pushed temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F) for roughly six hours, impacting over 700 French supermarkets and forcing them to discard food. French cybersecurity authorities advised supermarkets to disconnect them from the internet. The attacks targeted Intermarché and Netto, Coopérative U, Carrefour, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc. The affected systems are said to be internet-facing and running outdated firmware. "The username is admin and the password changes every day automatically to.. the current date," security researcher Kevin Beaumont said. "Every single one is like this. You can just log in and change the temperature. Anybody can do it, easily scriptable." To make matters worse, the affected stores likely also failed to put the devices behind a VPN and create an allowlist of trusted IP addresses permitted to log in. "Two things would have changed the outcome," Pen Test Partners said. "Cyber hygiene would have prevented the access: take the controller off the public internet, put remote access behind a VPN and an IP allowlist, bring third-party kit onto the network in a controlled, owned and documented way rather than leaving it on a contractor's own connection, change known and default credentials, and patch to a current release." Multiple vulnerabilities have been disclosed in the affected models, with Claroty warning that the issues could be exploited to "defrost the food."
- Collabora RCE Flaw Exploited to Backdoor Nextcloud Servers — Threat actors are exploiting a critical command execution flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110447 (CVSS score: 9.2), in the Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server app for Nextcloud to backdoor servers. It has been patched in version 26.4.303. The attacks involve issuing a malicious request to the app's "proxy.php" endpoint to trigger command injection and plant a PHP web shell with the end goal of conducting reconnaissance and searching for password databases, password manager artifacts, and cryptocurrency wallets.

Join this webinar to learn how to uncover hidden AI agents on employee devices, detect malicious agent skills, identify risky permissions, and put practical controls in place before they lead to a security incident.
- How to Find Security Gaps and Build Faster Defenses Against AI-Powered Cyberattacks → AI-powered cyberattacks are evolving faster than traditional defenses can keep up. Join this webinar to learn how to assess your organization's AI threat readiness, uncover critical security gaps, strengthen detection and response capabilities, and build a practical defense strategy against emerging AI-driven threats.
📰 Around the Cyber World
- Meta said it addressed an issue after reports emerged that some Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses were recording people's conversations without the wearer knowing. The recordings occurred without users saying the "Hey, Meta" prompt phrase. "This issue has been resolved," Meta told Android Authority. "People can manage, review, and delete voice logs of their interactions with Meta AI via settings at any time." Meta did not say what caused the smart glasses to record people without user consent, or how many of them were affected.
- Fortra said it's tracking a 12-fold increase in emails using requests for quotation, project invitations, and procurement inquiries as phishing lures from October 2025 to September 2026. "These messages impersonate prospective buyers seeking pricing, availability, or project participation," Fortra said. "Their purpose is not to obtain a legitimate quote, but to persuade a recipient to access an attacker-controlled file-sharing, document-viewing, or procurement portal."
- A fake download site for the WatchGuard Mobile VPN with SSL ("watchguard-vpn[.]net") has been observed using a browser pop-up prompt to steal the victim's VPN server address, username, and password. As of October 13, the domain was offline. "In a unique twist, after collecting credentials twice (the first attempt gets rejected as 'incorrect' in a likely attempt to collect multiple credentials), the site then downloads the genuine, validly signed WatchGuard installer directly from WatchGuard's own content delivery network (CDN), meaning there is no malicious file for endpoint security tools to flag," Huntress said. "Meanwhile, unbeknownst to the victim, the threat actor now has access to their credentials, giving them access to victims' networks."
- A set of 42 malicious RubyGems packages has used typosquatting, brandjacking, and plausible utility names to target cryptocurrency and Web3 developers. The packages are designed to spawn a reverse shell and download a crypto theft kit capable of rerouting cryptocurrency transactions by replacing the destination address with an attacker-controlled wallet and harvesting wallet material, such as seed phrases and private keys. The names of some of the packages are: lightinng-invoice, cryoto-toolbox, etheremu.rb, bitcoin-rpc-lite, web3-sign-helper, and crypto-mnemonic-tools. The activity has been codenamed Ghost Dev by Open Source Malware.
- GreyNoise said it has observed a spike in scanning and exploitation attempts targeting Digital Video Recorders (DVRs) in Ukraine between September 21 and October 1, 2026. The majority of the activity attempts to exploit CVE-2021-36260, which allows unauthenticated command injection against unpatched Hikvision products.
- A series of email campaigns have been targeting the accommodation industry with fake guest complaints or reviews that deliver blockchain technology-abusing malware. "These emails appear to likely be a continuation of a prior series of predominantly Booking.com-spoofing emails that were seen delivering various remote access trojans (RAT) via ClickFix fake CAPTCHA websites," Cofense said. The activity leveraged the Ethereum and TON blockchains, a technique called EtherHiding, to deliver EtherRAT and TONResolver malware.
- As AI agents increasingly are being used to automate coding workflows, it increases the risk associated with credential exposure, Trellix warned. "Agents constantly take credentials out of the safe places your operating system keeps them, and put them somewhere far more exposed," Trellix said. "This happens as a normal side effect of everyday work. And even good security telemetry has a hard time distinguishing this from a developer doing their job -- or from an attacker who is already inside."
- MITRE released version 20 of its ATT&CK framework, adding entries that cover AI abuse, MFA bypass, and recent attacks on water utilities. This includes nine new Techniques and Sub-Techniques under the Enterprise domain for prompt injection, AI-enabled exfiltration, AI result poisoning, attacks on AI-assisted defenses, CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart) evasion, and application-specific password theft. For Mobile, MITRE also un-deprecated a technique for delivering malicious apps outside official app stores, last included in v11.
- Fake AI tool campaigns that impersonate Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and other AI brands are being used to plant infostealers on compromised systems using ClickFix lures. Some of the prominent targets include the U.S. and India. "The attacks share one trait: the employee performs the decisive step," ANY.RUN said. "They paste an 'install command,' run a convincing installer, or sign in to a fake window. That can put source code, cloud and AI API keys, active business sessions, ad accounts, and billing access at risk, turning a single user action into potential data exposure, account compromise, financial loss, or disruption to development and marketing operations."
- An official OpenAI skill, render-deploy, suffered from a first-of-its-kind supply-chain vulnerability which instructed production apps to send their tokens to an unregistered domain ("render-internal[.]com"). "It builds apps that trust a domain nobody owns, so any attacker could register it and start receiving tokens from real production apps," AIR Security said. "Vulnerable servers in the wild sent tokens to the domain, users are advised to update to the patched version of the skill."
- The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned that scammers could exploit the 2026 U.S. midterm election to perpetrate financial fraud schemes. "As previously reported, scammers use the names, images, logos, and slogans of candidates to fraudulently solicit campaign contributions, sell merchandise that is never delivered, or steal personally identifiable information (PII) that can be used for other fraud," the FBI said. "Scammers also exploit artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate highly realistic voices, images, and written messages that impersonate candidates, campaigns, government entities, and trusted contacts."
- A new study from Semperis revealed that ransomware actors are threatening their victims with physical violence as part of triple extortion schemes. In all, 40% of attacks in the past 12 months involved psychological or physical threats against staff. "Bad actors are threatening victims with psychological intimidation in nearly 25% of all attacks in the U.S., UK, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Singapore, Canada and Australia," Semperis said. "In 53% of cases, the victims reported that the hackers followed through on their threats; 24% of victims or family members were swatted; 25% of victims sought psychological and medical treatment because of the ransomware attack; and 24% of victims or families hired personal security."
Conclusion
If there's one thing this week made clear, it's that small gaps can lead to big problems. A weak password, an old bug, a trusted connection, or a device that wasn't checked properly. None of these sounds unusual on its own. But attackers keep finding ways to turn them into something much worse.
The lesson isn't to worry about every new threat. It's to pay closer attention to the things we already know can go wrong. Check what's exposed, question what you trust, fix what you can, and don't assume something is safe just because it's been working fine. Sometimes the simplest checks prevent the biggest headaches.

articles.title: Nabta Health advances $3 million pre-Series A with backing from PVP
articles.text: UAE-based healthtech startup Nabta Health has secured a fresh investment from Phoenix Venture Partners (PVP), which led the second close of the company's ongoing $3 million pre-Series A round. PVP's investment includes both primary and secondary capital, while the amount raised in this closing was not disclosed. Founded in 2017 by Sophie Smith, Nabta Health develops AI-powered preventive healthcare solutions, with a focus on women's health, combining early disease detection, digital health services and clinical care. The company offers Aya, an AI-supported care navigation tool, alongside preventive screening and personalised care pathways, connecting patients, employers, insurers and healthcare providers to facilitate earlier intervention and coordinated care. The funding will support Nabta Health's commercial expansion, customer acquisition and strategic partnerships, particularly with employers, insurance companies and healthcare providers. In November 2025, Nabta Health raised $2 million pre-Series A , bringing its total funding to $4.5 million. Press release: Phoenix Venture Partners Limited (“PVP”), a venture capital fund manager domiciled in the Abu Dhabi Global Market (“ADGM”) and regulated by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (“FSRA”), today announced that it has led the second close of Nabta Health's (“NABTA”) ongoing $3 million Pre-Series A financing. PVP’s investment comprises a blend of primary and secondary capital, further institutionalising a longstanding relationship with NABTA as the company enters its next stage of growth. The Pre-Series A has attracted participation from institutional investors, venture capital firms, family offices and high-net-worth investors. Founded in 2017 by Sophie Smith, NABTA has evolved significantly from its origins as a direct-to-consumer women’s health platform. Following years of investment in technology, clinical infrastructure and R&D, the company is entering a new phase focused on building AI-powered preventive healthcare infrastructure for employers, insurers and healthcare providers. NABTA combines early disease detection, AI-supported care navigation through Aya, and hybrid digital and clinical care, positioning the business as a connecting layer across patients, payors and providers. The company’s model is increasingly focused on enabling earlier intervention, more coordinated care and improved health outcomes, while helping employers and insurers address long-term healthcare costs through prevention and better population health management. NABTA’s clinics and expertise in women’s health remain important enablers of this broader platform. The investment marks the next chapter in PVP's longstanding relationship with NABTA. Dr. Mussaad Al-Razouki, Co-Founder and Non-Executive Director of PVP, who has supported NABTA since its early days as a founding investor and former Executive Chairman, will transition from his position on NABTA's Board, with Steve Khayat joining the Board as PVP's representative. The transition comes as NABTA moves from an extended period of product development and R&D into a phase increasingly focused on commercialisation and scale. Steve Khayat, Founder and CEO of Phoenix Venture Partners, said: “NABTA has done the hard work of building its technology, clinical infrastructure and model, and is already demonstrating strong commercial traction. We believe the company is now at an inflection point where the focus can shift decisively toward go-to-market and sales acceleration. Our role at PVP will be to work alongside Sophie and the team to deepen strategic partnerships, accelerate customer acquisition and help translate that traction into scalable growth.” Sophie Smith, Founder and CEO of Nabta Health, added: “We are delighted to welcome PVP as a shareholder and Steve to our Board at an important stage in NABTA’s journey. PVP brings not only capital, but also the regional relationships and hands-on support that can help us accelerate our next phase of commercial growth and deepen our partnerships with employers, insurers and healthcare providers.” The funding will support NABTA as it accelerates its go-to-market strategy, expands its enterprise proposition and develops new commercial relationships across the employer, insurance and healthcare ecosystems. PVP will work alongside NABTA’s leadership team to support this next stage of growth, leveraging its regional network and value-creation capabilities to help accelerate commercial partnerships and position the company for its next phase of institutional growth.

articles.title: Gemini tiene nuevos nombres: así cambian algunas funciones en la IA de Google
articles.text:
Google reorganiza los nombres de varias funciones de Gemini y modifica la forma en que los usuarios acceden a las instrucciones personalizadas de su inteligencia artificial. El cambio alcanza a Gems, Spark y Acciones programadas, con un cronograma que arranca en octubre de 2026 y se extiende hasta 2027 para cuentas corporativas y educativas.
La transición no es solo cosmética. Cada función conserva su propósito, pero cambia el modo en que se activa y, en algunos casos, se integra dentro del chat principal en lugar de abrir una ventana propia.
Cuáles son los cambios en los nombres de Gemini
- De Gems a Skills
Los Gems funcionaban como bots personalizados independientes: cada uno se seleccionaba desde una barra lateral y abría una conversación separada. Esa lógica desaparece con la llegada de las Skills, un sistema que incorpora las instrucciones personalizadas directamente al chat principal de Gemini.
Para activar una Skill, basta con escribir una barra diagonal dentro del cuadro de solicitud y elegir la opción necesaria. Gemini también puede aplicarla de forma automática cuando detecta que las instrucciones coinciden con el pedido del usuario.
La diferencia con el esquema anterior es la posibilidad de combinar varias Skills en una misma conversación: una puede fijar la identidad de marca de una empresa y otra el tono de escritura, sin necesidad de trasladar resultados entre bots distintos.
Las Skills usan el formato abierto SKILL.md, basado en Markdown, lo que permite crear y transferir instrucciones entre herramientas sin depender de una sola plataforma. Están disponibles en la aplicación de Gemini y también en Google Workspace, algo que los Gems nunca permitieron.
No todas las funciones migraron todavía. Canvas, Investigación profunda, Aprendizaje guiado y la generación de vídeo y música siguen sin funcionar dentro de una Skill, como tampoco es posible compartirla ni adjuntar archivos de Drive, opciones que Google prometió incorporar más adelante.
- Spark se convierte en Tarea
Spark es el agente de Gemini que continúa trabajando después de que el usuario cierra la computadora o bloquea el teléfono. Google dejó de destacar ese nombre y ahora lo presenta como Tarea, visible en un selector junto al cuadro de solicitud, mientras que su página de configuración pasó a llamarse Configuración de tareas.
La herramienta opera en máquinas virtuales de Google Cloud y puede ejecutar procesos de varios pasos en aplicaciones y sitios web, como investigar competidores o monitorear precios de vuelos.
Google incorporó puntos de control: la función pide aprobación antes de enviar mensajes, modificar datos, realizar compras o completar formularios, y devuelve el control cuando un sitio solicita contraseñas o datos de pago.
Cuál es la función que no cambia de nombre
A diferencia de Gems y Spark, Acciones programadas mantiene su denominación. Permite escribir una solicitud, definir cuándo debe ejecutarse y establecer la frecuencia, con un límite de 10 acciones activas de forma simultánea.
En la versión web, el chat correspondiente aparece como no leído; en móviles, Gemini envía una notificación que puede mostrarse en la pantalla de bloqueo según la configuración del dispositivo.
Cuándo se realizarán los cambios en Gemini
El despliegue de Skills en Workspace comenzó el 5 de octubre de 2026 para dominios de lanzamiento rápido y se extendió a dominios programados a partir del 19 de octubre, con finalización prevista a mediados de noviembre.
En la aplicación de Gemini, las Skills empezaron a lanzarse el 13 de octubre de 2026 para todos los usuarios, con el mismo cierre estimado a mediados de noviembre. Durante ese período conviven ambos sistemas.
El 17 de noviembre de 2026 es la fecha clave para cuentas personales: Google empezará a convertir de forma automática los Gems en Skills, que quedarán como borradores inactivos hasta que el creador los revise y active.
Para empresas, el cambio definitivo llega el 1 de marzo de 2027, cuando ya no se podrán crear, editar ni usar Gems, y los flujos de Google Workspace Studio con el paso “Pregúntale a una Gem” dejarán de funcionar.
En educación, el mismo cierre se aplicará el 1 de junio de 2027, con la eliminación de Gems en Google Classroom y en los sistemas de gestión de aprendizaje compatibles con Gemini mediante LTI.

articles.title: Privacy Badger, l'anti-tracker de l'Electronic Frontier Foundation, s'invite sur Safari
articles.text:
L'extension anti-pistage de l'EFF, déjà utilisée par plus de quatre millions de personnes, est désormais disponible sur Safari pour macOS. Le module nécessite Safari 26.5 ou d'une version plus récente.
Privacy Badger était jusqu'à présent réservé à Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave et Firefox. Malgré la demande des utilisateurs, il restait absent du navigateur d'Apple. L'EFF vient d'annoncer que les récentes évolutions du système d'extensions de Safari lui ont finalement permis de porter le module.
Safari limite les pisteurs, Privacy Badger les empêche de se charger
Safari dispose déjà de ses propres protections. Par défaut, il restreint les informations auxquelles les traqueurs peuvent accéder, mais il les laisse quand même se charger. Privacy Badger les bloque dès le départ. L'EFF explique que certaines techniques de suivi parviennent à contourner les protections natives de Safari.
L'extension apprend d'elle-même à repérer les pisteurs, y compris ceux que d'autres outils n'ont pas dans leur base ou choisissent de ne pas bloquer. Elle traite aussi les widgets intégrés aux pages, comme les tweets, les commentaires ou les lecteurs vidéo, lequels peuvent transmettre des données même si l'internaute n'a pas cliqué dessus. Privacy Badger empêche leur chargement et les remplace par un encart sur lequel il faut cliquer pour les afficher. Elle envoie par ailleurs le signal Global Privacy Control (GPC), qui demande aux sites de ne pas vendre ni partager vos données personnelles. Aux États-Unis, ce mécanisme a une valeur légale dans plusieurs états, dont la Californie, le Colorado, le New Jersey et le Connecticut.
Privacy Badger peut s’utiliser seul, avec un bloqueur de publicités ou avec les réglages de Safari contre le pistage. L'installation passe par l'App Store. Si un site s'affiche mal, il est possible de désactiver l'extension pour ce dernier, ou signaler le problème. L'EFF annonce qu'une version iOS est à l'étude, une fois que l'édition macOS sera stabilisée et dépourvues de tout problème.
En 2020, l'EFF publiait Cover Your Tracks, la nouvelle version de Panopticlick, l'outil qui teste la résistance d'un navigateur aux pisteurs. L'organisation y recommandait un navigateur protégé contre le fingerprinting, comme Safari ou Brave. D'ailleurs, à ce sujet, rappelons que multiplier les extensions contribue à rendre un navigateur plus unique, et donc plus facile à reconnaître au niveau de l'empreinte matérielle.
- Application claire et minimaliste.
- Détection automatique des trackeurs.
- Personnalisation de l'analyse possible.

articles.title: AI just found new solutions for magnetic fields in fusion reactors
articles.text:
'It’s over, AI won': Google Gemini 4 Argon shatters 59-year-old nuclear fusion conjecture in just a few hours
Humans stalled for 59 years, but AI found a way in a few hours
- Google’s AI explored magnetic field equations relevant to experimental fusion reactors
- AI agents found new magnetic configurations within hours of starting their investigation
- Gemini helped extend mathematical solutions linked to a 59-year-old fusion research problem
Google’s Gemini 4 Argon has helped researchers extend mathematical solutions to a problem involving magnetic fields inside experimental fusion reactors, building on research that challenged a longstanding scientific conjecture.
The achievement concerns calculations used to model how magnetic fields contain superheated fuel, rather than a breakthrough that produces electricity or makes fusion commercially viable.
Instead of proving that an impossible problem could finally be solved, the team used AI to extend existing solutions into configurations that earlier examples had not covered.
Gemini finds new solutions by extending existing mathematics
Magnetic confinement fusion uses powerful fields to contain extremely hot, electrically charged gas, preventing it from escaping before atomic nuclei can combine and release energy.
Scientists need accurate mathematical models of those fields because computer simulations help them understand plasma behaviour and design configurations capable of maintaining confinement.
In 1967, physicist Harold Grad proposed a conjecture about the mathematical conditions governing equilibrium in three-dimensional magnetic fields, influencing research into plasma configurations.
In September 2026, University of Maryland researcher Matt Landreman published exact solutions that contradicted this conjecture, with assistance from OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Pro.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Those earlier solutions mattered because they supplied mathematical examples that researchers could use to test software modelling magnetic confinement, rather than relying entirely on approximations.
However, both families of solutions shared a particular geometric symmetry, leaving researchers without equivalent exact examples for configurations that lacked that property.
A subsequent study by Opal Issan, Jonathan Citrin, Landreman and Brendan Tracey extended the existing solutions by introducing a parameter that breaks this symmetry.
The resulting mathematical configurations give researchers additional reference cases for checking computer programs that calculate magnetic equilibrium in complicated three-dimensional arrangements.
AI shortened the search, not the entire scientific process
The researchers used Gemini 4 Argon through Google’s Antigravity environment, where multiple AI agents explored Landreman’s earlier results and investigated ways to extend them.
The agents found ways to remove a mathematical symmetry restriction from Landreman’s solutions, producing new configurations that researchers could verify.
The researchers reported that promising mathematical candidates emerged within hours, suggesting AI can accelerate difficult investigations involving extensive calculations and interconnected mathematical conditions.
This speed matters because developing and examining potential solutions requires researchers to work through complicated calculations and determine whether the resulting mathematical relationships hold together.
However, the initial discovery was only part of the process, since the researchers still needed to check the derivations and establish that the proposed solutions were mathematically consistent.
The team also used computational verification and AI assistance when preparing parts of the research manuscript, while the authors retained responsibility for the published work.
The immediate achievement is a more extensive set of exact mathematical solutions for researchers studying magnetic confinement, not evidence that AI has solved nuclear fusion or removed its engineering obstacles.
Via arXiv
