articles.title: GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories
articles.text:
The threat actor behind the GhostAction supply chain attack has expanded beyond injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows into compromised projects to phish open-source developers and deliver a stealer malware disguised within a fake font file.
The latest evolution, detailed by OpenSourceMalware, signals that the attackers are actively refining their modus operandi in response to steps taken by GitHub to prevent the workflow from running.
According to the threat intelligence platform, the threat actor registered the domain "my-github[.]com" and pointed it at "193.32.204[.]199," the same IP address that's used as an exfiltration endpoint for data harvested from running the malicious workflow.
The domain was registered on October 9, 2026, 17 days after "my-gitlab[.]com" was registered. There is no evidence at this stage to suggest that the two code-hosting-themed domains are operated by the same threat actor.
"It follows the same my-<code-host>.com naming pattern, making it a useful pivot, but current infrastructure does not directly connect it to GhostAction," security researcher Paul McCarty said. "They use different registrars, registrant records, Cloudflare nameserver pairs, IP addresses, ASNs, and DNS designs, and no shared certificate or account artifact has been recovered."
Since then, the "my-github[.]com" domain has been used in a phishing email impersonating a GitHub security alert to target an open-source maintainer. The message, sent from "noreply@my-github[.]com" and on the same day the domain was registered, warned of a suspicious new login to their GitHub account from Moscow, Russia, and instructed them to click on a link to secure their account.
The deceptive page, per OpenSourceMalware, is said to have acted as a reverse proxy, harvesting the victim's password and two-factor authentication (2FA) code, and injected JavaScript that authorized an OAuth app with permissions to modify their workflows so as to facilitate a GhostAction-style attack.
The fake login page also includes JavaScript to silently authorize a GitHub OAuth device flow with repo, workflow, and read:org scopes, granting it broad permissions to read/write repositories, modify Actions workflow files, and gain visibility into organization membership and related organizational data.
The idea is the same as device code phishing, where the end goal is to obtain an access token from GitHub and exfiltrate it to "my-github[.]com" on TCP/8443.
"The script receives a device code and user code, loads /login/device, extracts GitHub's forms from the returned HTML, and submits them automatically," McCarty explained. "It inserts the user code, locates an authorization form, adds authorize=1, and posts the approval through the victim's authenticated proxied session."
"The victim does not need to type the device code or consciously approve the OAuth application. This kit goes further by automating the user-code and authorization steps through the reverse-proxied session."
By stealing a repository-scoped OAuth token, it gives the attacker a reusable API credential. Furthermore, the permissions granted through the stealthy OAuth authorization are consistent with GhostAction's ability to enumerate repositories and inject malicious workflow files under ".github/workflows/."
"The actor can now combine repository-scale automation with individual social engineering against people whose accounts provide access to projects, organizations, registries, and downstream users," OpenSourceMalware said.
To make matters worse, the campaign has also been observed incorporating a second-stage component that persists on developer machines even after the malicious workflow has been removed.
Specifically, the approach takes a leaf out of North Korea's playbook by committing three different files -
- A Microsoft Visual Studio Code (VS Code) tasks.json file with a "runOn: folderOpen" trigger that causes it to run automatically when the folder is opened in the application.
- A "public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2" file that contains a stealer payload designed to harvest AWS keys, PyPI tokens, npm tokens, Git logins, Kubernetes cluster credentials, SSH private keys, and AI provider credentials for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini. The font file name is the same as one used in North Korea's Fake Font/PolinRider campaign from January 2026.
- A second GitHub Actions workflow that's activated if the infostealer never runs.
The VS Code task is set up to auto-run the credential stealer, which, besides collecting data, installs a cron job that runs attacker-supplied code every five minutes. The collected data is sent to the same server over plain HTTP on port 8080. A total of 94 compromised repositories with the second-stage component have been identified.
As for the second CI workflow, it's the same as the original malicious workflow, but with added credential formats to look for and a fallback that uploads findings to a secret GitHub gist if the POST fails. The second workflow goes by the following names -
- lint.yml
- ci-check.yml
- build-check.yml
- repo-health.yml
- audit.yml
- code-review.yml
- test-suite.yml
- cache-cleanup.yml
OpenSourceMalware said the 94 repositories belong to 66 owners, out of which 15 have since been deleted, renamed, or made private. Of the still accessible repositories, most of them appear to have been largely abandoned, with one of them left untouched for more than nine years. Sixty-five of the 79 went without a commit for more than a year.
"Stage 1 needs GitHub to run the workflow," OpenSourceMalware said. "On October 9, GitHub started preventing the malicious workflow from running, and the waves on October 10 and 12 extracted no secrets. Stage 2 adds a launcher that doesn't need a runner at all, and it arrived six days after the block. We can’t say the block caused it. We can say the operator moved to a place GitHub's controls don't reach."
To mitigate the threat, developers should revoke GitHub access and tokens from a clean device, change their passwords, audit their repositories, rotate every credential the workflows can reach, and alert users who have cloned the repositories.
"We don't know who the operator is, but their work suggests limited experience," Jenn Gile, co-founder of OpenSourceMalware, told The Hacker News. "The stealer's environment-variable filter misses most API keys, its home-directory search can time out and discard its own results, and a single IP handles exfiltration, phishing, and noisy internet scanning. That last mistake is why searching for the IP still finds infections."

articles.title: GTA 6 aún no sale, pero ya hay estafadores vendiendo versiones falsas por hasta mil dólares
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 todavía no llega al mercado, pero ya circulan sitios web que prometen copias filtradas, acceso anticipado y versiones de prueba a cambio de hasta USD 1.000. Las falsas ofertas utilizan la expectativa por el estreno previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026 para obtener pagos, datos personales o descargas de archivos desconocidos.
El riesgo crece porque muchos jugadores llevan más de una década esperando la nueva entrega de Rockstar Games. La compañía de seguridad digital, Kaspersky, detectó varias páginas dirigidas a los seguidores de GTA VI, con promesas de reservas gratuitas, pruebas beta y criptomonedas vinculadas con el juego. Ninguna de estas alternativas ofrece acceso legítimo antes del lanzamiento oficial.
Ofrecen una supuesta filtración por USD 1.000
Uno de los casos detectados corresponde a una página llamada CyberLeek. El sitio afirma disponer de una versión preliminar de GTA VI y presenta tres formas de obtenerla antes de su salida.
La primera opción promete el “juego completo” por USD 1.000, junto con contenido exclusivo y un enlace de descarga directa. La web asegura que la oferta tiene un límite de una copia por cliente.
También ofrece una prueba de 24 horas por USD 100. La tercera propuesta consiste en una campaña de financiación colectiva. Sus responsables aseguran que reunirán USD 50.000 para liberar el juego, aunque la letra pequeña eleva de forma repentina el objetivo a USD 500.000. Quienes aporten al menos USD 100 recibirían, según el sitio, acceso prioritario.
La página incluso promociona servicios para empresas. Por USD 5.000, propone introducir logotipos, productos o menciones de marca en un supuesto contenido futuro de Grand Theft Auto. La oferta resulta contradictoria con la promesa de una versión completa ya disponible para descargar.
Todos los pagos se realizan con Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT o Litecoin. El sitio indica que las operaciones son definitivas y no admite devoluciones.
CyberLeek fue el apodo del responsable de una intrusión en Rockstar Games y de una filtración de contenido de GTA VI. Después, otros actores comenzaron a utilizar ese nombre para crear webs con diseños distintos, pero con la misma promesa: acceso a una versión filtrada u oficial del juego.
Algunas de esas páginas invitan a descargar un lanzador desconocido o a “desbloquear” la versión completa. Los archivos e instaladores distribuidos desde estas webs pueden representar un riesgo, por lo que no conviene utilizarlos ni ejecutarlos en el ordenador personal.
Las falsas reservas solicitan correos, pagos y datos personales
Otra modalidad se dirige a quienes buscan reservar el juego. Una página ofrece códigos para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, y solicita al usuario elegir una consola e introducir su correo electrónico.
Para reforzar la apariencia de legitimidad, el sitio muestra 3.480 usuarios activos y asegura que solo quedan 121 códigos. Tras pulsar “Revelar código”, la página enseña cuatro caracteres y exige una verificación adicional que debe completarse en 15 minutos.
La comprobación lleva a una página en alemán que pide descargar y ejecutar una aplicación de chat con inteligencia artificial, además de aceptar sus condiciones. El objetivo puede ser enviar tráfico a páginas de terceros, algunas de ellas fraudulentas, con GTA VI como señuelo.
También existen páginas que imitan la PlayStation Store. Una de ellas, dirigida a usuarios brasileños, ofrece reservas por 449,9 BRL (cerca de 90 dólares), una cifra similar al precio oficial. El pago se puede efectuar con tarjeta o Pix, pero exige datos personales, incluido el CPF.
Los sitios que aseguran que GTA VI ya está disponible también son una trampa
Otros estafadores simplifican el engaño. Crean páginas con estética de GTA y logotipos de Rockstar Games, donde invitan a “probar GTA 6” o descargarlo para PC, PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
El juego no está disponible antes del 19 de noviembre de 2026. Por eso, cualquier descarga previa puede ocultar archivos no deseados. La barra de direcciones suele revelar el fraude: es necesario revisar el dominio y compararlo con la web oficial de Rockstar Games.
Otra web promociona una criptomoneda llamada $GTAVI, diseñada con referencias a Vice City. Sus creadores afirman que quienes posean el token podrían acceder al juego en el futuro, aunque no garantizan una copia.
El sitio declara una capitalización de USD 51.600 y un volumen de negociación diario de USD 7.880, sin explicar el origen ni la precisión de esas cifras. El modelo puede responder a una estrategia de inflar el valor del activo y venderlo después, con pérdidas para quienes lleguen tarde.
La recomendación es instalar juegos solo desde fuentes oficiales, no introducir datos de pago ni información personal en webs sospechosas y evitar lanzadores, archivos comprimidos o programas desconocidos. Ninguna beta, clave o filtración sustituye el lanzamiento oficial de GTA VI.

articles.title: Trust in AI: What adoption really looks like for Gulf SMEs
articles.text: An article by Ahmed Sameh, Chief Marketing Officer at Fortis Every AI story coming out of the UAE this year seems to feature the same cast: sovereign AI strategies, enterprise transformation programmes and government ministries preparing to deploy agentic AI across 50% of federal services and operations within two years . It’s an impressive story, but it is also the wrong one if you want to understand how AI is changing the way most Gulf businesses operate. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) account for 94% of businesses in the UAE, according to the Ministry of Economy , yet relatively little of the AI conversation focuses on them. We see the gap between these two stories every day. What we hear from merchants rarely matches the enterprise AI narrative. Their concerns are more practical, their resources more constrained, and their adoption story arguably more interesting. The readiness gap A 2025 study of 315 respondents from UAE hospitality SMEs found that top management support was among the strongest predictors of intention to adopt AI, alongside competitive pressure and government regulation. These factors carried more weight than the technology’s perceived usefulness. The problem is not simply whether the technology works. It is whether someone inside the business trusts it enough to champion it and has the time to put it to use. This helps explain why so much enterprise-grade AI tooling falls flat with SME merchants. A restaurant owner running three venues with a skeleton back-office team does not need a sprawling analytics suite that requires a dedicated administrator to configure. During our field research with food and beverage (F&B) merchants, operators often described software decisions in terms of risk rather than features. They wanted fast checkout, an easy way to set up menus, minimal staff training, reliable support and clear pricing. Our main conclusion was straightforward: "POS systems are chosen to minimise risk, not to maximise features." That distinction matters. Enterprise software is often designed around the breadth of its capabilities, while SME merchants are primarily concerned with whether it will make their day-to-day operations easier or more complicated. AI adapted from enterprise software can demand exactly what smaller businesses lack: dedicated IT staff, lengthy onboarding and patience for features built around problems they do not have. Where AI adoption is taking hold On the customer-facing side, AI is already changing how merchants sell. And much of that change is happening on customers’ terms, not merchants’. Consumers in the region are increasingly using AI to inform their purchasing decisions. Tabby’s 2026 shopping survey , covering more than 20,000 respondents in the UAE and Saudi Arabia, found that 43% use AI to help decide what to buy. Among 18- to 29-year-olds, 51.8% have used AI somewhere in their shopping journey. But adoption does not automatically mean trust. The same survey found that only 30% fully trust AI recommendations. For merchants, the opportunity is clear, but so is the challenge. AI-powered ordering, personalised loyalty offers and customer messaging may help businesses respond to changing shopping habits, but only if customers see value in the experience. We are observing a similar pattern from our end, although at an earlier stage. In our research into merchants’ use of AI, the tools they had adopted independently — ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek — clustered around a fairly consistent set of tasks. Most of these were marketing-related: writing social media captions, generating campaign ideas and coming up with product names. Merchants were also using AI to explore pricing decisions, such as what to charge for a new item or how to structure a bundle or discount. A smaller number were experimenting with AI-generated product images. What they had not explored, at least among the merchants we researched, was AI-powered sales analytics or forecasting. That gap is not necessarily about hesitation. It is also about the limitations of the tools they are using. A standalone AI assistant has no visibility into a merchant’s actual business performance unless it is connected to the relevant sales and operational data. And without that visibility, its usefulness has limits. Operations present a different but equally pressing challenge. For UAE retailers and hospitality businesses, staffing and inventory planning can be complicated by employment costs, visa requirements and seasonal fluctuations in demand. AI could help with forecasting, reordering and shift planning without requiring particularly sophisticated systems. But that is not what the merchants we speak to are asking for right now. They want faster answers. Not another dashboard, but a simple way to ask: What were today's sales? What changed from yesterday? What's selling best? Is anything unusual? Are we on track? Who sold the most? Which customers came back? Across our research, one request came up more frequently than any other: "Tell me what's happening in my business right now." That is a much more immediate starting point than predictive analytics. Before merchants can trust AI to tell them what might happen next week, they need to trust it to tell them what is happening today. Why the gap will get harder to close The difference between experimenting with AI and using it to improve business performance is already becoming clear. McKinsey’s 2025 State of AI report found that organisations it classified as AI high performers, representing about 6% of respondents, were three times more likely than their peers to report strong senior leadership ownership and commitment to AI initiatives. They were also more likely to have moved beyond experimentation and started scaling AI across their businesses. These findings concern organisations of different sizes, not Gulf SMEs specifically. But the underlying lesson is relevant: adopting AI tools and extracting measurable value from them are two different things. For smaller merchants, the implications could be significant. A restaurant that can anticipate a slow Tuesday and adjust staffing accordingly, or a retailer that can identify and re-engage customers who have stopped returning, may be able to operate more efficiently than a competitor relying entirely on manual decisions. Over time, those advantages can compound, particularly in retail and hospitality, where margins leave little room for error. But getting there requires tools designed around how SMEs actually operate: thin teams, tight margins and no time for a six-month rollout. It does not require SMEs to become AI companies. Nor should they have to make do with a stripped-down version of a platform designed for a 500-person enterprise. The starting point is simpler: it gives merchants access to their own business information in a way that is immediate, understandable and useful. Build trust through reliable answers before asking them to rely on more complex predictions or automated decisions. For Gulf SMEs, the next stage of AI adoption may have less to do with how sophisticated the technology becomes and more to do with how well it fits the businesses expected to use it. The merchants who find tools that fit will be better placed to pull ahead.

articles.title: I played the Resident Evil 4 remake on Nintendo Switch 2, and it's a solid way to experience the survival horror masterpiece, though it isn’t without its flaws
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Nintendo Switch 2 port of Resident Evil 4 does a solid job, with fairly smooth frame rates and decent-looking visuals, as well as some most-welcome motion control support. Texture pop-in can slightly dampen your immersion in both docked and handheld mode, and you’ll experience the occasional frame drop throughout your journey, but this is still a good way to play a true great of the survival horror genre.
Reasons to buy
- + Core experience still a survival horror masterpiece
- + Solid visual fidelity
- + Generally smooth gameplay…
Reasons to avoid
- - …but there are some noticeable frame drops
- - Texture pop-in issues in docked and handheld
- - Motion controls not implemented all too well
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
When the remake of Resident Evil 4 launched in 2023, it was met with universal acclaim, even netting a Game of the Year nomination. And that came as no surprise to me. This is a brilliant entry in Capcom’s legendary series, packing in spectacular survival horror gameplay, a massively engaging story, and a memorable cast of characters.
Platform reviewed: Nintendo Switch 2
Available on: PS4, PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox One, Xbox Series X and Series S, PC, iOS
Release date: October 16, 2026 (Switch 2 edition)
And now, Resident Evil 4 (Gold Edition) has arrived on Nintendo Switch 2. I’ve put about 20 hours into the game, during which time I’ve played through a good chunk of the main story and completed many a request. So how does this game hold up on Nintendo’s hybrid platform? Here’s everything you need to know.
Let me start by saying that the core Resident Evil 4 remake experience is incredible. Leon is a charming and likeable protagonist, the gunplay is excellent with a fantastic suite of weapons to choose from, and the narrative is top-class too. Sure, this entry perhaps lacks the chilling, claustrophobic atmosphere of its predecessors, but there’s plenty of high-octane action segments, fun puzzles, and big scares to experience. So if you haven’t played this game just yet, I highly recommend it.
A remake that's great on the go...but has a few graphical gremlins
How exactly does this title perform on Switch 2, though? Well, between this game and the other two entries recently ported to Nintendo Switch 2 — Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 3 — Resident Evil 4 is the one that has the highest amount of performance issues. This is totally understandable — it’s a newer release than the other two entries and carries a higher technical demand — but this isn’t quite the definitive way to play through Leon’s adventure.
So, let’s take a look at some of the blemishes I noticed on this port. The largest of these relates to texture pop-in. Whether I was playing in handheld or docked mode, some visual elements — such as trees or cliffs — would appear lower in resolution from a distance, and suddenly appear more detailed and intricate as I drew closer to them. Is this a major issue? Not really. It had no impact on my ability to vanquish my foes. But it’s something I did encounter regularly, and it could sometimes make the experience a little less immersive.
In addition, I encountered a few frame drops throughout my playthrough. When I ventured into a cave with a purple flickering flame, the game appeared to run less smoothly. This only lasted for a second or two, but it happened a good handful of times during my time with the game. Like the Resident Evil 2 Switch 2 port, and the Resi 3 Switch 2 port, the motion of some distant enemies appeared shaky, with some noticeable frame drops. With that said, combat was generally very smooth, and I rarely found said frame drops to give me a disadvantage in skirmishes.
Another thing worth noting is that this version of the game supports motion controls, something I was really hoping to see in the recent ports of the game’s predecessors. This is a most welcome inclusion, giving fans of gyro aiming another way to play…but it could’ve been implemented more effectively. While vertical aiming feels precise and responsive, horizontal movement is sluggish by comparison. Still, traditional controls work like a dream, and there are a number of schemes you can choose from in the Options menu to suit your personal preferences.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
When I rescued the friendly dog (wolf?) in the village, I felt like I’d done my good deed for the day. And what do you know, when it was time to face off against a towering giant, the trusty pooch came to my aid, distracting my towering foe as I blasted him repeatedly with my rifle. Talk about good karma.
I want to be clear: this game doesn’t perform badly, not by any means.
For the most part, Resident Evil 4 plays nicely on the Switch 2, with largely smooth performance and solid graphical fidelity, especially in docked mode. Of course, some textures look a bit less refined in handheld mode, but the dark and dismal environments still translate over nicely. The game also has HDR support for enhanced contrast, and character models look pretty sharp too. And all in all, I found the port to be totally serviceable — just expect an experience closer to the PS4 version than the PS5 one.
In the end, the Nintendo Switch 2 port of the Resident Evil 4 remake is decent. A lot of the issues, like pop-in and occasional frame drops, feel relatively minor in the grand scheme of things, though I wish motion controls felt more precise. Still, you get generally smooth performance, good visual fidelity, and all of the major DLC bundled in, including the excellent Separate Ways.
Is this the definitive way to play through Leon Kennedy’s journey? Perhaps not. But if you want to experience Resident Evil 4 on the go, this Switch 2 port is a perfectly fine option.
Should you play Resident Evil 4 for Nintendo Switch 2?
Play it if…
You want to experience Leon’s adventure on the go
As is the case with any Switch 2 port, the system’s hybrid capabilities are a huge plus. The game runs relatively well, even in handheld mode, so if you want to take Leon on the go, the Switch 2 version is a serviceable way of doing so.
You’re yet to experience the RE4 remake
If you missed the Resident Evil 4 remake, now is the time to play it. The Switch 2 version is the Gold Edition, meaning you get the base game along with the major DLC like Separate Ways.
Don’t play it if…
You want best-in-class performance
While Resident Evil 4 runs fairly well on Switch 2, there are some clear blemishes. The most obvious is texture pop-in, which means that some parts of the environment, like trees and cliffs, switch from a lower to a higher resolution as you approach them. There are also a few frame drops here and there, which isn’t overly problematic, but still something you’re less likely to experience on PS5, for instance.
You’re new to Resident Evil
The story beats of Resident Evil 4 won’t hit as hard for you if you’ve not played some previous entries in the series, mainly Resident Evil 2. I highly recommend playing that title first, and believe me it’s well-worth it.
Accessibility features
The options menu allows you to make a few changes to your experience, with a range of camera options, a number of control schemes including motion aiming, toggle or hold run modes, and a range of voice and text languages available. What’s more, you can change the color of the reticle, laser dot sight, and biosensor scope, alter HUD opacity, and tone down damage display if you’d prefer.
How I reviewed Resident Evil 4 for Nintendo Switch 2
I put more than 20 hours into the Resident Evil 4 remake on Nintendo Switch 2, during which time I played through the main story and completed as many requests as possible while playing in both docked and handheld mode.
The vast majority of the time, I played the game docked, with my Switch 2 connected to the Sky Glass Gen 2 TV and Marshall Heston 120 soundbar. I also dabbled in handheld gameplay now and then, though, and used my JBL Live Beam 4 earbuds to experience the game’s virtual spatial sound.
More generally, I’m an experienced gaming hardware and software reviewer, and have been testing all kinds of games and accessories at TechRadar for years now, where I serve as a Senior Reviews Writer. I’ve reviewed all sorts of Nintendo Switch 2 titles, from major first-party releases like Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave to ports like Yakuza Kiwami. I’ve also played a number of Resident Evil games, including the Switch 2 ports of the Resident Evil 2 and 3 remakes.
First reviewed October 2026
Harry is a Senior Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He reviews everything from party speakers to wall chargers and has a particular interest in the worlds of audio and gaming. Harry has a background in business tech journalism, particularly around the telecoms industry.

articles.title: Apple rachète Samplab, l'app d'édition audio dopée à l'IA
articles.text:
Apple a repris en juin une partie des actifs de Samplab, une start-up suisse spécialisée dans l'édition audio par IA, et propose un poste à une partie de ses salariés. L'accord n'a été rendu public que lundi, via la liste des acquisitions de la Commission européenne.
Samplab proposait une application et des plug-ins pour retoucher un morceau note par note. Son service a fermé mi-septembre et son site redirige désormais vers Apple.com.
Samplab transformait un fichier audio en partition modifiable
Dans son avis, la Commission indique qu'Apple reprend, par l'intermédiaire d'une filiale, une partie des actifs de Samplab GmbH et propose un emploi à une partie de ses salariés. L'accord date du 17 juin. Samplab, fondée à Zurich en 2020 par Manuel Fritsche et Gian-Marco Hutter, compterait dix employés au maximum, et peut-être seulement ses deux fondateurs d'après LinkedIn. La start-up avait annoncé sa fermeture fin juin et prévoyait de rembourser le solde des abonnements annuels. C'est le DMA qui force APple a rendre cet accord public. L'entreprise est classée contrôleur d'accès (gatekeeper) et doit informer Bruxelles de ses opérations touchant aux services de plateforme, aux services numériques ou à la collecte de données.
Concrètement, Samplab convertissait un enregistrement audio en MIDI. Ce format ne contient pas le son, mais une sorte de partition numérique. Il indique quelles notes sont jouées, à quel moment et pendant combien de temps. Une fois l'audio converti, il est possible de modifier une note ou un accord sans réenregistrer. L'outil détectait les accords, calait le tempo et la tonalité de plusieurs échantillons pour obtenir un ensemble harmonieux, et séparait les "stems", c'est-à-dire les pistes d'un morceau (voix, guitare, batterie par exemple). Il permettait aussi de retoucher des notes dans un audio polyphonique, où plusieurs notes sonnent en même temps, sans toucher au timbre.
Apple n'a pas commenté l'opération. La firme de Cupertino pourrait intégrer la technologies dans ses applications, qu'il s'agisse de Logic Pro, GaraBand, ou Final Cut Pro. Souligons que les plug-ins de Samplab fonctionnaient déjà avec Logic Pro.
Cet accord arrive une semaine après celui de Huxe, une start-up fondée par d'anciens ingénieurs de NotebookLM, spécialisée dans les briefings audio et les contenus de type podcast générés par IA. Nous rapportions en janvier qu'Apple avait déboursé près de 2 milliards de dollars pour s'offrir Q.ai, une jeune pousse israélienne dont l'IA interprète les micro-mouvements du visage. Pour Samplab, le texte publié ne mentionne aucun montant.
Sources : AppleInsider

articles.title: Un fallo expuso instrucciones secretas del chatbot de WhatsApp para evitar a reguladores de privacidad
articles.text:
Un fallo técnico expuso durante un tiempo indeterminado las instrucciones internas que Meta le da al chatbot de soporte de WhatsApp, entre ellas la orden de no mencionar a reguladores de protección de datos cuando un usuario pregunta por sus derechos de privacidad, según reveló la revista Wired.
La firma de privacidad Redact detectó el problema al rastrear el código de unas 80 páginas de ayuda y preguntas frecuentes del sitio de WhatsApp. Allí encontró cerca de 100 bloques de texto oculto, invisibles para los usuarios comunes pero pensados para guiar las respuestas del chatbot basado en un modelo de lenguaje de Meta.
Una de las secciones llevaba el título “QUÉ NO DECIR”. En la página sobre cómo eliminar una cuenta, las instrucciones ordenaban al asistente “no recomendar contactar a ninguna autoridad de protección de datos, regulador u organismo de supervisión” ante un reclamo del usuario.
En la página sobre cómo reportar o bloquear contactos, otro bloque indicaba qué hacer si alguien mencionaba “acciones legales, demandas, abogados o litigios”: el chatbot debía evitar citar, interpretar o hacer referencia a los Términos de Servicio o la Política de Privacidad de WhatsApp.
Las mismas instrucciones prohibían al asistente “ofrecer opiniones legales, defensas o interpretaciones en nombre de WhatsApp” y le impedían mencionar normas de protección de datos como el Reglamento General de Protección de Datos (RGPD) de Europa, la Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales brasileña o la Ley de Privacidad del Consumidor de California, incluso si el propio usuario las nombraba primero.
Otros fragmentos ocultos le indicaban al chatbot cómo responder si un usuario decía ser sordo o tener dificultades auditivas, con la aclaración de que ese dato era “información de contexto sobre el usuario, NO su pedido de soporte”. Otro bloque le prohibía mencionar funciones de la aplicación que todavía no estuvieran disponibles para el público.
Dan Saltman, fundador de la empresa Redact, dijo que su equipo analiza de forma habitual los sitios y las políticas de privacidad de las grandes tecnológicas. “Lo llamativo acá es la diferencia entre lo que se le dice a las personas y lo que se le dice a los modelos de lenguaje”, afirmó.
La respuesta de Meta
Saltman aclaró que buena parte de las instrucciones halladas eran simples y remitían a los canales oficiales de soporte, pero consideró que no parecían destinadas a quedar expuestas públicamente. El texto aparecía bajo un bloque de código llamado “HelpContentGalaxyLLMInclude”.
Después de que Wired consultó a Meta, la compañía retiró el texto de todas las páginas afectadas. El vocero de WhatsApp Joshua Breckman atribuyó la exposición a un error técnico ya corregido y dijo que las instrucciones estaban dirigidas al chatbot y no a los usuarios.
“Buscamos que nuestros chatbots de soporte se enfoquen en dar el mejor consejo sobre WhatsApp, no en ofrecer asesoramiento legal”, sostuvo Breckman. Agregó que la empresa sí brinda información transparente sobre los derechos de datos de sus usuarios y cómo ejercerlos.
Breckman no precisó cuánto tiempo estuvieron expuestas las instrucciones ni si chatbots de terceros llegaron a acceder a ese texto antes de que Meta lo eliminara del código de las páginas.
Una ventana a cómo se entrena a los chatbots
El hallazgo expone una práctica poco visible para el público: las empresas redactan reglas detalladas de comportamiento para sus asistentes de inteligencia artificial, que suelen incluir restricciones sobre qué temas evitar y cómo manejar situaciones delicadas.
En este caso, esas reglas quedaron momentáneamente a la vista de cualquiera que revisara el código fuente de las páginas de ayuda, incluidas versiones archivadas que todavía pueden consultarse en internet.
WhatsApp, utilizada por miles de millones de personas en el mundo, integró en los últimos años un asistente de inteligencia artificial generativa de Meta en su función de soporte técnico, además del chatbot conversacional que ya ofrece a los usuarios en sus chats.
Wired precisó que el texto expuesto todavía puede verse en copias archivadas de las páginas de ayuda, aun después de que Meta lo eliminó de las versiones activas del sitio.
.

articles.title: From Email-to-Case to the Boardroom: How Inherited Agents Break Governance Built for Software
articles.text:
In Salesforce Agentforce, the recommended way to make an agent respond to events is a Flow: a record is created or a case is updated, and the Flow passes data into the agent's prompt. Separately, Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case turn inbound customer messages into case records; it is how airlines and hotels run support intake. Both are standard, documented, as-designed features. Chained together, they produce this path:
public internet → email → case record → agent prompt → agent action → case comment → outbound reply
An unauthenticated outsider now has a route into an internal agent's instructions, and the agent's reply leaves through the same door. Nothing was misconfigured. The finding, documented by researchers in August 2026, is a clean example of how agents that arrive inside existing platforms fail: through the application around them, not the model inside them.
The risk is in the application, and the application is the thing nobody re-reviewed
Which intake features are enabled, which triggers fire, which objects are exposed to guest users, which automation passes untrusted data where, and which model version the agent is quietly calling underneath: these are the variables that decide whether the Agentforce chain is a support-queue nuisance or a data exposure. A vendor risk review performed once at procurement sees none of them, because the agent did not exist at procurement. A prompt filter watching the agent's inputs does not know that a particular input originated from a stranger, because prompt filters do not understand Email-to-Case.
Securing an inherited agent therefore means understanding its host application at the depth its own admins do. That depth is the one thing a questionnaire and a scanner both lack. The City-Forum campaign, an active worldwide data-theft operation against Salesforce and ServiceNow instances running since March 2025, was found in exactly this territory: the gap between platform features and the configurations enterprises actually run.
Builders are multiplying, and some of them are agents
The platforms have made agent creation as accessible as making a slide deck. Marketing operations builds an agent to pull pipeline reports. Finance builds one to reconcile invoices. Each rides its creator's permissions, because that is what makes it useful. Shadow AI was an employee pasting data into a chatbot. Shadow agents are that employee's access, running unattended, multiplied across everything they were ever granted.
Increasingly, agents also build agents. A coding agent tagged into a chat channel can scaffold and deploy another agent as easily as it opens a pull request; an orchestration platform spins up sub-agents to divide a task, each with its own connections and none with its own review. Any governance model that assumes a human requested each agent is quietly obsolete.
Why governance keeps producing a document
Ask a large enterprise about agent governance and the answer is usually a document: an acceptable-use policy, a monthly committee, a set of principles nobody disputes and nothing enforces. Ask the operational question, how many agents are running right now, what can they reach, and who owns each one, and the document does not know.
The OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 now describes the sharpest version of this gap under its "No Governance" category: a skill deployed and managed inside a third-party platform is unreachable by external scanners (OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 whitepaper, ast10-top10-whitepaper-2, published at owasp.github.io). The tools an enterprise points at the problem from outside cannot see inside the venues where most agents live. Governance fails most often because the rules get written before the security team can see the things the rules apply to.
The stack, bottom-up, with a test for each layer
The working order is bottom-up, and each layer is the precondition for the one above it. A practical way to check whether a program is real is to apply an operational test at each level.
| Layer | What it has to produce | The operational test | 
| Discovery | A continuously refreshed population across app configs, OAuth grants, network, endpoint, email metadata, and browser | Is the discovered count several multiples of the list IT keeps? If not, discovery isn't reaching where agents live. | 
| Posture | Every platform's agent-relevant settings, measured against how they should be configured | Can the team list the intake features and guest-user exposures wired to agent triggers on its top three platforms? | 
| Identity and ownership | An identity and a named owner per agent, with a lifecycle | Pick an agent at random. Does a human raise a hand within a day when asked "whose is this?" | 
| Usage | Who is building what, through which surface, with what data | Is there a sanctioned path that ships a business team's agent with secure defaults, or only a block? | 
| Agent controls | Least privilege against observed need, approval and quarantine for new agents, risk tiering that reflects each agent's full context | Does the same finding on a sandboxed dev agent and a customer-facing one show different severities? | 
| Runtime | Live inspection and intervention | Is it fed by the five layers above, or deployed first and enforcing blind? | 
The cost of paper compliance
The EU AI Act's penalties carry GDPR-level weight: up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited practices, up to €15 million or 3% for other violations. Every framework converging on it assumes the stack above exists. GDPR already showed what happens when it does not. British Airways (£20 million) and Marriott (£18.4 million) were not fined for having imperfect policies. Everyone has imperfect policies. They were fined because compliance existed on paper and could not be evidenced operationally when regulators asked. A governance practice built bottom-up generates that evidence as a byproduct: the inventory, the owners, the configurations, the review history.
Some platforms are designed to produce exactly that record. One leading example is Reco, which discovers agents across multiple vantage points, including the ones that never touch SSO, and assigns each a risk profile before any policy can be applied to it.
The Agentforce chain at the top of this article is not an exploit. It is a configuration, and configurations are governable, provided someone can see them. Chapters 1 to 3 of Into the Expanse cover the shift, the three launch vectors, and the governance practice in full: https://www.reco.ai/agent-ecosystem-security

articles.title: Workers are spending more time correcting AI-generated content than doing actual work
articles.text:
Workers are spending more time correcting AI-generated content than doing actual work
Does AI really save time?
- Workers using AI are finding that they need to spend time improving its output, new research finds
- Almost half say they have needed to make substantial corrections to AI-produced material
- Over a third believe checking the AI’s work takes longer than doing the task themselves
Is AI taking up more time than it should? That seems to be general view of users of workplace AI, according to new research that explores how AI impacts productivity. The answer? Not very well.
The Use.AI study surveyed over 8,000 adults who use AI in the workplace, and found that while it made it easier to produce work, it also requires substantial revision. Some respondents found that AI can produce documents and material they wouldn’t have created themselves, but almost 48% have found that the technology creates more problems.
Although the research indicates a “fire and forget” approach to AI-generated material, people who take the time to check the work find problems, and revisions take time to complete.
Editing AI
The survey of 8,316 adults using AI in the UK and European Union, as well as the US, Canada, Australia, and Latin America by Use.AI revealed both positives and negatives around how AI is used in the workplace.
For example, 62% were enthused by how much easier it made creating documents, memos, and even code. But what happens next in the process is where the problems are found. A worrying 34% of respondents were forwarding AI-produced (or assisted) work without checking the contents. This can lead to issues when the AI has produced something unsuitable or unreadable.
A worrying 48% answered that they had received AI-assisted work that required correction, and 43% stated they had been forced to redo unsuitable AI work. Sadly, this meant that additional time was required, with 39% saying checking the AI’s effort took longer than creating their own version from scratch, and 41% highlighting how much more reviewing and verifying AI produced material was required since AI was brought into the productivity process.
Is AI really a productivity boost?
The findings raise an interesting question. Big money has been spent on AI tools and implementing policies and procedures, replacing personnel, and employing “AI-ready” marketing tactics over the past few years.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
But the research suggests that rather than being an advantage, for many businesses, AI can be a problem. More oversight is required to ensure the AI is fulfulling tasks accurately. This means more time is being spent resolving errors, quality issues, and more. The productivity advantages that AI should provide are being negated by its production of sub-par material.
And for all of the trumpeting about AI in the workplace, there is one statistic that stands out: 58% of respondents state that there are no rules for checking AI-assisted work. This may account for the growing problem that we see around us day-to-day – obviously AI-produced slop, issued via a single prompt and distrubed without any form of review. Use.AI’s research can be read online.

He currently heads up the team at smart home website Matter Alpha, and writes about retro gaming at Gaming Retro.

articles.title: DirectX, Vulkan 1.3, Snapshots, l'outil de virtualisation UTM fait le plein de nouveautés
articles.text:
UTM, l'outil libre qui fait tourner Windows ou Linux dans une fenêtre sur Mac, iPhone et iPad, gère maintenant DirectX pour Windows 11 sur macOS et Vulkan 1.3 pour Linux. Il ajoute aussi un onglet Snapshots pour sauvegarder l'état d'une machine virtuelle.
Les notes de la version 5.0.8, publiées sur GitHub, rassemblent les changements de la branche 5.0. Plusieurs nouveautés dépendent de la version de macOS ou d'iOS installée.
DirectX, Vulkan, sauvegardes : les nouveautés et les précautions à prendre
Pour afficher de la 3D, une machine virtuelle (VM) passe par des interfaces comme DirectX (Windows) ou Vulkan et OpenGL (Linux). UTM sait désormais gérer DirectX pour Windows 11 sur macOS. Le pilote reste expérimental et la compatibilité avec les jeux est limitée, d'où la recommandation de repartir d'une installation neuve pour éviter les instabilités. le pilote doit être choisi pendant l'installation des "guest tools", les outils à installer dans Windows. Si l'ancien pilote, limité à l'affichage, est déjà en place, il faut d'abord lancer le script de désinstallation fourni avec ces outils. Nous rapportions dans un article sur Windows 11 et les Mac M3 que Windows passait sur ces machines par sa version ARM, la seule gérée par Parallels Desktop, et que celle-ci pouvait d'ailleurs rencontrer quelques problèmes avec les logiciels conçus pour les processeurs Intel. Avec DirectX, UTM s’attaque à un autre point faible de Windows sur Mac : l’affichage 3D, et donc les jeux et les applications graphiques.
Côté Linux, UTM gère désormais Vulkan 1.3, grâce aux pilotes VirtIO Venus de Mesa (la bibliothèque graphique de Linux). Pour l'interface OpenGL 4.1, il s’appuie sur un nouveau moteur, Apple Core OpenGL. Celui-ci est réservé à macOS et ne prend en charge ni Vulkan ni DirectX. Attention, l’affichage du bureau Linux lui-même ne fonctionne pas avec Vulkan, car certaines commandes de dessin 3D ne sont pas gérées. Il faut alors régler le Linux installé dans la machine virtuelle pour qu’il utilise l’ancien pilote VirGL.
Le nouvel onglet Snapshots fonctionne comme un point de restauration. Il est possible de figer l'état d'une VM pour y revenir plus tard. Il s'applique aux VM QEMU sur macOS et iOS 26, et aux VM Apple Virtualization (la technologie d'Apple) sur macOS 27. Sous macOS 27, ces dernières acceptent aussi les périphériques USB, le Secure Boot pour Linux (qui vérifie le démarrage) et l'exécution sans enregistrer les modifications. De nouveaux modes réseau permettent également aux VM de communiquer entre elles. Sur iOS, les gestes tactiles répondent immédiatement, avec clic central, glisser-clic droit et un mode de défilement par glissement. Sur l'iPhone Duo, plié comme un ordinateur portable, la moitié basse sert de clavier ou de pavé tactile.
Avant de mettre à jour, les développeurs recommandent d'éteindre toutes les VM. Celles qui sont suspendues risquent de ne pas reprendre correctement ensuite. UTM nécessite désormais macOS 12 ou iOS 15 au minimum, contre macOS 11.3 et iOS 14 auparavant.
Quelle différence avec CrossOver ?
Du côté de CrossOver, de l’éditeur CodeWeavers, les choses sont différentes. Le logiciel n’est pas un émulateur. Il traduit les appels des programmes Windows en appels macOS, sans machine virtuelle. Nous rapportions en mars 2025 que CrossOver 25 permettait alors de jouer à Red Dead Redemption 2 sur Mac. La version 26, publiée le 10 février dernier, repose sur Wine 11 et sur D3DMetal 3.0, la couche qui traduit DirectX vers Metal, l’interface graphique du Mac. UTM, lui, fait tourner un Windows 11 complet dans une machine virtuelle et s’appuie aussi sur D3DMetal pour DirectX 12, quand il est disponible. CrossOver fait usage de Rosetta 2, la couche d’Apple qui traduit les programmes Intel pour les puces Apple Silicon. Rosetta 2 doit disparaitre avec macOS 28 en 2027. CodeWeavers a donc présenté cet été une préversion de CrossOver 27 native pour Apple Silicon, laquelle abandonne les Mac Intel. Cette version de test n’inclut pas encore D3DMetal et de nombreux lanceurs de jeux n’y fonctionnent pas. La version finale est attendue début 2027.
- Une solution de virtualisation compatible avec les Mac M1
- De nombreux profils pour les différentes machines virtuelles
- Un design récent

articles.title: Fake Web3 Accelerator Uses npm Packages to Spread Malware and Hijack AI Agent Traffic
articles.text:
A fake Web3 accelerator has been observed pushing information stealers and backdoors to Windows and macOS systems using malicious npm packages under the pretext of offering free artificial intelligence (AI) credits for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini, coding tools, and security audits.
"The tools delivered information-stealing malware and backdoors for macOS and Windows machines," Elastic Security Labs researchers Jia Yu Chan and Daniel Stepanic said. "The operation also repackaged a legitimate coding agent to send model requests through attacker-controlled services, while its audit tools generated fabricated security findings."
The scheme poses as a Web3 venture capital accelerator named Apex Accelerator to target cryptocurrency startups and founders. It's being tracked under the moniker REF8801. The names of the npm packages, each of which targets both Windows and macOS machines, are listed below -
- @apexacc/cli (Apex Copilot CLI — AI advisor for Web3 founders) -
- @apexacc/audit (Web3 Security Scanner — 18 tools for DYOR and smart contract auditing)
While both the packages and their associated GitHub repositories are no longer accessible, "@apexacc/cli" was advertised as an "AI advisor for Web3 founders" that's powered by Claude Fable 5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash.
"@apexacc/audit," on the other hand, claimed to be a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing 18 security tools for scanning tokens, wallets, and smart contracts. Both packages were published by an npm user named "apexaccelerator" and linked to a GitHub account called "apexaccs" and an entity referred to as the Apex Foundation.
It's unclear who is behind the operation, but Elastic Security Labs said it spotted Russian-language comments in the source code commit history. However, these clues alone are not sufficient to definitively establish their identity or origins.
Interestingly, the campaign itself is not new. In late July 2026, SafeDep detailed three other npm packages linked to the same operation that were found distributing a macOS stealer belonging to the Atomic Stealer (aka AMOS) family -
- @apexfdn/apex
- @copilot-mcp/apex, which features the same package description as "@apexacc/cli"
- @apexfdn/copilot-mcp, which claims to be an Apex Copilot and MCP server for "portfolio diligence and operator tools"
Artifacts captured by Socket show that the Apex Foundation has been linked to at least two distinct domains since April 2026
- apexaccs[.]org
- apexfdn[.]xyz
According to Internet Archive snapshots dating back to March 19, 2026, the foundation states: "The Apex Foundation offers $235,000 investments, grants, and partnerships, and connects projects with VCs, angels, and private equity if they don't meet our criteria."
Posts shared on X show the accelerator approaching developers of cryptocurrency wallets and market intelligence tools for traders with offers of direct investment and instructions to run their due diligence tool ("@apexacc/cli"). In the case of the latter, the npm package has been found to drop an encrypted malware loader disguised as an Apple app ("com.apple.system.loader").
"The group also sought to build credibility through its presence at TOKEN2049 in Singapore and other in-person events it has hosted in the past," Elastic said. "The group attempts to manufacture legitimacy by appearing at widely attended conferences, indirectly lending credibility to the project."
Once installed, neither of the npm packages provides the promised functionality. The 18 security tools part of the @apexacc/audit package generate fabricated findings, while @apexacc/cli's scoring test returns an unsupported assessment of a fictitious project.
Instead, their primary responsibility is to propagate a macOS backdoor called CloudSyncD and a custom Windows information stealer that exfiltrates data through Telegram. The platform-specific executables are retrieved from the projects' GitHub releases.
Both packages implement a distinct verification path for Windows and macOS by sending an HTTP POST request to "win32" or "darwin" to "vrf.apexaccs[.]org/api/v1/vrf" to initiate the appropriate next stage. The Windows and macOS infection chains are as follows -
Windows -
- The malware retrieves a Base64-encoded PowerShell command, which reaches out to another endpoint ("0auth-chromium[.]com/APIService") to fetch a second PowerShell script ("drop.ps1") that downloads an executable ("bludness.exe") from "ehegisnightmare[.]icu" and launches it in a hidden window.
- The PyInstaller executable is a Python loader that checks if it already has administrator privileges and, if so, downloads the next stage from "ehegisnightmare[.]icu," saves it as "%TEMP%\exegis.exe," and launches it. If not, it attempts to bypass User Account Control (UAC) using UACME's ucmDebugObjectMethod().
- The "exegis.exe" binary is another PyInstaller executable that collects system metadata, running processes, and performs anti-virtual-machine (anti-VM) checks before decrypting and launching a bundled loader as "%TEMP%\updater_loader.exe."
- The Golang executable patches Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) and Event Tracing for Windows (ETW), unhooks "ntdll.dll" to blind endpoint security tools, and loads the next-stage shellcode into its own memory.
- The shellcode is a native information stealer that examines for signs of a prior infection and then harvests system information, clipboard text, process listings, Wi-Fi profile names, screenshots, and data from wallets, browser extensions, messengers, remote-access and file transfer protocol (FTP) applications, virtual private network (VPN) clients, browsers (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and Yandex), and game clients. The stealer can also bypass Chrome's app-bound encryption (ABE) protections to extract saved passwords, session cookies, browsing history, download records, and profile metadata. The collected data is exfiltrated through Telegram.
macOS -
- The malware downloads a remotely hosted bash script and executes it on the machine.
- The shell script downloads a GZIP-compressed archive from "verify.apexfdn[.]xyz/unix/," saves it as "package.tar.gz" in a temporary directory, and extracts its contents.
- The archive contains a dropper for CloudSyncD, which first phishes the victim's system login password using a fake authorization prompt and then uses it to launch an embedded payload with sudo privileges. The payload performs host discovery, collects hardware and operating-system details, and then contacts an external server ("ccmihr[.]com") to transmit the data and receive further tasks that allow the malware to download and run additional payloads.
It's worth noting that CloudSyncD was first documented by Jamf Threat Labs late last month, detailing its propagation via a fake Zoom installer. The malware was detected in the wild in mid-September 2026.
"Its behaviors illustrate how macOS malware continues to move toward native implementations, string protection, and execution paths that attempt to avoid writing payloads to disk, while still depending on the oldest technique available: asking the user for their password," Jamf said.
Besides deploying a stealer and backdoor depending upon the infected operating system, the packages are capable of intercepting and redirecting OpenRouter large language model (LLM) traffic, as well as registering an MCP server under their control in the victim's agent configuration.
"These changes allow the attacker-controlled API to receive the prompts, conversation history, code snippets, and tool outputs included in the agent's LLM requests," Elastic researchers explained.
"The attacker's MCP server can also supply instructions that are added to the agent's prompt, along with tool names, descriptions, and accepted inputs that help the model decide which tools to invoke and how to use them. Together, these mechanisms give the attacker visibility into the submitted data and a way to influence the agent's subsequent actions."

articles.title: Es posible ir preso por hacer música con IA: descubre si es mito o riesgo real
articles.text:
La condena de Michael Smith, un hombre de 54 años residente en Carolina del Norte, reavivó una duda entre quienes usan herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) para componer o producir canciones: ¿hacer música con IA puede derivar en una sanción legal o incluso en una pena de prisión?
La respuesta depende del uso. Crear una obra con asistencia tecnológica no es, por sí solo, un delito. Smith fue condenado el 6 de octubre de 2026 a 18 meses de prisión por un esquema de fraude de reproducciones musicales.
La Fiscalía del Distrito Sur de Nueva York sostuvo que obtuvo más de 8 millones de dolares en regalías mediante cuentas falsas, programas automatizados y cientos de miles de canciones generadas con IA. Recibió dos años de libertad supervisada y una orden de decomiso por 8 millones de dólares.
Qué riesgos hay al componer una canción con IA
Componer una melodía, escribir una letra con apoyo de un sistema generativo o producir una base instrumental mediante IA no configura, de forma automática, un delito.
El riesgo aparece si el resultado reproduce una obra protegida sin permiso, suplanta la voz de una persona, utiliza datos personales de forma ilegítima o se integra en una maniobra de fraude.
La diferencia central está entre la herramienta y la conducta. La inteligencia artificial puede intervenir en la creación musical, pero no elimina las obligaciones sobre derechos de autor, contratos de plataformas, identificación de contenidos sintéticos y protección de la identidad de artistas o terceros.
Por qué una persona sí terminó condenada por usar IA en canciones
El caso no castigó la generación de música mediante IA, sino la obtención de regalías a través de reproducciones ficticias. Entre 2017 y 2024, Smith creó miles de cuentas falsas en Spotify, Amazon Music, Apple Music y YouTube Music. Luego usó programas para que esas cuentas reprodujeran continuamente canciones de su catálogo.
La Fiscalía estadounidense indicó que la operación llegó a utilizar hasta 10.000 cuentas automatizadas de manera simultánea. Smith distribuía la actividad entre miles de pistas para evitar alertas de fraude. En abril de 2023, sus cuentas acumularon 80,9 millones de reproducciones fraudulentas en YouTube Music mediante planes familiares.
Qué sucede si la IA copia una canción protegida por derechos de autor
En Colombia, la Ley 23 de 1982 y las reformas posteriores protegen los derechos patrimoniales de autor. El artículo 271 del Código Penal prevé penas de cuatro a ocho años de prisión para ciertas formas de explotación no autorizada de obras protegidas, con ánimo de lucro y perjuicio para los titulares de los derechos.
En Argentina, la Ley 11.723 contempla sanciones de un mes a seis años de prisión para quien edite, venda o reproduzca una obra sin autorización. La creación asistida por IA puede generar un conflicto si el resultado copia una canción identificable o partes sustanciales de una composición ajena.
En qué países se debe informar que un audio fue creado con IA
En España y el resto de la Unión Europea, el Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial establece obligaciones de transparencia para determinados contenidos sintéticos.
Los sistemas que producen audio generado o manipulado deben incorporar marcas técnicas que permitan detectar su origen artificial. Quienes difundan un audio que constituya una suplantación sintética deben informar de manera clara que fue generado o alterado por IA.
La norma contempla una excepción parcial para obras artísticas, creativas, satíricas o de ficción. Aun en esos casos, debe revelarse la existencia del contenido manipulado de un modo que no afecte la experiencia de la obra.
La música creada totalmente por IA tiene derecho de autor: una duda común
No existe una regla internacional única que otorgue protección automática a una canción creada sin intervención humana. En buena parte de los sistemas jurídicos, el derecho de autor parte de una creación atribuible a una persona.
La utilización de IA tampoco habilita a apropiarse de obras ajenas ni a simular actividad comercial. El caso de Smith mostró que la sanción penal apareció cuando la música sintética fue parte de una estructura para falsear reproducciones y cobrar regalías.

articles.title: ReactOS, le Windows open source, s'invite sur les partitions NTFS
articles.text:
ReactOS n'est plus limité au FAT32 : le clone open source de Windows peut désormais s'installer sur une partition NTFS. Son nouveau pilote peut d'ailleurs également formater un disque dans ce format.
ReactOS a récemment annoncé que son pilote NTFS était assez abouti pour installer et faire tourner le système. Le projet, toujours en alpha, s'approche peu à peu d'une première bêta.
Un pilote qui installe et formate, mais sans cache ni journal
Le système de fichiers NTFS date de Windows NT 3.1 en 1993, et sa version arrivée avec XP en 2001 est toujours utilisée par la plupart des systèmes Windows. Jusqu'ici, ReactOS devait être installé sur une partition FAT32. Or les développeurs ont pour but de rendre le projet compatible avec les binaires de Windows Server 2003. ReactOS doit donc être capable de faire tourner tels quels les programmes et pilotes de ce système. La tâche était beaucoup trop complexe en restant sur du FAT32.
Et le moins qu'on puisse dire, c'est que le chantier est long. La lecture seule du NTFS est arrivée en 2016, puis le chargeur de démarrage FreeLoader (le programme qui lance ReactOS) a su lire ces partitions en 2022. Il restait à pouvoir installer et utiliser le système dessus, et dix ans plus tard, c'est désormais possible. L'équipe ajoute que le formatage en NTFS est maintenant possible et compatible avec Windows.
Mais les développeurs ne s'avancent pas trop et il reste encore pas mal de travail. Le pilote n'a pas de cache et cela affecte donc les performances puisque le disque sera sollicité plus fréquemment. Notons également l'absence de journalisation. Il manque également la gestion de la sécurité, autrement dit des droits d'accès aux fichiers. Enfin, à ce stade il est évidemment possible de rencontrer des bugs pas encore connus à ce jour.
Fin janvier, pour les 30 ans du projet, l'équipe de ReactOS annonçait travailler sur ce pilote aux côtés d'un nouveau pilote ATA et la prise en charge du multiprocesseur.

articles.title: Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers
articles.text:
A flaw in Broadcom's Wi-Fi setup software lets an attacker within radio range run code as root on Broadcom-based routers, without the network password or any pairing step, security researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed on October 16.
He showed the attack working against home gateways supplied by three Belgian internet providers, in one case reading the Wi-Fi password off the device and in another opening a remote shell over the air. No CVE has been assigned to the flaw, and no fix has been deployed to the affected routers, Kaiser says.
The flaw is in Broadcom's version of Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS), the feature that lets a device join a Wi-Fi network without the password being typed in. Broadcom's code mishandles the reassembly of fragmented WPS setup messages, so an attacker in range can send crafted messages that corrupt the router's memory. From there, Kaiser built two things: a way to read memory back off the device, and a way to run his own code on it.
Against an Orange Belgium gateway, the Askey TCG3000 read the Wi-Fi password (the PSK) from the router's stored settings, sent it back over the air, and then joined the network with it.
Against a Proximus gateway, the Sagemcom-built BBOX3V+, the exploit opened a reverse shell, a remote command line, carried over Wi-Fi frames, so no outside server was needed.
Both ran without any login, and the attack works at a distance, not only up close, Kaiser says. He reports no real-world attacks using the flaw. The working exploits are his own.
What's Affected
Broadcom's WPS code is embedded in routers and access points from dozens of vendors, and Kaiser estimates that millions of devices worldwide are affected.
The vulnerable chips fall into two families: older eCos-based models (the BCM3380, BCM3383 and BCM33834), where he found no usable fix and calls the bug a permanent "forever day," meaning a flaw that will never be patched on those devices, and newer Linux-based models (the BCM3390, BCM65xx and BCM68xx), which could be fixed if their makers switch Wi-Fi software.
In Belgium, Kaiser found the flaw present and exploitable on gateways from three of the four big providers: Proximus, Orange Belgium and VOO. A fourth, Telenet, may be affected too, but he could not test one.
A wider list he published, ranging from Cisco small-business access points to Huawei and ARRIS routers, mixes confirmed and unconfirmed entries, and some rest on an automated check that only flags a device as "likely vulnerable."
The Belgian per-provider counts, he says, run into the hundreds of thousands of gateways, but are rough estimates.
Why There's No Patch, and No CVE
The flaw is old. Kaiser traces the code back to at least 2010 and says Broadcom shipped an incomplete fix in 2018, then told customers to switch to a different Wi-Fi software package, called hostapd, rather than relying on the fix. On the older eCos chips, he says, no working fix was ever shipped, which is why he calls it a forever day.
No CVE, the tracking identifier that lets defenders and vendors follow a flaw, has been assigned to it. Kaiser says Broadcom told him it has known about the bug since 2018 and had heard about it from others, but would not register a CVE or say anything publicly, which he believes is why so many device makers never patched.
When he took the case to the CERT Coordination Center, it was closed the same day, because Broadcom itself holds the authority to assign CVEs for its products and would not do so. The Hacker News found no CVE for the flaw as of October 19.
What Defenders Can Do
There is no patch to install, and no setting Kaiser points to that blocks the attack over the air. What he provides instead is a way to find affected gear: YARA rules that spot the vulnerable code in extracted firmware, and a script that listens to a live access point and reports whether it looks vulnerable.
Both are triage aids, he notes: a patched device can still match the rules, so a hit is a reason to check further, not a confirmed finding. For gear that will never be fixed, replacement is the practical option.
Kaiser frames the bug as well suited to attackers who reach a target over nearby Wi-Fi rather than the internet, a technique Russian state hackers have used to breach networks from across the street.
