articles.title: Criptomonedas: el precio de Bitcoin para este lunes
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Valor de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 82505.77 dólares. Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio de 0.88% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
Bitcoin alcanza un nuevo récord y lidera el auge en el mercado de las criptomonedas
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Apple’s HomeView can recognize your face — but it still needs a recent iPhone to give you the full personal AI experience
articles.text:
Apple’s HomeView costs $299 / £299, but that doesn't unlock all of its best features — here’s what you actually need to use options like Personal Context and video analysis
Buying a HomeView doesn’t independently provide the full experience
Apple’s new AI-powered home hub, the HomeView, is officially shipping on November 13. Featuring a 7-inch touchscreen, and coming in wall-mounted or tabletop versions, the new must-have Apple device seems a snip at just $299 / £299 / AU$449 — but that price doesn't reflect the true cost of accessing its best features.
One of the things that really makes the HomeView unique is that it recognizes your face, then adapts its display so you see your personal content in apps like Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. It’s a great feature, because having to keep logging in manually all the time would be a real time-consuming turn-off for a device that’s used by all the family.
But a note on the Apple newsrooms page about HomeView says “Apple HomeView setup and multiuser support require a compatible iPhone or iPad running the latest software.” It goes on to say that “Personal Context requests require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad running the latest software version with Siri AI turned on and set to a supported language.”
You need a modern iPhone or iPad
Apple’s wording features two overlapping statements. A compatible iPhone or iPad is required to set up the HomeView, but one that runs Apple Intelligence is required for Personal Context requests. In practical terms, you need an iPhone 15 Pro, any iPhone 16 or newer model, an A17 Pro iPad mini, or an M1-or-newer iPad. The standard iPhone 15 does not qualify.
The Apple HomeView isn’t useless without those devices — it can still answer general-knowledge questions, control compatible smart-home products, and offer improved music discovery. However, it won’t be able to process requests involving personal information, such as finding details in Messages or Calendar and taking actions across apps, which require a modern iPhone or iPad. Siri AI must be enabled, and the HomeView and paired device must use a supported language.
But there is one even narrower requirement: customizing Siri’s expressiveness and speaking speed requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo, or an M4-or-newer iPad with at least 12GB RAM. Obviously, that's a small voice-personalization feature, not the threshold for ordinary Personal Context requests, but it’s still worth noting.
The complete Apple AI home costs considerably more
When we look into the HomeView’s smart-home features, which are part of Apple’s wider smart-home ecosystem, things get even more complicated. With a compatible HomeKit Secure Video camera, Apple Intelligence can do the following, genuinely useful, things:
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
- Summarize recorded activity: Instead of merely saying “Motion detected,” the Home app can describe what happened, such as a person leaving a package or a dog entering the garden.
- Search recordings conversationally: You can search using requests such as “Show me when the parcel was delivered”, or, “When did the children get home?”, rather than manually scrolling through clips.
- Connect related activity: The Home app can group or surface significant moments captured across different cameras.
Once again, an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone or iPad is required — this time to set up and enable the camera-intelligence features. Apple says footage is processed locally by the home hub or using Private Cloud Compute, rather than simply handing the analysis to the paired iPhone.
The complete list of what you need for these features to function is: a HomeKit Secure Video-compatible camera, HomeView or another compatible Apple home hub, an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone or iPad, and an eligible iCloud+ subscription. In other words, simply buying a HomeView alone does not give you the AI camera summaries or searchable recording history.
iCloud+ plans start at $0.99 / AU$1.49 for 50GB of storage a month, then $2.99 / AU$4.49 for 200GB and $9.99 / AU$14.99 a month for 2TB. Recorded HomeKit Secure Video footage is retained for 10 days, and does not count against your normal iCloud storage allowance.
Of course, you can still view a compatible camera’s live feed and receive basic accessory notifications without paying for recorded history, but you need that iCloud+ subscription for HomeKit Secure Video storage, and for AI features that analyze and search those stored recordings.
At $299 / £299 / AU$449 the HomeView therefore doesn’t independently provide the complete experience Apple demonstrates. Owners of an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16 or another qualifying device may already have everything they need for Personal Context. But people using a standard iPhone 15 or an older model could discover that their new household AI device is considerably less personal unless they upgrade their phone too.
That may suit Apple perfectly: HomeView isn’t just another product, but another reason to keep every device in your home relatively new, compatible and attached to an Apple service. For buyers who haven’t studied the footnotes, however, the difference between what HomeView can do alone, and what Apple shows it doing, could prove frustrating.

Graham is the Senior Editor for AI at TechRadar. With over 25 years of experience in both online and print journalism, Graham has worked for various market-leading tech brands including Computeractive, PC Pro, iMore, MacFormat, Mac|Life, Maximum PC, and more. He specializes in reporting on everything to do with AI and has appeared on BBC TV shows like BBC One Breakfast and on Radio 4 commenting on the latest trends in tech. Graham has an honors degree in Computer Science and spends his spare time podcasting and blogging.

articles.title: Alemania tardó 45 años en atreverse a rodar una película bélica como ésta y ahora puedes verla en Prime Video
articles.text:
'Stalingrado', la película de Joseph Vilsmaier de 1993 que retrata la cruenta batalla entre alemanes y rusos que marcó el destino de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, está ahora mismo en el catálogo de Prime Video y de Filmin. Coincide con un momento en que el cine bélico alemán ha vuelto a dar que hablar gracias a 'Sin novedad en el frente' y 'Der Tiger (El tanque)'.
Aunque esta fue la primera superproducción almemana que retrató la derrota, tiene un ilustre preceente: en 1959 Frank Wisbar ya había llevado la batalla al cine en ‘Stalingrado: Batalla en el infierno’, 97 minutos en blanco y negro entrelazados con metraje real de los noticiarios alemanes y soviéticos. Wisbar no tenía, eso sí, la holgura de medios de Vilsmaier: 20 millones de marcos, 12.000 extras y como productor a Günter Rohrbach que venía de estrenar una de las mejores películas bélicas de la histooria, 'El submarino'. Se estrenó en Múnich el 21 de enero de 1993, días antes del 50 aniversario de la rendición alemana.
El frío de esta película es auténtico: parte del rodaje se realizó en Finlandia por falta de nieve, y Vilsmaier, buscando verosimilitud en las imágenes, reclutó a amputados de un hospital de veteranos cercano a Praga para que dieran vida a loss mutilados en el campo de batalla. En la película seguimos al pelotón del teniente que interpreta Thomas Kretschmann desde un permiso en la costa italiana hasta un batallón de castigo, y que vivirá por medio conflictos tan impactantess como la carga de los carros soviéticos contra hombres a campo abierto.
Muy cerca en el tiempo se estrenó otra película basada en la batalla de Stalingrado, 'Enemigo a las puertas' de Jean-Jacques Annaud. EL director francés, sin embargo, optó por romatizar el choque yy visualizarlo de forma muy distinta a Vilsmaier. Éste da una devuelve a la guerra toda su cruddeza y la baña en un frí gélido que hace perfectamente comprensible que a Hitler, en aquella ocasión, le vencieran los elementos.

Monday, October 19th 2026
AMD Ryzen AI 7 HX 455 Surfaces with 16 CU Radeon Graphics
It seems as though AMD is readying a new mobile APU that bears a striking resemblance to the existing Ryzen Z2 Extreme. The AMD Ryzen AI 7 HX 455 was recently leaked by Golden Pig Upgrade on Weibo, with the post suggesting that the new CPU would launch with eight cores and 16 threads and a 16 CU iGPU, while the 16 CU iGPU will reportedly be identical to the existing Radeon 890M on the Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme, which has proven itself capable of very decent gaming performance in our in-depth review of the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X.

articles.title: Neural Concept launches MCP to help AI agents operate commercial CAD tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Neural Concept launches MCP to help AI agents operate commercial CAD tools
Switzerland-based artificial intelligence-native engineering company Neural Concept SA today launched Model Context Protocol Bridge to help AI agents operate commercial computer-aided design and simulation tools.
The capability will also help large engineering organizations automate complex software environments that are fundamental to designing and simulating physical products. This is an important part of manufacturing and proving prototypes before they are prepared for the real world.
In a typical simulation cycle, running solvers is the only step that doesn’t require human engineers. It’s largely already automated through retrieving proper physical geometry, cleaning it up and turning it into a virtual simulated mesh.
Founded in 2019, Neural Concept serves leading original equipment manufacturers and engineering organizations in industries throughout automotive, aerospace, energy, consumer, electronics, semiconductors and defense. It integrates an AI-augmented engineering platform and deep learning directly into computer-aided design and computer-aided engineering workflows.
With the new MCP Bridge, the platform will give AI agents access to the tools that make this happen, as well as the engineering know-how to use them, while companies retain control and ownership of their software and data.
“For the first time, the software that shapes every physical product can be operated by AI at enterprise scale,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Pierre Baqué.
Ideally, Baqué added, the opportunity is to reduce the tedium for engineers, who can then take on harder problems and work faster. This comes at a time when manufacturers are looking to shorten development lifecycles with fewer engineering experts available.
If an agent can handle an approved task in design and simulation software, every hour it takes is an hour handed back to an expert for more critical work. In one customer case, an engineer using MCP Bridge cleaned up the geometry of a wheel rim in three minutes, compared with a day using a manual process. That work is needed to get a physical product from physical to virtual model preparation and into simulation.
Thiat process, virtual model preparation and simulation, shifts engineering from reaction, physical trial-and-error into proactive data-driven digital environments by creating “digital twins.” These digital twins can be simulated in high fidelity, but only if they are “cleaned up” to act, look and react like their real-world counterparts with real-world physics before manufacturing happens.
That preparation works off spec sheets, materials guidelines and vast amounts of data. It can be extremely tedious, long work that requires extensive validation.
Once it’s done, engineers can test thousands of design scenarios simultaneously in virtual labs instead of waiting for real-world physical prototypes. However, getting one set up and into a rough draft an expert can refine can take weeks or more; an AI agent working in computer-aided engineering software can cut that time to hours. An engineer can fine-tune the result.
“AI agents have completely changed the way I work,” said Ciro Alosa, an electromagnetic design engineer at Traton SE, a subsidiary of Volkswagen Group that manages its heavy truck, bus and light commercial vehicle brands. “I can run more work in parallel, and going from a research paper to a validated script in our simulation toolchain now takes a couple of days.”

articles.title: Selon cette nouvelle étude, les chatbots IA changent de "personnalité" selon la langue employée
articles.text:
La prochaine fois, vous lui parlerez en chinois ! Votre chatbot IA préféré propose-t-il des réponses différentes selon la langue ? Selon des chercheurs chinois, les demandes en mandarin offiraient plus d'ouverture d'esprit aux LLMs.
ChatGPT, Le Chat, Gemini et autres chatbots IA, ne répondraient pas de la même manière selon la langue dans laquelle les requêtes sont formulées. C'est ce que révèle une étude publiée dans la revue Royal Society Open Science, menée par des chercheurs de l'Université de science et technologie de Chine.
Un test de personnalité standardisé soumis à cinq modèles
Pour évaluer ces variations, l'équipe de recherche a soumis cinq chatbots au questionnaire de personnalité Big Five Inventory-2, composé de 60 affirmations. Les IA concernées sont : ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Ernie 3.5 et Le Chat de Mistral. Tous ont été testés en anglais et en mandarin à travers 30 sessions par langue, tandis que Le Chat, pépite nationale, a également été testé en français.
De manière générale, les modèles ont fourni des descriptions d'eux-mêmes stables et favorables, mettant en avant leur fiabilité et leur sens de la coopération. Cependant, les résultats font apparaître certaines variations selon la langue choisie.
- Compréhension avancée du langage naturel
- Réponses adaptées à des contextes variés
- Disponible en plusieurs langues
Par exemple, sur l'évaluation de l'ouverture d'esprit (notée sur 5), ChatGPT-4o a obtenu une moyenne de 4,74 en anglais contre 4,81 en mandarin. À l'inverse, DeepSeek-V3 s'est hissé à 4,83 en anglais contre 4,81 en mandarin. De son côté, Gemini 2.0 Flash a affiché une conscience professionnelle plus élevée et une émotivité négative plus faible lorsqu'il était interrogé en mandarin. En comparant ces profils aux données d'enquêtes humaines issues des États-Unis, de Chine et de France, les chercheurs ont constaté qu'aucun modèle ne correspondait parfaitement au groupe humain de référence de son pays d'origine ou de sa langue.
Des constatations avec certaines limites
Les chercheurs soulignent toutefois les limites des constats réalisés lors de leur étude. Ladite étude met en évidence la manière dont les modèles réagissent à des consignes spécifiques, mais ne démontre pas l'existence d'une réelle "personnalité" chez les chatbots.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
La méthodologie employée n'a pas permis de séparer l'effet réel de la langue de celui des données d'entraînement, de l'architecture des modèles ou de l'interprétation des affirmations traduites.
Une chose semble toutefois ressortir de manière sérieuse. Pour les utilisateurs bilingues notamment. Formuler une demande dans une seconde langue peut amener le chatbot à fournir une réponse différente, pas une simple traduction de la langue initiale.
Source : DigitalTrends

articles.title: Las Guerreras K-pop vs el equipo 7 de Naruto: cómo recrear esta pelea con IA
articles.text:
Una imagen generada con inteligencia artificial (IA) puede enfrentar a Las Guerreras K-pop con el equipo 7 de Naruto a partir de referencias visuales y un prompt detallado.
El proceso puede hacerse desde el navegador, sin instalar aplicaciones de origen desconocido ni utilizar programas externos que pidan permisos innecesarios.
La clave está en ordenar las imágenes antes de escribir el prompt. Las referencias permiten conservar los rasgos de las protagonistas de la película de Netflix y de los personajes del anime, mientras que el texto define la acción, las posiciones, los ataques y el escenario.
La escena puede mostrar a las tres guerreras frente a Naruto, Sasuke y Sakura en un campo de batalla, con efectos de energía y elementos propios de cada universo.
Qué imágenes conviene elegir como referencia para generar la ilustración
El primer paso es seleccionar una imagen grupal de Las Guerreras K-pop en la que se distingan con claridad los rostros, peinados, prendas y accesorios de las tres integrantes.
Una foto de cuerpo entero o tomada desde la cintura ayuda a que el generador diferencie a cada personaje y reduzca el riesgo de que mezcle los vestuarios o repita rasgos faciales.
Asimismo, hay que conseguir una referencia del equipo 7 con Naruto, Sasuke y Sakura. La imagen debe mostrar sus atuendos, peinados y elementos identificables, como la banda ninja, el traje naranja de Naruto, la ropa oscura de Sasuke y el vestuario rojo de Sakura.
Dónde se cargan las imágenes sin descargar aplicaciones
Las imágenes pueden adjuntarse en el chat de Gemini, la herramienta de inteligencia artificial de Google. El acceso se hace desde la página oficial en un navegador actualizado, una alternativa que evita la descarga de archivos desde sitios no verificados o aplicaciones que no pertenecen a desarrolladores identificados.
Dentro de la conversación, los archivos se cargan mediante el botón de adjuntar o con la función de arrastrar y soltar. Conviene enviar las dos referencias en un único mensaje para que la herramienta reciba toda la información visual antes de generar la escena.
Luego es necesario comprobar que las miniaturas aparezcan completas y que no haya recortes, imágenes borrosas ni figuras ajenas que puedan alterar el resultado.
Qué prompt permite obtener una primera versión de la pelea
El pedido debe indicar el estilo, los participantes, las posturas y los efectos. Un prompt es el siguiente: “Crear una ilustración de acción estilo anime. Tres guerreras K-pop inspiradas en las referencias visuales luchan contra Naruto, Sasuke y Sakura en una arena destruida. Ubicar a las guerreras a la izquierda y al equipo 7 a la derecha. Mostrar un plano panorámico, movimiento, escombros, destellos de energía y expresiones de combate”.
Después se pueden sumar detalles para separar los ataques. Por ejemplo: “Naruto sostiene una esfera azul de energía en la mano; Sasuke concentra rayos azules alrededor de su brazo y empuña una espada; Sakura avanza con el puño levantado”.
Cómo ajustar los errores de la imagen generada con IA
La primera creación de la IA debe revisarse por partes. Es común que una imagen con inteligencia artificial presente manos con dedos adicionales, accesorios repetidos, ojos desalineados, armas deformadas o personajes que no respetan su ubicación.
Las correcciones funcionan mejor cuando son breves y específicas. Se puede solicitar: “Mantener tres guerreras”, “corregir la mano derecha de Naruto”, “eliminar el arma duplicada”, “poner a Sakura detrás de Sasuke” o “hacer que el escudo violeta esté frente a la guerrera de cabello trenzado”.
Qué hacer antes de descargar y compartir el resultado
Una vez elegida la versión final, el archivo puede descargarse desde la misma conversación. Antes de publicarlo en redes sociales, enviarlo por mensajes o incluirlo en una nota, corresponde identificarlo como una imagen creada con IA. Esa aclaración lo distingue de una pieza de Netflix o de los titulares de derechos de Naruto.
El material debe presentarse como una recreación hecha por usuarios y sin vínculo oficial con las producciones originales. Conviene evitar usos que induzcan a error sobre su origen o que lo hagan pasar por una imagen promocional auténtica.

articles.title: O Walkman está de volta: R$ 30 mil e acabamento em ouro • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
O Walkman está de volta: R$ 30 mil e acabamento em ouro
Nova versão promete reproduzir músicas com alta qualidade e é voltada para público mais exigente.
Resumo
- O novo Sony Walkman foi anunciado em duas versões, NW-WM1ZM3 e NW-WM1AM3, com preços de cerca de R$ 30 mil e R$ 15 mil, respectivamente.
- O dispositivo oferece reprodução de música em alta qualidade, com suporte a arquivos DSD, som de alta fidelidade e armazenamento de até 256 GB.
- O Walkman tem bateria com até 35 horas de autonomia e sistema operacional Android 16, permitindo a reprodução de músicas via streaming e download de aplicativos.
O Sony Walkman está de volta ao mercado, agora como um dispositivo premium voltado para audiófilos e profissionais da música. Com promessa de reprodução em alta qualidade e acabamento em ouro, o modelo foi anunciado por US$ 5,9 mil, cerca de R$ 30 mil em conversão direta. Há ainda uma versão intermediária à venda por US$ 2.999,99, aproximadamente R$ 15 mil.
O aparelho traz suporte a arquivos DSD (Direct Stream Digital), som de alta fidelidade e armazenamento de 256 GB, além de leitor de cartões microSD. Já em termos de conectividade, estão disponíveis Wi-Fi e Bluetooth, além de duas entradas P2, de 3,5 mm, permitindo escutar músicas tanto em um único canal balanceado quanto em formato estéreo, com sons independentes nos dois lados do fone.
Outro fator que contribui para a alta resolução de som é o uso de cobre “puro” no hardware, processado sem oxigênio. O produto conta ainda com tela de 5,5 polegadas e sistema operacional Android 16. Vale lembrar que a Sony saiu do Brasil em 2020, e o Walkman é um dos produtos que não deve chegar oficialmente por aqui.
Produto premium para audiófilos
O novo Walkman chega em duas versões na linha SIgnature Series: NW-WM1ZM3 e NW-WM1AM3. O diferencial fica por conta do design, com acabamento em ouro da opção mais robusta, a ZM3, além de maior espaço de armazenamento, com 256 GB contra 128 GB no modelo mais simples.
As especificações são praticamente as mesmas: o uso de OFC (cobre livre de oxigênio, em português) na composição promete maior qualidade de som, enquanto os fios internos trazem assinatura Kimber Kable para redução de ruídos e alta fidelidade na reprodução. Segundo a Sony, usuários poderão aproveitar as músicas exatamente como produzidas pelos artistas, nos mínimos detalhes.
Além do hardware, há soluções de software que reforçam a proposta premium do modelo. A fabricante garante tecnologia S-Master HX, suporte a arquivos DSD e otimização dos áudios reproduzidos, sejam eles processados localmente ou via Wi-Fi.
Vale reforçar que músicas tocadas pelo Spotify ou outros aplicativos de streaming terão uma perda natural de qualidade. Para ter maior qualidade, alguns apps oferecem recursos lossless nas configurações que vão garantir detalhes que ficariam de fora no processamento em MP3. De qualquer forma, a melhor maneira de escutar música em um acessório como o novo Walkman é por meio de arquivos baixados.
Bateria, conectividade e mais
Por ser focado em reprodução de músicas, o Walkman promete uma boa autonomia de bateria. São até 35 horas de áudio a depender do tipo de arquivo. Formatos mais pesados, como FLAC ou DSD, devem significar menos tempo, mas sempre numa média de 30 horas de música. Além das variações entre as duas entradas físicas (balanceado ou estéreo), a autonomia também muda de acordo com o tipo de conexão (até 41 horas no Bluetooth) e o aplicativo utilizado, com maior tempo garantido pelo uso do W.Music App nativo da Sony.
O sistema operacional do dispositivo é o Android 16, permitindo baixar apps, acessar internet e reproduzir músicas via streaming. Ainda assim, pela proposta de som mais robusto, o armazenamento máximo de 256 GB mal deve dar para os arquivos de áudio baixados localmente. É possível expandir a memória com cartão microSD.
Considerando a proposta, o Walkman também pode fazer sentido para músicos e produtores que quiserem avaliar seus trabalhos com maior qualidade mesmo quando não estiverem em estúdio. A opção de mobilidade é interessante, já que outros dispositivos vão ter uma reprodução com compressão e perder detalhes importantes no processo de gravação, por exemplo.

articles.title: Intel Readies XMX-Accelerated XeSS Support for Valve's Proton Compatibility Layer
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
Intel Readies XMX-Accelerated XeSS Support for Valve's Proton Compatibility Layer
Intel is preparing to add support for XeSS, accelerated by XMX cores in its graphics cards, to Valve's Proton compatibility layer. This is great news because the Valve Proton layer currently uses a slower version of the upscaler that is not very efficient. The XMX cores would significantly accelerate upscaling and bring substantial performance improvements. Intel is promoting XeSS and its latest version 3.0, which features multi-frame generation (MFG). This version integrates up to three generated frames between two rendered frames, resulting in up to a fourfold increase in frame rate using MFG, similar to NVIDIA's DLSS MFG technology. Intel is joining the trend of AI-generated frame insertion, which seems to be gradually expanding.
Looking at the latest "Panther Lake" SoC with Xe3 cores, each Xe3 core includes eight vector engines, eight matrix engines (XMX), and a dedicated ray tracing unit. These execution units now operate with higher utilization thanks to refined thread dispatch and load balancing. The vector and matrix engines double peak FP16 and INT8 throughput compared to Xe2, benefiting both traditional rendering and AI-assisted tasks such as denoising, upscaling, and frame generation. Hence, supporting XMX-accelerated XeSS will finally give Intel Xe gamers on Linux a much-needed performance bump.
Sources:
				Intel on GitHub, 				via Phoronix

articles.title: The Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid brings premium esports performance to a compact format
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid isn’t for everyone, but it is a great pick if you’re an aspiring or professional esports competitor with a generous accessories budget. It’s not cheap, but you’re paying for top-of-the-line specs and a suite of specialist features. The plastic build and lack of wireless connectivity is a shame given the price, however.
Reasons to buy
- + Highly customizable
- + Top-of-the-line 8kHz response rate
- + Useful on-board memory
- + Compact layout and attractive loo
Reasons to avoid
- - Very pricey for a plastic, wired-only model
- - Built-in display could be more useful
- - Poor wrist rest
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid review: Two-minute review
Let’s get one thing out of the way: the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid commands a premium price tag. At $229.99 / £209.99 / AU$399.95, it sits near the top of the gaming keyboard market — costing more than similarly high-end alternatives like the Razer Huntsman V3 HE or Corsair K70 Max. It’s currently the most expensive gaming keyboard that Logitech sells, reflecting its positioning as the very best of the best.
What does that price get you, though? The big draw here is the custom KS-20 POM switches. They’re manufactured by Gateron, one of the most popular keyboard switch brands, with contactless Hall effect operation. They feature a customizable actuation point, allowing you to select actuation depth all the way from 4mm to a very shallow 0.1mm in 0.05mm increments.
Raising the actuation point reduces the time taken for each keystroke to be registered, facilitating lightning-fast responses in intense competitive titles like Counter-Strike 2 or Valorant. You can customize the actuation point on a per-button basis as well, meaning you can make your movement inputs as sensitive as possible while leaving the button to switch weapons, for example, a more deliberate press to prevent misclicks in key moments.
This works in tandem with the rapid trigger setting, which sets the point at which a key needs to be lifted in order to reset. You can practically remove the delay between rapid inputs, meaning much more responsive movement. Getting used to the snappy responses certainly took some adjustment in my testing, but I found strafing felt much more precise, and this could make a big difference in a competitive setting where speed can make the difference between a win and defeat.
You can also set up key priority, which determines how the keyboard interprets almost simultaneous inputs via metrics like key travel or a chosen override. This sounds great on paper, as it should allow for much easier counter-strafing or ‘jiggle peeking’ (emerging from cover for a split second to try and bait an opponent into taking a shot), but there’s a big catch. This feature is banned in some competitive titles (including Counter-Strike 2) and will result in automated server kicks, so it should be treated with some degree of caution.
The built-in OLED display is also a pretty cool addition, though honestly, it’s not as useful as I first assumed it would be. It’s a small vertical display positioned on the far right-hand side of the keyboard above a small button and a little scroll wheel. By default, the wheel controls your system volume, but a quick tap of the button opens a menu with access to activation point adjustment, rapid trigger, mkey priority, RGB lighting, and game mode settings.
Adjusting them like this is very fiddly and much more easily accomplished right in the compatible Logitech G Hub software. With G Hub, you can save settings directly onto the keyboard’s memory, and I suspect that most pro players would rather create their settings in advance with the software rather than try and adjust them on the fly in the middle of a game.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The spec sheet is also impressive, with highlights like an optional 8,000Hz report rate. The keyboard also has a physical game mode switch, designed almost like a light switch. Flick this on to enable your game mode preset, which disables the two Windows keys by default to prevent accidental tab changes.
The physical design of the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid exudes quality too, with the compact TKL form factor making it easy to incorporate into your setup. All three colorways (Black, White, and Magenta) look excellent, and key presses feel suitably satisfying with a very smooth motion and lovely sound. It feels great to type on as a result, but I am still disappointed that the exterior of the keyboard is entirely plastic when most gaming keyboards above a hundred bucks incorporate more durable metal faceplates instead.
I also don’t understand why Logitech G didn’t opt to go for a nice braided USB Type-C cable rather than a rubbery plastic one at this price. Maybe there’s some reason for pro players to prefer plastic, but if that’s the case, the brand could surely just throw in two alternate cable options given the $229.99 / £209.99 / AU$399.95 price tag.
There’s also the matter of the included wrist rest, which I unfortunately don’t think is particularly good. It’s basically just a huge rectangular hunk of cold, rubbery plastic that you have to flop awkwardly onto your desk. It’s not well padded, and I quickly relegated it to confinement back in the box. It’s presumably a very cheap extra to include, but I’m not too happy with the prospect of having to store it.
Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid review: Price & availability
- Costs $229.99 / £209.99 / AU$399.95
- Available via the Logitech website or online retailers
- More expensive than many alternatives
At $229.99 / £209.99 / AU$399.95, the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid is expensive for a gaming keyboard, particularly a wired-only model with a predominantly plastic construction.
To give just two examples, similarly priced high-end options such as the Razer Huntsman V3 HE or Keychron Q1 Ultra 8K incorporate more premium materials like aluminum and, in the case of the Keychron model, offer wireless connectivity.
Still, it’s not offensively bad value by any means, as you are paying specifically for the high-end spec sheet, built-in screen, custom switches, and suite of esports features. You also get a wrist rest in the box and, while I’m not a huge fan, it might be useful for some.
The Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid can be purchased directly from the Logitech G website or at online retailers like Amazon.
Should I buy the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid?
Scorecard
| Value | Expensive for a wired gaming keyboard, but goes some way to justify its price with its feature set. | 4/5 | 
| Design and features | Looks great and is tuned to deliver serious esports performance with specialist features like rapid trigger and custom actuation points. | 4/5 | 
| Performance | A joy to type on and an excellent pick for competitive games. | 4.5/5 | 
| Final score | Expensive, but worth it if you’re serious about competitive gaming given the performance and features. | 4/5 | 
Buy it if…
You want esports-grade performance
The Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid is all about competitive gaming performance with features like the optional 8,000Hz polling rate and custom actuation point settings designed to help you do your best when it counts.
You’re after the ultimate switch customization
The Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid offers multiple ways to customize its KS-20 POM switches. You can adjust the actuation depth to your preference on a key-by-key basis, or enable the rapid trigger mode for accurate repeat inputs.
Don't buy it if…
You’re used to more premium materials
The exterior of the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid is fully plastic, which is unfortunate when cheaper alternatives offer more durable-feeling metal elements. 
Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid review: Also consider
Razer Huntsman V3 HEThis Razer keyboard offers Hall effect magnetic switches and features an integrated OLED screen, yet costs significantly less than the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid. It even has a metal faceplate, which feels more premium than the X2 Rapid’s plastic.
Read our full Razer Huntsman V3 HE review
Keychron Q1 Ultra 8K
This high-end option from Keychron is often on sale for cheaper than the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid and delivers an excellent typing experience with a robust aluminium chassis. It’s also capable of an 8K report rate, but unfortunately isn’t widely available in the UK or Australia.
Read our full Keychron Q1 Ultra 8K review
How I tested the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid
- Tested for multiple weeks
- Used as main keyboard for work and gaming
- Compared to other gaming keyboards
I tested the Logitech G Pro X2 Rapid for multiple weeks alongside the Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike mouse, with my hands on both before and after the official reveal and release.
I used it for gaming sessions and productivity tasks throughout my days. This included plenty of time in popular esports titles such as Counter-Strike 2 and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. I also played a range of other games, including the likes of Gears of War: E-Day, Cities: Skylines 2, and Far Cry 6.
Throughout my time with the keyboard, I compared it to my hands-on testing of other gaming keyboards across the price spectrum.
- Read more about how we test
- First reviewed: October 2026
Dash is an experienced tech journalist who specializes in video games, electronic entertainment products, and the wider industry that surrounds them. He currently serves as the Gaming Editor at TechRadar, leading our review, preview, feature, and news coverage of the latest and greatest releases.
Before joining the team, he was Contributing Writer at PLAY (formerly Official PlayStation Magazine UK) and has written articles for many of the UK's other biggest gaming magazines including the likes of Edge, PC Gamer, and SFX.
Now, when he's not getting his greasy little mitts on the newest hardware or gaming gadget, he can be found listening to J-pop or feverishly devouring the latest Nintendo Switch otome.

articles.title: Motive brings agentic AI to physical operations with agents that act before problems escalate - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Motive brings agentic AI to physical operations with agents that act before problems escalate
Motive Inc., the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence platform provider for physical operations, today announced the launch of Agents, a new capability that automatically responds to safety, maintenance and operational issues before they escalate into accidents, costly breakdowns or business disruptions.
The new Agents platform moves beyond alerts to automatically contact drivers, initiate maintenance and coordinate operational responses. The launch advances Motive’s strategy to bring agentic AI to the physical economy.
Motive’s technology uses operational data already collected through their platform to identify potential problems and initiate corrective actions. Agents can contact drivers, create maintenance work orders, alert managers and coordinate responses across fleet operations without requiring personnel to manually process every notification.
The launch targets one of the biggest challenges facing transportation, logistics, construction and other physical industries: Organizations have more operational data than ever, but acting on that information still requires significant manual coordination.
Motive estimates that companies lose approximately $46 billion to preventable operational problems, including vehicle downtime, compliance violations and unnecessary idling. According to the company’s 2026 ROI Report, 42% of surveyed organizations cite operational inefficiencies, including excessive administrative work, as a leading concern.
“Our customers don’t need another alert. They need action,” said Hemant Banavar, chief product officer at Motive. “The data that prevents collisions and breakdowns already lives in Motive. Agents put it to work the moment it matters, so teams can grow without adding headcount.”
Agents are available now to Motive customers. The company is demonstrating the new capabilities this week at the American Trucking Association’s Management Conference & Exhibition in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Motive plans to expand the technology in early 2027 with natural-language agent creation, allowing customers to describe a workflow in plain English and have AI build the corresponding automation. That future capability represents a progression beyond the rule-based and AI-assisted workflows available today. Motive has not provided independently validated performance results for the newly launched Agents platform.
The announcement builds on technology introduced earlier this year, including the company’s Atlas AI assistant, AI-powered automation tools and expanding edge computing capabilities.
Analysis: Motive’s bigger play is moving physical AI from insights to action
The Motive announcement is a good example of what I see emerging as one of the most important trends in enterprise AI: the transition from systems that generate insights to intelligent systems that actually do work.
For years, enterprise software has focused on collecting information, improving visibility and giving people dashboards to manage their businesses. The cloud era made that data more accessible. Generative AI made it easier to query, summarize and interpret. Agentic AI introduces a different opportunity: closing the gap between understanding what’s happening and taking action. This will be very important in the physical economy.
The deeper opportunity isn’t simply automating individual tasks. It’s eliminating the operational latency between detecting a problem, making a decision and executing a response.
This is where agentic AI could change the unit economics of physical operations. Companies have spent years investing in sensors, cameras, telematics and operational software. Those technologies generate enormous amounts of information, but much of the responsibility for converting that information into action still falls on people.
Agents introduce the possibility of compressing that coordination layer.
When intelligence can initiate an approved operational response instead of simply generating another alert, the economics begin to change. Fleet managers can potentially oversee more vehicles, maintenance teams can respond earlier, and organizations can improve utilization without adding proportional administrative overhead.
The real prize in physical AI may not be automating the workflow. It may be redesigning the operating model around intelligence that continuously turns signals into action.
The roadmap was already visible in our June 2026 interview
During a recent interview on theCUBE’s NYSE Wired: Physical AI & Robotics program, Motive Chief Product Officer Hemant Banavar discussed the company’s evolving architecture. “The next era of AI is about action and not insights,” Banavar said.
He was describing an industry that had spent years deploying telematics, cameras and monitoring devices but had created a new problem in the process: too much data and too little time to respond.
Banavar outlined a real-world scenario involving a fatigued driver. Motive’s computer vision technology could detect signs of fatigue and issue a warning. If the condition persisted, an automated workflow could initiate a conversation with the driver, encourage a safe stop and alert the fleet manager. “Imagine now nobody needs to be watching a dashboard in real time,” he explained.
The technology is designed to turn a sequence of disconnected activities — monitoring, detecting, notifying, communicating and coordinating — into an integrated operational workflow. This matters because the strategic value of agentic AI isn’t simply automating an individual task.
Physical AI requires a different architecture
In our recent interview, Banavar also explained why AI in physical operations has fundamentally different requirements from AI in traditional digital environments. He emphasized that accuracy in physical AI can be a matter of life and death, unlike many digital AI applications where an incorrect response may have limited consequences.
A slightly incorrect email generated by a language model is inconvenient. A safety system that fails to recognize a dangerous operating condition can have serious consequences. That places a premium on real-time processing, reliable models and the integration of intelligence directly into physical environments.
Motive has been investing in edge AI technologies, including its AI Dashcam Plus and AI Omnicam Plus, which extend computer vision and processing capabilities inside and around vehicles.
Banavar discussed the company’s relationship with Qualcomm, whose chips power these devices. He said Motive’s latest hardware can run three times more computer vision models than competing devices in its comparison, increasing the number of conditions the system can detect.
The performance comparison is Motive’s claim, but the architectural implications are meaningful. Motive is combining processing at the edge with cloud-connected operational systems and AI-driven workflows. The edge detects events. The platform provides operational context. Agents initiate approved actions. Atlas enables direct communication with people.
This integrated stack could become an important competitive differentiator as agentic AI moves into industries where reliability, real-time decision-making and safety are critical.
Practical AI: The ROI story is already taking shape
One of my recurring themes on theCUBE is that the real opportunity in AI isn’t just technological innovation. It’s the ability to produce measurable economic value.
During my July 2025 interview with Nyanya Joof, then Motive’s regional vice president for the U.K. market, at the RAISE Summit in Paris, we discussed the economics of physical AI and the opportunity to bring intelligence to industries that have traditionally relied on manual processes.
I characterized the opportunity as practical AI — not another demonstration of a powerful language model, but technology that can deliver measurable operational improvements.
Joof provided several examples. Phoenix Global, a metals and mining company, had reduced safety incidents by 40%, according to Joof, while improving its operational performance.
Ernst Concrete, an 80-year-old construction materials business, had deployed Motive’s AI cameras and video coaching after experiencing costly safety incidents. Joof said the company achieved $6.5 million in savings and a 2,000% return on investment over 13 months.
Motive also reported significant reductions in collisions and accident-related costs among Motive customers, along with improvements in vehicle uptime and administrative productivity.
In the physical economy, companies can measure AI’s value in cost per mile, vehicle uptime, accident rates, fuel consumption, maintenance expenses and labor productivity. Those metrics create a more direct connection between technology investments and business outcomes than many early generative AI productivity applications have demonstrated.
Agents could potentially extend those benefits by reducing the time and human intervention required to resolve problems once detected.
From blue-collar operations to AI-augmented knowledge work
Another important theme from my conversation with Joof was how AI could transform the role of frontline workers.
Much of the AI debate has focused on replacing white-collar jobs. But physical AI offers a different narrative: using intelligence to augment people operating vehicles, machinery and industrial equipment.
A driver who previously had to rely on personal experience or contact a supervisor can now receive contextual guidance from an AI assistant. A fleet manager who previously spent hours reviewing alerts and contacting drivers can increasingly focus on exceptions, higher-value decisions and operational improvements.
This creates an interesting shift in the nature of frontline work. AI can make specialized knowledge more accessible at the point of activity, potentially improving productivity and safety while reducing repetitive administrative demands.
The objective isn’t necessarily removing the human from the process. It’s changing where human judgment is applied. Agents will need clear operating policies, reliable escalation mechanisms, transparency and human accountability. The industry has considerable work ahead in demonstrating how autonomous systems can operate safely and predictably in the physical world.
The bigger industry shift: Systems of intelligence become systems of action
The Motive launch connects to a larger thesis we’ve been developing around the evolution of enterprise computing and systems of intelligence.
Traditional systems of record were designed to capture business information. Systems of engagement improved how people interact with that information. Systems of intelligence introduced AI-powered analysis, context and recommendations.
Now agentic AI is adding an execution layer. Instead of merely showing managers what happened or recommending what they should do, AI systems can initiate the next operational step within defined business policies.
Motive provides a concrete example of this evolution in the physical economy. The company’s early approach is relatively constrained: Customers define triggers and actions, while AI interprets operational conditions and assists in executing the workflow.
The longer-term roadmap moves toward goal-oriented agents that determine how to achieve business outcomes. That’s a much bigger architectural transition, and it introduces important questions about governance, explainability, human oversight and accountability.
But the strategic opportunity is clear. The competitive advantage in enterprise agentic AI may increasingly come from the combination of domain-specific data, real-time context and the ability to execute reliable actions.
Foundation models will continue improving. But the models themselves are only part of the value chain. The systems that understand a business’s unique operating environment and can take appropriate action may ultimately capture more durable value.
For Motive, its integrated hardware, software and AI strategy provides a foundation for pursuing that opportunity. The challenge now is proving that Agents deliver incremental improvements in operational outcomes while maintaining the reliability required for physical-world applications.
Bottom line
The bigger story isn’t another AI agent entering the market. It’s the emergence of a new operating model where intelligence becomes an active participant in how physical businesses function.
For Motive, the opportunity is to turn years of investment in edge computing, computer vision and operational data into a system that not only understands what’s happening but can coordinate what happens next. The competitive test will be whether that integration produces measurable improvements beyond conventional automation — fewer accidents, lower downtime, better asset utilization and greater operating leverage.
My takeaway: The physical economy could become one of the most compelling proving grounds for agentic AI because the outcomes are tangible, the economics are measurable and the consequences of execution are immediate.
The next wave of AI value won’t be measured by how many agents companies deploy, but by how much operational friction they eliminate and how effectively intelligence translates into real-world outcomes.

articles.title: La luz subió en septiembre y dos tercios del aumento tienen una explicación: los servicios de ajuste de Red Eléctrica
articles.text:
Hace unos días, varios medios de la prensa económica publicaban que gran parte de la subida de la tarifa regulada se debía a sobrecostes aplicados por el operador del sistema, Red Eléctrica (REE). Sin embargo, la empresa, que pertenece a Redeia, ha salido al paso a desmentir esto a través de un comunicado en su página web en el que explica que esta subida se debe a las restricciones técnicas que el sistema aplica para poder garantizar su seguridad, dentro del menor coste posible.
Y es posible que las dos afirmaciones sean ciertas al mismo tiempo.
¿Qué ha pasado? La factura regulada ha subido en septiembre un 6,5% más que en agosto (incluso con las olas de calor), con el PVPC llegando a alcanzar los 148 €/MWh de precio promedio. En términos absolutos, el incremento fue de 15,03 €/MWh. De esa subida, algunos medios indican que casi 10 euros (9,86 €) se deben a los sobrecostes de los servicios de ajuste que aplica Red Eléctrica, a través de la “operación reforzada”.
Sin embargo, el operador del sistema se ha defendido aclarando que no es el encargado de fijar este coste, sino que este depende de otros factores como los servicios de ajuste, y que, en las últimas cuatro semanas, el «coste de la electricidad en el mercado mayorista ha subido un 21,4% mientras que el coste de las restricciones técnicas ha bajado un 8,2%».
¿Qué son esos servicios de ajuste? El mercado eléctrico funciona con antelación, haciendo una planificación de lo que generará cada tecnología en cada momento. Cuando esa previsión no se corresponde con la electricidad que se está generando a tiempo real (porque haya menos viento del previsto, porque una central tenga que parar o porque la demanda cambia de lo que se había estimado), Red Eléctrica, como operador del sistema, tiene que “corregir” esa desviación a través de ajustes que garanticen el suministro. Puede hacerlo pidiendo a una central que produzca más, modificando la producción, o utilizando mecanismos como la operación reforzada.
Dentro de estos mecanismos están las restricciones técnicas. El mercado puede haber asignado una determinada combinación de centrales porque es la opción más barata, pero esa combinación no siempre es físicamente viable en la red. Si ocurre, Red Eléctrica tiene que modificarla para evitar problemas de seguridad.
En la operación reforzada está la cuestión. Tras el apagón del 28 de abril de 2025, Red Eléctrica adoptó algunas medidas adicionales, y algo más conservadoras, para evitar que un fenómeno como aquel se repita y reforzar así la seguridad del sistema. La compañía sostiene que estas medidas se adoptaron después de detectar incumplimientos normativos y comportamientos inadecuados de algunos agentes relacionados con las circunstancias que estuvieron en el origen del apagón. Una de esas medidas, como explica Cinco Días, es la programación masiva de centrales de ciclo combinado de gas en el llamado mercado de restricciones, que funciona al margen de la subasta diaria. Esto significa que, aunque esas centrales no hubieran entrado primero en el mercado mayorista, tendrían que ponerse a funcionar si se les solicita, con el coste que eso conlleva. Y en el caso del gas, ahora mismo es mucho.
Sin embargo, Red Eléctrica aclara que ese coste por la operación reforzada supuso en el mes de septiembre unos 8,8 millones de euros: una cifra que, a pesar de sonar elevada, tan solo supone unos 2 céntimos al día para un usuario con PVPC contratado, con un consumo medio anual de 300 kWh, según el operador.
Entonces, ¿por qué ha subido la luz? Por dos factores. El primero es que, por la difícil de ignorar coyuntura global, el mercado mayorista (una de las variables de cálculo de la tarifa regulada) ha subido un 4% durante el mes de septiembre, lo cual ha incidido directamente en el PVPC. El segundo factor son los servicios de ajuste. Según los datos recogidos por Cinco Días, estos mecanismos explicaron 9,86 €/MWh de los 15,03 €/MWh que aumentó el PVPC entre agosto y septiembre: aproximadamente dos tercios de la subida.
Lo que Red Eléctrica defiende es que esos casi 10 euros en realidad se deben al conjunto de servicios de ajuste, necesarios para que la combinación de generación y consumo sea físicamente viable, y no únicamente a la operación reforzada que es solo uno de los mecanismos para lograrlo, como indican algunos medios. Es un precio, además, en el que el operador no decide nada y que depende enteramente de la cantidad de energía que sea necesario movilizar y del precio que ofrezcan los generadores de electricidad.
¿Sobrecoste sí o no? Depende de lo que entendamos por sobrecoste. Por un lado, para Red Eléctrica, estos son costes necesarios para que la electricidad llegue a los consumidores de forma segura y al menor precio, por lo que sería incorrecto denominarlo así. Para el consumidor, quizá parezca diferente: sí existe un coste adicional con respecto al precio de la casación del mercado mayorista, que acaba pagando más de lo que se había previsto en la subasta.
Y como nadie se libra, también se han quejado las grandes eléctricas del mercado libre, que acusan a Red Eléctrica de falta de transparencia y que piden incluir en la parte fija del recibo un cargo regulado, de manera que no tengan que asumir temporalmente el impacto cuando ofrecen contratos a precio fijo.

articles.title: Alerte maximale dans le cloud : une faille critique de Linux menace l’étanchéité des serveurs
articles.text:
Une vulnérabilité découverte dans le noyau Linux menace l’isolation des machines virtuelles sur les serveurs KVM. Baptisée PwnEscape et notée 9,3/10 en gravité, elle pousse déjà plusieurs hébergeurs à prendre des mesures d’urgence.
Pour un hébergeur cloud, l’une des pires situations serait de voir un client prendre le contrôle du serveur qui héberge ses machines virtuelles. C’est précisément le risque soulevé par PwnEscape (CVE-2026-99999), une faille critique du noyau Linux révélée par les chercheurs de pwn.ai.
Le problème concerne les infrastructures utilisant KVM, une technologie de virtualisation largement répandue sous Linux. Dans les configurations exposées, un attaquant disposant de privilèges élevés dans une machine virtuelle peut exploiter son interface réseau virtuelle de type virtio pour franchir les protections qui l’isolent du serveur hôte. Il pourrait alors compromettre ce serveur et, potentiellement, les ressources d’autres clients.
Une simple erreur réseau ouvre une brèche dans Linux
La faille ne se trouve pas directement dans KVM, mais dans la manière dont Linux traite certains paquets réseau. Lorsqu’une machine virtuelle transmet des données, elle peut confier au noyau de l’hôte le calcul de leur somme de contrôle, une opération destinée à vérifier l’intégrité des informations échangées.
Or, une mauvaise validation permet de détourner cette opération pour modifier une partie du paquet que Linux avait déjà vérifiée. Cette manipulation peut alors provoquer des accès mémoire qui n’auraient jamais dû être autorisés.
Des chercheurs de pwn.ai ont ainsi réussi à récupérer des informations présentes dans la mémoire du serveur hôte. Ils sont ensuite parvenus, sur leurs propres machines de laboratoire, à exécuter du code avec les privilèges administrateur. Leurs essais ont également provoqué le plantage d’un serveur et des machines virtuelles qu’il hébergeait.
Vercel confirme également qu’une fuite de mémoire de l’hôte a été démontrée sur ses infrastructures de production dans le cadre de son programme de recherche de vulnérabilités. La prise de contrôle complète du serveur a, elle, été obtenue sur les machines de laboratoire des chercheurs.
Ces démonstrations confirment la gravité de PwnEscape, même si aucune exploitation malveillante sur des infrastructures de production n’a été publiquement établie à ce stade.
Les hébergeurs commencent à sécuriser leurs serveurs
La divulgation de PwnEscape a déclenché une course aux correctifs. Le patch a été intégré au code réseau de Linux le 8 octobre, avant d’être repris dans le noyau principal quelques jours plus tard, le 14 octobre exactement.
Debian propose déjà des versions corrigées, notamment les noyaux 6.1.190-1 pour Bookworm et 6.12.113-1 pour Trixie. Chez Ubuntu, plusieurs versions étaient encore en cours d’évaluation au moment de notre vérification.
Les hébergeurs n’ont toutefois pas tous choisi la même méthode. Selon Heise, Netcup a commencé à redémarrer ses serveurs de virtualisation pour appliquer les corrections. Hetzner a de son côté mis en place une protection temporaire reposant sur eBPF, une technologie permettant notamment de filtrer certains comportements directement dans le système.
Pour les clients utilisant un serveur virtuel, la correction de cette faille dépend avant tout de l’hébergeur. Ce sont les machines hôtes qui doivent être protégées, et l’installation d’un nouveau noyau nécessite généralement un redémarrage.
Trois jours et 700 dollars pour découvrir une faille critique
L’histoire de PwnEscape est aussi révélatrice de la place prise par l’intelligence artificielle dans la cybersécurité.
Les chercheurs expliquent avoir découvert la vulnérabilité en seulement trois jours, en s’appuyant sur un système d’analyse automatisé utilisant notamment GPT-5.6 Sol. Le coût des requêtes au modèle serait resté inférieur à 700 dollars.
L'IA n’a pas travaillé seule. Les chercheurs ont orienté les investigations, vérifié les hypothèses et confirmé les résultats. Mais cette méthode leur a permis d’explorer rapidement un volume considérable de code. La correction, elle, a demandé plusieurs semaines de travail et d’échanges avec les mainteneurs du noyau Linux.
Un VM escape désigne une attaque où un acteur, depuis une machine virtuelle (VM), parvient à sortir de son environnement isolé pour interagir avec le système hôte. Sur KVM, l’hôte Linux pilote le matériel et orchestre plusieurs VM ; si l’hôte est compromis, la séparation entre clients peut s’effondrer. L’impact va au-delà de la VM attaquante : accès à la mémoire de l’hôte, altération de la configuration du serveur, et possibilité d’atteindre d’autres VM cohébergées. C’est critique en cloud multi-tenant, car l’isolation est la base de la sécurité et du modèle économique.
Virtio est une interface paravirtualisée qui permet à une VM de dialoguer efficacement avec l’hôte pour des fonctions comme le réseau et le stockage, avec moins de surcharge qu’une émulation matérielle complète. Concrètement, la VM transmet des paquets à une couche côté hôte qui les traite via la pile réseau Linux. Si cette pile ou une étape associée (validation, offload, copie en mémoire) comporte un bug, la VM peut déclencher un comportement anormal sur l’hôte. Virtio devient alors un point d’entrée privilégié, car il est conçu pour des échanges rapides et fréquents entre invité et hôte.
Le checksum offload consiste à laisser l’hôte (ou le matériel) calculer la somme de contrôle d’un paquet réseau à la place de l’émetteur, pour gagner en performance. Ce mécanisme s’appuie sur des métadonnées décrivant quelles parties du paquet sont couvertes par les vérifications d’intégrité. Si le noyau valide une structure puis autorise ensuite une modification de champs pourtant supposés figés, on crée une incohérence entre ce qui a été vérifié et ce qui est réellement traité. Dans le pire cas, cela peut provoquer des lectures/écritures mémoire hors limites : fuite d’informations sensibles en mémoire, crash, voire exécution de code avec de hauts privilèges sur l’hôte.

articles.title: Batteries tout-solide : “pour répondre aux besoins de demain”, le français Saft inaugure leur fabrication à Bordeaux
articles.text:
Batteries tout-solide : “pour répondre aux besoins de demain”, le français Saft inaugure leur fabrication à Bordeaux
Filiale de TotalEnergies, la société Saft inaugure ce 19 octobre 2026 de nouvelles lignes de production de batteries à électrolyte solide sur son site de Bordeaux. Cette première en France doit aboutir à un large spectre d'applications avec des batteries nouvelle génération.
Alors que les batteries silicium-carbone révolutionnent l'autonomie des smartphones grâce à la Chine, dans d'autres domaines de la tech ce sont les batteries tout-solide (ou Solid-State) qui sont à l’honneur. Ce 19 octobre 2026, Saft, une filiale de TotalEnergies, a annoncé l'inauguration à Bordeaux de nouvelles lignes de production de batteries à électrolyte solide.
Batteries tout-solide Saft : sécurité, légèreté et fabrication française
Saft se vante ainsi d'être “le premier fabricant français à disposer de capacités de développement et de production de batteries à électrolyte solide combinant les technologies sulfures et polymères à température ambiante”. Pour le moment, cette ligne de production devrait atteindre une densité énergétique proche de 400 Wh/kg, avec pour objectif de dépasser 500 Wh/kg dans quelques années.
	
Les batteries “tout-solide” figurent parmi les innovations les plus prometteuses pour répondre aux besoins de demain en matière d'électrification. Avec cette nouvelle ligne, Saft franchit une étape majeure en transformant plusieurs années de recherche en capacités industrielles concrètes.
Cette technologie remplace donc l’électrolyte liquide traditionnel par un électrolyte solide. Le gain obtenu est un niveau de sécurité accru en éliminant les composants inflammables, un poids inférieur, ainsi que des densités d’énergie jusqu’à 50 % supérieures à celles des batteries lithium-ion conventionnelles.
De plus, le procédé de fabrication serait plus écoresponsable en réduisant jusqu'à 40 % les émissions de CO₂, notamment lors de la production d’électrodes par voie sèche. L’absence de solvants les rendrait également plus propres.
Aéronautique et spatial : les cibles prioritaires de la technologie Solid-State
Ces batteries tout-solide ont pour vocation d'accompagner l’électrification et la décarbonation de deux secteurs en particulier, où sécurité et performances sont centrales, à savoir l'aéronautique et le spatial. Dans son communiqué, Saft indique avoir “déjà franchi une première étape avec la livraison de cellules semi-solides pour évaluer les futures architectures d'avions électriques et hybrides”.
Pour rattraper la Chine dans ce domaine, où elle est en avance, Cédric Duclos, directeur général de Saft déclare que “pour rester dans la course, le soutien des pouvoirs publics est essentiel, car cette filière a besoin de beaucoup d’investissements. L’Europe devra aussi faire ses choix, soutenir ses filiales souveraines pour ne pas aggraver sa dépendance aux importations étrangères.

articles.title: Cuánto cuesta la criptomoneda ethereum este día
articles.text:
Ethereum es una plataforma digital que adopta la tecnología de cadena de bloques (blockchain) y expande su uso a una gran variedad de aplicaciones, mientras que ether es su criptomoneda nativa. En el mundo de las finanzas digitales es común que la criptomoneda sea llamada como la red, aunque en realidad no son lo mismo.
La plataforma ethereum, creada en el 2015 por el programador Vitalik Buterin, buscaba ser un instrumento para aplicaciones descentralizadas y colaborativas sobre las que se pueden hacer contratos inteligentes (dAPPs)
Al igual que el bitcoin, el valor de ether se disparó en un corto periodo de tiempo. En enero de 2016, ether cotizaba alrededor de un dólar y actualmente tiene un máximo histórico de 4.953,73 dólares.
El precio de la criptomoneda de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2407.26 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio del 0.62 las últimas 24 horas, así como una variación del 0.0 % en los últimos 60 minutos.
Actualmente, ethereum se encuentra en el lugar #2 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta criptodivisa es de 4891.7 dólares por unidad.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: GALAX Prepares GeForce RTX 5090 HOF with Swarovski Crystals
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
GALAX Prepares GeForce RTX 5090 HOF with Swarovski Crystals
GALAX has officially teased its GeForce RTX 5090 Hall of Fame Edition GPU, featuring unique details with Swarovski crystals. What the company originally showcased at Computex 2026 now appears to be a product scheduled for launch on October 22. The GeForce RTX 5090 HOF maintains the distinctive white aesthetic that GALAX GPUs are known for. However, this time, the design is enhanced with Swarovski crystals embedded across the GPU shroud, adding a nuanced touch. This should help the GPU stand out in all-white builds, especially when RGB lighting hits the crystals, reflecting and bursting in multiple directions.
Another interesting aspect is that the card is expected to feature dual 12V-2×6 power connectors, providing significant power headroom. GALAX has already offered its flagship GeForce RTX 5090D HOF Edition GPUs with dual 12V-2x6 power connectors, but this will be the first time an overclocking-focused graphics card receives such a luxurious finish with crystals. Initially, the GPU's appearance at Computex 2026 was thought to be a preview for the GeForce RTX 6090. However, it is now clear that the item will be more of a collectible, as GeForce RTX 5090 GPUs have become extremely expensive on their own.As a reminder, NVIDIA has denied reports that the GeForce RTX 5090 is being discontinued, confirming that shipments will continue despite industry-wide supply constraints that have led to severe shortages and prices far above its $1,999 MSRP. Some SKUs are retailing for the price of a small used car, with prices of $8,000 not unheard of. Therefore, we can only imagine that this GeForce RTX 5090 HOF Edition from GALAX will be an even more expensive option, as the Swarovski collaboration will likely add additional costs.

articles.title: Fortanix extends Confidential AI to Kubernetes workloads through Confidential Containers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Fortanix extends Confidential AI to Kubernetes workloads through Confidential Containers
Data security company Fortanix Inc. today extended its Fortanix Confidential AI platform to support the Cloud Native Computing Foundation’s Confidential Containers project, so enterprises can run artificial intelligence workloads on Kubernetes inside hardware-based trusted execution environments.
The release goes after the exposure that comes during inference, when model weights and the data fed to them have to be decrypted in processor memory. Privileged administrators and cloud operators with access to the infrastructure can potentially reach them at that point.
Fortanix published survey figures last week on how AI leaders view that risk. Atomik Research polled 300 of them at large U.S. companies on Fortanix’s behalf, and 93% said traditional encryption does not protect data while AI is processing it. Security concerns had led 41% to block a deployment completely.
Fortanix’s answer builds on Confidential Containers, which reached incubating status at the CNCF in July. The open-source plugins the company is writing for the project verify that a container is genuine before it gets anywhere near an encryption key. That check runs through Fortanix Confidential Computing Manager, which attests the CPU and GPU together so an inference job spanning both is covered in full.
The company’s Data Security Manager hands over the keys only if the result satisfies the customer’s security policy. They go nowhere but the protected environment.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Anand Kashyap said moving AI into containers “doesn’t change the threat,” since models and agents still touch a company’s most sensitive data while they run. With the plugins in place, deploying a container into a confidential computing environment takes one click on supported hardware and Kubernetes platforms.
Fortanix is pitching the update at regulated industries that need confidential AI to hold up in production. Key release runs on a cluster, so losing one server does not block it. Customers with sovereignty requirements can run the platform on-premises or fully air-gapped, and the company says that also lets an enterprise host a frontier lab’s proprietary model next to its own data without putting the lab’s intellectual property at risk.
“Attestation is a protocol. Trust is an operation,” said Anuj Jaiswal, Fortanix’s chief product officer. Having attestation and key management on one platform spares enterprises from building the trust layer themselves when they adopt standard Confidential Containers, he said.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Intel Corp. and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. are among more than a dozen companies Fortanix lists as supporting the work. John Fanelli, vice president of enterprise software at Nvidia Corp., said Fortanix is building on open standards for attestation and secure key release “at production scale.” Nvidia and Fortanix launched a joint on-premises confidential AI platform last October.
Fortanix Confidential AI for Confidential Containers is available now. The company plans to demonstrate it on Nvidia GPUs with confidential computing enabled at Nvidia GTC Berlin, which runs Oct. 20-22.

articles.title: Russia's next tool to fight VPNs appears to be AI — and the numbers suggest it's scarily effective
articles.text:
Russia's next tool to fight VPNs appears to be AI — and the numbers suggest it's scarily effective
A new draft national plan proposes using artificial intelligence to hunt down circumvention tools, but industry experts warn legitimate traffic could end up in the crossfire.
Russian authorities have reportedly explored using artificial intelligence to identify and block virtual private networks with a staggering 95% effectiveness.
According to a report by Russian newspaper Kommersant, the proposal surfaced in a draft national plan for implementing AI technologies through 2030. The ambitious scheme envisioned AI models analyzing the characteristics of 70% of VPN services targeted for censorship.
While Russia’s Digital Development Ministry claims this AI measure is absent from the plan's current iteration, the underlying intent remains clear. Moscow is already heavily investing in a permanent censorship infrastructure, with recent reports highlighting plans for Russia to double its internet censorship budget.
For citizens or visitors trying to secure their connection, finding the best VPN is increasingly difficult as the state tightens its grip on circumvention tools. Currently, Russia relies on "intelligent algorithms" rather than true AI to analyze internet traffic. However, the government still intends to increase the capacity of its traffic-filtering infrastructure 2.5-fold to 954 terabits per second by 2030.
Collateral damage and false positives
An AI-powered system would sit atop Russia's existing technical systems for countering threats (TSPU), the dedicated filtering hardware already installed on telecom operators' networks.
Speaking to Kommersant, a source in the Russian networking industry explained the technical mechanics. “AI automates and accelerates the analysis of connection patterns,” the source noted. The technology would evaluate data points like packet size and timing, session duration, traffic ratios, and neighboring IP addresses to indirectly root out VPN infrastructure.
However, deploying artificial intelligence to blindly hunt down hidden traffic comes with a steep cost.
Industry sources cautioned that an AI layer could lead to a surge in false positives, trapping legitimate business and corporate traffic in the dragnet. One source estimated that the algorithmic error rate is already 5% to 6%, and early-stage AI models would likely produce a significant number of incorrect blocks.
As noted by United24 Media, rolling out such a system requires immense resources. A fully operational AI detection net requires large-scale telemetry storage, massive computing clusters for model training, and a complex infrastructure to distribute updated models directly to filtering nodes.
A broader push for "sovereign" tech
The drive to automate VPN detection is just one piece of a broader effort by Moscow to tightly control mobile communications and escalate VPN blocks. Alongside restricting circumvention tools, Russia is attempting to force the tech industry to adopt strictly domestic security standards.
A recent draft order from the Digital Development Ministry mandates that smartphones operating on Russia's future 5G networks must support "Kuznyechik", an encryption algorithm developed with participation from the FSB’s information-security centre and InfoTeKS. Scheduled to take effect on March 1, 2032, this is not part of the standard 3GPP encryption suite.
Because the algorithm must be baked into modem chipsets, it could effectively force global manufacturers like Apple and Samsung to build Russia-specific hardware just to operate in the country.
Ultimately, it appears the Kremlin is prepared to use every technological weapon at its disposal to isolate its digital borders.
