articles.title: 5 Quotes from the book It Matters a Lot by Shubhra Saxena
articles.text:
5 Quotes from the book It Matters a Lot by Shubhra Saxena
Explore five thought-provoking quotes from Shubhra Saxena’s It Matters A Lot on success, happiness, ambition and finding meaning in life.
We spend much of our lives working towards milestones that society considers important. Degrees, careers, financial security, relationships and recognition often become measures of success.
But what happens when we achieve these goals and still feel that something is missing? This is one of the central questions explored in It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena, an IAS officer and author. Published by Rupa Publications, the book examines identity, ambition, happiness, relationships, failure and the experiences that shape how we understand ourselves.
Rather than prescribing a universal formula for a meaningful life, Saxena encourages readers to question their assumptions and reflect on what genuinely matters to them.
5 Thought-provoking quotes from the book
1. “Because you can tick every box and still miss your own life.”
This line captures the central message of It Matters A Lot. We often follow a familiar checklist for success, pursuing educational qualifications, professional achievements, financial stability and personal milestones without stopping to question whether these goals reflect our own desires.
The problem is not ambition itself. Working towards something meaningful can bring satisfaction and purpose. However, when our goals are shaped entirely by external expectations, we may lose sight of what makes us happy.
Saxena invites readers to consider whether they are building a life that feels right to them or simply one that looks successful to everyone else.
The lesson: Achievement and fulfilment are not always the same. A meaningful life begins with understanding what success means to you.
2. “You can tick every box and still feel like something is missing.”
This line explores the gap between outward success and inner contentment. A person may have a stable career, a comfortable lifestyle and relationships that appear ideal, yet still struggle to understand why they feel unfulfilled.
Such feelings can arise when we pursue goals without examining the reasons behind them. We may believe that the next promotion, purchase or milestone will finally bring happiness, only to discover that the feeling does not last.
It Matters A Lot encourages readers to look beyond achievements and examine their emotional needs, values and expectations.
The lesson: Before chasing another milestone, pause and ask yourself what you hope it will bring into your life. Sometimes, understanding that desire matters more than achieving the goal.
3. “What happens when everything looks right and still doesn't feel enough?”
This question reflects a familiar struggle in a world that encourages constant comparison. Social media, professional competition and cultural expectations can make us feel that we are falling behind, even when we have made meaningful progress.
The difficulty is that there is always another achievement to pursue and another person against whom to measure ourselves. If our satisfaction depends entirely on reaching the next milestone, contentment can remain perpetually out of reach.
Saxena's book encourages readers to reconsider these expectations and develop a more personal understanding of happiness and fulfilment.
The lesson: You do not have to keep pursuing every goal that society celebrates. Learning to recognise what is enough for you can be just as important as striving for more.
4. “Why do we seek approval?”
The desire for approval can influence our decisions more than we realise. From choosing a career to navigating relationships, we may find ourselves prioritising other people's opinions over our own judgement.
Seeking acceptance is a natural human experience. Problems arise when external validation becomes the primary measure of our worth. We may begin making decisions to avoid criticism rather than to pursue what genuinely matters to us.
By encouraging readers to examine their beliefs and motivations, It Matters A Lot opens the door to greater self-awareness and more conscious choices.
The lesson: Other people's opinions can offer useful perspectives, but they do not have to determine the direction of your life. Understanding your values can help you make decisions with greater confidence.
5. “What are we really looking for in love, ambition, happiness, and success?”
These questions bring together several of the themes explored throughout It Matters A Lot. We often pursue different things without examining what we expect them to provide.
We may seek success because we want security, relationships because we want connection, or recognition because we want to feel valued. Yet the things we pursue and the needs we hope to fulfil are not always the same.
Taking time to understand these motivations can help us recognise unhelpful patterns and make choices that better reflect our priorities.
The lesson: Self-awareness begins when we become curious about our own desires. Asking honest questions can help us understand not only what we want, but why we want it.
Final thoughts
It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena invites readers to reconsider the assumptions that shape their understanding of a successful and meaningful life. Its central message is that achievements alone cannot determine whether we feel fulfilled.
Through questions about identity, ambition, relationships and happiness, the book encourages readers to pause and reflect on the lives they are building.
Perhaps the most important question is not whether we have achieved everything we once wanted, but whether the life we are living reflects what truly matters to us.

articles.title: Pasos para canjear los códigos de Free Fire este 19 de octubre de 2026: gana diamantes gratis
articles.text:
Garena habilitó una nueva ronda de códigos de Free Fire para este lunes 19 de octubre de 2026. Las combinaciones permiten a los jugadores con cuentas registradas intentar reclamar premios dentro del videojuego, entre ellos diamantes, trajes, skins de armas, cajas y otros objetos de disponibilidad limitada.
El acceso a cada beneficio depende de la región de la cuenta, la vigencia de la clave y los cupos de canje disponibles. Por ese motivo, conviene ingresar los códigos cuanto antes y utilizar únicamente el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena, que evita problemas de validación y riesgos de seguridad.
Cuáles son los códigos de Free Fire disponibles este 19 de octubre de 2026
La lista para la jornada incluye más de 15 combinaciones. Cada una debe copiarse como aparece, en mayúsculas y sin espacios antes o después de la secuencia. Un carácter incorrecto puede impedir que el sistema acepte el código.

Las claves pueden tener restricciones territoriales y un número limitado de usos. Por esa razón, que una combinación figure en la lista no garantiza que funcione para todas las cuentas ni que entregue el mismo objeto a todos los usuarios.
Dónde se ingresan los códigos de recompensa de Free Fire
El canje se realiza en el sitio oficial reward.ff.garena.com. El jugador debe acceder desde un navegador, iniciar sesión y seleccionar el método de vinculación que corresponda a la cuenta utilizada habitualmente en Free Fire.
El portal admite perfiles asociados con Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei o VK. La vinculación previa es necesaria para que el premio llegue al perfil correcto. Las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar el sistema hasta que queden enlazadas con una de las plataformas habilitadas.
Cuál es el proceso para reclamar diamantes y otros premios
Después de iniciar sesión, el usuario debe localizar el campo de canje, pegar o escribir una de las claves y confirmar la solicitud. Si el código continúa activo, tiene cupos disponibles y es válido en la región de la cuenta, la página mostrará un mensaje de confirmación.
Las recompensas pueden tardar hasta 24 horas en aparecer en el buzón interno del juego. Para comprobar la acreditación, el jugador debe abrir Free Fire con el mismo perfil que vinculó en el portal. Si el objeto no aparece de inmediato, conviene esperar ese plazo antes de repetir la operación con otra clave.
Qué significa el mensaje de código de Free Fire es inválido o expirado
El aviso “código inválido o expirado” indica que la combinación ya no puede utilizarse. Puede ser porque venció el período de activación, se agotaron los canjes disponibles o la clave no está habilitada para la región desde la cual se intentó validarla.
Además, puede tratarse de un error de escritura. Los códigos combinan letras y números que pueden parecerse entre sí, como la letra O y el número 0, o la letra I y el número 1. Antes de realizar un segundo intento, es clave revisar cada carácter y eliminar posibles espacios añadidos al copiar la secuencia.
Cuáles recompensas pueden otorgar los códigos de Garena en el juego
Los diamantes gratis se encuentran entre los beneficios más buscados porque permiten adquirir artículos en la tienda virtual de Free Fire. Con esta moneda, los jugadores pueden acceder a elementos estéticos, pases, accesorios y otros contenidos que forman parte de las campañas disponibles dentro del juego.
Asimismo, las claves pueden habilitar trajes, skins de armas, personajes, emotes, cajas y objetos coleccionables. El premio final depende de cada código y de la campaña activa, así que no todas las combinaciones otorgan diamantes ni entregan el mismo contenido a todos los perfiles.
En aniversarios, fechas conmemorativas y eventos especiales, Garena suele incorporar artículos temáticos que no forman parte del catálogo habitual. En esos casos, los códigos incluyen prendas, accesorios y otros objetos vinculados con una campaña puntual.

articles.title: Votre smartphone connecté à un satellite sans passer par Starlink ? Orange et trois géants européens préparent la riposte
articles.text:
Ce n’était encore qu’une rumeur en septembre, comme nous l’expliquions alors. C’est désormais officiel. Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica et Vodafone ont annoncé ce lundi 19 octobre avoir signé une lettre d’intention pour étudier « une éventuelle candidature conjointe » à l’attribution, en Europe, des fréquences réservées aux services mobiles par satellite. Ce sont elles qui permettent à un smartphone classique de se connecter directement à un satellite, sans antenne particulière, là où le réseau terrestre ne passe pas.
Les quatre opérateurs ne construiront pas leurs propres satellites. Ils prévoient de déployer en Europe les infrastructures au sol ainsi que les fonctions de coordination et de supervision du réseau, la constellation étant fournie par « un partenaire satellitaire qui reste à sélectionner ». Ils promettent aussi un accès « ouvert et non discriminatoire » à tous les opérateurs mobiles. Bouygues Telecom, Free ou SFR pourraient donc, en théorie, en profiter eux aussi.
Des fréquences convoitées par SpaceX
Tout se joue sur la bande des 2 GHz, dont les licences actuelles, détenues par Viasat et EchoStar, expirent en mai 2027. Or SpaceX a racheté en 2025 une partie du spectre d’EchoStar, et les licences européennes de ce dernier doivent lui être transférées en 2027, selon le site spécialisé Light Reading. Pour garder la main sur ces fréquences, la Commission européenne a proposé en mai, la Commission européenne a proposé en mai de découper la bande en trois parts égales : une pour les communications gouvernementales, intégrée à la constellation IRIS², une réservée aux nouveaux entrants européens et une ouverte à tous, Starlink compris. C’est la part européenne que vise le quatuor. Le texte doit encore être adopté, et l’attribution des nouveaux droits n’est pas attendue avant 2029.
L’alliance n’est pas dénuée de paradoxes. La lettre d’intention des quatre opérateurs « ne remplace pas les partenariats satellitaires existants », et ils sont nombreux. Deutsche Telekom a signé avec Starlink pour un lancement en 2028, Vodafone partage une coentreprise avec l’américain AST SpaceMobile, et Orange, qui vend déjà son option Message Satellite, travaille aussi avec AST. Seulement, aucun d’eux n’a seul la puissance de feu de SpaceX, qui vient encore de racheter pour près de 8 milliards de dollars de fréquences aux États-Unis. En s’alliant, les opérateurs évitent surtout que Starlink ne vende un jour ses propres forfaits mobiles en se passant d’eux.
Washington brandit la menace
Le projet européen irrite déjà les États-Unis. L’ambassadeur américain auprès de l’Union européenne, Andrew Puzder, a averti dans le Financial Times que les entreprises européennes présentes aux États-Unis pourraient subir des représailles « dévastatrices » si Bruxelles restreignait l’accès de Starlink à ces fréquences. La Commission assure de son côté que son projet reste ouvert aux acteurs non européens.
Pour les abonnés, l’enjeu concerne surtout les zones blanches, la montagne, la mer et les situations où les antennes terrestres tombent en panne. Il faudra toutefois s’armer de patience : trouver un partenaire satellitaire, de préférence européen, ne sera pas simple, alors qu’IRIS² n’est pas attendu avant 2030.

articles.title: Axonius launches AI Workforce virtual workers as AI Companion and MCP Server go live - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Axonius launches AI Workforce virtual workers as AI Companion and MCP Server go live
Asset intelligence company Axonius Inc. today added Axonius AI Workforce to its Asset Cloud platform to let security teams hand ongoing remediation work to autonomous, artificial intelligence-powered virtual workers.
AI Workforce is meant to take over follow-up work that security teams rarely have time for. A lot of that work exists because asset data ends up split across dozens of tools, and the scheduled jobs most teams rely on only catch conditions somebody thought to define ahead of time. Anything outside those rules is left for a person to sort out, Axonius says, down to working out why a single endpoint agent stopped reporting.
Two tools Axonius announced in July also moved to general availability today. The Axonius AI Companion takes plain-language questions about a customer’s environment and can act on the answer in the same conversation, opening a ticket or tagging devices when asked. Outside AI tools and agents get at the same asset data through the Axonius MCP Server, which runs over the Model Context Protocol.
The virtual workers at the center of the launch come in more than 50 types, covering security outcomes that include exposure triage, shadow AI and readiness for post-quantum cryptography. Every worker tracks a metric tied to its outcome, which is meant to save teams from building custom reports to see if anything is improving. When an asset drifts from the state it should be in, the worker responsible for it carries out the fix, and the results feed a Daily Digest that Axonius ranks by urgency.
A mode setting controls how far a worker goes on its own, and Axonius recommends a starting mode for each job based on its own best practices. In Off mode, the worker waits for approval on everything. Teams that want to watch first can use Shadow mode to preview what the worker would do, then switch to Live and let it act automatically within set guardrails. Outbound messages and changes to connected systems count as sensitive and are held for approval before they execute.
Each customer also runs a private large language model instance inside its own dedicated environment, and an audit trail marks every action as either agent-driven or human-driven.
Moshe Ben Simon, chief product officer at Axonius, said every vendor is shipping AI agents now and “the question nobody is answering is what those AI agents are acting on.” An agent that acts on one vendor’s incomplete view of an asset is going to be wrong, he said.
Axonius spent years building a platform that draws on more than 1,400 bidirectional integrations, and Ben Simon described AI Workforce as what can safely be built on top of it. The company made the same data-quality argument in April, when it launched Axonius Verified Assets on the premise that AI agents act on their inputs without questioning them.
AI Workforce, the AI Companion and the MCP Server all run on the same asset model that already powers the Asset Cloud. Axonius builds it by reconciling and deduplicating data across more than 80 asset and exposure entity types. If the software can’t verify something, it is designed to say so.
Theresa Lanowitz, principal analyst for cybersecurity at Omdia, said what stands out is how directly the launch ties autonomous remediation to a verified view of the environment. She expects that pairing, plus human oversight where it matters, to separate AI that security teams “can actually trust” from tools that merely add noise.
AI Workforce is generally available to Axonius customers now. Security engineering teams can see how many AI credits their users and the virtual workers spend, and what that costs.

articles.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
articles.text:
A Russian military satellite maneuvered in “extreme proximity” of a commercial Earth-imaging satellite in recent days in the first known example an unsanctioned rendezvous in low-Earth orbit, according to the orbital intelligence company LeoLabs.
The Russian spacecraft, Kosmos 2612, “conducted a deliberate series of maneuvers toward ICEYE-X36, a US-operated commercial imaging satellite,” LeoLabs said. “Kosmos 2612 closed from hundreds of kilometers away to extreme proximity to ICEYE-X36. It then maneuvered around ICEYE-X36, remained nearby for an extended period, and then began moving away.”
US military officials and independent analysts have tracked Kosmos 2612 since its April launch on a Soyuz rocket from a spaceport in northern Russia. Within weeks, it became apparent that at least four of the six satellites from that launch were stalking ICEYE-X36 after they adjusted orbits to line up with the orbit of the ICEYE spacecraft.
Russia’s modus operandi
The situation remained stable until last week, when Kosmos 2612 began rapidly moving toward ICEYE-X36. By Friday, Kosmos 2612 was holding station 2 to 3 kilometers away before shifting positions ahead of and behind the ICEYE satellite, LeoLabs said. The satellites were within 500 meters (1,640 feet) of one another over the weekend, and “likely quite a bit closer than that,” said Adam Marsh, LeoLabs’ vice president of technical solutions.
LeoLabs operates a global network of radars to track objects as small as 2 centimeters, about the size of a marble, in low-Earth orbit. The proximity of Kosmos 2612 and ICEYE-X36 “occasionally made it difficult to distinguish the two spacecraft independently,” LeoLabs said.
“This was not a routine conjunction or ‘fly by,’” LeoLabs said. “The sequence included a controlled approach, changes in relative position, close-proximity loitering, additional small maneuvers, and a controlled departure. The behavior is consistent with sophisticated rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO).”

articles.title: Fuse Energy’s new plug-in solar kit promises to save you £180 a year in electricity bills — but it's not legal yet
articles.text:
Fuse Energy reveals UK's first plug-in solar and battery system combo for £181-a-year savings — but you can't buy it yet
Solar power for renters and apartment dwellers
- The UK’s Fuse Energy has announced a plug-in solar product
- It combines solar panels with a 2.5kWh plug-in battery
- It’s due on sale next year, provided plug-in batteries are made legal
With energy prices soaring thanks to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, you might be looking to plug-in solar panels to help cut your bills. To that end, the UK’s Fuse Energy has just announced the country’s first plug-in solar panels that come with an included battery, so you can harvest your own energy and store it for when it’s needed most — though the combination isn't yet legal in the UK.
The Jules by Fuse scheme lets you plug up to four 500W solar panels into a standard socket and use them to collect solar energy. This can be stored in the included 2.5kWh battery, with the Fuse app deciding when to store power and when to start using it from the battery.
Fuse frames the device as a handy product for people who a renting, living in an apartment or whose house roof is not suitable for solar panels. Instead of requiring scaffolding and a suitable home structure, the panels and battery can be placed on a balcony, mounted on a wall or placed in a garden.
That means accessing solar energy and storing it at home need not be limited to homeowners living in properties with suitable roof spaces. That said, there is a catch to be aware of with Fuse’s new initiative.
Waiting to clear the legal hurdle
As we noted earlier, you can’t get one of Fuse’s Jules setups installed today, as they’re not technically legal in the UK yet. Fuse says that the first deliveries of the product are “expected post legislation approval in 2027,” so if you’re interested, all you can do for now is pre-order one using Fuse’s waitlist.
Once the relevant legislation is passed and the Jules does become available, Fuse says it will cost £577 and will save you around £180 a year in electricity bills, meaning it’ll be paid off in a little over three years. In contrast, Fuse says that standard rooftop solar panels can set you back between £7,000 and £8,000, plus scaffolding and installation costs.
The big difference with plug-in solar kits — which only became legal in the UK in August 2026 — is Fuse’s inclusion of a battery in its Jules setup. This can make a real difference because it lets you power your house using the energy you’ve collected even when the sun isn’t shining, keeping you juiced up in all conditions.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Rival provider Octopus Energy is planning similar home battery products called the Nook Cube (2kWh) and Nook Colossus (5kWh or 10kWh, expandable to 30kWh) — also due to launch in 2027. Octopus’s own plug-in solar panels have repeatedly sold out since going on sale, although they don’t come with their own batteries.
While we’re waiting for battery legislation to pass, it’s a good idea to read up on the existing rules surrounding solar batteries and panels, as they’re not as simple as you might think. Hopefully things will become clearer next year, when the likes of Fuse and Octopus are confident that plug-in batteries will have passed the legal hurdles in their way.

articles.title: Investitionsgipfel: Warum Milliardenversprechen der Bundesregierung nicht reichen
articles.text:
Investitionsgipfel: An diesen Stellschrauben muss die Bundesregierung drehen
Deutschland braucht dringend mehr Investitionen. Die Bundesregierung will deshalb am Montag und Dienstag beim Investitionsgipfel in Berlin internationale Wirtschaftsentscheider:innen davon überzeugen, hierzulande zu investieren. Mit Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang ist sogar einer der derzeit gefragtesten Manager der Technologiebranche in Berlin dabei. Doch prominente Gäste und große Investitionsversprechen allein werden die deutsche Wirtschaft nicht wieder in Schwung bringen. Dass der Nvidia-Chef hier auftritt, ist kein Zufall. Die Bundesregierung sieht in künstlicher Intelligenz – wenig überraschend – eine der wichtigsten Schlüsseltechnologien für die nächsten Jahre. Nvidia könnte sich laut Medienberichten zum Standort Deutschland bekennen und industrielle KI, Robotik und leistungsfähige KI-Modelle damit voranbringen.
Doch damit es Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz zusammen mit Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (beide CDU) und Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) gelingt, Milliardenbeträge und neue Technologiestandorte einzuwerben, braucht es mehr als warme Worte. Die Anlageinvestitionen in Deutschland sind zwischen 2019 und 2025 um 6,4 Prozent gesunken, während die im restlichen Euroraum im selben Zeitraum um 6,7 Prozent anstiegen, in den USA sogar um 20,2 Prozent zulegten.
Dass diese Bilanz so ausfällt, hat weniger mit fehlendem Vertrauen und fehlendem Kapital zu tun, sondern eher mit den Rahmenbedingungen, unter denen sich Investitionen zuverlässig planen und wirtschaftlich umsetzen lassen. Deutschland muss hier konkret werden – und an jenen Stellschrauben drehen, die in der Vergangenheit zu wirtschaftlichem Wachstum und Wohlstand beigetragen haben.
Da ist zunächst einmal die Bürokratie: Wenn wir ehrlich sind, kommt die im Koalitionsvertrag versprochene Bürokratieentlastung bislang weder bei den Unternehmen noch bei jedem einzelnen von uns an. In einer Ifo-Umfrage vom September 2026 nannte jedes zweite der befragten Unternehmen Bürokratie und Regulierung als größtes Standortproblem. Das beginnt bei Dokumentationspflichten und beim Ausfüllen von branchenspezifischen Formularen, hat aber vor allem auch mit der Komplexität und zeitlichen Unberechenbarkeit von Genehmigungen zu tun. Gerade für investierende Unternehmen bedeutet das, nicht verlässlich kalkulieren zu können, wann sich eine Maßnahme rechnen wird.
Natürlich kann das nicht heißen, dass sämtliche Vorschriften abgeschafft werden, denn Genehmigungsverfahren erfüllen wichtige Funktionen beim Umwelt-, Sicherheits- und Verbraucherschutz. Dennoch ließe sich manches vereinfachen, ohne die gewohnten Standards aufzugeben. Ziel muss es daher sein, verbindliche Bearbeitungsfristen und parallele Prüfungen vorzugeben – und einen digitalen Zugang für alle Beteiligten zu schaffen. So könnten Unternehmen zentral alle Genehmigungen beantragen, die beteiligten Behörden hätten Zugriff auf sämtliche Erkenntnisse der anderen Beteiligten und Daten, die einer Behörde bereits vorliegen, müssten nicht erneut eingefordert werden.
Klingt vielleicht utopisch, ist aber in skandinavischen und baltischen Ländern schon üblich. Und auch die Initiative „Gemeinsam Schneller Gründen“ des Bundesdigitalministeriums zeigt, dass das mit der zentralen Anlaufstelle auch in Deutschland in vielen Fällen gut funktioniert. Ziel sollte es daher sein, die Zeit zwischen Investitionsentscheidung und Projektbeginn deutlich zu straffen und entsprechende Kennzahlen als aussagekräftiges Signal an die Wirtschaft zu schicken.
KI-Infrastruktur und –Anwendung müssen gemeinsam gedacht werden
Dass Deutschland mit seiner vielfältigen Industrie, seinen Forschungseinrichtungen und seiner großen Zahl an Hidden Champions über gute Voraussetzungen verfügt, KI-Technologien in konkrete Anwendungen zu überführen, daran besteht kein Zweifel. Doch nachhaltiges Wachstum ist mehr als der Bau großer Rechenzentren. Es funktioniert nur, wenn die Unternehmen die KI produktiv einsetzen und daraus neue Produkte und Dienstleistungen oder effizientere Prozesse entstehen.
Es geht daher nicht nur um die großen Leuchtturmprojekte, die medienwirksam angekündigt werden (und in der Vergangenheit dann nicht in allen Fällen Realität wurden), sondern vielmehr auch um den Nachholbedarf im Mittelstand.
Laut dem KfW-Digitalisierungsbericht 2025 haben zuletzt nur noch 30 Prozent der Mittelständler Digitalisierungsprojekte durchgeführt – weniger als vor der Pandemie. Auch die Digitalisierungsausgaben sind gesunken. Wenn also über industriellen KI-Einsatz gesprochen wird, kann es nicht nur um prominente Großprojekte gehen, sondern vor allem auch um die gesamte Wirtschaft.
Standort für Startups und Scaleups attraktiver machen
Neben dem Mittelstand könnte aber vor allem aus der Startup- und Scaleup-Welt nachhaltige Innovation kommen. Hier hat sich in den letzten Jahren das Bild verändert: Investorenkapital fließt vor allem in einige wenige Unternehmen, wohingegen viele andere weiterhin Schwierigkeiten haben, ihre nächste Wachstumsphase zu finanzieren.
Auch wenn die USA über viele Jahre als bevorzugter Platz für Gründer:innen mit besten politischen und wirtschaftlichen Rahmenbedingungen galten, sind zuletzt gerade einige KI- und Deep-Tech-Unternehmen wie Codesphere, Langdock und Focused Energy nach Deutschland zurückgekehrt. Sie berichten durchaus davon, dass Kunden diesen Reverse Flip im Hinblick auf digitale Souveränität und Planbarkeit schätzen.
Doch damit Deutschland in der Startup-Welt relevant bleibt, braucht es neben dem entsprechenden Investitionsklima auch verlässliche Vorgaben, mit denen die Unternehmen arbeiten können. Das gilt insbesondere für die steuerlichen Rahmenbedingungen sowie für Rechtssicherheit im Kontext mit KI‑Entwicklungen. In diesem Bereich hat Deutschland in den letzten Jahren schon an vielen Stellen EU-Recht mitgestaltet.
Zwischen Grundstimmung und harten Fakten
Letzten Endes wird aber auch ein weiterer Faktor relevant sein, wenn es darum geht, dass das „starke Willkommenssignal“, das die Bundesregierung senden will, bei den Entscheider:innen auch verfängt: die Grundstimmung im Land. Deutschland steht nämlich in einigen Feldern deutlich besser da, als es in den öffentlichen Debatten über den Standort rüberkommt: Da sind zum einen solide Staatsfinanzen mit einem Triple-A-Rating (als einziger G7-Staat), zum anderen immer noch hervorragende Forschungseinrichtungen und Universitäten mit gut ausgebildeten Fachkräften (insbesondere in Bereichen wie Biotechnologie und künstlicher Intelligenz).
All das könnte für eine nach wie vor hohe Innovationskraft stehen. Auch bei den Patentanmeldungen am Europäischen Patentamt liegt Deutschland weit vorne. Hinzu kommen die zentrale geografische Lage, die Größe und Bedeutung des Marktes und nicht zuletzt der Zugang zum europäischen Binnenmarkt. Dass diese Faktoren international schon wahrgenommen werden, belegt eine aktuelle Befragung der Deutschen Bank unter 1.200 Führungskräften aus außereuropäischen Ländern. Demnach ist Deutschland das attraktivste Investitionsziel innerhalb Europas. Der Blick von außen fällt damit positiver aus, als es die wirtschaftspolitische Debatte hierzulande vermuten lässt.
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz warb erst vor wenigen Tagen beim Deutschen Arbeitgebertag für mehr Zuversicht – und verhedderte sich in der Frage, ob das Glas nun halb voll oder halb leer sei. Tatsächlich spricht einiges dafür, Deutschlands wirtschaftliche Perspektiven nicht ausschließlich durch die Brille der aktuellen Probleme zu betrachten.
Und doch lässt sich Zuversicht nicht einfach verordnen, sie entsteht dann, wenn Reformen greifen und sich wieder wirtschaftliche Erfolge einstellen. Vielleicht ist also gerade das die zentrale Aufgabe, die auf die Bundesregierung nach dem Investitionsgipfel zukommt: dafür zu sorgen, dass das Glas mit schnellen Sozialreformen tatsächlich voller wird – statt nur darüber zu diskutieren, wie voll es bereits ist.

articles.title: Petition launches to can Anthropic Nova Scotia data centre project
articles.text:
A change.org petition has been launched to stop the construction of an AI data centre in Nova Scotia, and it is rapidly gaining support.
The petition, which was posted by resident Kevin Fifield, calls the decision to build the data centre as “a decision that significantly impacts our environment, our power grid, and our community at large.”
According to CBC News, the data centre in question is a proposed data centre just outside Port Hawkesbury in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia. EverWind Fuels, a renewable energy company based in Halifax, will own the facility, and Anthropic will lease it to power Claude.
The company noted it will build the facility in two stages, with the first phase coming online by the end of 2027 and the second in 2028. Both companies say they will pay for any required upgrades to the province’s electricity system, and EverWind has raised $8 billion in private capital.
Currently, the petition has 12,142 shares, 174 comments, and 11,800 signatures.
“This data centre is poised to benefit a select few while the costs are disproportionately shared by Nova Scotians,” writes Fifield. We must scrutinize who truly benefits from such projects and weigh these against long-term impacts on our environment and economy.”
Interestingly, Jacob Glick told Global News during a protest in Halifax against the data centre that “Canadians are using Claude in growing numbers, and we want our infrastructure to be closer to the people who rely on it.”
However, the people don’t exactly want the infrastructure close to them. Beyond these recent protests, the cities of Hamilton, Ontario, and Vancouver, British Columbia both sought a pause on AI data centres, with Hamilton rejecting a proposal for a large-scale project after public outcry.
Image credit: Shutterstock
Source: Kevin Pifield — Change.org

articles.title: 5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery
articles.text:
5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery
Explore five Richard Osman quotes that reveal how mysteries explore human nature, friendship, loneliness and the unexpected complexity of life.
Mystery novels are often associated with murder, hidden clues, unexpected suspects and shocking revelations.
But the most memorable crime stories are not always about discovering who committed a crime. Sometimes, they are about understanding why people behave the way they do, what they hide from others and what they need most from life. British author Richard Osman explores these themes in his bestselling crime fiction, particularly The Thursday Murder Club.
The novel follows four older residents of a retirement community who investigate unsolved murders, bringing together suspense, humour, friendship and reflections on ageing.
What makes Osman's writing appealing is the way ordinary human experiences sit alongside extraordinary crimes. His characters have regrets, complicated relationships, personal ambitions and a deep desire to feel connected to others.
5 Richard Osman quotes that reveal the human side of mystery
1. “I know the difference between alone and lonely”
This line from The Thursday Murder Club captures an important distinction between solitude and loneliness.
Being alone does not necessarily mean feeling isolated. Some people genuinely enjoy their own company, while others can feel lonely even when surrounded by friends, family or colleagues.
The difference lies in whether solitude is a choice or an experience that leaves someone feeling disconnected. Osman's characters challenge the assumption that older people naturally become less interested in the world around them. They continue to seek companionship, excitement, intellectual stimulation and opportunities to make a difference.
The quote also reminds readers that meaningful relationships are not simply about having people nearby. They are about feeling understood, valued and included.
The takeaway: Loneliness is not always visible. A person can have a busy social life and still long for a deeper connection with someone who understands them.
2. “We all want to be chosen”
In The Thursday Murder Club, Osman explores the complicated relationship between choice, belonging and the desire to be wanted. The novel's reflections on this subject are collected among its widely shared quotations.
The desire to be chosen appears in many aspects of life. People want to be selected for opportunities, appreciated by friends, loved by partners and remembered by those who matter to them. Even people who appear independent may quietly wonder whether they are important to anyone else. This is one reason mysteries can be so emotionally engaging.
Beneath the investigation, characters may be struggling with rejection, insecurity, jealousy or the fear of becoming irrelevant. Their actions become easier to understand when readers look beyond the evidence and consider their emotional needs. Osman's characters demonstrate that the need for acceptance does not disappear with age. It remains part of being human, regardless of experience or social status.
The takeaway: Wanting to matter to someone is not a weakness. The important thing is to recognise your worth without allowing other people's approval to define it.
3. “Count the good days”
Osman's writing frequently balances the darker elements of crime fiction with observations about appreciating everyday life. In The Thursday Murder Club, this idea appears in a reflection about recognising good days and carrying their memories forward.
Crime stories often revolve around loss, uncertainty and the consequences of past decisions. Yet these difficult circumstances can make ordinary pleasures feel more meaningful. A conversation with a friend, a shared meal or a peaceful afternoon can become precious when life feels unpredictable.
The residents of Coopers Chase have lived long enough to understand that happiness does not always arrive through dramatic achievements.
Sometimes, it comes from small moments of companionship and the freedom to enjoy the present. This perspective gives Osman's mysteries an emotional depth that goes beyond solving crimes. Readers are encouraged to notice the good in their own lives rather than waiting for everything to become perfect.
The takeaway: Not every day needs to be extraordinary to be worthwhile. Learning to appreciate small moments can change how we remember our lives.
4. “Always look where the action isn't”
This observation from The Thursday Murder Club reflects the attention to detail that makes a good detective.
In a mystery, the most obvious suspect is not necessarily the person responsible. A convincing investigation requires looking beyond dramatic events and paying attention to the details that others overlook.
The same principle applies to understanding people. Someone's loudest reaction may not reveal their deepest concern, while a quiet change in behaviour can suggest that something important is happening beneath the surface.
Osman's approach to crime fiction places considerable emphasis on character.
In an interview with PBS Books, he explained that he begins with his characters and develops the murder plot around them. This approach encourages readers to become observers of human behaviour rather than simply followers of clues.
The takeaway: Important truths are not always found in the most obvious places. Sometimes, listening carefully and noticing what others miss can reveal more than making quick assumptions.
5. “Don't let it be in charge”
Osman's observations about everyday life also extend to money and the influence it can have on personal decisions. A short line from The Thursday Murder Club captures this idea: “Don't let it be in charge.”
Although the novel is a murder mystery, its characters encounter concerns that extend well beyond crime. Money, relationships, family responsibilities and personal independence all shape how people navigate the world.
Financial security can provide freedom and comfort, but the pursuit of money can also influence priorities, create conflict and complicate relationships. When material success becomes the only measure of achievement, other sources of happiness can be overlooked.
This theme also connects to the wider appeal of Osman's characters: they are not defined by a single ambition or social role. They have different motivations, values and ideas about what makes life meaningful.
The takeaway: Money can be an important tool, but it should not become the sole measure of a successful life. Personal relationships, peace of mind and a sense of purpose matter too.
Final thoughts
Richard Osman’s mysteries blend crime and humour with thoughtful insights into loneliness, friendship, ageing and belonging. The Thursday Murder Club resonates because its characters face familiar emotional struggles.
Ultimately, the human side of a mystery is what gives its revelations lasting meaning. Discovering who committed a crime may resolve the central puzzle, but understanding the people involved is what makes the story memorable.

articles.title: Future Call of Duty Modern Warfare game could be set in Sydney - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Australia could become the setting for a future Call of Duty game according to a key game design director who has just landed in Sydney ahead of the launch of Modern Warfare 4.
“It’s such a stunning and beautiful city,” says Alex Norris, Associate Design Director at Infinity Ward – the developer behind the Call of Duty Modern Warfare games.
“I cannot go anywhere without looking at the surroundings and thinking about how to have combat in those surroundings – so you never know.
“At a minimum there would be some inspired elements but yeah, absolutely. Definitely a possibility.”
Norris is part of the Infinity Ward team that has shaped the memorable Call of Duty campaigns for more than a decade but he says Modern Warfare 4 takes a different approach.
“The thing I think is really separating it from Modern Warfare 1, 2, and 3 is that we’ve gone a bit back to our Call of Duty roots with this one,” Norris told Tech Guide.
“It really touches back into the infantry perspective, the grunt cog-in-the-machine approach.
“A lot of the previous Modern Warfare games were really about smaller directed raids going after terrorists in small townhouses or chasing them into the mountains.
“This is a bit of a change-up in that now we’re answering and resolving the storyline of Price and the things that happened to him, pushing the line wherever he needed it, and seeing how that kind of came to a head in Modern Warfare 3, reinvigorating the franchise by bringing us back to our Modern Warfare with a touch of infantry roots.
“We’ve got our grounded perspective from our South Korean grunts mixed in with U.S. Marines, that’s kind of our big swing on this one.”
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 goes on sale on October 23.
TO HEAR THE FULL INTERVIEW WITH INFINITY WARD’S ALEX NORRIS – LISTEN TO EPISODE 716 OF THE TECH GUIDE PODCAST

articles.title: Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A little over a month ago, Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale announced a $45 billion compute deal. Now the duo may be about to do it again.
Bloomberg reports that the two companies are said to be on the verge of announcing yet another $45 billion compute deal, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources cautioned that talks are still underway and that the details could change.
If the deal goes through, it would be the latest in a long string of giant compute deals Anthropic has struck over the past year. TechCrunch reached out to Nscale and Anthropic for more information and will update this story if we hear back.
The massive amount of money being sunk into AI compute deals has spooked a certain segment of investors, who worry that companies are spending too much money for too little profit. Still, Anthropic has pressed on with such partnerships, driven by the belief that it will all pay off in the end.
Both Anthropic and Nscale are also currently pursuing IPOs. Anthropic is still expected to go public this year. Nscale is also seeking to go public, although Bloomberg reported on Monday that the company is experiencing investor pushback over its proposed valuation of $30 billion.

articles.title: La pareja de Elizabeth Holmes recaudó USD 20 millones para una startup que evoca a Theranos
articles.text:
Billy Evans, pareja de la fundadora de Theranos Elizabeth Holmes, recaudó hasta USD 20 millones para una startup de diagnóstico médico llamada Haemanthus, según documentos revisados por The New York Times y citados por Wired. La empresa busca testear sangre, orina y saliva con un aparato de mesa.
El propio Evans se resiste al apodo que la prensa y hasta él mismo mencionan: “Theranos 2.0”. En un comunicado público, Haemanthus afirmó que “no es Theranos 2.0” y que su enfoque es “un paradigma diferente”, no una mejora de la tecnología que llevó a Holmes a prisión.
Sin embargo, en el documental You Can See Everything, dirigido por Nathan Fielder y Lance Oppenheim, Evans acepta esa comparación frente a cámara mientras discute con Holmes ideas de producto para la compañía, según reconstruyó Wired. “Podría pensar que esto fue lo más estúpido que hice”, dijo el heredero hotelero sobre su participación en el filme, en declaraciones al podcast All-In conducido por David Friedberg.
Una tecnología distinta a la de Theranos
Si bien Haemanthus fue fundada formalmente en 2024, Evans comenzó a trabajarla de manera oculta a finales de 2022. Apenas tiene presencia pública: no publicó productos y su perfil en LinkedIn es mínimo, indicó Wired. La compañía obtuvo una patente el 21 de enero de 2025 para un sistema basado en espectroscopía Raman, una técnica que analiza cómo la luz rebota en una muestra biológica para detectar patrones moleculares.
A diferencia de Theranos, que intentó miniaturizar análisis de laboratorio existentes a partir de una gota de sangre, la nueva startup plantea usar luz láser para leer información molecular que las pruebas actuales no detectan, de acuerdo con el comunicado de la empresa citado por Wired.
Eric Potma, profesor de química de la Universidad de California en Irvine y consultor de la compañía, explicó a la recista que “los ingenieros de Haemanthus son legítimos y están llevando la detección por Raman hacia direcciones interesantes”. Aclaró que su vínculo como asesor le impide profundizar más en los detalles técnicos.
El dinero y la falta de supervisión
Según The New York Times, Haemanthus había recibido el año pasado una inversión de USD 3,5 millones de “amigos y familia”. Wired reporta que esa cifra creció hasta unos USD 20 millones. La empresa les dijo a sus inversores que perfeccionar el sistema láser y llevarlo a un dispositivo portátil del tamaño de una estampilla demandaría tres años y USD 70 millones adicionales.
Materiales de presentación revisados por The New York Times sugirieron a inversores que la compañía no enfrentaría “ninguna supervisión regulatoria”, en parte porque el aparato se probaría primero en enfermedades veterinarias. El diario confirmó con el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos que esa agencia sí regula los diagnósticos veterinarios.
Evans manifestó a Times que la empresa está “en modo sigiloso” y que seguirá así: “No van a encontrar nada asociado con el nombre Haemanthus”. Las direcciones vinculadas a la empresa corresponden en su mayoría a viviendas particulares en un barrio de Austin, Texas, y empleados contactados por Wired se negaron a confirmar su rol.
Quién es el hombre detrás de la empresa
Evans se graduó en economía en el MIT y trabajó en LinkedIn y en Luminar Technologies, una empresa de sensores para autos autónomos, antes de fundar Haemanthus. Conoció a Holmes en 2017, durante un evento benéfico en la bahía de San Francisco, y la describió en una carta al juez como alguien que lo “cautivó” con su “asombro infantil”.
Esa carta fue una de varias que familiares y amigos enviaron antes de la sentencia de Holmes en 2022, cuando un tribunal la condenó a 11 años y tres meses de prisión por fraude contra inversores de Theranos. Una corte de apelaciones confirmó esa condena.
Según una persona cercana al negocio citada por The Wall Street Journal, Holmes no tiene ningún rol formal en Haemanthus. Wired también consignó que, en la documentación de constitución de la empresa, el nombre de Holmes no figura en ningún lado. Pese a eso, NPR había informado en 2025 que Holmes asesoraba a Evans sobre la startup desde la prisión federal donde cumple condena en Bryan, Texas, aunque la naturaleza exacta de ese asesoramiento nunca quedó clara.
Wired señaló que, de acuerdo con reportes periodísticos, Holmes podría trasladarse a una casa de transición el año próximo. Mientras tanto, Haemanthus sigue sin mostrar un producto terminado ni abrir su sitio web al público. El contraste entre el hermetismo de la empresa y la decisión de Evans de participar en un documental de varios años de filmación llamó la atención de Wired, que describió esa combinación como poco habitual para una compañía que se define a sí misma como secreta.

articles.title: Beyond the GenAI hype: Amazon's Rajeev Rastogi bets on agentic AI to boost enterprise operations
articles.text:
Beyond the GenAI hype: Amazon's Rajeev Rastogi bets on agentic AI to boost enterprise operations
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, Rajeev Rastogi, Vice President of Machine Learning at Amazon, highlighted the rise of agentic AI in the entire enterprise operating layer, marking a transition from static software to autonomous systems capable of understanding natural language instructions.
“Clearly the entire operating layer is becoming agentic,” said Rajeev Rastogi, Vice President of Machine Learning at Amazon, pointing to a decisive transformation in business technology.
This marks a transition from static software to autonomous systems capable of understanding natural language instructions. Unlike conventional software that follows rigid, pre-programmed scripts, agentic systems possess dynamic execution paths.
“Agents prepare plans dynamically to solve a problem... and invoke the appropriate tools,” Rastogi explained during a fireside chat at the 17th edition of YourStory’s flagship tech-startup event, TechSparks.
Instead of relying on human intervention at every step, these autonomous agents evaluate queries, formulate a sequence of actions, and call specialised digital tools to complete complex tasks end-to-end.
Within Amazon, this operating layer is active in systems like Rufus, a conversational shopping assistant that parses customer requests, applies price filters, invokes search engines, and guides users through product comparisons and checkout journeys. Similarly, autonomous seller assistants pre-fill product listings, monitor inventory levels, and guide small businesses through international export compliance.
Beyond the generative AI hype
Despite intense market enthusiasm surrounding generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI), Rastogi emphasised that generative models are not a universal cure for every computing challenge. Generative AI excels at complex reasoning, text summarisation, review analysis, and creative tasks such as editing product image backgrounds. However, it struggles with high-volume, low-latency applications.
“For certain applications, Gen AI models will never match the performance that you can get from traditional machine learning models,” Rastogi pointed out.
Traditional machine learning relies on classical algorithms such as gradient-boosted decision trees or standard neural networks that process structured numerical data with extreme speed.
For large-scale operational needs such as ecommerce product search handling tens or hundreds of billions of items, generative models suffer from prohibitive computing costs and slow response times, he said. High-performance architectures therefore use agentic orchestrators to parse human intent while relying on underlying traditional search engines for lightning-fast data retrieval.
Where generative capabilities are genuinely required, enterprise leaders do not need to rely exclusively on massive foundation systems. Frontier models, which represent the largest, most computationally heavy artificial intelligence architectures, carry substantial operational overheads.
Rastogi highlighted a far more economical alternative, noting, "Fine-tuning some of the open-base models... can give you models that perform a lot better than some of these large models out there... at one-fifth or one-tenth of the cost.”
Fine-tuning involves taking a smaller, publicly available open-source model, such as Qwen, and training it on specific proprietary application data. By adopting fine-tuned open models, businesses can achieve equal or superior accuracy for specialised classification or prediction tasks compared to giant closed models like Claude or ChatGPT, while dramatically lowering their computational expenses.
Unlocking the white spaces
For technology entrepreneurs and enterprise architects, the most compelling opportunities lie in vertical workflow automation rather than attempting to construct foundational models. Developing new frontier models requires unsustainable financial capital and computational infrastructure.
Instead, Rastogi advises that "building on top of the frontier models, using agentic AI to automate workflows in domains... that’s definitely promising.”
Taking inspiration from coding tools like Cursor, major opportunities exist across specialised domains including law, finance, healthcare, agriculture, and human resources. A particularly valuable white space lies in automating standard operating procedures, which are natural language documents detailing step-by-step instructions for human workers to resolve complex operational issues.
An agentic automation platform can clarify poorly written instructions using internal knowledge bases, break down long procedures into manageable sub-tasks, and delegate them to networks of specialised sub-agents that automatically browse internal tools, extract document data, analyse images, and resolve issues.
Looking ahead, the underlying design of AI models must evolve to remain sustainable. Current frontier models face severe physical and financial constraints.
“The frontier models today are massive, computationally super expensive, consume a lot of energy and resources... and I don’t think that’s sustainable,” Rastogi noted.
Furthermore, today’s monolithic models function primarily as statistical next-token prediction engines, guessing the most likely next word in a sequence without a genuine understanding of physical laws, 3D spatial geometry, or cause and effect.
According to Rastogi, to overcome these boundaries, the future landscape will transition toward networks of smaller, domain-specific models directed by central routing orchestrators. Rather than storing vast amounts of world knowledge inside giant model parameters, future AI architectures will separate core reasoning capabilities from data storage, relying on external, high-speed search engines for information retrieval.
Eventually, the industry will advance towards genuine world models that possess an internal understanding of physical spaces and environmental behaviour, establishing a practical, cost-effective framework for enterprise automation.

articles.title: « Une crise » : le nouveau patron d’Apple accorde sa première grande interview et évoque la pénurie de mémoire
articles.text:
John Ternus a accordé sa première grande interview au magazine américain TIME, qui le place en couverture de son numéro consacré aux inventions de l’année, en kiosque le 26 octobre. Le successeur de Tim Cook, en poste depuis le 1er septembre, y revient sur ses débuts éclairs, lui qui a dévoilé l’iPhone Duo huit jours seulement après sa prise de fonction. Interrogé sur la flambée des prix de la mémoire, il répond sans détour : « les contraintes qui pèsent sur la mémoire sont absolument une crise ».
Une crise assumée jusque devant Washington
La phrase répond à la lettre d’un groupe bipartisan de sénateurs, opposés au test de puces mémoire issues d’un fournisseur chinois, une piste explorée pour élargir un approvisionnement devenu critique. Ternus ne cède rien : « notre conviction profonde est que toutes les options doivent être sur la table ».
Le fournisseur en question serait CXMT, le champion chinois de la DRAM, dont des échantillons seraient déjà en cours d’évaluation à Cupertino. Le secrétaire américain au Commerce s’était pourtant opposé publiquement, dès le mois d’août, à l’idée de voir de la mémoire chinoise équiper les produits des grands groupes du pays. La mémoire pèse environ 10 % du coût des composants d’un iPhone, et les calculs de la banque JPMorgan la voient grimper jusqu’à 45 % d’ici 2027. Les prix de la RAM avaient déjà quadruplé au printemps, avant même les records battus cet été.
L’iPhone ne fait plus exception
Fin juin, Apple relevait de plusieurs dizaines à plusieurs centaines d’euros les tarifs des Mac, des iPad et de nombreux accessoires, en épargnant soigneusement l’iPhone. La digue a tenu trois mois. Les iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max présentés en septembre coûtent chacun 150 euros de plus que leurs prédécesseurs, à 1 479 et 1 629 euros. Les iPhone 17 restés au catalogue ont subi la même hausse, et l’iPhone Duo s’affiche à 2 339 euros.
Le keynote de rentrée a surtout confirmé une absence : aucun iPhone 18 classique n’accompagnait les modèles Pro et le pliable, une première pour la gamme. Le modèle qui porte traditionnellement les volumes de la marque n’arriverait qu’au printemps 2027, accompagné d’un iPhone 18e et d’un nouvel iPhone Air. La pénurie de mémoire est citée parmi les causes de ce décalage, Apple préférant réserver ses stocks de composants aux appareils les plus rentables.
Repousser le modèle le plus vendu, c’est aussi retarder le moment de fixer son prix en pleine tempête. Une hausse de 150 euros passe sur un téléphone à plus de 1 400 euros, beaucoup moins sur celui qui sert de porte d’entrée à l’écosystème.Tim Cook, devenu président exécutif du conseil d’administration, assure de son côté qu’il ne « se mêle pas » de la gestion quotidienne. Cette crise sera donc le premier vrai test de son successeur. Réponse au printemps, lorsque l’on saura si les iPhone grand public échappent encore à l’inflation qui a rattrapé tout le reste du catalogue.

articles.title: “Les précommandes de l’iPhone Duo ont été un véritable désastre” : jusqu’à trois mois d’attente, l’incroyable pari risqué d’Apple
articles.text:
L’ouverture des précommandes de l’iPhone Duo a rapidement tourné au vinaigre dès les premières minutes vendredi dernier. À peine l’Apple Store ouvert, les délais de livraison ont glissé vers le mois de novembre, avant d’atteindre décembre, puis la fin du mois de janvier. Pour un premier smartphone pliant, facturé à partir de 2 339 €, cette attente inédite de trois mois cache un choix délibéré de la firme à la pomme, vivement critiqué par Mark Gurman.
	
		
Les précommandes de l’iPhone Duo d'Apple ont été un véritable désastre. Mais cela pourrait profiter à l'iPhone 18 Pro.
Une pénurie mondiale délibérée pour l’iPhone Duo qui ne passe pas
Le journaliste et analyste de chez Bloomberg n’a pas raté Apple et son lancement des précommandes de l’iPhone Duo. Face à des livraisons repoussées de plus de 3 mois, Mark Gurman déplore une “erreur majeure” de la part de l’entreprise. “Elle savait qu'elle serait confrontée à de graves problèmes d'approvisionnement, mais a tout de même décidé de procéder au lancement, donnant apparemment la priorité à son souhait de commercialiser l'appareil dès le début de son premier trimestre fiscal plutôt qu'à la satisfaction de la demande”, explique-t-il dans sa dernière newsletter.
Pire encore, aucune clarté n’a été apportée sur les stocks réellement disponibles en boutique le 23 octobre. Pour une marque réputée pour sa maîtrise logistique, “une attente de trois mois pour un nouvel iPhone est pratiquement sans précédent”, souligne le journaliste. Il rappelle d’ailleurs qu’un client livré fin janvier recevra son appareil seulement neuf mois avant la sortie attendue de l’iPhone Duo 2.
Pourtant, Cupertino avait initialement prévu de limiter la sortie aux États-Unis et à la Chine pour éviter toute pénurie, d’après ses sources, avant de l’étendre à plus de 70 pays dès le premier jour. Un choix qui ressemble fort à “une grave erreur de calcul” ayant dilué des stocks déjà très limités.

Rediriger vers les iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max, quitte à décevoir et entailler l’image de marque d’Apple
Selon Mark Gurman, cette pénurie délibérée cacherait finalement un potentiel avantage commercial. En interne, Apple estime en effet que cette rareté profiterait directement aux ventes des iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max. De nombreux clients attirés en Apple Store par l’effet de mode du modèle pliant pourraient en effet repartir avec un modèle Pro, par dépit face aux ruptures de stock ou devant un tarif deux fois moins élevé.
Si cette manœuvre permet de gonfler les ventes de la gamme traditionnelle, elle n’excuse en rien ce lancement chaotique aux yeux de l’analyste. En décidant de lancer son téléphone mondialement malgré les difficultés de production, Apple prend le risque de “frustrer certains de ses clients les plus fidèles — ceux-là mêmes qui sont prêts à dépenser plus de 2 000 dollars pour un produit de première génération”.
Mark Gurman conclut d’ailleurs sèchement en déclarant que “pour une entreprise qui a passé des décennies à faire de sa chaîne d’approvisionnement un avantage concurrentiel, cela fait mauvais genre”.

articles.title: iPhone Duo desde 76,50 euros al mes: Movistar ofrece una forma más cómoda de hacerse con la versión de 2 TB del plegable de Apple
articles.text:
El iPhone Duo ya ha aterrizado en España y lo ha hecho arrasando en casi todas las tiendas. Si eres de los que no ha podido hacerse con él y buscas uno, Movistar sigue teniendo disponible la versión de 2 TB del mismo. Además, nos permite adquirirlo pagándolo de forma cómoda a un precio que parte desde los 76,50 euros al mes. Te contamos más sobre ello.
Apple iPhone Duo 2 TB - Blanco Estelar | Pantalla interior de 7,6″ y pantalla exterior de 5,4″ Super Retina XDR, chip A20 Pro, gran autonomía, cámara Fusion 48 Mpx
El nuevo iPhone Duo, disponible para clientes de Movistar
Se trata de una ocasión para tener el primer plegable de Apple que está disponible para clientes de Movistar. Para ello, tenemos que hacernos con uno de los packs que ofrece esta compañía. El precio que tengamos que pagar al mes por el mismo va a depender del que elijamos, partiendo desde los 76,50 euros al mes con el 'Pack Premium'. Los precios serían los siguientes
- Con el pack Premium, el iPhone sale por 76,50 euros al mes (3.672 euros en total).
- Con el pack Avanzado, el iPhone sale por 78 euros al mes (3.744 euros en total).
- Con el pack Base, el iPhone sale por 80 euros al mes (3.840 euros en total).
¿Y cómo funciona adquirir el iPhone así? Nosotros estaremos pagando dicha cantidad durante 24 meses que se prorrogarán, automáticamente, otros 24 meses (es decir, un total de 48 meses). Una vez transcurra ese tiempo, tendremos que pagar 1 euro para quedarnos con el dispositivo. El precio total, eligiendo el 'Pack Premium' es de 3.672 euros, 167 euros menos de lo que cuesta en tiendas. Y con la comodidad de ir pagándolo mes a mes.
Este iPhone Duo es el primer plegable de Apple, un dispositivo que además es potente gracias al chip A20 Pro y que cuenta, en esta configuración, con 2 TB de almacenamiento. Cuenta con una autonomía de hasta 24 horas usando ambas pantallas y un sistema de doble cámara de 48 megapíxeles.
| ⚡ EN RESUMEN: iphone duo de movistar | 
|---|
| ✅ LO MEJOR | 
| ❌ LO PEOR | 
| 💡 CÓMPRALO SI... Buscas un iPhone Duo ahora mismo, te interesa que tenga la máxima capacidad y quieres, además, tener algún plan de Movistar. | 
| ⛔ NO LO COMPRES SI... Prefieres una versión más económica de este móvil o simplemente no quieres contratar ningún plan de Movistar. | 
Movistar Plus sigue ofreciendo su catálogo de películas, series y documentales por 4,99 euros al mes
Además de lo anterior, no podemos perder de vista Movistar Plus. Es una plataforma de streaming con un catálogo muy grande de pelis, series y documentales con mucha producción propia, como 'El Castillo'. Podemos ver todo el contenido con su Plan Libre por 4,99 euros al mes sin permanencia. ¿Quieres ver también deporte, como partidos de la Champions League o LaLiga? Entonces, puedes optar por la suscripción con deporte, que cuesta 9,99 euros (también si permanencia).

articles.title: 1 169 ch et une recharge en 12 minutes : Mercedes dévoile l'AMG GT SUV, un monstre prêt à atomiser les supercars
articles.text:
La branche sportive AMG de Mercedes continue à explorer des territoires inédits. Un an après avoir présenté son tout premier modèle électrique, l’AMG GT Coupé 4 Portes Électrique, elle enchaîne avec son premier SUV à batterie, l’AMG GT SUV. Si ce dernier se veut infiniment plus familial que la berline, il en conserve les principales caractéristiques, comme une recharge explosive et un surpuissant triplé de moteurs à flux axial.
Sur la version haute GT63, deux de ces machines électriques prennent ainsi place sur le train arrière alors que la troisième s’invite sur le train avant. En fonctionnant de concert, le trio développe 1 169 ch et 2 000 Nm de couple. C’est franchement beaucoup, et suffisant déjà pour abattre le 0 à 100 km/h en 2,7 secondes avant d’atteindre les 270 km/h en pointe. Est-ce bien raisonnable ? Le modèle intermédiaire GT55 tient lui aussi la dragée haute.
Jusqu’à 710 kW : la recharge la plus rapide du marché ?
Avec 816 ch, 1 860 Nm de couple et un 0 à 100 km/h enrhumé en 3,1 secondes, c’est tout aussi appréciable. Dans les deux cas, l’autonomie atteint les 700 km sur le cycle WLTP grâce à un pack de 128 kWh. L’entrée de gamme GT53 se limite pour sa part à deux machines électriques développant 544 ch et 800 Nm de couple pour un 0 à 100 km/h en 4,2 secondes. Toujours très bien, même si l’autonomie flanche à 668 km avec une batterie de 106 kWh.
La recharge est expéditive avec 600 kW en courant continu DC pour l’accumulateur de 106 kWh et 710 kW pour le pack de 128 kWh. De quoi gratter 380 km d’autonomie en 10 minutes dans le premier cas et 450 km dans le second. Notons que le chargeur embarqué bascule automatiquement entre les modes 800 V et 400 V selon les bornes. Commode pour sûr, mais pas réellement impressionnant.
Une suspension ultra-technologique qui se passe de barres antiroulis
Ce qui l’est davantage est l’inédit système de suspension nommé Active Ride Control+ associant des ressorts pneumatiques à trois niveaux à un réservoir de pression de 8,2 litres. Une interconnexion hydraulique se joint à l’ensemble, qui permet de se passer des traditionnelles barres antiroulis contrôlant habituellement le tangage et le roulis. On passera sur le style très particulier de l’engin de 5,08 mètres pour se focaliser sur l’aérodynamisme.
L’aileron de toit présent en série sur les GT55 et GT63 adapte sa position pour réduire la traînée au-delà de 150 km/h alors que des ailettes présentes sous la calandre s’ouvrent ou se ferment en fonction des besoins de refroidissement. Côté équipement, l’AMG GT SUV retient une sonorisation Burmester 4D, un toit panoramique opacifiant, des roues arrière directrices, des freins en céramique, un assistant vocal avec ChatGPT et plus encore.
Prix et disponibilité : à partir de quel tarif est-il proposé ?
La planche de bord est identique à celle de l’AMG GT 4 Portes Électrique avec une instrumentation numérique de 10,2 pouces, un écran multimédia central de 14 pouces et une troisième dalle côté passager de 14 pouces. Mercedes promet avoir particulièrement travaillé la position de conduite pour retranscrire les sensations d’une vraie voiture de sport. L’AMG GT SUV débute à 112 350 € en Allemagne.

articles.title: Chip legend Jim Keller's Tenstorrent raises $1.5B to expand its open compute ecosystem - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Chip legend Jim Keller’s Tenstorrent raises $1.5B to expand its open compute ecosystem
Artificial intelligence computing hardware startup Tenstorrent Inc. is pushing hard to position itself as an alternative to Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units after raising a massive $1.5 billion in a late-stage funding round today.
The Series E round was jointly led by Trace Capital and Innovation X and saw participation from new and existing backers including Protagonist, Morgan Stanley, Fidelity Management & Research Co., ARK Invest and T. Rowe Price. It brings the startup’s valuation to $6.2 billion.
Toronto-based Tenstorrent is led by its Chief Executive Jim Keller (pictured), who is widely regarded as a legend in the semiconductor industry, having previously helped to design a number of groundbreaking processors for the likes of Intel Corp., Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Apple Inc. and Tesla Inc.
The startup originally set out as a chip designer but quickly pivoted to offer more than just the bare silicon. Today, it sells a complete portfolio of AI compute platforms, ranging from its Galaxy servers, TT-QuietBox workstations and its Blackhole cards for laptops.
Those platforms are powered by its specialized Tensix Neo accelerators and its Ascalon central processing units, which are both based on the open-standard RISC-V instruction set. They’re designed to be extremely scalable and energy-efficient, capable of producing top-tier performance for AI workloads without runaway power consumption, ensuring costs remain low.
Its best-selling products are the Galaxy Tenstorrent servers, which are enterprise-class systems that can work in coordination with others to create massive superclusters for training and running advanced frontier models. According to Tenstorrent, the Galaxy servers are already being used by companies such as Virtu Financial Inc. to power on-premises AI trading agents, while the data center colocation provider Equinix Inc. also makes them available to enterprises.
Developers who need immense compute locally may be more interested in Tenstorrent’s TT-QuietBox (below), which is a liquid-cooled desktop AI workstation that has enough power to test and run cutting-edge models right out of the box, with minimal setup. These systems are powered by Tenstorrent’s Blackhole cards, which are infinitely scalable PCIe boards packed with massive RISC-V cores and GDDR6 memory to enable high-performance AI processing in a very small package. For larger workloads, it’s possible to network multiple Blackhole cards and TT-QuietBoxes to pool their memory and compute.
Hardware is one thing, but where Tenstorrent really sets itself apart is that it also develops all of the software needed to make its platforms usable. It has also developed an open-source software stack that gives developers the ability to bring any AI workload to its hardware.
This stack consists of TT-Forge, a compiler that bridges machine learning frameworks like PyTorch to its RISC-V chips; TT-Metalium, which is a software development kit for hardware optimization and custom kernel development; and TT-LLK, for low-level kernel optimizations. These three components combine to enable developers to compile, fine-tune and then execute AI models on its custom silicon.
Keller said Tenstorrent’s platform approach allows it to scale from a single workstation to massive cloud-based clusters. “We’ve built one architecture and we sell it at every size,” He explained. “The future of compute is open, scalable and owned by the people building on it.”
Constellation Research analyst Holger Mueller told SiliconANGLE that Tenstorrent is one of a growing number of innovative startups trying to build more efficient computing platforms for AI, and the pedigree track record of its CEO Keller means it’s also one of the most promising. “Tenstorrent gets the funding it needs to keep innovating, and this is good news for enterprises,” the analyst said. “Nvidia is not the only option anymore. More competition and deployment options for AI compute can only be beneficial for enterprises, making AI workloads cheaper and more flexible.”
The funds from today’s round mean that Tenstorrent now has the muscle to ramp up production of its Galaxy servers, which will be deployed globally to support developers running massive large language models and video generation workloads. Some of the money will be given to its research team, which will look to advance innovation in the RISC-V ecosystem. Finally, Tenstorrent plans to expand its workforce globally.
Protagonist co-founder and Managing Partner George Bousis said Tenstorrent’s full platform approach sets it apart from the legions of startups scrambling to provide a viable alternative to Nvidia’s GPU ecosystem. “Few companies design the chip and the software that runs on it, but Tenstorrent does both, and its video generation results beat industry benchmarks ahead of our expectations,” he said.

articles.title: Services mobiles par satellite : Orange et 3 opérateurs européens vont concurrencer Starlink
articles.text:
Starlink ne devrait pas être le seul à l'avenir à proposer un service mobile par satellite. En Europe, un consortium des plus grands opérateurs du Vieux Continent se met en place sur le créneau !
Il y a un peu plus d'un mois, nous nous faisions l'écho d'une information de Bloomberg, qui indiquait que des opérateurs européens voulaient se lancer ensemble dans l'aventure du service mobile par satellite. Le média américain listait alors Deutsche Telekom, Telefonica, Vodafone et notre Orange national. Et le projet commence à se matérialiser, comme on le découvre avec cette nouvelle information !
Orange, Telefónica, Deutsche Telekom et Vodafone veulent travailler ensemble pour un service mobile par satellite européen
Orange va se lancer dans un nouveau monde : le service mobile par satellite, qui existe déjà du côté de Starlink avec son « Direct to cell ». Et pour ce faire, le géant français va être accompagné par Telefónica, Vodafone et Deutsche Telekom.
Les quatre opérateurs européens ont en en effet annoncé officiellement aujourd'hui avoir signé une lettre d'intention exprimant leur volonté d'étudier une candidature commune pour l'attribution de fréquences satellitaires en Europe. Une formulation qui montre que l'on n'en est encore qu'au début du projet, qui livre pourtant certains détails techniques.
Les satellites n'appartiendront pas au consortium
Car les quatre opérateurs veulent concentrer leurs investissements sur des infrastructures au sol, et développer les fonctions de supervision et de coordination du réseau. Pour ce qui est de l'élément critique, à savoir les satellites, Orange et ses partenaires ne suivront pas le chemin de SpaceX, qui s'est doté de sa propre constellation de satellites Starlink.
Les quatre grands nom du domaine ont ainsi déjà établi qu'ils ne souhaitent pas « investir directement dans une constellation de satellites. Celle-ci serait fournie par un partenaire satellitaire qui reste à sélectionner. » Ensemble, ils veulent soutenir les efforts de la Comission européenne pour renforcer et et garantir la souveraineté et la résilience du Vieux Continent dans ce domaine critique. On attend maintenant de voir quel sera le résultat à l'avenir de cette initiative.
Source : Orange.com

articles.title: Apple deve lançar novos Macs em evento de 28 de outubro • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple deve lançar novos Macs em evento de 28 de outubro
Apresentação pode ter novos MacBooks Pro com tela OLED e touchscreen, além de iPad mini e Macs com chip M6.
A Apple anunciou nesta segunda-feira (19/10) um novo evento marcado para 28 de outubro, em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos. A apresentação começa às 14h, no horário de Brasília, e foi divulgada sob o slogan “Pro and tell”.
Ainda não há nenhuma informação oficial sobre quais produtos devem aparecer neste evento, o quarto de lançamento de produtos da empresa no ano. No entanto, o jornalista Mark Gurman, da Bloomberg, adiantou há algumas semanas que uma nova rodada de lançamentos neste mês teria foco em Macs e iPads.
Entre os principais possíveis lançamentos esperados para o evento estão novos MacBook Pro de 14 e 15 polegadas com tela OLED sensível ao toque. Essa seria uma das maiores mudanças na linha desde a reformulação de 2021.
As informações apontam para a substituição do notch por uma Ilha Dinâmica, presente nos iPhones desde a linha 14 Pro, além de uma redução no peso. As versões mais avançadas devem manter os chips M5 Pro e M5 Max, que já apareceram na linha nos lançamentos de março. Porém, a versão de entrada do modelo de 14 polegadas pode avançar para o M6.
À primeira vista a situação parece bastante incomum, mas é importante notar que o chip M6 foi lançado como um modelo de transição pela Apple, tanto que não receberá versões aprimoradas (como Pro e Max). Espera-se que a companhia introduza o chip M7 já no primeiro semestre do ano que vem — esse sim receberia versões aprimoradas para os aparelhos mais potentes.
Com a tela sensível ao toque, a Apple naturalmente também estaria trabalhando em adaptações no macOS para o uso com os dedos, o que devei incluir elementos maiores na interface e suporte a gestos comuns em iPads, por exemplo.
Outros produtos esperados para o evento são:
O lançamento dos novos produtos nas lojas deve ocorrer apenas em novembro, também de acordo com Gurman.
O “Pro and tell” ocorre pouco mais de duas semanas após o evento Welcome Home, em Nova York. Na ocasião, a Apple apresentou produtos para casa, como a tela inteligente HomeView, o HomePod mini 2, uma nova geração da Apple TV 4K e outros acessórios para casa conectada em parceria com a LG.
Aquele foi o terceiro evento da companhia no ano apenas para lançamento de produtos. Considerando também a WWDC, realizada em junho, a Apple já promoveu cinco grandes eventos. É o maior número desde 2021, em que distribuiu lançamentos em três ocasiões, além da conferência sobre as novidades de software.
Essa maior quantidade de eventos de lançamento deve ser um padrão na gestão de John Ternus, que, segundo a Bloomberg, quer lançamentos menos concentrados no grande evento de setembro, geralmente dedicado aos iPhones mais potentes.
