articles.title: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in "proof point" test
articles.text:
The world’s first demonstration of a subsea geothermal power plant has taken place near an active underwater volcano almost a mile below the ocean surface. It generated less than 10 seconds of net-positive electricity but showed the technical feasibility of tapping another form of renewable energy underwater.
The three-week test deployment of the 3-ton prototype power plant took place at the Axial Seamount in the northeast Pacific Ocean in September. Endurance Energy, the Seattle-based startup behind the effort, aims to eventually commercialize subsea geothermal power for Pacific island nations and other customers looking for alternatives to importing expensive fossil fuels.
“The deep ocean gives us unlimited cold seawater for cooling, and its weight keeps the system and the well pressurized, so our plants can be compact,” said Andrew Redd, founder and CEO of Endurance Energy, in an email to Ars.
But efforts to tap geothermal power on the seafloor face many different challenges from land-based geothermal projects, which can also add up to higher installation and operational costs. So Endurance Energy must demonstrate consistent underwater operations as well as prove the approach can be cost-effective.
“It’s probably technically feasible, but it would undoubtedly be more expensive than to do it on land,” said Roland Horne, professor of energy science & engineering at Stanford University, in an emailed response to Ars.
Deep sea drilling
Endurance Energy’s deployment required a subsea lander drill to deploy from the ship Ocean Guardian—operated by Stabbert Maritime—and drill two holes in the seafloor at a depth of about 5,000 feet (1,524 meters). That means the test took place at a depth exceeding 2.5 times the height of the One World Trade Center building in New York City, which is the tallest building in the United States.
Both the drilled holes started venting hot hydrothermal fluid measured at a temperature of about 500° F (260° C). The Endurance Energy team proceeded to case and cement the second hole before installing a valve to create a well.
Next up, the company deployed its 100-kilowatt power plant, named Adélie, that is designed to vaporize incoming hydrothermal fluid to spin a turbine and drive an electric generator. It used the assistance of Canada’s remotely operated submersible ROPOS to help connect the power plant to the newly drilled well.
Adélie also connected to Endurance Energy’s Seattle command center by plugging into the Regional Cabled Array, a 559-mile (900-kilometer) network of undersea fiber-optic and electric cables that provides both power and connectivity to scientific sensors on the seafloor. The undersea network is funded by the US National Science Foundation and is operated by the University of Washington.
That all set the stage for the Adélie power test. But a major hitch soon arose—the drilled well extending 52 feet (16 meters) down into the seafloor was not delivering enough of the hydrothermal fluid to run the power plant.
“For our first well, the goal was to show we could drill, case, cement, and cap a well on the seafloor, so we kept it small and shallow,” Redd explained. “That limited how much fluid it could deliver, and deeper wells should change that.”
The test well was also just 2 inches (5 centimeters) wide, compared to oil, gas, and onshore geothermal wells that typically have casings 20 to 36 inches (51 to 91 centimeters) across.
Endurance Energy plans to avoid this issue in the future by drilling deeper wells to access more fluid. The company’s current lander drill can reach about 260 feet (80 meters), which would be five times deeper than the initial test well.
Powering on
To try running the Adélie power plant anyway, the team redeployed it to a nearby natural vent where hydrothermal fluid was already flowing out at about 538° F (281° C). On September 27, they gave it a try.
Over nearly half a minute, the power plant turbine reached about 26,000 rpm and enabled the generator to produce 60 watt-hours of electricity.
The power plant also became net-positive by producing more electricity than it consumed for about 8.7 seconds. It produced a median of about 2 kilowatts of net power and peaked at 16.5 kilowatts of net power.
“It’s the proof point,” Redd told Ars. “Net-positive is the threshold that matters: the plant made more power than it took to run itself on the seafloor, which no one had done before.”
The 100-kilowatt power plant named Adélie was designed to tap geothermal energy from the seafloor.
Credit:
Endurance Energy
The 100-kilowatt power plant named Adélie was designed to tap geothermal energy from the seafloor.
Credit:
Endurance Energy
But then a software issue brought the power run to a halt. Before the generator takes over, Adélie first relies on a battery to run its pumps, thrusters, and controls, along with spinning the turbine to get it up to speed, Redd explained. A battery module recorded a brief spike in current during the spin-up process and then stopped reporting.
That prompted Adélie’s software to automatically stop the power plant as a safety precaution, because it kept relying on the old reading from the battery module.
When the team was restarting the power plant, a power cable feeding the refrigerant pump also failed when an imperfection in the cable casing allowed seawater to seep in and short two of the electrical conductors. That ended the trial run, although Endurance Energy already plans to use the experience to improve how it builds and tests subsea cables.
Future deployments
Placing the geothermal plant on top of a natural hydrothermal vent was a one-time test for purely research and demonstration purposes, Redd said. His company still plans to rely on drilled wells in future deployments.
Endurance Energy also described taking steps to reduce potential environmental impacts on the seafloor and marine life. The team described choosing the “least disruptive” site for the test run and continuously monitored the process by sampling the water and recording the seafloor array of tubeworms, snails, crabs, and bacterial mats. It also checked findings against scientific sensors run by independent researchers and sent water, rock, and mineral samples for independent lab analysis.
The company’s next trial run planned for the winter of 2026—2027 will involve a refurbished and upgraded Adélie—renamed Gentoo in keeping with the penguin-inspired naming—that will aim to sustain higher power generation.
The company is also developing a larger 2-megawatt commercial generator for its first planned commercial deployment with the Kingdom of Tonga in 2027. The Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific Ocean runs its power grid primarily on imported diesel fuel, which has significantly increased in price since the United States and Israel launched their war with Iran.
“The 2 MW commercial generators will be about the size of a shipping container, and we are deploying up to six of these generators [to] offshore Tonga,” Redd told Ars. “The physical footprint of this project will be relatively small.”
Geothermal energy projects are already cost-effective on land but “on the edge of competitive pricewise,” said Horne at Stanford University. So he cautioned that any factors making geothermal more expensive would “push it to the noncompetitive side.”
Still, other customers may consider Endurance Energy’s approach if the company can demonstrate reliable operations over time with the Kingdom of Tonga. The skyrocketing cost of imported fossil fuels is a huge factor that has already spurred multiple governments to invest in more renewable energy alternatives.
“Large markets with ample offshore geothermal resources include the United States—Pacific Northwest and Alaska—Taiwan, and Japan,” Redd said. “As the technology matures, we expect to compete on cost and deliver continuous, weather-independent power to utilities and large energy users.”
Jeremy Hsu is a reporter exploring a wide range of topics across deep tech and AI. He has previously written for New Scientist, Scientific American, IEEE Spectrum, Wired, Undark Magazine and MIT Tech Review, among many other publications, about topics such as deepfakes, data centers, drones, battery tech, robotics, and GPS jamming. He also has a Master of Arts in Journalism from NYU, and a bachelor's degree from University of Pennsylvania in History and Sociology of Science, with a minor in English.

articles.title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenCode, an open source AI coding agent that has been gaining ground among developers as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said Saturday that attackers broke into an older system overnight, affecting 1.4% of users of its online platform, OpenCode Console, where some users store the API keys, or digital passwords, they use to access AI services.
As the OpenCode team struggled to keep pace with the attack, the scramble to respond highlighted a growing problem: Companies without vetted access to AI models with fewer safety restrictions have a hard time defending against large-scale, AI-driven cyberattacks.
“We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the company wrote on X. “We have notified them all this morning via email.” Users who did not receive an email were not impacted, the company said.
While the company didn’t specify how the distillation attack occurred, leaked API keys can help users in countries with restricted access to American models generate the high volume of outputs needed for that process. Some skeptics called the framing an overstretch, arguing that the incident was a straightforward breach whose use for distillation remains unproven.
Overnight, developers began posting spending alerts and unauthorized charges on Reddit and X: “I saw my Open AI, Anthropic, and Google AI spend alerts all fire off before going to bed wondering what was going on,” a developer wrote.
Other users reported charges in the hundreds of dollars on individual accounts; a few described totals above $1,000.
Anthropic and Google both blocked the API keys they believed were exposed, while OpenAI said it worked with OpenCode to restore access and refund its API customers for credits used in the attack. OpenCode said refunds for unauthorized charges are underway.
The exposed keys were confined to Console, where some users had them in workspaces. The open source app and command-line tool were not affected, according to co-founder Dax Raad. “Note this is the OpenCode Console, not OpenCode itself, those keys never come to us,” he wrote on X.
Even as users and AI companies moved to disable the exposed keys, the OpenCode team was still under pressure. Raad said attackers had been trying to break into its systems nonstop for 48 hours, requiring the team to keep AI defensive agents running around the clock. AI models that the OpenCode team turned to for analysis helped for a while, but started refusing to work when the malicious code they were asked to examine activated safety filters.
“[T]hat was a bit frustrating,” he wrote on X.
OpenCode later received access to OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue program, which gives vetted users AI models that are less likely to refuse requests for defensive security work. Raad said the access improved the team’s ability to investigate the attack.
OpenCode isn’t the first company to hit this wall. In July, AI platform Hugging Face said commercial AI models blocked its attempts to analyze activity logs from an intrusion by autonomous AI agents, which OpenAI later revealed were its own models running with safeguards lowered during a test. In a section of its blog post titled “The asymmetry problem,” Hugging Face wrote that guardrails “cannot distinguish an incident responder from an attacker.”
Security researchers have raised similar complaints, saying the restrictions are inconsistent and have pushed some toward foreign open-weight models, which anyone can download and run.
The weekend episode drew a response from David Sacks, co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
“OpenCode (and earlier Hugging Face) hit the same wall mid-attack: frontier models refused to analyze the very exploits needed for defense because the payloads tripped safety filters. The guardrails backfired,” he wrote on X.
The breach occurred the same night OpenCode made GLM-5.3-Flash free for users. The broader GLM-5.3 family has drawn attention from researchers who study open-weight models and note that its cybersecurity capabilities approached levels previously associated with restricted-access models like Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview.
OpenCode has not detailed how attackers gained access to the older system, how keys were stored, or the full extent of any misuse. It has told affected users to revoke and replace their keys directly with each provider. The company said the incident remains ongoing.
The breach lands amid a run of AI-enabled cyber incidents. Earlier this month, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike said a China-based hacker likely used an AI penetration-testing agent, which probes computer systems for weaknesses, and Claude in attacks on South Korean banks. Last week, India’s cybersecurity agency warned that AI agents, including some being tested by AI companies, had reached Indian organizations’ systems without authorization.

articles.title: OWC Announces General Availability of Dock Ejector 2.1
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
OWC Announces General Availability of Dock Ejector 2.1
Other World Computing (OWC), a trusted leader in high-performance storage, memory, connectivity, software, and accessories that empower creative and business professionals to maximize performance, enhance reliability, and streamline workflows, today announced the general availability (GA) launch of OWC Dock Ejector 2.1 software that adds one-click safe ejection for connected data volumes, for Mac and PC. In addition, on Mac, OWC Dock Ejector 2.1 now provides seamless high-power USB port enablement.While OWC docks are fully functional without OWC Dock Ejector, the v2.1 software adds another layer of convenience, data protection, and capability. With OWC Dock Ejector 2.1, users can:
- Safely eject all detected connected data volumes with a single click on Mac or PC, protecting against data corruption or loss before disconnecting from a dock.
- Safely eject SoftRAID, AppleRAID, and other connected non-raid volumes, including camera cards, without having to locate and eject each volume individually.
- Reduce the risk associated with improperly unmounting volumes, particularly ExFAT and FAT32 media commonly used with camera cards and in cross-platform creative workflows.
- On Mac, automatically enable supported OWC dock USB ports for higher-power operation recognized by macOS, allowing compatible devices to access the additional power they require without changing macOS security settings.
- Support devices such as Apple SuperDrive and mobile devices that may require macOS to recognize a USB port as high-power enabled for proper operation or faster charging.
- Download Dock Ejector 2.1 free from OWC.com or, for the first time, through the Apple App Store.
"OWC Dock Ejector takes something that can be a tedious manual process and turns it into one-click assurance for your data," said Larry O'Connor, Founder and CEO, Other World Computing (OWC). "Whether you're on a Mac or PC, it detects and safely ejects connected data volumes so you can disconnect your dock without worrying that you missed a drive. That's especially important for creators working with camera media and ExFAT or FAT32 volumes, where an improper disconnect can result in data loss or corruption. OWC docks stand on their own - OWC Dock Ejector simply makes the experience safer, easier, and better."
"On the Mac, OWC Dock Ejector goes even further by enabling macOS to recognize the higher-power capability already built into supported OWC dock USB ports, so devices that require additional power can operate or fast charge as intended," O'Connor continued. "It does that without requiring users to dig into messy security settings. Bringing together one-click drive safety and high-power port enablement in a free, integrated software experience is another OWC difference - adding even more capability, convenience, and value to an OWC dock."

articles.title: Chinese chipmaker could hugely ramp up RAM production in 2028 — but it's not likely to help the average consumer in the ongoing memory crisis
articles.text:
Analysts forecast Chinese RAM surge through 2028 — but it's not likely to help the average consumer, as Dell CEO warns the memory crisis could last until 2030
CXMT predicted to ramp up DRAM production, but here's why you shouldn't get excited
- Chinese chipmaker CXMT is predicted to be ramping up RAM production
- It could double memory production by 2028, we're told
- This extra RAM is likely to service the domestic market, though, and meanwhile, Dell's CEO is warning that the memory crisis is likely to persist to 2030
A major Chinese chipmaker has plans to expand its DRAM production in a big way over the next couple of years, but this won't be a silver bullet for wider RAM problems, and Dell's CEO is warning on the memory crisis getting worse, too.
First, the news on the Chinese company CXMT, which was flagged by P Equity Research on X (via Wccftech) in a post that highlights forecasts from Counterpoint Research and TrendForce.
According to those research firms, CXMT is set to expand its DRAM wafer production from around 320,000 units this year, to 420,000 units over the course of 2027.
That translates to a growth of just over 30% in a year, and the further prediction is that in 2028, production capacity might hit 500,000 to 600,000, so given that most optimistic scenario, it would nearly double compared to this year.
There's some excitement on that point because while others are focusing on HBM, or high-end RAM for the AI industry, this is an expansion of traditional RAM production, meaning the kind that'll go in a PC as opposed to a data center server.
However, before we start mulling the prospect of RAM supply being shored up to some extent, there are obvious caveats to consider here – including a new warning from Dell's CEO as mentioned at the outset.
Analysis: domestic relief – and more pessimism from Dell
The problem with CXMT is that even if the predicted near-doubling of RAM production does happen in 2028 as these analysts are theorizing, where is this memory going to end up?
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Most likely it'll serve the domestic market in China, and the chances of it making any kind of a meaningful difference to the balance of RAM supply outside of Asia are minimal. China's own memory requirements are substantial, and as we've discussed before, the government is likely to exert its influence in terms of keeping local demand fulfilled rather than selling abroad.
And yes, while it's true that CXMT's RAM is being used by some manufacturers in the west already, it's on a very limited basis currently – and it isn't like it's some kind of a bargain, either. Indeed, the cost of CXMT's memory is reportedly much the same as what you'll pay if buying from Samsung.
Meanwhile, as Wccftech also picked up, the CEO of Dell, Michael Dell, added his voice to the growing consensus that the memory shortage will get worse next year, and that these RAM woes are going to be prolonged for quite some time.
Dell told the Wall Street Journal that memory supply problems could keep on making us miserable for up to four years, meaning until 2030. Again, this echoes some of the many negative calls on the RAM crisis which have been heard in the past few months.
CXMT expanding its RAM production in a beefy way certainly won't hurt, but it's unlikely to help the average consumer outside of China.
Meanwhile, as RAM continues to get pricier (somehow, even though the cost was already through the roof), it's worth considering workarounds to get more from your gaming PC.

articles.title: MonoRace: Wie eine KI mit billiger Hardware die besten Drohnenpiloten der Welt abhängt
articles.text:
MonoRace: Wie eine KI mit billiger Hardware die besten Drohnenpiloten der Welt abhängt
Bei der Abu Dabi Autonomous Drone Racing Competition treffen jährlich die besten Renndrohnen und ihre Pilotinnen und Piloten in den Emiraten aufeinander. Mit bis zu 100 Kilometern pro Stunde fliegen die kleinen Drohnen durch die abgesteckten Tore des anspruchsvollen Parcours. Für Zuschauer sind sie oft nur als leuchtende Umrisse und am kreischenden Geräusch ihrer Rotoren erkennbar. Es ist ein Wettbewerb, in dem es auf Technik, Reaktionsgeschwindigkeit und Fingerspitzengefühl ankommt.
Im vergangenen Jahr musste sich der Weltmeister Yuki Hashimoto im großen Finale gegen Team MAVLab aus den Niederlanden geschlagen geben. Doch es war ein ungleiches Duell: Denn während Hashimoto seine Drohne selbst steuerte, schickte MAVLab eine Künstliche Intelligenz ins Rennen.
MonoRace heißt das System, das nun, rund anderthalb Jahre nach dem Rennen, von unabhängigen Expertinnen und Experten geprüft in der Fachzeitschrift Science Robotics vorgestellt wurde. Es zeigt nicht nur, dass KI-Systeme menschlichen Drohnenpiloten inzwischen überlegen sind. Das waren sie auch schon in früheren Vergleichen. Sondern vor allem, wie sich mit vergleichsweise eingeschränkter Hardware erstaunliche Ergebnisse erzeugen lassen. MonoRace hat nämlich nur eine einzige kleine Kamera in Kombination mit einer inertialen Messeinheit (IMU) benutzt, um durch den Parcours zu navigieren. Kein GPS, keine externen Tracking-Systeme.
Drohnenrennen mit begrenzten Ressourcen
„Das Fliegen mit sehr hoher Geschwindigkeit und nur einer Kamera ist eine Herausforderung, da die Bilder unscharf und verzerrt sind und das KI-System nur sehr wenig Zeit hat, um die Position der Drohne präzise zu bestimmen“, sagt Stavrow Bahnam von der TU Delft und Hauptautor der Studie.
Die Forscher haben das von den Veranstaltern bereitgestellte Drohnen-Modell mit einer Acht-Megapixel-Kamera, die es für knapp 30 Euro zu kaufen gibt, einem für KI-Anwendungen optimierten Jetson-Orin-Kleincomputer von Nvidia, sowie mit einem Flugcontroller ausgestattet.
Der Ansatz von MonoRace besteht darin, dass die Drohne nicht vorab den richtigen Pfad durch einen vorgegebenen Parcours mit mehreren Toren lernt, sondern in Echtzeit auf den Parcours reagieren kann. Um das zu gewährleisten, muss sich das System auf das Wichtigste beschränken, was in diesem Fall bedeutet: Es muss durch die Tore fliegen, ohne sie zu touchieren. „Anstatt die Drohne mit immer leistungsfähigeren Sensoren und Computern auszustatten, wollten wir herausfinden, wie viel Intelligenz wir aus sehr begrenzten Ressourcen herausholen können“, sagt der Forscher Christophe De Wagter.
Das Kameramodul gibt die Bildinformationen an den Begleitcomputer weiter. Um Rechenleistung zu sparen, verarbeitet die KI nicht das komplette Bild, sondern konzentriert sich auf einen bloß 384 mal 384 Pixel großen Ausschnitt. Zudem berechnet das System anhand der aktuellen Position vorab, wo die nächsten zwei Tore im Bild liegen müssten.
Bis zu 500 Steuerbefehle pro Sekunde
Die angepassten Bilder werden in ein neuronales Netzwerk eingespeist. Das verwandelt die Bilder in Masken, die die Pixel des Torrahmens vom Hintergrund trennen, sodass quasi nur noch weiße Objekte auf schwarzem Hintergrund zu sehen sind. Im nächsten Schritt werden diese Masken algorithmisch auf ihre Linien hin analysiert und die Schnittpunkte identifiziert – wodurch das System genau die Ecken des nächsten Tores berechnet.
Im letzten Schritt werden diese Informationen an den Flugcontroller weitergegeben, und zwar mit bis zu 500 Befehlen pro Sekunde. Die Steuerung wurde vorab mithilfe von verstärkendem Lernen in einer Simulation trainiert. Dadurch hat MonoRace unter anderem die physikalischen Eigenschaften und das aerodynamischen Verhalten der Drohne gelernt. Auch wurde es mit realistischen Störungseffekten konfrontiert, etwa mit Bildrauschen oder mit Bewegungsunschärfe (Motion Blur). Anders gesagt: Es hat gelernt, wie man die Drohne steuert und wie weit man an ihr Maximum gehen kann, bevor sie abstürzt.
Das System war so effektiv, dass es 2025 in Abu Dhabi nicht nur die besten menschlichen Drohnenpiloten (die natürlich auch noch in eigenen Rennen unter sich angetreten sind), sondern auch andere autonome Systeme geschlagen hat. Für das Team, der TU Delft sind Drohnenrennen eine gute Gelegenheit, um Roboter an ihre Grenzen zu bringen. Die Erkenntnisse könnten für andere autonome Systeme adaptiert werden. Die vorliegende Studie zeige, dass die neuronalen Netze das Potenzial haben, „selbst bei den kleinsten und kostengünstigsten Robotern eine optimale Steuerung zu ermöglichen“, heißt es in der Studie.

articles.title: La "ameba de fuego" rompe el récord de calor para la vida compleja y obliga a replantear dónde buscar vida extraterrestre
articles.text:
A la hora de buscar vida extraterrestre, tenemos muy en cuenta la temperatura del planeta o satélite en cuestión. Generalmente se necesita que estén a una distancia adecuada de su estrella. Ni demasiado lejos, ya que haría frío, ni tampoco tan cerca como para que la temperatura sea abrasadora. La zona de habitabilidad suele ser esa en la que la temperatura podría mantener el agua líquida, ni helada ni en forma de gas. Sin embargo, si lo que queremos es encontrar organismos eucariotas, se tiende a afinar más, ya que suelen llevarse muy mal con el calor.
El récord estaba en 60ºC, pero ahora un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Siracusa ha descubierto una ameba capaz de reproducirse a 63ºC e incluso de recuperar su actividad después de los 70ºC. Puede parecer una diferencia mínima, pero cambia bastante las reglas del juego.
Ameba de fuego. La ameba en cuestión fue hallada en pozas de agua caliente del Parque Nacional Volcánico Lassen (California). Resistía tan bien el calor que fue bautizada como Incendiamoeba cascadensis y, más coloquialmente, como ameba de fuego. Hay varias cifras a tener en cuenta a la hora de analizar sus niveles de resistencia. Para empezar, puede reproducirse por división celular hasta a 63ºC. A los 64ºC sigue activa, aunque ya no se reproduce. Después, a los 66ºC sigue parcialmente activa, aunque empieza a sufrir los efectos del calor. A los 70ºC ya se inactiva, pero aún puede volver a activarse. Sin embargo, a los 80ºC muere por completo.
Otros organismos termófilos. Los organismos extremófilos son aquellos capaces de resistir a condiciones consideradas muy extremas. Cuando dichas condiciones tienen relación con la temperatura alta, se les considera termófilos. Hay organismos termófilos que resisten mucho más calor que la ameba de fuego. Por ejemplo, la arquea Methanopyrus kandleri puede sobrevivir a 110ºC. Pero hay una diferencia. Las arqueas, como las bacterias, son organismos unicelulares procariotas. Esto significa que están compuestas por una sola célula, sin un núcleo delimitado. Son más simples, por lo que es más fácil que resistan condiciones extremas.
En cambio, las eucariotas sí tienen un núcleo delimitado. Si además tienen orgánulos y una maquinaria celular más compleja, como esta ameba, hay muchas más estructuras que podrían fallar por el calor, por lo que suelen resistir menos. Hasta ahora, el récord de temperaturas que puede soportar un organismo eucariota lo tenían algunos hongos y algas rojas, que alcanzan los 60ºC aproximadamente. La ameba de fuego los ha superado a todos.
Su modus operandi. La clave para resistir tan bien las temperaturas reside en los genes de esta ameba. Los científicos que la han descubierto han observado que cuenta, por un lado, con genes que le permiten reparar el ADN por los daños del calor. Además, por su conformación, sus proteínas son más estables también cuando suben las temperaturas. Por otro lado, tiene la capacidad de percibir su entorno y el calor que la rodea, de modo que pueda activar o desactivar los genes que necesite en cada momento.
Más lugares en los que buscar. Cada vez se conocen más organismos extremófilos que amplían los lugares en los que se puede buscar vida extraterrestre. Esta ameba de fuego nos indica que, quizás, habría planetas que se han desechado por ser demasiado calientes y que no se deberían haber abandonado tan rápido. Eso sí, hay que tener en cuenta que un organismo puede resistir muy bien al calor, pero no a la salinidad, la acidez o las radiaciones cósmicas.
De momento, la Tierra es el único planeta que reune todas las condiciones de habitabilidad posibles. Por todo esto, seleccionar posibles mundos en los que florezca la vida no es tan sencillo como medir su temperatura. Sin embargo, ahora vemos que, al menos, en lo que a calor se refiere, podemos ampliar un poco el rango.

articles.title: Les étoiles vertes n'étaient pas censées exister : des astronomes viennent pourtant d'en trouver une
articles.text:
On ne peut pas voir d’étoile verte. Vous l’avez peut-être constaté en levant les yeux vers le ciel étoilé, ces astres ne peuvent pas nous apparaître verdâtres. Pourtant, une nouvelle étude surprend les astronomes. Pour la première fois, ils ont identifié une étoile qui nous apparaîtrait verte si nous pouvions l’observer de près.
Cette découverte, annoncée par l’université de Warwick en Angleterre le 15 octobre 2026, est détaillée dans la revue RAS Techniques and Instruments. Les scientifiques ont étudié les naines blanches, des vestiges très denses laissés par des étoiles en fin de vie (c’est ce que deviendra le Soleil après sa mort). Or, selon ces chercheurs, certaines naines blanches peuvent briller dans une large gamme de couleurs, y compris en vert.
Pourquoi les étoiles n’ont pas toutes la même couleur
Pour les astronomes, la couleur d’une étoile renseigne d’abord sur sa température de surface. Comme un fer de forge qui passe du rouge au blanc en chauffant, l’astre change de teinte selon sa température : les étoiles les plus chaudes (on parle de températures de l’ordre de 40 000 °C) sont bleutées, tandis que les étoiles aux surfaces les plus froides (environ 3 000 °C) sont rougeâtres.
« On pensait que les naines blanches, ces vestiges denses laissés par les étoiles de type solaire à la fin de leur vie, suivaient la même règle », explique le communiqué de l’université de Warwick. Mais cette croyance vacille désormais car, selon les auteurs de la nouvelle étude, si l’on pouvait regarder de plus près ces astres, nous découvririons une panoplie de couleurs bien plus riche : vert, mais aussi rose, cyan, jaune et même violet !
« Des couleurs auxquelles personne ne s’attendait »
La majorité des étoiles sont des sortes de « radiateurs parfaits », selon les mots de Mark Hollands, l’astrophysicien qui a mené ces recherches, cité par son université. « Leur couleur est presque entièrement déterminée par leur température. » Mais lui et son équipe ont découvert que certaines naines blanches pouvaient aussi « produire des couleurs auxquelles personne ne s’attendait ».
L’explication repose sur la densité des étoiles. « Nous avons étudié comment la combinaison de la température et de la composition chimique peut influencer les couleurs perçues des naines blanches », peut-on lire dans l’étude. Les naines blanches sont particulièrement denses : pour les plus froides, l’atmosphère peut atteindre une masse volumique de 1 gramme par centimètre cube (proche de celle de l’eau, et des millions de fois supérieure à celle de la surface visible du Soleil).
Si certains éléments présents dans l’étoile, comme le carbone, le calcium ou le sodium, interagissent avec le plasma d’hélium très dense qui les entoure, ils absorbent la lumière sur une plage de couleurs beaucoup plus large qu’à des densités plus faibles. Ce phénomène dévie la couleur de l’étoile par rapport aux teintes classiques (orange, blanc et bleu) d’un corps rayonnant parfait.
La vraie couleur des naines blanches
Le spectre lumineux est une décomposition de la lumière par longueur d’onde (comme un prisme décompose la lumière du Soleil). L’arc-en-ciel est un phénomène bien connu de décomposition de la lumière.
Sauf qu’aucune naine blanche n’est assez proche de nous pour que les scientifiques observent directement sa couleur à l’œil nu. Pour contourner cette difficulté, l’équipe est partie des spectres lumineux de ces astres, des données que les astronomes collectent déjà en routine. En passant ces spectres dans un modèle de la vision humaine des couleurs, elle a calculé la « vraie » couleur perçue de ces étoiles.
- Les naines blanches riches en carbone ont une teinte rose ou violette,
- Celles qui ont été enrichies par des débris d’astéroïdes et de comètes tendent vers le jaune,
- Enfin, les plus froides, aux atmosphères mêlant hydrogène et hélium, prennent souvent une teinte cyan ou bleu pâle.
Les scientifiques ont notamment été marqués par l’étoile WD J1330+6435, l’étoile verte de l’étude. Cet objet, situé dans la Voie lactée, se trouve à environ 280 années-lumière de la Terre. Sa température est d’environ 4 000 °C, et on sait que cet astre a accumulé de la matière rocheuse originaire de son propre système planétaire.
Avec cette atmosphère chargée en calcium, lithium et sodium, WD J1330+6435 est apparue en vert dans les modèles des scientifiques. « Les traces de sodium dans l’atmosphère de cette naine blanche absorbent la partie orange du spectre, ce qui laisse une lueur verte fantomatique », explique Mark Hollands. À la connaissance des chercheurs, aucune autre étoile, vivante ou morte, n’avait jusqu’ici été décrite de façon crédible comme verte. WD J1330+6435 serait donc la première véritable étoile verte connue de la Galaxie.
Ces teintes inhabituelles restent rares. Sur les 151 naines blanches situées à moins de 65 années-lumière de la Terre, l’équipe n’en a trouvé que 5 aux couleurs atypiques (2 jaunes et 3 roses), et aucune verte. Les auteurs en déduisent qu’environ une naine blanche sur 30 brille d’une couleur inattendue dans l’Univers.

articles.title: Licences d'occasion : la justice inflige un camouflet (de plus) à Microsoft
articles.text:
La justice britannique vient de refuser à Microsoft l’autorisation de porter son litige avec ValueLicensing devant la Cour suprême. Un nouveau revers pour l’éditeur, déjà contraint de s’expliquer sur un document interne vieux de treize ans.
Microsoft peine décidément à faire entendre ses arguments dans l’affaire des licences logicielles d’occasion. Le 13 octobre, la Cour d’appel britannique a rejeté sa demande d’autorisation de recours devant la Cour suprême sans même détailler les motifs de sa décision. L’éditeur espérait pourtant faire annuler un jugement favorable à ValueLicensing, une entreprise spécialisée dans la revente de licences Windows et Office.
Cette décision conforte les précédents jugements reconnaissant, sous certaines conditions, le droit de revendre des licences perpétuelles déjà utilisées. Mais elle ne clôt pas le contentieux opposant les deux entreprises.
Microsoft dispose encore d’une dernière possibilité de recours
L’entreprise américaine peut en effet toujours saisir directement la Cour suprême britannique. Elle dispose pour cela de 28 jours (à compter du refus du 13 octobre) et devra convaincre les juges que son dossier mérite un nouvel examen.
Le conflit remonte à 2021, lorsque ValueLicensing a réclamé 270 millions de livres sterling à Microsoft. Le revendeur accuse le groupe d’avoir organisé la raréfaction des licences Office d'occasion, notamment en accordant des remises aux entreprises acceptant de conserver ou d’abandonner leurs anciennes licences lors de leur passage à Microsoft 365.
Microsoft conteste ces accusations et a tenté de défendre sa position sur le terrain du droit d’auteur. Sans succès jusqu’ici. En novembre 2025, le tribunal britannique de la concurrence avait reconnu la possibilité de revendre certaines licences perpétuelles, y compris lorsqu’elles provenaient de contrats achetés en volume. La Cour d’appel avait confirmé cette décision en juillet dernier.
La légalité de cette revente a donc été reconnue dans le cadre du litige, mais la justice doit encore déterminer si les pratiques commerciales reprochées à Microsoft étaient anticoncurrentielles.
Un document interne de 2013 pourrait compliquer les affaires de Microsoft
Les ennuis judiciaires de l’éditeur ne se limitent pas à ses recours. Une ordonnance du 14 septembre 2026 impose à Microsoft de nouvelles recherches documentaires auprès de plusieurs dirigeants actuels et anciens. Elle réclame également des explications sur la communication tardive d’une présentation interne de 2013 consacrée aux logiciels d’occasion.
Baptisé Second-Hand Software Presentation, ce fichier est qualifié dans la procédure de Known Adverse Document, une catégorie qui désigne des éléments potentiellement défavorables à la partie qui les détient.
Son contenu n’a pas été rendu public, mais une question embarrassante se pose déjà. Pourquoi Microsoft a-t-il attendu décembre 2025 pour communiquer ce document, alors que la procédure avait commencé quatre ans auparavant ? L’entreprise doit fournir des explications d’ici au 31 octobre.
Une autre action pourrait coûter plusieurs milliards à l’éditeur
Le dossier intéresse également Alexander Wolfson, qui porte un projet d’action collective distincte au nom de millions de clients britanniques. Cette procédure réclame entre 1,3 et 3,5 milliards de livres sterling de dédommagements pour les pratiques présumées de Microsoft sur le marché des licences d'occasion.
La bataille judiciaire pourrait donc prendre une ampleur financière considérable. Avant cela, Microsoft devra encore expliquer quand ses responsables ont eu connaissance du document de 2013 et poursuivre la communication des pièces réclamées par le tribunal. Winter is coming.
Source : The Register

articles.title: Data, not chips, will decide India’s AI and biotech future, say deeptech founders
articles.text:
Data, not chips, will decide India’s AI and biotech future, say deeptech founders
Founders of CoreMantle and Loopworm say compute and applications can be replaced, but trusted, context-rich data cannot, and India must take charge of it to scale AI and biotech.
When people talk about technology infrastructure, they usually mean semiconductors, data centres, and AI models. But the layer that decides how well these technologies work is the data underneath them, and India still has to build it.
At a panel discussion on 'The invisible infrastructure of the new tech order' at TechSparks 2026, moderated by Chhavi Mahajan, Chief Content Officer, YourStory, the panellists said India’s advantage will come from owning trusted, context-rich data in fields ranging from language AI to biotech.
Arvind Pani, Founder, CoreMantle, an AI data intelligence startup, said data is the one part of the technology stack that cannot be swapped out. “You can continue to replace compute. You can continue to replace the application, but you cannot replace the data,” he said.
Ankit Bagaria, Co-founder and CEO, Loopworm, an insect biotechnology company, said the gap is especially wide in biopharma, where too much work still happens through trial and error. Better data, he said, could cut the time it takes to bring a product to market.
Bagaria said biotech deserves the same attention as AI, quantum and chips, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic. He noted that India still imports about 73% of its key materials, including active pharmaceutical ingredients and reagents, from China. And although the country supplies a large share of the world’s vaccines by volume, that accounts for only about 5% of the market by value.
“We have operated in the biosimilar space for a very, very long time, where somebody else is discovering the molecules for us,” he said. He argued that India now needs to move into drug discovery.
Pani said the same need for local context applies to language. India’s internet was built for English users, which put up two barriers at once for most citizens, who had to learn the technology and a new language. Only about 4 to 5% of India’s population is comfortable using English alone, he noted.
He added that even English is not a solved problem for AI. Models trained mostly on American English often struggle with Australian or regional accents, and English as spoken across Indian states varies widely. “These are the nuances that nobody else will understand, that India will understand,” he said.
Both panellists agreed that a bigger dataset is not necessarily a better one. Pani said AI models built on smaller amounts of enriched, contextual data outperform those trained on large volumes of raw data. Many Indian language datasets are recorded in studios from scripts, he noted, so models trained on them perform well in controlled settings but fail in real-world conversations.
Bagaria said that across biological data, “it’s garbage in, garbage out.”
Loopworm spent about 12 to 13 months cleaning existing data while building a digital tool that maps the inner workings of the silkworm. The work had to be tailored to Indian silkworm strains and the pathogens that affect them.
Loopworm uses silkworms to produce sustainable animal feed and high-value recombinant proteins.
Bagaria said Loopworm chose silkworm because silk is over 98% protein, which makes the insect one of nature’s most efficient converters of plant leaves into protein. The silkworm has been domesticated for about 4,000 years, its genome was sequenced in 2007, and around 175 institutes in India teach sericulture and related biotech.
He added that this data-led approach has already cut a set of experiments from 10 months and Rs 25 lakh to two and a half months and about Rs 4.5 lakh. “I am sure that in 10 years’ time, all of us would be saying that the largest impact of AI has come on biotech,” he said.
Pani said proprietary data is already becoming a competitive moat. He cited legal AI company Harvey, which has changed both its models and its compute while keeping its domain-specific data as its core advantage.
On what needs to change, Pani said India must design technology for its own needs. He recalled that his previous company brought Indian language support to Android in 2011 through a partnership with Qualcomm, before Google did. “If we continue to think that somebody else is going to solve our problem, then we will always be behind the curve,” he said.
Bagaria welcomed government initiatives such as the BioE3 policy and the Research, Development and Innovation Fund. But he called for more public and foundational funding for basic data generation, such as the in-depth sequencing and characterisation of Indian organisms, because traditional investors are unlikely to fund fundamental science.

articles.title: JEP 543 Finalizes Structured Concurrency in JDK 28, Ending Seven Preview Rounds
Estados Unidos destinó USD 4.400 millones a reabrir tres centrales nucleares para la IA
articles.text:
El Departamento de Energía de Estados Unidos otorgó préstamos por hasta USD 4.400 millones para reabrir tres centrales nucleares cerradas y usar esa energía en centros de datos de inteligencia artificial, según informó la agencia Associated Press.
Las plantas son Palisades, en Michigan; Crane Clean Energy Center, en el sitio de Three Mile Island, Pensilvania; y Duane Arnold, en Iowa. Juntas sumarán 2,25 gigavatios, suficiente para abastecer a unos 2 millones de hogares y comercios.
Ningún reactor comercial había vuelto a generar electricidad después de iniciar el proceso de desmantelamiento, aunque sí hubo reactores reactivados tras largas paradas sin llegar a esa etapa, según precisó Associated Press.
Microsoft y Google pagan la cuenta
Dos de las tres plantas ya tienen comprador. Constellation Energy, dueña de Crane, firmó un acuerdo a 20 años con Microsoft para venderle la energía una vez reactivado el reactor, con una inversión prevista de USD 1.600 millones y un préstamo del Departamento de Energía de USD 1.000 millones.
NextEra Energy, propietaria de Duane Arnold, selló un contrato a 25 años con Google para abastecer a sus centros de datos. El gobierno le otorgó a la compañía un préstamo de hasta USD 1.900 millones, según confirmó el Departamento de Energía en septiembre.
“Este es un ejemplo perfecto de que los centros de datos pagan su propia cuenta”, dijo John Ketchum, presidente y director ejecutivo de NextEra Energy, en referencia al contrato con Google. “Ninguno de los costos lo pagan los clientes residenciales de Iowa”, agregó.
El gobierno de Donald Trump impulsa la reactivación de plantas nucleares como parte de una estrategia para ampliar la oferta eléctrica frente a la demanda creciente de la inteligencia artificial y la industria manufacturera.
La reactivación de Duane Arnold generaría más de USD 9.000 millones en beneficios económicos para Iowa durante 25 años, según un estudio de la consultora Strategic Economic Research citado por NextEra Energy.
El proyecto crearía cerca de 1.500 empleos durante la construcción y mantendría más de 450 puestos permanentes una vez que el reactor vuelva a operar, de acuerdo con datos del Departamento de Energía.
Plantas que cerraron por costos, no por fallas
Palisades funcionó entre 1971 y 2022, cuando su entonces dueña, Entergy, decidió abandonar el mercado eléctrico mayorista. Holtec International compró la planta y empezó a desmantelarla antes de que el estado de Michigan impulsara su reapertura.
En agosto, Holtec comenzó a cargar combustible nuclear, uno de los últimos pasos antes de reactivar un reactor, pero pausó el proceso después de que un ensamblaje de combustible se inclinara de su posición vertical. La empresa debe determinar la causa antes de continuar.
Duane Arnold operó desde 1975 y cerró en agosto de 2020 tras sufrir daños por una tormenta, antes de lo previsto en su plan original de cierre. El reactor de Three Mile Island que ahora busca reactivar Constellation fue apagado en 2019 por pérdidas económicas.
Esa misma central fue escenario, en 1979, del peor accidente de la historia de la energía nuclear comercial en Estados Unidos, que destruyó uno de sus dos reactores. El otro, el que hoy se busca reactivar, siguió operando hasta su cierre por motivos de rentabilidad.
Apoyos y objeciones a los subsidios
Todd Allen, experto en ingeniería nuclear de la Universidad de Michigan, comparó el proceso con volver a poner en marcha un auto que estuvo parado varios años: hay que revisar que cada pieza funcione y que los permisos sigan vigentes. “Hay una demanda en el país de más energía”, dijo Allen. “Para cualquiera que quiera cero emisiones de carbono, la energía nuclear lo ofrece. Para el gobierno de Trump, que realmente quiere apostar por lo nuclear, esto también encaja con ese objetivo.”
Edwin Lyman, director de seguridad de energía nuclear de la organización Union of Concerned Scientists, cuestionó que el dinero público no se esté usando para reforzar la seguridad de plantas diseñadas entre 1970 y 1990, antes de que el cambio climático agravara los fenómenos extremos.
Jack Spencer, de la Fundación Heritage, dijo que no puede pensar en un peor uso del dinero de los contribuyentes, porque considera que estos proyectos tienen una demanda garantizada y no necesitan fondos federales. Jennifer Gordon, del Atlantic Council, defendió en cambio el financiamiento como una forma eficaz de conseguir energía necesaria.
La Asociación Mundial Nuclear señaló que la reactivación de reactores debería celebrarse, aunque consideró preferible evitar que las plantas cierren antes de tiempo. Países como Canadá, Armenia, Bélgica, Japón, India y Corea del Sur ya reactivaron o repotenciaron reactores tras paradas prolongadas.
Palisades podría convertirse en la primera planta del mundo en volver a generar energía después de haber iniciado formalmente su desmantelamiento, de acuerdo con la asociación. Sus contratos de compra de energía exigen que esté en servicio antes de marzo de 2027.
Las tres reactivaciones todavía dependen de aprobaciones de la Comisión Reguladora Nuclear de Estados Unidos, el organismo que autoriza el funcionamiento de los reactores. Ninguna de las plantas tiene, por ahora, una fecha de reinicio confirmada ante ese regulador.

articles.title: Vinted et Leboncoin envahis par des annonces de produits volés pendant les manifestations
articles.text:
Ces 17 et 18 octobre, un nombre conséquent de magasins ont été pillés à travers la France. Certaines enseignes, grandes et petites, ont été vandalisées, parfois durant plusieurs heures. Et après les pillages, arrive maintenant l’heure de la revente. À ce titre, Vinted a enregistré une hausse soudaine d’annonces suspectes à la suite du 17 octobre.
Les produits volés se revendent maintenant sur Vinted et Leboincoin
Sur les sites de revente en ligne, comme Vinted et Leboncoin, les annonces suspectes se multiplient. Dans certains cas, des produits présentant toujours une étiquette et un antivol sont mis en vente. Dans d’autres cas, les vendeurs indiquent explicitement qu’il s’agit de produits volés durant les événements du 17 octobre.
Seulement voilà, ne pas avoir été pris la main dans le sac au moment des faits n’implique pas d’être sorti d’affaire. Pour cause, la plupart des plateformes en ligne obligent les revendeurs à fournir un certain nombre de données confidentielles afin de pouvoir poster des annonces, comme un nom, un prénom, une adresse postale, un IBAN, voire dans certains cas une copie de la carte d’identité. C’est pourquoi certains candidats à la présidentielle, ont apelé les plateformes de revente en ligne à coopérer avec l’État afin d’identifier certains pilleurs.
Vinted annonce collaborer d’ores et déjà avec les autorités françaises
L’appel semble avoir été entendu de la part des plateformes. Un porte-parole de Vinted a déclaré dans un communiqué que l’entreprise « a immédiatement pris des mesures pour identifier et supprimer les annonces liées au pillage » et a « renforcé la surveillance des annonces suspectes ». Il précise qu’ « En cas d’infraction à notre règlement, nous prenons des mesures contre les comptes concernés, pouvant aller jusqu’à la suspension définitive ». Enfin, notons que Vinted annonce collaborer « activement avec les forces de l’ordre et les autorités françaises ».
Il reste maintenant à déterminer comment vérifier avec précision si un article revendu en ligne provient bel et bien d’un pillage survenu le 17 octobre. Si certains articles intègrent une puce ou un numéro de série, ce n’est pas le cas de tous les produits mis sur le marché. Dans tous les cas, rappelons que le recel, qui consiste notamment à détenir ou à revendre un bien en sachant qu’il a été volé, est passible de cinq ans d’emprisonnement et de 375 000 euros d’amende en France.

articles.title: Fabriqué par Stellantis en Espagne, ce SUV électrique chinois à moins de 30 000 € pourrait coûter encore moins cher en France
articles.text:
Fabriqué par Stellantis en Espagne, ce SUV électrique chinois à moins de 30 000 € pourrait coûter encore moins cher en France
Le Leapmotor B10 est maintenant assemblé par Stellantis en Espagne. Une production européenne qui devrait clairement réduire la facture du SUV électrique en France, et ce, pour deux raisons bien précises.
Confrontées aux taxes douanières sur les importations de voitures électriques, les marques chinoises produisent de plus en plus en Europe. Le Leapmotor B10 commence d’ailleurs à sortir des chaînes de production espagnoles de Stellantis. Un choix qui devrait rendre le SUV électrique beaucoup plus concurrentiel dans les semaines à venir. La prime CEE en France pourrait aussi alléger son tarif, mais à une condition bien précise.
Leapmotor B10 : l'assemblage européen par Stellantis fait chuter son prix
Stellantis vient d’accueillir Leapmotor au sein de son usine espagnole de Figueruelas. Assemblant déjà les Peugeot 208, Opel Corsa et Lancia Ypsilon, elle est maintenant mise à profit pour le B10, un SUV électrique vendu aujourd’hui juste en dessous de 30 000 €. Cette opération permet au géant automobile de rentabiliser son outil industriel, tout en aidant son partenaire chinois à accélérer son implantation en Europe avec ses modèles à bas prix.
Cette stratégie permet en effet à ce véhicule d’échapper aux 30,7 % de droits de douane imposés par l’Union européenne sur les importations d’électriques chinoises. En prime, cette relocalisation le rapproche des critères d’éligibilité à la prime CEE renforcée en France, comprise entre 3600 et 6100 €. Pour décrocher ce coup de pouce gouvernemental, le SUV devra toutefois intégrer des cellules de batterie produites localement et valider son éco-score auprès des autorités françaises.
Pour rappel, le Leapmotor B10 est un SUV familial de 4,52 m de long équipé d’un moteur de 218 ch et d’une autonomie de 361 ou 434 km WLTP en fonction de la batterie choisie. Affiché à partir de 29 900 € pour le moment sur le site officiel de la marque, ce modèle pourrait facilement passer sous la barre des 26 000 € (voire 24 000 € selon les revenus) s’il obtient bien le précieux sésame.
Ce partenariat industriel ne fonctionne cependant pas à sens unique. Dès 2028, un nouveau SUV électrique badgé Opel devrait être assemblé à Saragosse en reprenant les composants de l’écosystème Leapmotor afin d’abaisser ses coûts de revient. Un second modèle chinois rejoindrait au passage l’usine Stellantis de Madrid pour entretenir cette alliance. Un échange de bons procédés qui permet à Leapmotor de contourner les barrières douanières européennes, pendant que Stellantis profite d’une technologie électrique abordable pour ses propres marques.

articles.title: Steam on Linux is going 64-bit as Valve leans harder on the platform
articles.text:
Ripple effect: One of the most popular pieces of computer software is about to deliver a better experience on Linux machines. The Steam client is going 64-bit, providing feature parity with versions designed to run on different operating systems.
A recent Steam Client Beta update brought the program into the 64-bit era on Linux. The native Linux version of the massively popular gaming client is now a 64-bit application, which means it gains access to a few significant enhancements and, hopefully, a more reliable software experience.
Until last week's beta update, Steam's main binary ran as a 32-bit application even on 64-bit Linux distros. Some components, such as steamwebhelper, were already 64-bit. Now the main client uses 64-bit code as well, which should significantly expand memory access and improve the software's overall security.
Steam is going 64-bit, but Linux users will still need to provide 32-bit libraries and graphics drivers for compatibility reasons. Valve said Linux operating systems that only work with 64-bit software are not supported just yet, which might further complicate the job of distro maintainers. The Fedora team floated dropping 32-bit library support last year, but withdrew the proposal after pushback over Steam compatibility – or lack thereof.
The same beta brings a few additional changes to Steam's experience. The gaming client now runs inside its own "Steam Runtime" container, which should help the program behave more consistently across different Linux distros. The same technology is used by Steam games, which can use either 32- or 64-bit code regardless of the client's architecture.
Another notable change is Steam Achievement Sets, a new way to organize and track in-game achievements across base game releases and additional downloadable content. The sets should also give developers a new type of seasonal goal. Games already supporting the new beta feature include Left 4 Dead 2, Portal 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and more than a dozen others.
Steam's new 64-bit architecture on Linux is a significant change, as Steam is becoming a major driving force behind Linux gaming experiences and products. Most of Valve's hardware devices rely on SteamOS, which is based on a special version of Arch Linux. Even modders are having a lot of fun exploiting the open source nature of SteamOS to build some interesting handheld projects.

articles.title: La toute nouvelle montre connectée Garmin Fenix 9 avec écran AMOLED et cartographie express connait sa 1ère réduction — Frandroid
articles.text:
La Garmin Fenix 9 est une montre connectée haut de gamme, faite pour les sportifs exigeants, notamment en outdoor, qui reprend l’ADN technique de la marque en musclant son équipement d’affichage et de navigation. Garmin l’a présentée le 25 août 2026, avec des commandes ouvertes dès le 28 août. Elle a une lunette et un fond en titane, une cartographie jusqu’à 30 % plus fluide que sur la Fenix 8 et un GPS multibande, avec une large palette de métriques de santé. Elle vise d’abord les longues sorties en montagne, en trail ou en natation. Le modèle 47 mm est la taille intermédiaire (entre 43 et 51 mm), vendue au même prix que la 43 mm, et son prix est en baisse de 6 %.
Les atouts de la Garmin Fenix 9
- Son autonomie jusqu’à 16 jours en mode montre connectée
- Un écran AMOLED de 1,4 pouce deux fois plus lumineux que sur la Fenix 8 (environ 2 000 nits)
- La cartographie intégrée avec un déplacement sur la carte jusqu’à 30 % plus rapide
La Garmin Fenix 9 en 47 mm est sortie à 999,99 euros, et elle passe à 941,91 euros en ce moment sur Amazon.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant la Garmin Fenix 9. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un écran plus lumineux et une carte plus fluide
Cette version de 47 mm associe un fond et une lunette en titane à un boîtier en polymère renforcé. La déclinaison Pro passe au boîtier intégralement en titane et propose, dans ses versions inReach, une connexion LTE et satellite. La Fenix 9 classique pèse 75 grammes (53 grammes pour le boîtier seul), à peine moins que la Pro en 47 mm (78 grammes). Le compromis se joue donc surtout sur le prix. Elle a un écran AMOLED tactile de 1,4 pouce (454 x 454 pixels) protégé par un verre saphir anti-rayures, et un stockage interne doublé à 64 Go par rapport à la Fenix 8.
La dalle est aussi deux fois plus lumineuse que celle de la Fenix 8, avec un pic autour de 2 000 nits, pour une bonne lecture en plein soleil. Certes, la version Pro pousse ce curseur jusqu’à 3 000 nits, mais les 2 000 nits de la version classique restent amplement suffisants. Côté carte, Garmin ajoute 50 % de mémoire vive et un moteur cartographique revu, pour un déplacement dans les cartes topographiques jusqu’à 30 % plus rapide selon la marque. Le gain doit surtout se sentir au zoom et au défilement. Les 64 Go de stockage permettent aussi de charger deux fois plus de cartes que sur la Fenix 8 (routières ou de stations de ski) et jusqu’à 7 000 morceaux de musique, pour s’entraîner sans dépendre d’un smartphone.
Une avalanche de données et des capteurs de pointe
Au dos du boîtier, la Fenix 9 propose un capteur cardio-optique Elevate de 5e génération, une technologie déjà éprouvée qui n’évolue pas sur cette itération. Il assure toutefois un bon suivi de la fréquence cardiaque, de l’oxygénation du sang (SpO2), de la température cutanée et permet même de faire un ECG. Côté logiciel, la fonction Garmin Epic regroupe plusieurs activités (une aventure de plusieurs jours, par exemple) en un seul récit illustré de vos données et photos, à partager. Le suivi Stamina, qui estime en temps réel l’énergie qu’il vous reste pendant l’effort, gagne une courbe et des zones de Stamina.
La montre propose le suivi GPS multibande via la technologie SatIQ, avec une géolocalisation GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, QZSS et BeiDou, avec une bonne optimisation de la batterie. Elle est aussi plus connectée au quotidien, avec la présence d’un micro et d’un haut-parleur pour passer des appels ou utiliser un assistant vocal, sans oublier la lampe torche à LED, la certification 10 ATM et même un mode dédié à la plongée de loisir jusqu’à 40 mètres de profondeur. Le tout avec une autonomie annoncée jusqu’à 16 jours en mode montre connectée et 30 heures avec le GPS actif (12 heures avec la musique), ce qui reste élevé pour une montre avec dalle AMOLED.

Analisamos prós e contras das principais Smart TVs de 50 polegadas de marcas como Samsung, LG e TCL; descubra qual é a ideal para você
Para escolher a melhor TV de 50 polegadas, é preciso analisar especificações que vão além do tamanho da tela, incluindo o tipo de painel, resolução máxima, processamento de imagem e áudio, sistema operacional e recursos de conectividade suportados.
Smart TVs com painel MiniLED — como o da Samsung M75H, por exemplo — oferecem melhor contraste, enquanto outras, como a Hisense Q6Q, focam em redução de borrões e suporte a Dolby Vision.

Para escolher a melhor TV de 50″, verifique especificações que vão fazer a diferença na exibição de conteúdos, como tipo do painel e tecnologias de otimização. Fique de olho em:
Não existe unanimidade, já que a escolha varia com base no portfólio e experiências individuais. Mas um levantamento da Counterpoint indica que Samsung, TCL, Hisense e LG (nessa ordem) dominaram o envio global de TVs no primeiro semestre de 2026.
Sim. TVs de 50 polegadas têm telas relativamente grandes para mais imersão durante as jogatinas. Esses televisores também costumam oferecer imagens em 4K — resolução compatível com consoles de última geração. No entanto, se a taxa de atualização é um fator decisivo para sua gameplay, é importante ficar atento, já que muitos modelos de TVs de 50″ (geralmente mais baratos) se limitam a 60 Hz.
A distância entre o sofá e a TV deve ser de no mínimo 1,5 metro para um televisor de 50 polegadas. A metragem tem como base uma das referências usadas pela indústria, que define o tamanho de tela ideal ao usar a distância entre sofá e TV (em centímetros) e dividir o valor por três.
No entanto, o gosto pessoal do usuário também interfere nessa escolha e, por isso, as distâncias podem variar.
Uma TV de 50 polegadas tem diagonal de 127 cm, considerando que cada polegada equivale a 2,54 cm. E também costuma ter entre 110 cm e 115 cm de largura, e cerca de 65 cm de altura, com variações de modelo para modelo.
Depende das suas preferências de usabilidade. O Tizen se destaca pela integração com aparelhos Samsung e vários anos de atualizações, enquanto o webOS da LG é conhecido pela interface intuitiva. Já o Google TV é baseado no Android TV e costuma oferecer recomendações de conteúdo mais personalizadas.
QLED e QNED são tecnologias de telas similares baseadas em displays LCD retroiluminados por LEDs (ou MiniLEDs) com filtro de pontos quânticos para melhorar a reprodução de cores.
Essas Smart TVs ocupam o segmento intermediário premium, abaixo de TVs OLED. O termo QNED é proprietário da LG, enquanto marcas como Samsung e TCL adotam o QLED.
Já UHD é a sigla de “Ultra High Definition” (ou “Ultra Alta Definição”, em tradução livre). O termo se refere à resolução de 3840 x 2160 pixels, conhecida como 4K, e geralmente acompanha modelos com painéis mais simples, como a linha Crystal UHD da Samsung ou a série LG UHD 4K.

articles.title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
articles.text:
Open source Windows alternative ReactOS has reached a major milestone: The operating system can now be installed directly onto an NT Files System drive partition. As reported by Phoronix, the move to NTFS clears a long-standing hurdle for the project and brings it one step closer to finally reaching beta.
Prior to this latest announcement, ReactOS required users to keep a FAT32 partition for installations. A proprietary Microsoft-developed filesystem, NTFS can trace its roots back through the Windows NT family lineage starting in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1. The variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001 remains the standard used by most Windows systems today. With ReactOS’s stated goal of reaching binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, being confined to FAT32 partitions was a practical barrier to clear on the way to reproducing the Windows environment.
However, users looking to hop off the Windows train shouldn’t be grabbing their bags just yet. ReactOS wrote that the new driver still “lacks caching (which causes inferior performance), journaling and security support.” So while the new driver is here, even the most intrepid of OS tinkerers should tread carefully. The ReactOS team warned in its announcement on X that there are still “potentially undiscovered bugs.”

articles.title: Even Realities G2s are my new daily smartglasses; the R1 ring is clutch
articles.text:
I’ve really been on a smart glasses kick, but of the many I’ve tried out, the Even Realities’ Even G2 is among the best. These camera-less smart glasses keep privacy in mind and offer two displays on each lens. The Even G2 paired with the R1 smart ring makes for a pair that I really enjoy, as it keeps my interactions with the smart glasses very discreet. Though the pair aren’t without some faults, the Even G2 and R1 ring are honestly great.
One Ring
The Even G2s look stylish; you can barely tell there’s anything different about them. The temple tips by your ear are a bit thicker than usual, but that’s pretty much the only indicator they might be smart glasses. The glasses are slim and light, weighing only 36g; you’d forget they’re smart glasses if not for the displays. Seriously, I’ve had people be shocked to know I’m wearing smart glasses. And if these had cameras, maybe that’d be a problem, but they don’t, so no issue here.
I could see the Even R1 smart ring being too thick for some women. It’s a pretty thick ring, but I didn’t mind it at all. There’s a flat part of the ring with an ‘E,’ and my finger naturally gravitates towards it, playing with the ring all the time. The flat part doesn’t control the ring or anything, but indicates the correct placement of the ring on the charging stand and helps you dive into the R1 a little more. The smart ring is able to navigate your smart glasses with different gestures. Below the E on the ring, you’ll see dots indicating where you’re supposed to touch. The different gestures include a single tap, a double tap, and a double tap that you hold on the second tap, and you’ll swipe up and down.
Discreet
The screens on the lenses aren’t very evident; people can’t ever tell I’m reading my HUD. Well, until they realize I’m not making eye contact because I’m reading a lengthy text message — or a literal book. Often, people can’t even tell I’m wearing smart glasses; even other journalists and creators in tech who have used the glasses themselves take a moment or two to realize I’m wearing the G2 glasses. Even I don’t always clock when people are wearing the glasses; like in this picture of George Clooney at the Venice International Film Festival, it took me a moment to realize that the star was wearing the smart glasses.
The Even Realities G2 two panels can do a variety of things. Whenever I put on my smart glasses in the morning, I’m greeted by my dashboard that offers the time, date, and the battery percentage of the smart ring and glasses in the top left corner. The bottom left corner shows the temperature, sunset, and the forecast for the following day. The right side shows my calendar for the day, but by swiping on the ring or the temple tips, I can see upcoming tasks and my steps, calories, sleep score, heart rate (beats per minute), and my O2 — based on data provided by the smart ring. Of course, this is all customizable and based on what you want to see. Other widgets include the news, stocks and quick notes.
A double tap — one short, one long — opens a menu which shows notifications, conversate, teleprompter, translate, Even AI, photos and books. This menu can also be customized, and you can add a lot more plugins as well, including one for navigation, one to play chess, and even add the Bible. Books and Photos weren’t there by default either; I added them.
Conversate
While checking your notifications is always useful, my favourite feature is ‘Conversate.’ Conversate writes down all the words being said, kind of like subtitles. I always feel like I have difficulty hearing people around me, so giving everyone subtitles helps. And Conversate offers insight into what’s being said; for instance, the first time I used the feature, I had a family member in the hospital and while Conversate offered subtitles, when I asked my cousin why she needed her sodium up before surgery, a pop-up indicator appeared. To my surprise, the indicator explained why someone would need more sodium in their blood before surgery. It offers a lot of details, pretty much about anything anyone is talking about. I had someone sort of give me an astronomy lesson, and it was able to correct some of the information he was talking about — a single year on Venus is 29.5 Earth years, not 33 years — and even while at church, when the preacher said a bible scripture, the smart glasses showed the verses.
Other cool features include a teleprompter; I haven’t needed to use it yet, but I’ve tried it out, and I can see how it’s very helpful, especially if I’m saying lines in front of the camera. And I had my partner speak with me in Spanish, and I could understand clearly what he was saying. Even Realities’ Even AI can answer any and every question; you can even set it for continuous listening, so it can listen for follow-up questions. You can summon the AI with the phrase “Hey Even,” and it works in English and French, among other languages.
Some of the downsides
The Even Realities G2s aren’t perfect, though. Sometimes, I find the R1 ring a little finicky, and it takes a few swipes before it registers. I’ve had issues with the ring connecting a couple of times, but it’s not a constant problem. Randomly, I’ve seen “ring disconnected”; check it, and it’s already connected again.
This one is a me-thing, but even though the G2s are IP65 water-resistant, I’m always worried about the smart glasses getting wet in the rain or if I’m going to sweat too much and damage them. Another me-thing, but I needed to remind myself to silence my smart glasses before playing badminton because I got a shuttlecock to the forehead when I looked up, saw my dashboard and couldn’t see the birdie anymore.
And unfortunately, the price tag is a bit of a con. The Even Realities G2s are US$599 (C$846) and the R1 smart ring is US$249 (C$352), and this is before including your prescription lenses.

articles.title: Intel "Nova Lake" Xeon E Series Carries Only P-Core or E-Core SKUs, No Hybrid Configurations
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
Intel "Nova Lake" Xeon E Series Carries Only P-Core or E-Core SKUs, No Hybrid Configurations
Intel is preparing to launch its upcoming "Nova Lake" processors in multiple versions, and the latest leaks highlight a particularly interesting Xeon E lineup. According to well-known leaker Jaykihn, Intel will be releasing its Xeon E-series based on "Nova Lake" silicon in two versions: big P-Core only or efficiency E-Core only SKUs. Reportedly, the P-Core only lineup will include five configurations with 4, 6, 8, 12, and 16 P-Cores. Meanwhile, the E-Core lineup will be slightly smaller, featuring four SKUs with 4, 8, 16, and 32 E-Core versions. At the top of the range, Intel Xeon E-series buyers can choose between a 16 P-Core design or a 32 E-Core configuration. There will be no hybrid SKUs with both P-Cores and E-Cores, as those will be reserved for the regular "Nova Lake-S" desktop processors.
Intel's new Xeon E designs will be powered by the W980 chipset platform. Motherboards with the W980 chipset will support native DDR5 memory with ECC, up to 48 PCIe lanes, including 12 PCIe 5.0 lanes directly from the chipset alongside 12 PCIe 4.0 lanes, and Intel vPro technology, along with numerous other optimizations typical of workstation chipsets. The DMI chipset bus bandwidth is set to 128 Gbps per direction, thanks to the implementation of DMI 5.0 x4, which is another great platform addition. It also offers two 40 Gbps USB4 or Thunderbolt 4 ports from the CPU. The PCI-Express 5.0 x16 PEG slot from the processor can be segmented into x8/x8 or other combinations using lane switches. Both CPU-attached M.2 NVMe slots can be configured as Gen 5.Finally, we have no information about pricing, launch dates, or any specifics, as Intel hasn't confirmed any details or a possible Xeon E update. Since the regular "Nova Lake-S" designs are expected to arrive first in the first quarter of 2027, we can anticipate these other configurations to follow closely after partners complete their motherboard designs and system integrators prepare the workstation designs that will use this platform.

articles.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Tolan, the AI companion designed to help people manage their daily lives, navigate relationships and emotions, and accomplish their goals, has just expanded its runway with another $30 million in capital.
The startup’s investors in the latest round include Union Square Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Homebrew, doubling the total amount it has raised to date and pushing its valuation beyond the previous $120 million, according to a new report by Upstarts Media. (The startup didn’t disclose its new valuation, but PitchBook estimates it at more than $268 million, with “medium confidence.”)
Users engage with Tolan’s app through a cartoonish character that’s meant to offer support and help them get through their to-dos.
Tolan generates revenue from its tiered memberships, which are required for full access to all features. The company told Upstarts Media its annual recurring revenue is now in the “double-digit millions.”
The startup is one of the few AI companions that have found some traction, as it claims to have more than 250,000 active users who have had more than 70 million conversations over the past year. Around 70% of its users are women, and 40% are parents, Tolan’s team told the news outlet. (Anecdotally, the app is said to appeal in particular to neurodivergent people, who may benefit from additional support, whether that’s emotional support or help with organizing tasks.)
Compared with other companions, Tolan seems to have found a balance between being helpful without being perceived as too weird. Compare that with the public shaming that Friend’s pendant-based AI companion faced; users dubbed Friend “very cringe,” The New York Times called it “hated,” and Wired said it “has no soul.”
Meanwhile, another former top contender in the space, Character.AI, recently filed for bankruptcy after its founder’s return to Google. (Its remaining staff is transitioning to Disney, which bought some of its assets.)
However, Tolan could end up facing increased competition from the more recent crop of AI agents, which help users plan, organize, and accomplish their tasks and goals, not just talk their way through them. For instance, Meta gave its AI agent Muse a cute avatar for its users to talk to, which it also plans to release as a hardware product in the future.
The startup also has to navigate the risks of offering AI-powered emotional support, given that multiple lawsuits have been filed against general-purpose AI app makers alleging that chatbot interactions contributed to users’ suicides.

articles.title: You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
articles.text:
You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
Less flashing means less worrying, but a modified VBIOS may still brick a GPU in other ways.
Panchovix on GitHub recently released a VBIOS configurator for RTX 30-to 50-series cards that doesn’t require flashing. The loader provides a UI for easy configuration and lowers the risk of bricking your GPU by avoiding a risky flash process, and it's available for Linux, too.
Software like MSI Afterburner or ASUS GPU Tweak is often the go-to tool for quickly changing your graphics card’s settings; however, those tools have hard limits to how much you can push the graphics card. If you want to tweak your GPU beyond the firmware’s set limits, you can change it by tweaking the parameters in the VBIOS. Configuring VBIOS is similar to changing BIOS settings in the BOOT menu. With the VBIOS loader, you can change settings beyond the firmware’s hard limits.
The way it works is by storing the modified VBIOS image in the GPU’s register key; as the Nvidia driver looks for a VBIOS override on startup, it finds the VBIOS image and restarts, applying the override settings. The flash chip on the graphics card is not overwritten, reducing the risk of bricking your GPU. However, this does not protect the card from any extreme settings that could destroy electrical components; it merely provides a safer and more convenient way to adjust and apply VBIOS settings, including a way to roll back to the default VBIOS settings should you face any instability.
Bricking a flash chip isn’t as catastrophic as it seems, however. As long as you have a backed-up version of the VBIOS, you can easily buy an SPI flash chip programmer or even build your own using a cheap Raspberry Pi Pico and its many clones; sometimes programming the flash chip may not even require desoldering. Programming a flash chip is very tedious and inconvenient, though, which is why avoiding the risk of a botched flash process altogether is so appealing.
Unless you’re familiar with power delivery, voltage tables, and the patience required to test for hours, we wouldn’t recommend jumping into this unless you’re prepared to risk your GPU. However, you can still safely take advantage of this software by tweaking the fan curves and other settings you’ve applied and tested in software like MSI Afterburner if, for some reason, the startup settings don’t stick. This software will give your GPU new default settings that override at every startup, so long as Nvidia doesn’t remove the registry key that allows the VBIOS override.
