articles.title: TeamGroup's 4TB SSD is $554 less than Samsung 990 Pro
articles.text:
This is the cheapest 4TB SSD you can buy — Team Group T-Force G50 EVO Gen4 SSD costs $370 or $0.09 per GB, $554 less than Samsung 990 Pro
I can't find a 4TB SSD cheaper than this right now
Could this be the best price per GB for a PCIe SSD this year so far?
The Teamgroup T-Force G50 EVO is the cheapest 4TB SSD you can buy right now. Newegg sells it for $369.99 after using promo code SSF74294 and the current gift card offer (buy $200, get $230). That’s an extraordinary $126 discount off its sticker price. I cannot stress enough how good of a deal that is!
At just over $0.09 per TB, it is significantly cheaper than the Acer FA200 I found a fortnight ago. The G50 Evo is easily the cheapest PCIe SSD of the year so far per TB. Nothing comes remotely close to it but it is sadly the odd one out, an anomaly in a sea of expensive SSDs especially with a 4TB capacity.
This 4TB SSD features a PCIe Gen 4 M.2 2280 interface, with read speeds up to 5,000MB/s. For the full discount, pick up two Newegg gift cards which gives you a bonus $30, then use code SSF74294.
Why I recommend this deal
I am guilty of recommending the Acer FA200 in a previous deal. You can always send it back and get this one. At $92 per TB, it is $110 cheaper than Acer’s model, which is a lot (although the FA200 is significantly faster) and far cheaper than anything I saw during Amazon October Prime Day.
The T-Force G50 Evo is an entry level PCIe 4.0 SSD with read/write speeds of 5000 MBps and 4700 MBps, which is towards the slower end of the spectrum but fast enough for everyday usage. Team Group says that the drive has a 1.5 million hour MTBF (mean time before failure), a 1.200 TBW endurance and a three-year warranty, which again is towards the lower part of the market.
Other things worth mentioning are the graphene heat spreader (which is basically a sticker in the packaging) and the lack of onboard DRAM. I haven’t found any reviews of the G50 EVO online yet.
More 4TB SSDs
The closest competitor to the FA200 in terms of price, but the speeds can't match it, reaching up to 5,500 MB/s.
Still one of the best internal SSDs we've ever tested, but the price is astronomically high right now, especially compared to the Acer FA200.
This deal is from Biwin, who manufacturer's the Acer SSD. It's for the 2TB model, so you could plug two in a RAID-0 to match the FA200's capacity.

articles.title: Wettlauf zum Mars: Warum Japan den USA und China über den Mond Phobos zuvorkommen könnte
articles.text:
Wettlauf zum Roten Planeten: Wie Japan auf dem Marsmond Phobos nach Marsgestein sucht
Wie die japanische Raumfahrtbehörde JAXA mit Sitz in Chōfu bei Tokio mitteilt, soll die Raumsonde „Martian Moons Exploration“ (MMX) am 19. Oktober 2026 um 21:41 Uhr mitteleuropäischer Sommerzeit (20. Oktober, 04:41 Uhr japanischer Ortszeit) vom Raumfahrtzentrum Tanegashima auf der gleichnamigen südjapanischen Insel starten. An Bord einer Trägerrakete vom Typ H3 bricht das aus drei Modulen bestehende Raumfahrzeug zu einer fünfjährigen Reise auf, um erstmals Bodenproben vom Marsmond Phobos zur Erde zu bringen.
Damit könnte Japan im Wettlauf um die ersten zurückgeführten Proben aus dem Marssystem an den USA und China vorbeiziehen. Wie der kanadische Sender CTV News unter Verweis auf die Nachrichtenagentur AFP meldet, hat die US-Regierung ihr eigenes Rückführprogramm Anfang 2026 aus Kostengründen gestrichen, während China den Start seiner Mission Tianwen-3 erst für 2028 anpeilt.
Allerdings steht das Vorhaben unter Vorbehalt, denn ursprünglich sollte die Sonde schon im Herbst 2024 abheben, verpasste dieses nur alle 26 Monate geöffnete Startfenster zum Mars jedoch wegen Verzögerungen nach dem gescheiterten Erstflug des Raketentyps H3 im März 2023. Zwar brachte die neue Trägerrakete in der Zwischenzeit mehrere Satelliten in eine Erdumlaufbahn, doch im Dezember 2025 fiel bei einer dieser anderen Missionen erneut ein Triebwerk vorzeitig aus.
Marsmond Phobos als Abkürzung für Gesteinsproben vom Roten Planeten
Auf der Marsoberfläche sammelt der US-Rover Perseverance zwar schon seit seiner Landung im Februar 2021 Gesteinskerne in Metallröhrchen. Ein Rücktransport von dort erfordert wegen der hohen Schwerkraft des Planeten jedoch eine eigene Aufstiegsrakete, weshalb Japan stattdessen den 27 Kilometer breiten Mond Phobos ansteuert.
Phobos umkreist den Mars dreimal täglich in einer Entfernung von rund 6.000 Kilometern. Durch diese geringe Distanz fängt der Mond regelmäßig sogenanntes Auswurfmaterial ein. Das sind Gesteinstrümmer, die bei Asteroideneinschlägen von der Marsoberfläche ins All geschleudert wurden. Wie The Guardian unter Berufung auf die Nachrichtenagentur Associated Press berichtet, soll dieses Material nach Schätzungen der JAXA etwa 0,1 Prozent der oberen Bodenschicht auf Phobos ausmachen.
Mit den restlichen 99,9 Prozent der Proben wollen die Wissenschaftler:innen klären, ob die beiden Marsmonde Phobos und Deimos eingefangene Asteroiden sind oder sich nach einer früheren Großkollision aus Marstrümmern geformt haben. „Durch die Analyse von Bodenproben können wir nahezu sicher zu einer Schlussfolgerung gelangen“, wird der wissenschaftliche Missionsleiter Kiyoshi Kuramoto von der japanischen Universität Hokkaido in Sapporo im Bericht des Guardian zitiert.
Trotz dieses Ansatzes hat die Methode aus geologischer Sicht eine Kehrseite, da die Sonde insgesamt nur mindestens zehn Gramm des lockeren Oberflächengesteins (Regolith) einsammeln soll. Auf den Mars selbst entfielen damit rechnerisch lediglich rund zehn Milligramm Staub, die sich im Gegensatz zu einer direkten Bohrung auf dem Planeten keiner bestimmten Region zuordnen lassen.
Quasi-Satelliten-Orbit und zwei Verfahren für die Probenentnahme
Nach einer Flugstrecke von 500 bis 600 Millionen Kilometern soll die Raumsonde im August 2027 den Mars erreichen und im September 2027 in einen sogenannten Quasi-Satelliten-Orbit einschwenken. Weil die Anziehungskraft des kleinen Mondes für eine stabile Umlaufbahn kaum ausreicht, umrundet die Sonde dabei weiterhin den Mars, bleibt durch ihre Flugbahn aber dauerhaft in der Nähe von Phobos.
Für die im Jahr 2030 geplanten zwei Landungen setzt die Mission auf zwei unterschiedliche Sammelverfahren, um sowohl Material von der Oberfläche als auch aus zwei Zentimetern Tiefe zu gewinnen. Während ein japanischer Bohrarm Untergrundproben entnimmt, nutzt ein zweites System der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa Druckgas, um Staub aufzuwirbeln und in einen Behälter zu leiten.
Deutscher Rover Idefix und das Risiko der geringen Schwerkraft
Vor der Landung der Hauptsonde setzt das Mutterschiff Anfang 2029 aus etwa 40 Metern Höhe zunächst den 25 Kilogramm schweren Erkundungsrover Idefix im freien Fall ab. Wie die Europäische Weltraumorganisation ESA erläutert, erreicht die Schwerkraft auf Phobos nur ein Zweitausendstel des irdischen Werts, sodass das Gefährt dort effektiv nur noch 15 Gramm auf die Waage bringt.
Diese sogenannten Milligravitationsbedingungen stellen ein erhebliches Missionsrisiko dar, weil Landegeräte beim Aufsetzen unkontrolliert zurück ins All prallen können und bisherige Landeversuche auf Phobos – zuletzt die russische Mission Phobos-Grunt im Jahr 2011 – gescheitert sind. Um auf dem unebenen Gelände nicht liegenzubleiben, erhielt der vom Deutschen Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt DLR und der französischen Raumfahrtagentur CNES gebaute Rover vier einzeln steuerbare Beine, mit denen er sich nach dem Aufprall selbstständig aufrichten und hundert Tage lang die Bodenfestigkeit prüfen soll.
Zur Untersuchung des Gesteins vor Ort nutzt Idefix unter anderem ein sogenanntes Raman-Spektrometer, das die Oberfläche mit gebündeltem Licht bestrahlt und anhand der reflektierten Wellenlängen die mineralogische Zusammensetzung misst. Das darin verbaute, 50 Gramm schwere Lasermodul wurde vom Fraunhofer-Institut für Angewandte Optik und Feinmechanik (IOF) im thüringischen Jena entwickelt. Ursprünglich war dieses Bauteil für die europäisch-russische Mission Exomars vorgesehen, gelangte nach dem Abbruch der Kooperation mit Russland im Jahr 2022 jedoch über das spanische Institut für Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik (INTA) in das japanische Projekt.
Verläuft die anschließende Probenentnahme durch die Hauptsonde ohne Zwischenfälle, wirft deren Rückkehrmodul die hitzegeschützte Kapsel nach einem Vorbeiflug am Nachbarmond Deimos im Jahr 2031 über Australien ab. Bis dahin misst ein Strahlenmonitor an Bord der Sonde zudem kontinuierlich die kosmische Strahlung, damit Forscher:innen beurteilen können, ob Phobos künftig als Stützpunkt für Astronaut:innen taugt oder ob die Strahlenbelastung im Marssystem dem entgegensteht.

articles.title: From implementation to innovation: The next step in your Gemini Enterprise journey
articles.text:
Google Cloud
View Brand Publisher
From implementation to innovation: The next step in your Gemini Enterprise journey
Join Google Cloud's AI and ML experts for the second edition of the Gemini Enterprise series, covering app connectivity, identity management, and enterprise-grade security.
How do you move from a basic Gemini Enterprise setup to a live, identity-aware, data-protected AI platform?
That is the question at the center of Google Cloud's next webinar, in partnership with YourStory. On October 23, Google Cloud's AI and ML experts return for the second edition of the Gemini Enterprise series, titled ‘Gemini Enterprise: Integrate, secure, and scale your AI strategy’.
Where the first series focused on initial setup, this session moves into the technical connectivity that determines whether a Gemini Enterprise deployment actually works inside an organization's existing ecosystem. Attendees will get a practical look at bridging Gemini Enterprise with the tools already in use, while maintaining the security and compliance standards enterprises cannot afford to skip.
Whether the challenge is navigating complex compliance requirements or automating workflows across multiple apps, the session is built to provide a clear roadmap for the next stage of the AI journey.
What attendees will learn
The session will open with a look at Workspace synergy, walking through how different Gemini Enterprise editions integrate with an organization's existing productivity suite to unlock more value from tools already in place.
From there, the focus will shift to app connectivity. Attendees will see how to securely link Gmail, Calendar, and Drive, allowing Gemini to reason over internal data and automate workflows that span multiple applications, rather than working in isolation.
The webinar will also cover identity and access, including a walkthrough of Workforce Identity Federation using providers like Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, to make identity management seamless across an enterprise's existing infrastructure.
Finally, the session aims to address security in depth, covering Safety Filters, AI Defense policies, and Model Armor, the tools organizations need to defend against prompt injection and protect personally identifiable information as AI usage scales.
Meet the speakers
The session aims to bring together specialists across connectivity, identity, and security.
Ria Patel, Platform Customer Engineer for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts at Google Cloud, opens with a walkthrough on connecting Google Calendar to Gemini Enterprise.
Janani Pandurangan, also a Platform Customer Engineer for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts, follows with a session on connecting Gemini Enterprise to Gmail.
Jared Houston, Security Customer Engineer at Google Cloud, covers connecting Google Drive to Gemini Enterprise.
Derian Tungka and Graciella Liander, both Platform Customer Engineers for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts, co-lead a deep dive into third-party identity provider integration, offering step-by-step guidance on Workforce Identity Federation using Okta or Microsoft Entra ID.
Methasit (Most) Tuwawit, Platform Customer Engineer for SMB, Scaled, and Specialist accounts, leads a session on securing a Gemini Enterprise application.
Eva Gao, Security Customer Engineer at Google Cloud, closes the technical program with a session on Model Armor, covering prompt injection and data leakage prevention through Safety Filters and AI Defense policies.
Why this matters
For organizations past the initial pilot stage, the risks shift. It is no longer just about getting Gemini Enterprise running, but about making sure it connects securely to the systems that hold sensitive data, respects existing identity infrastructure, and holds up against the kinds of attacks that come with wider AI adoption, such as prompt injection and data leakage.
This webinar is built for that stage. Rather than a high-level overview, it offers specific, technical guidance from the engineers who work on these integrations directly, covering the connectivity and security groundwork that determines whether an AI deployment can scale safely across an organization.
Register now to secure your spot and learn how to take your Gemini Enterprise deployment from basic setup to a fully integrated, secure, enterprise-ready platform.

articles.title: Onafriq negotiated Baxi’s sale months before its closure
articles.text:
When Onafriq announced it was shutting down Baxi, its Nigerian agent banking business, on October 16, it marked the end of a five-year expansion effort that began when the company acquired one of Nigeria’s largest independent agent banking networks. But months before announcing the closure, the pan-African payments company had been negotiating a sale of Baxi.
The proposed sale, which covered the entire agency banking operation active only in Nigeria, remained unresolved as of July, according to Onafriq’s audited financial statements filed in the United Kingdom.
In the statement announcing Baxi’s closure, the company cited inflation, naira depreciation, rising operating costs, shrinking margins, and growth in alternative payment methods such as account-to-account (A2A) transfers, which weakened offline payments. It said the economics of running an offline agent network had become unsustainable.
Onafriq’s statement did not mention the prospective buyer or the status of the negotiations. As of July 29, when the accounts were approved, negotiations were still ongoing, and Onafriq said it could not reliably estimate the structure, timing, or financial impact of a sale.
“During 2026, Onafrıq Nigeria Payments Limited entered into a non-binding memorandum of terms with a purchaser in respect of the proposed divestment of the agency business,” the company said in the financial statements. “The proposed transaction contemplates the sale of 100% of the agency business and related operations, subject to the terms and conditions to be agreed between the parties in a definitive asset purchase agreement.”
By then, the business had already suffered a sharp financial decline. Onafriq’s agency services revenue fell 56% to $13.4 million in 2024, from $30.4 million the previous year. The company also wrote off the remaining $4.56 million in goodwill tied to its Nigerian payments business, reflecting a decline in the value it expected to recover from the investment.
The attempted sale reversed the strategy that brought Onafriq into Nigeria. The company had acquired Baxi to connect a vast network of cash-based agents to its pan-African payments infrastructure.
Five years later, it was looking for an acquirer to take over that network. By October, it was telling Baxi’s agents—over 460,000 as of 2025—to move their funds elsewhere.
An unfinished sale
Baxi’s declining revenue was only part of its financial troubles. Although Onafriq cut agency services costs from $17 million in 2023 to $8.7 million in 2024, gross profit fell even faster, declining by 65% from $13.4 million to $4.7 million, according to its financial report.
The group’s agency business generated about $35 in gross profit for every $100 in revenue in 2024, down from $44 the previous year. That left considerably less money to cover salaries, technology, and other operating expenses.
By the time Onafriq began negotiating a sale in 2026, its agency services generated substantially less gross profit than they did two years earlier. The business also operated company-owned point-of-sale (PoS) terminals and provided short-term credit to agents whose wallet balances were running low.
According to Onafriq, agents typically had one to seven days to repay the loans, with interest rates ranging from 2.5% to 7% for each loan. The company funded the credit from its own resources, assessed agents’ creditworthiness, and collected repayments and managed defaults.
In July 2026, Onafriq said its Nigerian subsidiary, Onafriq Nigeria Payments Limited, owed ₦13.8 billion ($10.4 million) to Zenith Bank, a Nigerian tier-1 lender, and ₦6.1 billion ($4.6 million) to Stanbic IBTC Bank, a mid-tier bank, in outstanding overdrafts, bringing the total to ₦19.9 billion ($15 million), its filings showed.
“We entered Nigeria with conviction and commitment, but did not achieve the outcome we set out for,” Dare Okoudjou, Onafriq’s founder and chief executive officer, said in the statement announcing Baxi’s shutdown in Nigeria.
The economics behind Baxi’s retreat
Onafriq had already begun writing down the value of its Nigerian payments business before Baxi’s shutdown. It wrote off $2.4 million in goodwill in 2023 and the remaining $4.56 million in 2024, according to its filings.
Goodwill is the extra value recorded when a company buys a business, beyond the value of its identifiable net assets. The write-offs meant Onafriq no longer expected the business’s future earnings to justify that extra value.
However, other parts of Onafriq’s group-wide business were performing better. Revenue from money transfer fees grew by 20% to $43.9 million in 2024. The group’s card fee revenue also jumped 22%.
The contrasting performance helps explain why Onafriq retained its payments network and card-issuing services while closing Baxi. Yet, Nigeria’s wider PoS market presented a more complicated picture.
According to the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), the country’s payments switch, PoS transactions’ value rose 79% to ₦18.78 trillion ($14.1 billion) in the first quarter of 2026. The number of deployed PoS terminals had more than doubled, from 2.45 million at the end of 2023 to 5.56 million at the end of 2024.
But the growth in transaction value concealed a much slower increase in the number of payments. In 2024, NIBSS data showed PoS transaction volumes rose by just 8%, from 1.4 billion to 1.5 billion, even as deployed terminals increased by 127%.
The number of terminals was expanding much faster than the transactions passing through them. For agent banking providers, more devices in the market meant greater competition for customers, without a corresponding increase in the number of transactions from which they could earn commissions.
Nigeria added PoS machines faster than transactions
Between 2023 and 2024, deployed PoS terminals more than doubled, but transaction volumes barely grew. Explore what that meant for the number of transactions per terminal, as Onafriq’s Baxi business struggled.
In 2024, Nigeria recorded roughly 270 annual PoS transactions for every terminal deployed at year-end, compared with about 571 in 2023.
Meanwhile, Baxi’s economics were deteriorating
Onafriq’s reported agency services figures show what happened to the business as Nigeria’s wider PoS network expanded. These are group agency services figures, not a measure of transactions per Baxi agent.
Competition was also coming from much larger operators. Moniepoint, one of Baxi's rivals, already had over 800,000 PoS terminals in Nigeria at the end of 2024. By 2026, the number had grown to over one million active PoS terminals in the country.
The Nigerian fintech unicorn said it served over six million businesses in 2025, underscoring the scale of the networks Baxi was competing against, which made its business hard to justify.
From expansion to exit
Onafriq entered Nigeria's agent banking market in October 2021, when the company, then known as MFS Africa, announced its acquisition of Capricorn Digital Limited, the company behind Baxi. The deal was completed in March 2022 after receiving the Central Bank of Nigeria's (CBN) approval.
At the time, Baxi had more than 90,000 agents providing cash withdrawals, transfers, and bill payments. The network processed over $1.6 billion in transactions in 2021, making it one of Nigeria's largest independent agent banking networks.
The acquisition was intended to connect Baxi's physical distribution network to MFS Africa's cross-border payments infrastructure. In June 2022, the company also secured debt financing from Stanbic IBTC Bank to support Baxi's expansion.
Five years later, Onafriq is dismantling that strategy. Following the shutdown, it said it had transferred Baxi's agents to another principal bank and given them 30 days to move their funds to a principal bank of their choice.
Onafriq will continue operating in Nigeria through its payments network and card-issuing services, but without the agent banking business it acquired to establish a foothold in the country's offline payments market.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Points forts
- Dalle Amoled lumineuse et bien calibrée.
- Exynos 2600 convaincant au quotidien.
- Volet photo complet.
- Autonomie exemplaire.
Points faibles
- Formule qui peine à se renouveler.
- Bloc photo proéminent.
Le Samsung Galaxy S26+ ne cherche pas à réinventer la roue, mais il coche toutes les cases du très bon smartphone premium. Son écran est excellent, ses performances tiennent largement la route, son interface reste aussi complète que durable, et l’autonomie progresse malgré le retour de la puce Exynos. La partie photo se montre elle aussi convaincante. On regrette en revanche l’absence de véritable innovation, tant sur le plan matériel qu’esthétique. Le bloc photo et la nouvelle puce maison figurent parmi les principales évolutions, ce qui paraît un peu maigre et interroge sur l’intérêt de renouveler la série à ce rythme, année après année. Reste au final un haut de gamme très abouti, agréable au quotidien et sans réel faux pas, peut-être un peu trop sage pour vraiment surprendre.

articles.title: Anthropic creó un fondo de interés público para ayudar a la sociedad mientras crece Claude: destinará el 5% de sus acciones
articles.text:
Anthropic anunció que destinará el 5% de sus acciones a un nuevo fondo de beneficio público, sujeto a la aprobación de sus accionistas. La empresa detrás del asistente conversacional Claude informó que su directorio podrá sumar un 2% adicional de capital por cada aumento del 50% en la valoración de la compañía.
Anthropic es la compañía responsable de Claude, uno de los principales chatbots de inteligencia artificial, que compite de cerca con ChatGPT, de OpenAI, y con Gemini, de Google.
El nuevo vehículo se llama Fondo de Beneficio Público de Anthropic y funcionará como una sociedad de responsabilidad limitada de propiedad exclusiva de la empresa, no como una organización sin fines de lucro tradicional.
Según el comunicado oficial de la compañía, ese formato le da mayor flexibilidad para decidir cómo repartir el dinero, desde donaciones grandes a organizaciones sociales hasta transferencias directas a poblaciones específicas.
Anthropic precisó que ninguna porción del capital asignado al fondo se usará para actividades de cabildeo ni para contribuciones políticas, ni en Estados Unidos ni en otros países. La compañía adelantó que en los próximos meses dará a conocer más detalles sobre la estructura y el gobierno del fondo, incluidos los umbrales de valoración que podrían ampliar la participación.
El esquema está diseñado de manera que, cuanto más crezca el valor de Anthropic, mayor sea la porción de la empresa dedicada de forma expresa al bien público, según el texto difundido por la compañía.
El dinero y el impacto en el empleo
Entre los usos posibles que mencionó la empresa figura el impacto de la inteligencia artificial en los puestos de trabajo. “La inteligencia artificial podría generar un enorme valor económico, pero también provocar inestabilidad en muchos trabajadores”, advirtió Anthropic en su anuncio.
La compañía ya había destinado USD 200 millones a estudiar y atender ese problema, pero sostuvo que, dado el ritmo del progreso de la IA, podrían hacer falta enfoques más audaces para enfrentarlo. No precisó montos ni plazos para esas eventuales iniciativas adicionales.
Cuando se fundó la empresa, sus cofundadores se habían comprometido a donar el 80% de sus propias tenencias accionarias. Desde entonces, Anthropic también mantiene un programa de igualación de donaciones de capital en el que participa aproximadamente la mitad de su plantilla.
Sumado a este nuevo compromiso, cerca del 20% de las acciones de Anthropic quedará destinado al bien público, sin contar el porcentaje adicional que podría agregarse si la empresa alcanza determinados hitos de valoración, señaló la compañía.
Qué queda dentro de la empresa y qué pasa al fondo
Como sociedad de beneficio público, Anthropic explicó que gran parte de su trabajo en favor de su misión ya ocurre dentro de la propia empresa: investigación en seguridad e interpretabilidad de la inteligencia artificial, estudios biomédicos aplicados y descuentos en el acceso a Claude para organizaciones sin fines de lucro e instituciones científicas.
Esas actividades, según la compañía, combinan un componente de beneficio público con valor comercial, por lo que permanecen dentro de la estructura corporativa.
El nuevo fondo, en cambio, tendrá más escala para iniciativas que no encajan en ese esquema, como donaciones a terceros o transferencias directas de dinero a poblaciones puntuales.
Anthropic comparó la decisión con una práctica habitual en la industria tecnológica: ofrecer compensaciones accionarias crecientes a los ejecutivos a medida que sube el valor de una empresa. “En cambio, estamos dirigiendo ese capital al beneficio público”, señaló la compañía en su comunicado.
La industria de la IA bajo la lupa
El anuncio llega en medio de un clima de desconfianza pública hacia la industria de la inteligencia artificial. El director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, describió ese escenario como “fundamentalmente una crisis de confianza”, según declaraciones recogidas por TechCrunch.
Anthropic opera como una sociedad de beneficio público, una figura legal que obliga a sus directivos a sopesar objetivos sociales además de las ganancias para los inversores. La compañía prepara una salida a bolsa que podría convertirse en una de las mayores de la historia bajo esa estructura, según informó la agencia Reuters.
La empresa, que se presenta como una firma centrada en la seguridad de sus sistemas, ya había expuesto los riesgos de sus propios modelos en el prospecto de esa oferta pública, donde mencionó que la IA podría exhibir comportamientos de “autoconservación”, de acuerdo con una exclusiva previa de la misma agencia.
Anthropic adelantó que en las próximas semanas publicará un informe de beneficio público con el detalle de los avances logrados hasta ahora respecto de su misión declarada, junto con la información pendiente sobre la gobernanza del nuevo fondo.

articles.title: Haier se estrena en el mercado de la aspiración: así es su nueva gama I-Pro Clean Series 5 para plantar cara a Roborock y Dyson
articles.text:
Haier, conocida tradicionalmente por sus grandes electrodomésticos como frigoríficos o lavadoras, da el salto oficial al sector del cuidado del suelo. La firma ha presentado la I-Pro Clean Series 5, una nueva familia de dispositivos de limpieza que llega para competir directamente en un mercado cada vez más disputado.
La gama abarca desde aspiradores escoba inalámbricos hasta fregonas eléctricas y robots autónomos. La principal innovación técnica que introduce la marca es el sistema Double Roller, una tecnología basada en dos rodillos motorizados que giran de forma sincronizada para recoger la suciedad tanto al empujar como al tirar del dispositivo, reduciendo el número de pasadas necesarias.
Aspiradora inalámbrica I-Pro Clean M5
Fregona aspiradora Haier I-Pro Clean Z5
Tres modelos para cubrir todas las necesidades del hogar
La nueva serie de aspiración de Haier está compuesta por tres propuestas bien diferenciadas según el formato de limpieza deseado:
Haier I-Pro Clean M5: aspiradora escoba con autovaciado y gran autonomía
Es la apuesta principal en formato escoba inalámbrica. Combina el sistema Double Roller con un sensor de detección inteligente de suciedad que ajusta la potencia de succión automáticamente para optimizar el rendimiento de la batería. Entre algunas de sus características destacan:
- Autonomía: promete hasta 100 minutos de uso continuo con una sola carga.
- Diseño articulado: incorpora un tubo flexible ideado para limpiar debajo de sofás o camas sin agacharse.
- Estación base inteligente: al terminar, el aspirador se coloca en una base que vacía automáticamente su depósito de polvo para evitar el contacto directo con los residuos.
Aspiradora inalámbrica I-Pro Clean M5
Haier I-Pro Clean Z5: aspiración y fregado simultáneo con secado por aire caliente
Este modelo está pensado para quienes buscan eliminar manchas y fregar el suelo en la misma pasada. Sus características clave son:
- Modos de uso: dispone de un modo de aspiración en seco y tres niveles de limpieza en húmedo que gestionan el agua de forma inteligente según la suciedad detectada.
- Autolimpieza en cinco minutos: tras la limpieza, la base lava los rodillos y los seca mediante agua y aire caliente en solo cinco minutos para prevenir malos olores y humedad acumulada.
Fregona aspiradora Haier I-Pro Clean Z5
Haier I-Pro Clean R5: robot aspirador autónomo impulsado por IA
Esta es la opción totalmente automatizada de la gama. Este robot aspirador cuenta con navegación asistida por cámara e inteligencia artificial para mapear la casa y esquivar obstáculos cotidianos de forma más precisa. Su base de carga no solo recarga la batería, sino que también vacía el depósito de sólidos y lava y seca la mopa.
Disponibilidad y precios
Estos dos dispositivos ya se pueden comprar en la tienda oficial de la marca y tienen los siguientes precios:
- Aspiradora vertical Haier I-Pro Clean M5 desde 259 euros.
- Aspiradora-fregona Haier I-Pro Clean Z5 desde 239 euros.
- El robot aspirador, de momento, no se encuentra en la web de Haier.

articles.title: « C'est de l'argent public qui a été investi » : 3 bus à hydrogène à 1,7 million d’euros vont finir à la casse en France
articles.text:
En 2016, la communauté d’agglomération Castres-Mazamet (Tarn) a acheté trois bus à hydrogène fabriqués par l’entreprise locale Safra. Coût total pour ces trois bus : 1,7 million d’euros, dont plus de 500 000 euros de subventions de l’État. Après avoir été mis en circulation en 2018 et roulé moins de 5 000 km dans le réseau Libellus, ils finiront à la casse.
Trois bus achetés pour 1,7 millions d’euros, une destination : la casse
Autant dire que les trois bus à hydrogène fournis par l’entreprise Safra semblent ne pas avoir été à la hauteur des attentes. Comme le rapporte Franceinfo, Olivier Fabre, maire de Mazamet et président de la communauté d’agglomération Castres-Mazamet, explique : « Les bus n’ont jamais fonctionné. Ils ont très peu roulé. À chaque sortie, ils plantaient et tombaient en panne au bord de la route ». Son constat est sans appel : « C’est de l’argent public qui a été investi. On est victime de la défaillance de cette entreprise qui nous a fait de belles promesses. On s’est fait avoir ! ».
En septembre dernier, lors d’un conseil communautaire, la collectivité à donc voté la mise à la casse de ces trois bus à hydrogène. Une entreprise spécialisée va maintenant se charger de désosser les véhicules et de recycler leurs différents composants. Coût de cette nouvelle opération : 7.500 €, à la charge de la communauté d’agglomération.
Un remboursement impossible et un nouvel investissement dans des bus thermiques
L’agglomération a déposé un recours devant le tribunal administratif de Toulouse pour obtenir le remboursement des 1,7 million d’euros investis pour acquérir les trois bus à hydrogène, sans succès. Pour cause, en février 2025, l’entreprise Safra a été placée en redressement judiciaire. Elle est aujourd’hui officiellement tombée en faillite, mais a été reprise par le groupe chinois Wanrun, fin mai 2026.
Quoi qu’il en soit, la demande de remboursement ne semble pas aboutir, comme l’explique Olivier Fabre : « C’est impossible d’obtenir le remboursement. Personne ne répond ». Il regrette d’ailleurs que « cette histoire ternit l’image des véhicules électriques ». En fin de compte, les trois bus à hydrogène vont être remplacés par des bus thermiques, facturés 1,1 million d’euros, et « beaucoup plus fiables », selon le maire. Au total, il est donc question d’un investissement de près de trois millions d’euros pour trois bus, aux frais du contribuable.

articles.title: Mort de Gordon, combat ultraviolent... Le scénario annulé du Batman de Ben Affleck enfin dévoilé
articles.text:
Décidément, entre les derniers détails d’un projet annulé en provenance de Entertainment Weekly, le 17 octobre, et les problèmes du film avec Robert Pattinson, Batman est au cœur des discussions. Avant de renoncer à la réalisation en janvier 2017, puis au rôle début 2019 au profit de Robert Pattinson, Ben Affleck avait une vision bien précise pour son Batman. Le tournage chaotique de Justice League l’avait épuisé, et il luttait alors contre l’alcoolisme. Il devait en plus écrire, réaliser, produire et interpréter le film : il a fini par jeter l’éponge. Sur le papier, le projet était pourtant très ambitieux.
Deathstroke en mode démolition pour le Batman de Ben Affleck
Selon Joe Manganiello, qui devait renfiler l’armure de Deathstroke après ses brèves apparitions dans Justice League (2017) puis dans la version Snyder Cut (2021), Ben Affleck envisageait son film comme une version super-héroïque de The Game, le thriller paranoïaque de David Fincher sorti en 1997. Convaincu que le Chevalier Noir était responsable de la mort de son fils, Slade Wilson se lançait dans une vendetta sanglante visant à démanteler méthodiquement la vie de Bruce Wayne.
Le plan de Deathstroke prévoyait le meurtre du commissaire Gordon (J.K. Simmons), la prise d’otage d’Alfred (Jeremy Irons) avec une grosse dose de violence et une intrusion dans la Batcave. Au milieu du film, un affrontement voyait Deathstroke manquer de tuer Batman et Batgirl, avant que les deux héros ne s’échappent à bord d’un train aérien.
Un combat final tiré d’Arkham Asylum et un Ben Affleck sur tous les fronts
Le film devait se conclure par un duel en tête-à-tête dans les rues de Gotham. Pour cette séquence, Ben Affleck comptait s’inspirer d’une cinématique en images de synthèse du jeu vidéo Batman: Arkham Asylum (2009), réalisée par Tim Miller, futur réalisateur de Deadpool.
Ce cumul des rôles inquiétait Joe Manganiello. Il raconte avoir demandé à Ben Affleck si une seule personne pouvait vraiment porter autant de casquettes sur un projet de cette taille : « Je lui ai demandé s’il y avait un autre exemple de cette taille où une seule personne portait toutes ces casquettes. Mel Gibson avec Braveheart, peut-être ? Et encore, c’était loin d’être aussi gros. Ben m’a juste répondu : ‘Ouais, je sais… Mais t’inquiète pas, t’es entre de bonnes mains‘. »
Les détails donnés par Joe Manganiello plairont aux nostalgiques du style sombre de Zack Snyder. Ben Affleck a pourtant expliqué lui-même pourquoi il avait bien fait de renoncer. En 2020, il a raconté au New York Times avoir montré le scénario à quelqu’un, qui lui a répondu : « Je pense que le scénario est bon. Je pense aussi que tu vas boire jusqu’à en mourir si tu revis ce que tu viens de vivre. »

articles.title: Coupez Internet, gardez l'essentiel : ce logiciel gratuit fait presque tout sans connexion
articles.text:
Une encyclopédie, un assistant IA, des cartes et des outils personnels réunis sur un ordinateur, sans connexion permanente ni compte utilisateur. Avec sa nouvelle version 2.0, Offlined défend une autre manière d'utiliser l'informatique, loin de la dépendance aux services cloud.
Difficile aujourd'hui de se passer d'Internet, tant les services en ligne occupent une place centrale dans nos usages numériques. Même les assistants IA, devenus des outils du quotidien pour certains, reposent le plus souvent sur des serveurs distants. Avec Offlined, deux développeurs, Álvaro Cuadrado Chulvi et Eric Uguet, proposent de prendre le problème à l'envers : pourquoi ne pas conserver nos connaissances, nos outils et nos données directement sur notre ordinateur ?
Disponible sur Windows 10 et 11, leur logiciel vient de franchir une nouvelle étape avec sa version 2.0, lancée mi-octobre et déjà suivie de plusieurs correctifs, dont la version 2.0.2 du 18 octobre. Son ambition est de constituer un environnement numérique autonome, utilisable sans aucune connexion à Internet. 
Wikipédia, des cartes et une IA pour apprendre sans connexion
Le cœur d'Offlined repose sur une bibliothèque de connaissances consultable localement. Wikipédia, mais aussi Wiktionary, Wikivoyage, Wikiquote et WikiMed peuvent être téléchargés dans différentes langues, dont le français. Le logiciel s'appuie sur les archives ZIM, dont Kiwix se sert aussi pour rendre ces contenus accessibles sans connexion.
Offlined intègre un assistant IA reposant sur llama.cpp, capable de répondre à des questions en s'appuyant sur les ressources téléchargées et de citer les articles utilisés. Autre nouveauté de la version 2.0.1 : la possibilité de connecter un serveur IA local déjà installé, notamment avec Ollama, LM Studio ou LocalAI. Le modèle peut ainsi fonctionner sur une autre machine du réseau domestique, par exemple un PC plus puissant, tout en conservant les échanges en local.
Le logiciel propose aussi Michael Encartha, un assistant pédagogique dont le nom rappelle celui de l'ancienne encyclopédie Encarta. Il peut expliquer un article, générer des quiz ou interroger l'utilisateur pour vérifier ses connaissances. Une approche intéressante pour transformer une simple consultation documentaire en véritable séance d'apprentissage, même si la pertinence des explications produites par l'IA reste à vérifier.
L'environnement comprend enfin des cartes géographiques, une carte du ciel et plusieurs outils éducatifs. Autant de ressources que l'utilisateur peut préparer à l'avance pour les consulter ensuite sans réseau.
Un espace personnel portable, mais pas sans contraintes
Au-delà de la recherche documentaire, Offlined entend devenir un véritable espace personnel. Il rassemble un calendrier, des contacts, des outils de prise de notes, une bibliothèque multimédia et un coffre chiffré pour conserver des informations sensibles. Il permet aussi de récupérer des données provenant d'autres services, notamment des courriels au format MBOX ou PST, des contacts VCF et des calendriers ICS. Depuis la version 2.0.1, plusieurs membres d'un foyer peuvent utiliser des profils distincts pour conserver leurs propres informations et conversations avec l'IA.
L'un de ses principaux atouts est son fonctionnement portable. Le programme peut être lancé depuis un SSD externe ou une clé USB, sans installation Windows traditionnelle. Il faut toutefois prévoir de la place : les développeurs évoquent environ 12 Go pour le modèle IA gpt-oss proposé, tandis qu'une édition de Wikipédia avec images peut peser de 20 à 80 Go selon la langue. Les cartes du monde entier représentent, à elles seules, environ 120 Go. Heureusement, chacun reste libre de télécharger uniquement les ressources qui l'intéressent.
Côté matériel, Offlined demande au minimum 8 Go de RAM, mais 16 Go sont recommandés pour profiter plus confortablement de l'IA locale. Les performances dépendent naturellement du processeur et du modèle choisi ; une carte graphique dédiée n'est cependant pas obligatoire.
Quelques réserves méritent enfin d'être soulignées. Offlined est gratuit pour un usage personnel ou éducatif, mais n'est pas un logiciel open source au sens strict : son code est consultable sur GitHub, tandis que sa licence soumet notamment les modifications et les utilisations commerciales à l'autorisation des auteurs. Le programme Windows n'est pas non plus signé numériquement, ce qui peut déclencher une alerte Microsoft SmartScreen. Pour une première découverte, mieux vaut privilégier une machine virtuelle ou Windows Sandbox, sans y importer immédiatement de données personnelles, plutôt que désactiver les protections du système.
Offlined reste un projet jeune, dont la fiabilité et les performances demandent encore à être éprouvées. Mais son approche mérite l'attention. À l'heure où nos logiciels, nos documents et nos assistants IA dépendent toujours davantage de services distants, il rappelle qu'une partie de notre vie numérique peut encore tenir dans un ordinateur, voire sur un simple disque externe.
Pour découvrir Offlined et télécharger sa dernière version, rendez-vous sur son site officiel ou sa page sur GitHub.

articles.title: Copenhagen’s Plinto raises €2.9 million to help finance teams catch and fix errors with AI agents | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Plinto, a Copenhagen-based startup building an AI-powered controlling platform, has secured €2.9 million in pre-Seed funding.
The round was led by People Ventures and Emblem, with participation from a group of business angels.
“Companies have systems that record every single transaction, but checking whether those transactions actually match agreements and rules is still largely manual. We’re building AI agents that find deviations, investigate them and take action, so errors get fixed,” said Jakob Nielsen, co-founder and CDO of Plinto.
Plinto was founded in early 2025 by Nermina Suljevic, Nielsen, and Sebastian Rehnby, who previously worked for Peakon, the employee engagement platform acquired by US-based Workday in 2021. The company’s CTO Andreas Garnæs is also an alumnus of Peakon. Together, they bring experience across product development, engineering, commercial scaling, and working with large international organisations.
In large organisations, the volume of financial transactions exceeds what finance teams can review manually. This work is handled by controllers, who typically resort to spot checks or end-of-month reconciliations, leaving enough room for errors such as incorrect prices, duplicate invoices, or mismatched deliveries.
Plinto wants to solve this problem with AI agents that sit on top of the systems companies already use, such as ERP, documents, bank, and collaboration tools like Slack or Microsoft Teams.
When a transaction is flagged, Plinto’s agents are designed not only to alert someone but also to investigate, gather evidence, and follow up with relevant people within the organisation and external contacts. Plinto says the agents are capable of contacting a supplier about a wrongful invoice, requesting a credit note or preparing a correction for approval.
It says one of its customers uncovered around 430 deviations per month in a single part of the business. At another customer, the agents identified a duplicate invoice submitted with a different supplier name in the same minute it arrived.
“Many of our customers work with low margins, so even small errors can quickly add up. The problem is that they’re often only discovered after the money has been paid. We want companies to catch and fix errors before they hit the bottom line,” said Suljevic, co-founder and CEO of Plinto.
Plinto platform integrates with major ERP platforms, including Microsoft Business Central, Xero, and Visma, and connects to major Scandinavian banks as well as over 2,700 other banks. It counts paying customers and pilots in logistics, real estate, facility services, and food production. The platform covers both order-to-cash and procure-to-pay workflows, and all data is processed and stored within the EU. Plinto also says it never uses customer data to train AI models.
The company plans to use the pre-Seed funding for product development, bringing on more enterprise customers and making Plinto’s first move outside Denmark. It wants to bring its agents to enterprises beyond its home market and aims to help them find financial errors in real time.

articles.title: OVHcloud alerte ses clients : changez tous les secrets stockés sur votre PC — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous avez installé ou mis à jour l’outil en ligne de commande d’OVHcloud ce lundi 19 octobre, partez du principe que vos mots de passe et vos clés d’accès ont pu fuiter.
Dans un message publié sur X, Octave Klaba, fondateur et président de l’hébergeur roubaisien, a confirmé qu’un pirate avait piégé la version mise en ligne à 14 h 47 sur GitHub. Le programme ajouté fouillait le disque de la machine pour y récupérer les secrets, ces identifiants qui ouvrent l’accès à vos serveurs et à vos services.
Le logiciel visé est le CLI officiel d’OVHcloud (pour command line interface). Avec cet outil, on gère ses services en tapant des commandes dans un terminal au lieu de cliquer dans l’espace client. Il pilote les serveurs dédiés, les VPS, le Public Cloud ou les noms de domaine, et sert souvent dans des scripts d’automatisation. Son code est publié en open source sur le dépôt GitHub ovh/ovhcloud-cli. Il s’adresse surtout aux développeurs et aux administrateurs système, dont les machines contiennent justement beaucoup d’accès sensibles.
1 h 34 d’exposition, jusqu’au signalement d’un client
Le pirate a utilisé le compte GitHub d’un développeur d’OVHcloud. Avec ce compte, il a ajouté au dépôt un binaire (un programme prêt à être exécuté) chargé de récupérer les secrets stockés sur le disque. On ne sait pas encore comment il a pris le contrôle du compte.
Les versions v0.11.0, v0.12.0, v0.13.0, v0.14.0 et v0.15.0 sont compromises. Par contre, la v0.10.0 est saine, tout comme la v0.16.0 publiée depuis. OVHcloud a repéré et bloqué l’attaque à 16 h 21, soit 1 h 34 après la mise en ligne, parce qu’un client lui a signalé le problème.
Le site Cyberattaque.org a retrouvé sur GitHub l’alerte d’un utilisateur dont l’installation automatique avait échoué. Son système vérifiait l’empreinte SHA-256 du fichier téléchargé, une sorte de signature calculée à partir de son contenu. Les fichiers d’anciennes versions avaient été remplacés, et l’empreinte ne correspondait plus. Rien ne confirme officiellement qu’il s’agit du client remercié par Octave Klaba.
Version, mise à jour, secrets : ce qu’il faut faire
Octave Klaba demande aux utilisateurs concernés de mettre le CLI à jour très vite, ou de l’effacer. Ensuite, il faut changer « tous les secrets » présents sur le disque. Voici l’ordre à suivre :
- Vérifiez votre version en tapant ovhcloud version dans un terminal. Si elle va de v0.11.0 à v0.15.0 et que vous l’avez téléchargée ou mise à jour ce lundi, vous êtes concerné. Dans le doute, faites comme si.
- Supprimez le programme, puis installez la v0.16.0 avec le script officiel ou Homebrew. Vérifiez ensuite que le numéro de version a bien changé.
- Changez d’abord vos clés API OVHcloud. Le CLI les range dans le fichier .ovh.conf de votre dossier personnel ou dans des variables d’environnement, donc à portée directe du programme pirate. Révoquez-les dans votre compte OVHcloud, puis générez-en de nouvelles avec ovhcloud login.
- Passez ensuite au reste : clés SSH, jetons GitHub, identifiants d’autres clouds, mots de passe écrits en clair dans des fichiers de configuration.
- Si le CLI tournait dans une chaîne d’intégration continue (les scripts qui testent et déploient le code automatiquement), changez aussi les secrets de cette machine.
OVHcloud n’a pas encore dit combien de personnes ont téléchargé les versions piégées. Octave Klaba a promis de publier « sous peu » plus de détails sur le binaire.

articles.title: From Microservices to Agents: the Next Evolution of Distributed Systems
articles.text:
Key Takeaways
- Agentic AI systems shift distributed systems design from orchestrating services to orchestrating decisions made at runtime.
- Unlike microservices, agentic systems introduce non-deterministic execution paths driven by context, reasoning, and tool selection.
- Decision quality becomes a first-class reliability concern alongside latency, availability, and throughput.
- Production failure modes often manifest as silent degradation in reasoning quality rather than explicit system errors.
- Effective agentic architectures require bounded autonomy, evaluation loops, and hybrid deterministic fallback systems.
| This article is part of the "Agentic AI Architecture" article series. In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream. | 
Distributed Systems Are Entering a New Phase
Over the past decade, microservices have reshaped how large-scale software systems are designed and operated. They enabled teams to decompose monoliths into independently deployable services, scale ownership boundaries, and evolve systems incrementally. For many organizations, microservices became the dominant model for building distributed systems at scale.
At their core, microservices solved a fundamental problem: how to decompose functionality across services and teams in a way that supports independent evolution while maintaining system reliability. They introduced explicit service boundaries, well-defined APIs, and predictable execution flows.
A new architectural shift is now emerging, driven by advances in large language models (LLMs) and reasoning systems. Rather than focusing on decomposing functionality, this new paradigm focuses on decomposing decisions. Systems are beginning to move from static orchestration models toward adaptive, runtime decision-making systems. This is the foundation of what is increasingly referred to as agentic AI.
Agentic systems differ from traditional services in a fundamental way. Instead of executing predefined logic, they dynamically determine which actions to take, which tools to use, and how to sequence multi-step reasoning processes. Execution is no longer fully specified at design time; it emerges at runtime based on context, goals, and intermediate outcomes.
This shift introduces new capabilities. Systems can become more adaptive, more context-aware, and better able to handle ambiguous or evolving inputs. At the same time, it introduces new forms of complexity that are not well addressed by traditional distributed systems thinking.
The goal of this article is to explore this transition in depth: how agentic AI architectures differ from microservices, what architectural patterns are emerging, what failure modes we are beginning to observe in production systems, and how observability and reliability practices must evolve. The discussion is grounded in experience operating large-scale distributed systems in domains such as search, recommendation, and serving infrastructure.
Microservices Solved Service Decomposition — Agents Solve Decision Decomposition
Figure 1: Execution Model: Microservices vs Agentic Systems
(Source: created by the author with OpenAI ChatGPT)
[Click here to expand image above to full-size]
Microservices architecture introduced a clear model for structuring distributed systems. Instead of a single monolithic application, systems were decomposed into services aligned with business capabilities. Each service owned a bounded context — a clearly defined domain of responsibility and data ownership — communicated via APIs, and could evolve independently.
This decomposition enabled faster deployment cycles, clearer ownership boundaries, and improved scaling characteristics. However, despite their flexibility, microservices still rely on deterministic execution. The control flow of a request is explicitly defined through service-to-service interactions.
In a typical microservices-based system, a request follows a well-understood path: it enters a service, is processed, calls downstream services in a defined sequence, and returns a response. Even in highly complex systems, the execution path is known in advance and encoded in the system's logic.
Agentic AI systems introduce a different model of execution. Instead of defining the full sequence of operations upfront, systems determine execution paths dynamically. Decisions about which tools to invoke, which data sources to query, and which strategies to apply are made at runtime.
This represents a shift from service decomposition to decision decomposition. Rather than distributing functionality across services, systems distribute reasoning across components that participate in a dynamic decision loop.
In practice, this means that execution is no longer a fixed pipeline but an adaptive process. A system may choose different candidate sources depending on context, dynamically adjust ranking strategies, or re-evaluate outputs based on intermediate results. The structure of execution becomes contingent on both input and evolving system state.
This change has profound implications for how we reason about distributed systems. It introduces flexibility but also reduces predictability. It replaces static workflows with dynamic reasoning paths, which are inherently more difficult to trace and debug.
What Makes Agentic Systems Fundamentally Different
Figure 2: Agentic System Architecture
(Source: created by the author with OpenAI ChatGPT)
[Click here to expand image above to full-size]
Agentic systems differ from traditional distributed systems in three key dimensions: control flow, state management, and failure semantics.
Control flow is no longer fixed. In microservices architectures, execution paths are designed and encoded ahead of time. In agentic AI systems, execution paths are determined at runtime based on context and intermediate reasoning. This introduces flexibility but also variability in system behavior, since different requests may trigger entirely different execution paths depending on user intent, retrieved information, or prior decisions made during execution.
The state also becomes more fluid and less strictly defined. Traditional systems rely on explicit state transitions and well-defined persistence models. Agentic systems, by contrast, often operate over an evolving execution context that is continuously updated as reasoning progresses. This context may include conversation history, intermediate plans, retrieved documents, ranking signals, tool outputs, or prior evaluation results.
Managing this evolving context becomes a core systems concern. Context often must propagate across multiple agents, tools, and services while remaining sufficiently consistent to support coherent downstream reasoning. In practice, many systems introduce shared context stores, execution-scoped memory, or structured reasoning artifacts to avoid context fragmentation and contradictory decisions across execution steps. As execution chains become longer, context management begins to resemble distributed state coordination problems seen in earlier generations of distributed systems.
Failure semantics also change. In traditional systems, failures are typically binary: a request succeeds or fails, a service responds or times out. In agentic systems, failures often manifest as degraded decision quality. The system may continue to operate but produce suboptimal outcomes due to incorrect reasoning, poor tool selection, stale context, or incomplete interpretation of intermediate results.
These differences fundamentally change how distributed systems behave in production environments. They also require new architectural patterns to manage complexity, reliably propagate context, and maintain predictable system behavior at scale.
Architectural Patterns in Agentic AI Systems
As agentic systems begin to appear in production environments, several architectural patterns are emerging. These patterns are not formal standards but rather recurring structures that help manage complexity and control variability in decision-making systems.
One common pattern is the separation of planning and execution responsibilities. In this model, a planning component is responsible for interpreting intent and determining a high-level strategy, while execution components perform deterministic operations such as data retrieval, transformation, or ranking. This separation allows systems to isolate non-deterministic reasoning from deterministic execution, improving reliability and traceability.
A second pattern involves the specialization of agents. Instead of relying on a single general-purpose agent, systems are increasingly composed of multiple specialized agents, each responsible for a distinct capability such as retrieval, ranking, evaluation, or orchestration. These agents collaborate to produce final outcomes.
This structure resembles service decomposition in microservices architectures, but applied to decision-making rather than data processing logic. While specialization improves reasoning quality and modularity, it also introduces coordination overhead and increases system complexity. Latency becomes more variable, and failure modes can propagate across agent interactions.
A third pattern is the integration of evaluation directly into execution loops. Instead of treating evaluation as an offline process, systems increasingly evaluate outputs during runtime. Based on evaluation results, systems may dynamically refine, retry, or adjust strategies.
This introduces feedback loops into execution, enabling more adaptive behavior. However, it also requires careful control to avoid excessive retries or runaway execution cycles. Constraints such as latency budgets, iteration limits, and confidence thresholds become essential for maintaining system stability.
A further emerging pattern is the introduction of tool abstraction layers. As agents interact with a growing number of services and APIs, teams are creating standardized interfaces for tool use. These abstraction layers decouple agent reasoning from underlying service implementations and provide a consistent mechanism for capability discovery and invocation.
Over time, this abstraction layer begins to resemble a platform for capabilities rather than a collection of individual services. It becomes a critical enabler for scaling agentic systems across teams and domains.
Across these patterns, a consistent theme emerges: complexity is shifting from service orchestration to decision orchestration. Systems are no longer primarily concerned with how services interact, but with how decisions are made, evaluated, and adapted over time.
Failure Modes in Agentic Distributed Systems
Figure 3: Silent Failure Modes in Agentic Systems
(Source: created by the author with OpenAI ChatGPT)
[Click here to expand image above to full-size]
Agentic systems introduce new failure modes that differ significantly from those observed in traditional distributed architectures. While microservices typically fail due to latency, availability issues, or data inconsistencies, agentic systems often fail due to degraded decision quality.
One important failure mode is cascading decision degradation. In traditional pipelines, failures propagate through explicit dependencies. In agentic systems, early incorrect decisions can subtly influence downstream reasoning, compounding degradation in output quality. For example, if a system selects suboptimal candidate sources early in execution, subsequent ranking and evaluation steps operate over reduced-quality inputs, amplifying the initial error.
This pattern is particularly relevant in large-scale search and recommendation systems, where early-stage candidate generation significantly influences downstream ranking quality. Even when infrastructure remains healthy, small shifts in early decisions can lead to noticeable changes in system outcomes.
Another failure mode is retry amplification driven by evaluation loops. Agentic systems often include mechanisms for evaluating output quality and retrying when results are insufficient. While this improves adaptability, it can also lead to excessive iteration cycles. Unlike traditional retry mechanisms tied to explicit errors, these retries are driven by subjective quality judgments, making them harder to bound and control.
Without proper constraints, evaluation-driven retries can increase latency, amplify backend load, and create unpredictable execution patterns.
A third failure mode is silent quality degradation. In many cases, system performance may degrade without triggering traditional operational alerts. Infrastructure metrics such as latency and error rate may remain stable, while user-facing quality deteriorates due to changes in decision-making behavior.
This is especially common in systems that rely on ranking, personalization, or recommendation logic. Small shifts in tool selection, reasoning strategies, or context interpretation can accumulate over time, leading to gradual but significant changes in system behavior. Detecting these issues requires evaluation-aware monitoring rather than infrastructure-centric observability.
Coordination overhead and latency accumulation also emerge as important concerns. As systems distribute reasoning across multiple agents, execution paths become more complex and less predictable. Each additional coordination step introduces variability in latency and increases the risk of partial failures.
Finally, state drift and context inconsistency can lead to reasoning errors across multi-step execution flows. When context is updated incrementally across agents or steps, inconsistencies in state propagation can result in contradictory or incomplete decisions. This is analogous to consistency challenges in distributed systems but manifests as reasoning drift rather than data inconsistency.
Observability and Reliability for Agentic Systems
Traditional observability models based on metrics such as latency, throughput, and error rate remain necessary but are insufficient for agentic systems. A new dimension of observability is required: decision quality.
Instead of only observing system health, teams must observe how decisions are made. This includes tracing tool selections, reasoning steps, intermediate outputs, and evaluation outcomes. Decision-level tracing provides visibility into how system behavior evolves over time and where degradation originates.
Monitoring changes in system behavior also becomes important. Over time, shifts in tool usage patterns, strategy selection frequencies, fallback rates, or retry behavior can indicate that the system’s decision-making process is drifting. For example, a sudden increase in retries or a strong preference toward a single strategy may signal degraded reasoning quality, stale context, or poor evaluation signals.
These behavioral shifts often surface problems earlier than traditional user-facing metrics such as engagement or latency. Observing how decisions are distributed across the system can therefore serve as an early warning mechanism to detect quality degradation before it becomes operationally visible.
Evaluation infrastructure plays a central role in reliability. Rather than being treated as an offline validation mechanism, evaluation becomes part of the runtime system. It provides feedback loops that guide execution and help maintain quality. However, these loops must be carefully constrained to avoid excessive iteration or instability.
Reliability in agentic AI architectures also depends on bounded autonomy. Systems must operate within clearly defined constraints such as latency budgets, retry limits, and reasoning depth boundaries. These constraints ensure that flexibility does not come at the cost of predictability.
Fallback mechanisms remain essential. Deterministic execution paths provide stability when agentic reasoning becomes uncertain or when system confidence is low. In many production systems, hybrid architectures that combine agentic decision-making with deterministic fallback pipelines offer a pragmatic balance between flexibility and reliability.
Progressive rollout strategies are also critical. AI-based capabilities should be introduced gradually through experimentation, shadow execution, and controlled deployment. This allows teams to build confidence in the system's behavior while limiting exposure to risk.
Ultimately, reliability in agentic systems requires a shift in mindset. Instead of treating failures as binary events, systems must be designed to degrade gracefully in decision quality while maintaining a predictable user experience.
The Road Ahead
Agentic AI architectures represent a natural evolution of distributed systems. Microservices enabled the decomposition of functionality; agentic systems enable the decomposition of decision-making.
This shift introduces new capabilities in adaptability, personalization, and dynamic execution. It also introduces new challenges in observability, reliability, and system design.
The most important implication is that distributed systems are no longer only about orchestrating services. They are increasingly about orchestrating decisions. This requires extending established principles of distributed systems engineering to a new layer of abstraction.
As organizations adopt agentic architectures, success will depend on combining flexibility with discipline. The same principles that enabled microservices to scale—clear boundaries, observability, reliability engineering, and platform thinking—will be essential in this new paradigm.
We are still early in this transition. However, the direction is becoming clear. Distributed systems are evolving from systems that execute workflows to systems that make decisions. Understanding and shaping this shift will define the next generation of large-scale software architecture.

We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream. |

O Galaxy Tab S10 Lite (256 GB) está disponível por R$ 2.199,12 no Pix com o cupom OFFHOJENOML no Mercado Livre. O tablet intermediário da Samsung com tela de 10,9 polegadas e bateria de até 16 horas, lançado por R$ 3.199, recebe um desconto de 31% e atinge o menor preço desde agosto.
O Galaxy Tab S10 Lite traz uma tela LCD de 10,9 polegadas com resolução Full HD+ e taxa de atualização de 90 Hz. O painel com ampla área de trabalho é recomendado para estudos e consumo de mídia, oferecendo mais conforto visual para os usuários.
Apesar da configuração inferior ao S10 e S10 FE, o dispositivo com o chip Samsung Exynos 1380 e 8 GB GB de RAM entrega um desempenho equilibrado para tarefas leves e o uso dos recursos do Galaxy AI. Os 256 GB de armazenamento interno trazem um espaço satisfatório, mas a memória pode chegar até 2 TB utilizando cartões microSD.
Seguindo os padrões dos tablets Samsung, o Galaxy Tab S10 Lite traz a caneta S Pen como parte do kit inicial. Além de facilitar a digitalização de anotações e desenhos à mão, ele permite usar recursos de IA (Apagador de Objetos) e de pesquisa (Circule para pesquisar) para agilizar o dia a dia.
O Galaxy Tab S10 Lite oferece suporte ao Samsung Dex, função que transforma o tablet em um desktop ao ser conectado a um monitor. Ele ainda traz uma câmera frontal de 5 MP para videochamadas em Full HD e uma câmera traseira de 8 MP para fotografar documentos e outros cliques mais simples.
A bateria de 8.000 mAh garante uma autonomia de até 16 horas de reprodução de vídeo, variando conforme o uso das conexões sem fio Wi-Fi 6 e Bluetooth 5.3. Em relação ao software, ele vem de fábrica com o Android 15 e receberá atualizações do sistema operacional até 2032.
Pensando para o transporte em bolsas e mochilas, o Galaxy Tab S10 Lite (R$ 2.199,12 no Pix com cupom OFFHOJENOML) é fabricado com corpo em Armor Alumínio com 6,6 mm de espessura e pesa 524 gramas. Por fim, o certificado IP42 de resistência à poeira e à água protege o aparelho de respingos de água.

articles.title: This mod lets Nvidia GeForce owners run a custom VBIOS without flashing the card
articles.text:
Enthusiast zone: Nvidia's signed firmware has kept BIOS modding off the table for GeForce owners for the most part. A new set of tools sidesteps that lock rather than breaking it, loading a custom VBIOS through the driver itself. It reopens a door enthusiasts thought was closed, but it arrives on a platform where power connectors are already at risk of melting on high-end GPUs and a single driver update could shut it down. Proceed carefully.
A developer has released three tools that let GeForce RTX 30, 40 and 50 series owners run a modified VBIOS without writing to the card's flash chip: a VBIOS editor for Windows and Linux, plus separate loaders for each operating system.
The cool trick is that nothing gets flashed. On Windows, the loader stores the edited image in the GPU's driver registry key, a spot where Nvidia's driver already checks for a VBIOS override every time the device starts. The tool then restarts the GPU, and the driver's GSP firmware boots from the custom image instead of the one on the card.
The Linux version takes a different route, patching Nvidia's open kernel modules so the GSP firmware starts with the custom image. Both projects build on earlier override research, which the developer credits directly.
The editor exposes settings overclockers have wanted back for years: board power limits, voltage ceilings, clock offset ranges, 12V input current and output overcurrent protections, fan PWM frequency and fan channels. Blackwell cards get the full set, while Ada and Ampere images are limited to fields the developer has validated.
The numbers shared so far are aggressive. On what appears to be an RTX 5090 FE, the board power ceiling rose from 600 W to 700 W and the NVVDD and MSVDD voltage ceilings from 1,110 mV to 1,150 mV. An RTX 4090 had its power limit raised to 671 W, confirmed by nvidia-smi, up from 550 W. In the developer's own testing, an RTX 5090 reached 800 W, an RTX 5080 went from 360 W to 500 W, and an RTX 5060 Ti from 185 W to 300 W.
It works in both directions, too. On an RTX A2000, the loader dropped the card's power floor to just 5 W, and the developer says voltages can be lowered to a hard floor of roughly 0.4 to 0.45V depending on the GPU generation. That makes the tools just as interesting for anyone who wants a cooler, quieter card with an undervolt baked in rather than applied by Afterburner at every boot.
No flashing means no bricked card from a failed write, but of course, it doesn't make the hardware any tougher. The 12V-2x6 connector on these cards is rated for 600 W, and there have been plenty of reports of RTX 5090 connectors melting at stock settings. Pushing 800 W through one is a big gamble, and with RTX 5090 and 5080 supply tight and warranty claims unlikely to cover a modded card, a dead GPU won't be easy to replace. The developer advises keeping a copy of the original ROM and testing on a GPU that isn't driving the display, and documents a Safe Mode recovery path, since Nvidia's driver doesn't load there.
As for how long this will last, the developer isn't optimistic, saying that Nvidia will very likely patch the method he's using in upcoming drivers and urging users to enjoy it while they can. Meanwhile, some enthusiasts are thrilled to see BIOS editing return, others want it purely for undervolting, and plenty are already joking about how many cards will die before Nvidia closes the gap.

articles.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
articles.text:
Since its earliest days, the video game industry has been built on developers creating clones of competing games, with varying levels of originality and varying levels of enforcement from game platforms. Now, though, AI coding tools are making that cloning process so efficient that many developers are getting extremely cautious about sharing their early work too widely.
Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend, delaying the launch of a planned public demo for its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflux, which had been set to go live with today’s launch of Steam Next Fest.
In a post on social media Friday evening, the Alliance Arts team wrote that, in addition to concerns about managing streaming restrictions, “we’re concerned that the demo’s content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game’s presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools and that such works could be released before our launch.”
Instead, the developer now plans to share the demo only in “closed sessions” with those who agree to rules regarding posting and streaming gameplay.
Alliance Arts isn’t alone in taking a more defensive stance toward sharing ideas. Papers, Please developer Lucas Pope said on an April podcast that, in general, “you don’t really talk about stuff when you’re working on it because I don’t know it’s going to get slurped up by AI or people are going to copy it or something else like that… I just didn’t feel as comfortable talking about the stuff I was working on again.”
Whose game is it, anyway?
Concerns about ideas getting “slurped by AI” have been more than theoretical for a number of indie developers in recent months. In March, developer Freya Holmér attracted some viral social media attention after sharing a video of a prototype of a Tetris-style game played on a central rotating pivot point. Days later, Holmér was confronted with a number of vibe-coded copies that made the basic concept widely playable before Holmér could release her own version.
My only option to compete is to play the same spamming game which I've never wanted to do, much easier to let it die and accept it was fun whilst it lasted.

articles.title: Replika’s founder built the AI assistant she pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Twelve years ago today, Eugenia Kuyda stood up onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt and presented a conversational chatbot called IO that acted as a lifestyle concierge to help people book restaurants and vacations along with other tasks.
IO, the first product from her startup Luka, came before the deep learning breakthroughs that would eventually lead to today’s large language models. “It still worked,” Kuyda told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview. “It was pretty magical … but, of course, it’s nowhere near what we have today.”
Luka ended up becoming Replika, the popular AI chatbot companion company. Last year, Kuyda left as CEO of Replika and founded Wabi.
The technology has finally caught up with her original vision for Luka, just in time for Wabi to take on a wave of new personal AI assistants such as Muse and Instinct, which promise to do everything from manage your inbox to find you the best flight deals.
On Monday, Kuyda officially launched Wabi for all users, a multiplayer personal AI assistant that functions as a messenger app, allowing users to maintain multiple agentic threads dedicated to different tasks and long-term goals. Within each thread, users can build and use custom apps, like a weight-loss tracker inside a health thread or an app showing nearby children’s events inside a family thread.
The launch is something of a pivot for Wabi, though Kuyda describes it as more of an evolution. When TechCrunch covered Wabi’s initial launch last year, along with its $20 million pre-seed round, it was described as more of a social platform where you could create mini apps with prompts that you could share with friends or across the app.
Over the past year, Kuyda said the team realized that while people love personal software rather than “one size fits all solutions in the App Store,” they “maybe don’t want to spend a lot of time, or any time, building it.”
With Wabi 2.0, the agent decides what apps to build. The moment you connect it to your email, it automatically spins up a number of threads and apps to start with, and users can add to that by requesting custom apps or starting new threads.
“It’s doing what Instinct and Muse do, but it also has all these apps, which helps users do more stuff,” Kuyda said.
App-building isn’t Wabi’s only differentiator. Kuyda is also betting on its multithreaded, multiplayer design.
“It’s not just everything in one single thread like with Instinct and Muse, where you get buried in the information that it sends you every day,” Kuyda said. “Single thread experiences, if you think about it, get worse over time because it’s just so much context in one endless conversation.”
The longer an AI chatbot conversation goes on, the more likely it is to hallucinate, lose track of context, or respond in ways that would otherwise be blocked by safety guardrails, according to interviews with AI researchers.
Threads can also be shared, functioning as group chats.
“Today, all the agentic apps are just [conversations] between you and the agent, and I feel like it should be a lot more about bringing people together in a group chat together,” Kuyda said. “Not you doing it separately with your AI, and I’m doing it separately with my AI … I don’t think anyone has yet cracked multiplayer.”
Kuyda walked TechCrunch through some of her own shared threads. In one with her boyfriend, a row of apps along the top helps the two of them connect and find things to do together, including a live music tracker, an app that asks a question every day about their relationship, a running list of restaurant suggestions, important events from their shared calendar, and a list of books they’re reading together with suggestions for what to read next.
In her more family-focused thread, there is an app tracking her daughter’s schedule, another for finding kid-friendly events nearby, and another that quizzes her daughter on Japanese.
Within any shared chat, users can share as much or as little as they want, from email and calendar information to bank account details.
“So my partner can ask Wabi in the chat, ‘Is Eugenia free next Thursday?’ or ‘Did she buy those tickets?’” Kuyda said. She noted that access is scoped to individual chats, and everyone in a chat can see when someone’s personal information is requested.
On privacy more broadly, Wabi is SOC 2 compliant, meaning its data security controls have been independently audited. Wabi runs entirely in the cloud, and most user data is stored in the U.S., Kuyda said.
“My previous company Replika worked on AI that will make people feel … less lonely,” Kuyda said. “To a degree, that is [in Wabi] as well. AI can bring people together, even when it comes to just helping you spend time better together in real life, whether it’s going out and seeing a concert together or finding the next book that you will read together.”
Wabi is free for now, and the company hasn’t settled on a business model yet. Kuyda said Wabi is in talks to raise more funds.
