articles.title: Modern Warfare 4 has the best Steam rating for a Call of Duty game in 16 years
articles.text:
The big picture: Ahead of its official launch later this week, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is offering early access to its campaign for players who pre-order the game. As expected, thousands of players are taking advantage of the opportunity, and the vast majority apparently seem impressed with the gameplay, graphics, and storyline.
The game currently has 4,068 total reviews on Steam, including 3,438 from verified buyers. Of those reviews, 94% are positive, earning it a "Very Positive" rating overall and making it the best-reviewed Call of Duty release on Steam since 2010's Black Ops. The SteamDB ratings were first reported by Insider Gaming last week, when the game had around 900 reviews and an 81.5% positive rating.
In stark contrast to the overwhelmingly positive response to Modern Warfare 4, recent releases in the Call of Duty franchise have struggled to even reach the 50% mark. 2025's Black Ops 7 has a 38.7% rating on SteamDB, while 2024's Black Ops 6 and 2023's Modern Warfare III have ratings of 45.7% and 48.1%, respectively. The only other recent CoD title with a similarly high rating is Black Ops III, which currently has 84.3% positive reviews.
The positive initial reception for Modern Warfare 4 must come as a relief to Activision, which has struggled in recent years. Not only have the last few mainline CoD releases received lukewarm responses from players and reviewers alike, but the company has also faced significant financial and creative challenges, resulting in several rounds of layoffs since Microsoft's $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision in 2023.
However, Modern Warfare 4's unusually high rating could change considerably once the game becomes more widely available later this week and players get a chance to try its multiplayer offerings. These include 12 core 6v6 maps and the extraction-shooter mode "DMZ," in which multiple squads of up to three players deploy into an area known as the "exclusion zone."
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches Friday, October 23, on Windows, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2. It is the last big AAA release this year before the much-anticipated GTA 6 launch in November, with most publishers pushing their upcoming releases to 2027 to avoid clashing with Rockstar's open-world juggernaut.

articles.title: Attention aux cagnottes pour aider Pierre du Micromania de Nice, pillé pendant les manifestations
articles.text:
Samedi, si vous avez suivi les manifestations contre la vie chère, émaillées de pillages à Nice, Marseille ou Paris, vous êtes forcément tombé sur cette vidéo mettant en scène Pierre. Gérant du Micromania de l’avenue Jean-Médecin, à Nice, Pierre a tenu tête aux casseurs, plus nombreux que lui, pendant l’attaque de son magasin, même quand il a pris un coup de pied alors qu’il leur tournait le dos.
Pierre est devenu un symbole de résistance pour beaucoup de Français, horrifiés par certaines images qui circulent sur les réseaux sociaux. Une image résume parfaitement ce sentiment : on le voit avec une attitude pleine de confiance, juste à côté d’une affiche de Son Goku, le héros de la saga Dragon Ball. Pierre est celui qui ne s’est pas défilé face aux pillards. Il a donc reçu un immense soutien, et des cagnottes ont vite été ouvertes à son nom, sans qu’il en soit à l’origine.
Le gérant de Micromania dit n’être à l’origine d’aucune cagnotte
Sur son compte Instagram intitulé stonebrushstudio, Pierre a publié une Story le dimanche 18 octobre. Il a d’abord remercié ceux qui le soutiennent. « Les gens qui sont venus me voir en vrai, c’est adorable. Merci. Merci beaucoup. Mon équipe et moi, on est très touchés », a-t-il indiqué, avant de poursuivre : « Je n’ai pas l’habitude de m’exprimer face caméra. Ce n’est pas mon métier. Mais je me vois contraint de réagir. »
Le principal intéressé ne se voit pas en héros. « Je pense qu’il n’aurait pas fallu le faire », a-t-il reconnu auprès d’ICI Azur, avant de qualifier son geste de « bêtise ». Il a assuré s’en tirer avec « quelques éraflures ».
Il a surtout pris la parole pour évoquer le sujet des cagnottes : plusieurs ont effectivement été créées en son nom. Celle lancée par Double Pixels, par exemple, approche les 10 000 €. Dans un message publié ce lundi 19 octobre sur Leetchi, Double Pixels, qui est également une chaîne de contenu pop culture installée en Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur, a affirmé : « Nous avons rencontrer [sic] Pierre il est au courant pour la cagnotte, il est d’accord ! Votre soutien est énorme. » Quelques heures auparavant, l’intéressé disait pourtant : « Je ne suis au courant de rien. Personne ne m’a contacté pour ce genre de choses. Je ne suis en lien avec personne. »
Pierre n’a rien publié depuis son intervention et, dès lors, rien n’indique qu’il ait bel et bien approuvé l’initiative de Double Pixels. « Ne vous faites pas avoir. Pour le moment, rien est fait », a-t-il rappelé. En attendant que Pierre s’exprime de nouveau, pour confirmer ou infirmer son accord, on ne peut que vous inviter à la prudence concernant d’éventuelles cagnottes à son nom. Il en va de même pour des achats de certains produits sur les plateformes Leboncoin, Vinted et eBay.
Si une collecte venait à utiliser son nom pour tromper les donateurs, elle relèverait de l’escroquerie. L’article 313-1 du Code pénal punit ce délit de cinq ans d’emprisonnement et de 375 000 euros d’amende.

articles.title: Turbine Capital closes €54 million DeepTech fund to connect Nordic startups with industrial leaders | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Turbine Capital, a Swedish VC fund focused on early-stage DeepTech companies in the Nordics, announced the final close of its first fund at €54 million (SEK 608 million) and a new industrial investor.
Mycronic joins the fund alongside Saab, Scania, Volvo Cars and Stena, as well as a number of industrial family offices and private investors. Institutional investors in the fund include Saminvest and the European Investment Fund (EIF).
“Closing our first fund at more than SEK 600 million, with an investor base ranging from leading Nordic industry to European institutions, confirms that our model meets a real need. During our first year, we have shown that multi-corporate venture capital works in practice, not just in theory,” says Anders Ösund, Founding & General Partner, Turbine Capital.
Turbine Capital’s final close comes amid several specialised European VC fund announcements in 2026.
In Sweden, Norrsken Evolve reached a €62 million final close, also backed by Saminvest and the European Investment Fund (EIF). Elsewhere in the Nordics, Copenhagen-based The Footprint Firm closed its €76 million climate and DeepTech fund, PSV Tech finalised a €56 million early-stage fund, and Climentum Capital secured a €60 million first close for climate HardTech investments.
France’s 360 Capital also announced an €85 million closing for its research-driven DeepTech fund Poli360 2.
Together with Turbine Capital, these announcements represent approximately €393 million in reported fund capital.
Source EU-Startups”Mycronic brings cutting-edge expertise in semiconductors and advanced manufacturing that strengthens our entire industrial network. Together with Saab, Scania, Volvo Cars and Stena, we have a base of industrial partners spanning defence, transport, electrification and now also semiconductor technology – exactly the kind of cross-sector platform Europe’s DeepTech companies need to scale,” adds Pär Hedberg, founder of Sting, who also is initiator and co-founder of Turbine Capital.
Since its first close in April 2025, Turbine Capital says they have built a unique Nordic model for cross-sector collaboration in venture capital: close cooperation with seven university-affiliated incubators – ABI, Uminova, UIC, Sting, LEAD, GU Ventures and IDEON – combined with a broad base of industrial investors.
The model gives investors access to early-stage innovation, while portfolio companies gain access to capital, industrial expertise and customers.
As a new investor in Turbine Capital, Mycronic complements the fund’s existing industrial base. Mycronic is a high-tech company engaged in the development, manufacture and marketing of production equipment with high precision and flexibility requirements for the electronics industry.
The company is in a strong growth phase driven by AI-related infrastructure investments, and has at the same time strengthened its presence in defence-related electronics manufacturing. Mycronic brings deep expertise in semiconductor technology, photonics and advanced manufacturing – key areas within Turbine Capital’s investment thesis.

articles.title: Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info
articles.text:
The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) has begun notifying victims impacted by a recent data breach of driver’s license and motor vehicle data, but not everyone whose information was stolen will receive an alert.
In a notice posted Friday, FLHSMV confirmed that it took “immediate steps” after discovering that “a malicious actor accessed certain department records on September 4, 2026, using compromised credentials.” There’s “no evidence” that data has yet been misused, the department said, but law enforcement “determined the information potentially affected includes driver license and motor vehicle data, to include document images, and other personal information.”
FLHSMV is sending out letters to everyone affected, offering victims one year of credit monitoring from Sontiq, Inc. However, the state acknowledged that it may not have current contact information for many former Florida residents whose data was still being stored. Those potential victims can confirm if their data was stolen by emailing FLHSMV at customerinquiry@flhsmv.gov, officials said.
For all current and former Florida residents, FLHSMV recommended taking precautions, including monitoring financial accounts and reviewing credit reports for any suspicious activity. In a thread on the Florida subreddit, several Floridians confirmed that they had already taken officials’ third recommendation and placed “a fraud alert or security freeze with major credit bureaus.”
Some residents complained that they received notice only this week, even though the breach occurred more than a month ago. The breach was previously reported by news outlets.
ShinyHunters linked to hack
On a webpage describing the security incident, FLHSMV confirmed that an “international cybercriminal organization” was behind the breach but did not specify which group or how long they had access. Instead, officials claimed to have “promptly mitigated the breach, launched an investigation, and issued required notification to state authorities.”

articles.title: Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on inference, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. The round comes five months after the 10-year-old Nvidia challenger reportedly received acquisition interest from Intel and Qualcomm at valuations of as much as $5 billion.
The fresh round, which more than doubled Tenstorrent’s valuation from the $2.6 billion it fetched in late 2024, was led by Trace Capital, a new firm launched by Quiet Capital co-founder Ben Mahdavi, and Innovation X. Other backers included Cadence Ventures, Eclipse, Fidelity, SanDisk, and T. Rowe Price.
Jim Keller, a prominent microprocessor engineer and Tenstorrent CEO, told Bloomberg that the company decided to remain independent and raise more capital after it showed that its Galaxy servers could run DeepSeek models. The new capital will go toward scaling chips tailored for serving open-weight AI models and video generation.
Tenstorrent is part of a wave of AI hardware startups trying to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance. Among them is Etched, an AI chip maker that was fielding investment offers at valuations of $40 billion or more, TechCrunch reported earlier this month.

articles.title: ORICO Enters Laptop Market With Obook 15 AI Laptop
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
ORICO Enters Laptop Market With Obook 15 AI Laptop
ORICO, usually known for its storage and connectivity solutions, is officially entering the PC market with its first laptop design, the Obook 15 AI Laptop. For this initial design, the company has chosen AMD's Ryzen 7 6800H SoC, an eight-core, 16-thread mobile processor that can boost up to 4.7 GHz. The integrated Radeon 680M graphics handle visuals, and memory configurations include options of 12 GB or 24 GB running at 6,400 MT/s. Buyers can select up to a 1 TB NVMe SSD, and a second M.2 slot allows for storage expansion up to 4 TB. While not running the latest SoCs from AMD, the system wants to be a competitive solution price-wise. Obook 15 runs on Windows 11 out of the box and features a cooling system with selectable Eco, Normal, and Performance modes for fan profiles.
The Obook 15 boasts a 15.6-inch IPS display with a 1,920 x 1,080 resolution, an anti-glare finish, 170-degree viewing angles, and wide-frequency dimming. It includes Wi-Fi 6, a 54.29 Wh battery, and a bundled 100 W charger. Additional features include a 180-degree hinge, a physical webcam shutter, a full-size keyboard with a number pad, and a wide selection of ports. ORICO lists US prices starting at $689.99 for the version with 12 GB of RAM and a 256 GB SSD. A 12 GB/512 GB version is priced at $749.99, while the top configuration with 24 GB of memory and 1 TB of storage costs $899.99. The Obook 15 is now available in the United States and the Philippines, targeting students, office users, and content creators with its attractive price points, especially for this day and age, amid memory and storage shortages.ORICO is also focusing on software as a key feature of the product. The included XiaoAo AI Super Agent combines 11 specialized AI assistants, which the company claims can help automate workflows, manage a knowledge base, and control devices remotely. The usefulness of these capabilities in everyday work will depend on their implementation, but ORICO aims to make the Obook 15 stand out from conventional productivity notebooks.

I’d trust this 16TB Seagate Expansion drive with my backups and media library
High-capacity hard drive storage and Rescue data recovery
Seagate has made hard drives for decades, and the Expansion line is about as straightforward as external storage gets: plug it in and drag your files across, no software required. The included Rescue data recovery service is a useful safety net for a drive that’s likely to hold years of files.
If your photos, videos, and backups are scattered across too many small drives, a single 16TB Seagate Expansion lets you consolidate them. Currently, you can pick up the Seagate Expansion Desktop 16TB HDD for $420 (was $550) at Newegg with the current gift card offer (buy two for $200, get $230).
• Best for: Professionals who needs a lot of affordable backup or media storage for a desktop PC or Mac.
• Why we like it: We've had good experiences testing out Seagate's line of storage. Here, you get a huge 16TB capacity in one box, simple plug-and-play setup on Windows and Mac, and Rescue data recovery services included.
This 16TB desktop external hard drive connects over USB 3.0 and works with Windows 10 or later and macOS 10.12 or later (you may need to reformat it for Time Machine). It includes Seagate’s Rescue data recovery services and a one-year warranty. For the full discount, pick up two Newegg gift cards for the bonus $30 free.
Price Context & Historical Value
The $100 savings work out to 18% off, a modest discount on a high-capacity drive. If you also pick up two $100 Newegg gift cards, you’ll get $30 in bonus credit. External drive prices have risen over the past year, so this is a fair price today but not a bargain by older standards.

❌ Skip the Seagate Expansion 16TB if...
You need something portable, since this desktop drive needs wall power, you want the speed of an SSD or a faster USB-C connection, or a one-year warranty feels too short for a drive holding this much data.

articles.title: French rioters ransack eSports team premises and are seen looting RAM sticks from PCs — Team Vitality’s ‘V.Hive’ Paris HQ was wrecked during unrest
articles.text:
French rioters ransack eSports team premises and are seen looting RAM sticks from PCs — Team Vitality’s ‘V.Hive’ Paris HQ was wrecked during unrest
Reports also highlight eSports trophies being stolen, with gaming chairs being piled up in street fires.
Leading French eSports club Team Vitality has confirmed that its Paris HQ has been smashed up, with trophies, computer equipment, and more looted over the weekend. Thankfully, no team members or staff have been hurt. The team’s V.Hive premises were attacked by criminal opportunistic looters under cover of the widespread protests in France over issues related to school funding, living costs, and government spending cuts. Other shops, public buildings, and property have been smashed, looted, and sometimes burned.
Above, you can see the confirmation of the serious, unfortunate events seen over the weekend. “Our display windows were destroyed, and our trophies and computer equipment were stolen,” lamented the post [machine translation], while being thankful that no members, staff, or fans of Team Vitality were hurt. The bulletin ends with the news that the V.Hive will remain closed for now, until after damage has been assessed. More information is promised in due course.
There are a multitude of social media posts sharing images, videos, and pointing fingers at what they see as the cause of the protests, riots, and looting. Of course, fingers point in all directions, and unfortunately there are also reports of AI-generated rage-farming media, so keep a critical eye open should you dare to doom scroll.
Of course we’ve focused on the damage and looting of Team Vitality’s HQ due to the tech angle. The compendium of video clips shared by the news organization NEXTA provides evidence of the extent of the V.Hive attack. This 30-second clip appears to show rioters hammering at and kicking in the eSports HQ’s windows, taking items from the premises, and throwing gaming chairs onto bonfires in the street.
We also see accounts like ElBuni share clips of looters brandishing what appear to be eSports trophies from Team Vitality’s HQ (embedded above). The second clip shows looters with their hands inside gaming PCs opened up on the sidewalk. It looks like the hooded and gloved looter in the video is removing RAM sticks, an easily pocketable yet highly valuable PC component, as you will all know.
This morning, the French Prime Minister has called for local and partial curfews to contain the post-demonstration rioting. Meanwhile, there are concerns that there could be copycat behavior across Europe.

articles.title: Universal Cart: Warum Googles neuer Warenkorb für Händler zur Machtfrage wird
articles.text:
Ein Warenkorb für alle: Wie Google die Kontrolle über den Onlinehandel ausbaut
Google hat in den USA ein neues Einkaufs-Feature vorgestellt, den Universal Cart. Dabei handelt es sich um einen intelligenten Warenkorb, der das Shoppingerlebnis über unterschiedliche Händler hinweg ermöglichen und vereinfachen soll. Google sieh das Konzept als eine zentrale Anlaufstelle für Einkäufe. Die Idee dahinter klingt plausibel: Anstatt etliche Browser-Tabs offenhalten, Screenshots anfertigen zu müssen und Produkte in verschiedenen Merklisten und Warenkörben zu speichern, könnten Nutzer:innen in Zukunft Artikel und Angebote verschiedener Händler:innen in einem zentralen Warenkorb verwalten.
Google hatte das Konzept schon im Mai auf seiner Entwicklerkonferenz Google I/O präsentiert. Zunächst erfolgt eine Einbindung an zentralen Stellen wie der Google-Suche und in der Gemini-App. So kann an den zentralen Stellen auf bestimmte vorgemerkte Produkte verwiesen werden. Die Auswahl bleibt bestehen, sodass ein möglicher Einkauf jederzeit fortgesetzt werden kann. Perspektivisch sollen auch weitere Anwendungen wie Gmail und Youtube hinzukommen, was mittelfristig auch das Werbegeschäft bei den betreffenden Diensten verändern wird.
Zunächst testet Google das Feature in den USA und arbeitet hier mit Händlern wie Nike, Target, Walmart und Wayfair zusammen – sowie mit zahlreichen Shops auf Basis von Shopify. Ob und wann das Konzept auch in Deutschland ausgerollt wird, lässt das Unternehmen offen. In der Vergangenheit war Deutschland recht oft bei den ersten europäischen Ländern, in denen Services bereitgestellt wurden. Wenn es soweit ist, dürften Unternehmen, die auf einer Shopify-Basis arbeiten, ziemlich einfach anzubinden sein, wenn man den aktuellen Aussagen von Handelsexperten glauben darf.
KI überwacht Preise und sucht nach Rabatten
Googles neuer Warenkorb arbeitet dabei im Hintergrund und setzt auf den Shopping Graph des Konzerns, der nach Googles Angaben über 60 Milliarden fortlaufend aktualisierte Produktangebote bereitstellt. Der Universal Cart protokolliert und beobachtet Preisentwicklungen und Lagerbestände und weist Kund:innen entsprechend auf Veränderungen hin. Wenn etwa der Preis eines vorgemerkten Artikels sinkt oder ein bis dato ausverkauftes Produkt wieder verfügbar ist, erhält der Kunde einen entsprechenden Hinweis, wie man das von Preissuchmaschinen kennt.
Zudem zeigt Google hier, wie sich ein durchgängiger Handelsfunnel bezahlt macht: Denn durch die Anbindung an Google Wallet kann der Warenkorb die Vorteile bestimmter hinterlegter Kreditkarten berücksichtigen und etwa darauf hinweisen, mit welcher Karte sich zusätzliche Bonuspunkte oder Vergünstigungen erzielen lassen. Auch dazu passende Rabattcodes werden direkt im Warenkorb angezeigt. Das ist vor allem auch dann relevant, wenn Google hier bestimmte Vorteile wie ein Prime-Abo oder ein bestehendes Liefer-Abo berücksichtigen kann.
Auch hier wird es wieder darauf ankommen, wie nah Händler:innen die Plattform an sich heranlassen. Denn beim Kaufabschluss stehen zwei Möglichkeiten zur Verfügung: So können Nutzer:innen bei teilnehmenden Händlern die Bestellung mit wenigen Klicks direkt innerhalb der Google-Oberfläche über Google Pay abschließen oder aber die ausgewählten Produkte in den Warenkorb des jeweiligen Händlers übertragen und diese wie gewohnt über das Händler-UI kaufen.
Google setzt dabei auf das Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), einen gemeinsam mit Handelspartnern entwickelten offenen Standard, der für den Datenaustausch zwischen KI-Systemen, Handelsplattformen und den Shopsystemen der Händler gedacht ist.
Einzelnen Händlern bleiben weiterhin erster Ansprechpartner
Eine Beschränkung gibt es dabei aber schon: Denn der gemeinsame Warenkorb bedeutet, dass weiterhin jeder einzelne Händler Ansprechpartner für den eigentlichen Kaufvorgang sowie für Reklamationen und Retouren bleibt. Daher kommen auch Bestellbestätigungen sowie der Kundenservice vom jeweiligen Handelspartner.
Dennoch ist der Universal Cart eine entscheidende Veränderung, mit der Google seinen Status als Gatekeeper und Plattformbetreiber im Onlinehandel stärkt. Stand der Konzern in der Vergangenheit vor allem als Vermittler zwischen Produktsuche und Onlineshop, ändert sich das in Zukunft, weil Google hier zusätzliche Aufgaben übernimmt: bei der Produktauswahl, in der Preisüberwachung und nicht zuletzt in der Anbahnung der Kaufabwicklung. All das ist die Voraussetzung für einen funktionierenden Agentic Commerce, an dem Gemini, Shopping Graph, Google Wallet und UCP gleichermaßen beteiligt sind.
Auch wenn all das noch nicht komplett autonom funktioniert, können Händler erkennen, dass der Grad an Unterstützung durch die KI zunimmt – und man an Google auch in Zukunft schlecht vorbeikommt. Das ist entscheidend für die Händler, weil der alte Onlineshop einen Teil seiner Bedeutung verliert, wenn Kund:innen Produkte mehr als bisher bei Google auswählen, vergleichen und möglicherweise auch bezahlen.
Der Universal Cart ist damit auch ein weiterer Hinweis darauf, wie sich der Onlinehandel durch KI verändert. Zukünftig wird neben der Sichtbarkeit eines Händlers in Suchmaschinen wichtiger, ob seine Produkte und Schnittstellen für die Einkaufsassistenten der großen Plattformen zugänglich sind.

articles.title: 10 African startups named semi-finalists for $2m Milken-Motsepe Prize in Circular Economy - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ten African startups have been named semifinalists for the Milken-Motsepe Prize in Circular Economy, and will share US$500,000 in unrestricted funding as they compete for the US$1 million grand prize.
The Milken-Motsepe Prize is aimed at companies in Africa revolutionising using different technologies to revolutionise the circular economy on the continent. Run by the Milken Institute and the Motsepe Foundation, the prize will distribute a total of US$2 million in non-dilutive capital to companies using technology to scale circular economy solutions across Africa. Alongside funding, participants receive mentorship, investor connections and global exposure.
The 10 semi-finalists have now been announced, who will be whittled down to five finalists by judges assessing them on commercial viability, scalability, workforce and social impact, and environmental impact. The grand prize winner will be announced at the 2027 Milken Institute Global Conference in Los Angeles, with a US$250,000 runner-up prize also on offer.
Kenya leads the way with three semi-finalists. Bottle Logistics East Africa combines digital reverse logistics with industrial glass recovery to turn discarded glass into returnable packaging, cullet and other products; Sanergy converts urban sanitation and organic waste into organic fertiliser, biochar and other agricultural inputs; and Safi Organics turns rice husks and sugarcane bagasse into a carbon-negative organic fertiliser.
Ethiopia, Tanzania and Egypt each have two startups in the running. From Ethiopia, EKT Trade and Investment manufactures products from plastic waste, and Zafree makes tree-free pulp and paper for the packaging industry using banana farm waste. Tanzania’s Country Materials uses AI to identify, trace and recover scrap metal for the continent’s steel industry, while SafeSip recycles plastic waste into pressure-rated resin and drip irrigation equipment.
The Egyptian contingent comprises Papyrus Egypt, which converts banana plantation waste into biodegradable packaging and liquid fertiliser, and Triple M Electrical and Electronic Contracting, which extends the lifespan of power infrastructure by purifying transformer oil and refurbishing transformers, switchgear and panels.
Nigeria’s Cold Hubs, which builds and runs solar-powered cold rooms, refrigerated trucks and reusable crates for food markets and farm clusters, completes the list.
“Africa is uniquely positioned to lead in this transition,” said Emily Musil, managing director at the Milken Institute, who added that the prize backs entrepreneurs turning resource efficiency into competitive, job-creating businesses.

articles.title: Tesla Roadster : une quatrième version confirmée par le designer en chef
articles.text:
Dans la nuit du 15 au 16 octobre, Tesla a enfin officialisé son nouveau Roadster. Le constructeur américain y a mis la manière puisqu’il est parvenu à faire voler la voiture, grâce à des propulseurs à gaz froid développés avec SpaceX. Elon Musk, CEO de Tesla, a même évoqué un saut au-dessus du canyon de la Snake River, dans l’Idaho, là où le cascadeur Evel Knievel avait échoué en 1974.
La présentation s’est concentrée sur les prouesses exclusives du Roadster. Il a fallu attendre la mise en ligne de la page officielle pour découvrir qu’il y aura trois modèles différents. En réalité, il y en aura quatre, comme l’a confirmé Franz von Holzhausen, designer en chef de Tesla, dans une vidéo publiée par MotorTrend le 16 octobre.
Il y aura un modèle de Tesla Roadster plus abordable
Au début de la vidéo, Franz von Holzhausen a énuméré les différentes versions du Roadster, en commençant par un modèle « standard », placé sous la Performance et absent, pour l’instant, du site de Tesla. Il précise que les différentes variantes ajoutent des éléments supplémentaires : le système d’aspiration multimode sur la Performance, quatre propulseurs à gaz froid à l’arrière sur la Thrust, puis six de plus autour de la carrosserie sur la Rocket, la seule qui peut voler. Tesla précise sur son site que cette dernière n’est pas homologuée pour la route.
Tesla n’a publié aucune fiche technique pour ce Roadster de base. Selon Top Gear, repris par Motor1, il développerait tout de même environ 1 090 ch, contre quelque 1 360 ch pour la Performance. D’après la description de Franz von Holzhausen, cette version se passera du système d’aspiration multimode, qui n’arrive qu’à partir de la Performance. Pour tenir un prix plus bas, Tesla pourrait aussi retirer l’aérodynamique active. De fait, la voiture sera moins performante sur les accélérations. Elle pourrait en revanche offrir la meilleure autonomie. Comme les autres modèles, ce Roadster sera une propulsion, avec deux moteurs installés à l’arrière.
Ce Roadster standard pourrait aussi faire l’impasse sur des matériaux haut de gamme au sein de l’habitacle ou encore le revêtement doré sur les vitres teintées.
On rappelle que Tesla n’a fourni aucun prix sur le Roadster. En France, Tesla réclame un acompte de 50 000 € pour la Performance (5 000 € par carte bancaire, puis 45 000 € par virement sous dix jours) et de 250 000 € pour la Thrust. Aux États-Unis, les montants sont identiques, en dollars. La Rocket n’est proposée que sur invitation, sans acompte public. Tesla vise un début de production en 2028, même s’il est clairement indiqué dans les conditions générales de la réservation : « Vous comprenez que le Roadster est encore en cours de développement au moment où vous avez conclu le présent Contrat et que nous ne pouvons donc pas garantir la date à laquelle votre véhicule sera effectivement livré. »

articles.title: L'ARCOM exige des réponses au « OnlyFans français » sur le contrôle de l'âge de ses utilisateurs
articles.text:
L'autorité de régulation du numérique, l'ARCOM, a ouvert une enquête sur Mym, la plateforme française de contenus exclusifs souvent comparée à OnlyFans. Le régulateur soupçonne des manquements au DSA, notamment sur le contrôle de l’âge et la protection des mineurs.
L'ARCOM a ouvert une enquête sur Mym, soupçonnée de manquer aux règles européennes en matière de contrôle de l'âge et de transparence. Le régulateur l'a annoncé le vendredi 16 octobre, au terme d'une première analyse de cette plateforme née en 2019 et souvent présentée comme la cousine tricolore d'OnlyFans. Mym a quinze jours pour fournir des réponses, avec deux questions en toile de fond. L'autorité se demande si les mineurs ne peuvent pas s'y glisser trop facilement, et si on sait vraiment comment fonctionne sa vitrine.
L’ARCOM somme Mym de s’expliquer sur son contrôle de l’âge
Le premier souci, et pas des moindres, c'est celui de la protection des mineurs. L'ARCOM s'interroge notamment sur les « modalités » et l'« activation » du contrôle de l'âge. Derrière ces deux mots, il y a deux interrogations. D'abord, comment Mym s'assure-t-elle que ses utilisateurs sont majeurs ? En France, pour des contenus pour adultes, déclarer une date de naissance ne suffit plus, puisqu'il faut une méthode fiable, comme le recours à un tiers de confiance. Ensuite, ce contrôle se déclenche-t-il vraiment, pour tout le monde et avant l'accès aux contenus sensibles ? Un verrou n'est utile que s'il est solide et bel et bien fermé.
Si le sujet est si sensible, c'est que l'ARCOM décrit elle-même Mym comme un réseau social donnant accès à des contenus exclusifs et personnalisés, le plus souvent érotiques, voire sexuels. Mais pourquoi est-ce elle qui mène l'enquête ?
Depuis 2024, le règlement européen sur les services numériques (RSN, ou DSA en anglais) impose des règles communes à toutes les plateformes en ligne en Europe, de la lutte contre les contenus illicites à la protection des plus jeunes. Chaque pays désigne un gendarme pour surveiller les plateformes installées chez lui. En France, ce rôle revient à l'ARCOM depuis la loi SREN de mai 2024.
Quinze jours pour répondre, sous peine de sanction
Ensuite, il y a la question de la transparence. L’ARCOM pointe d’abord des conditions générales d’utilisation incomplètes. Ce règlement, que chacun accepte en s’inscrivant, doit pourtant dire clairement ce qui est permis, ce qui est interdit et comment la plateforme fonctionne. Le régulateur relève aussi un manque d’explications sur les systèmes de recommandation, en gros les algorithmes qui décident quels profils et contenus s’affichent à l’écran. Le DSA oblige en effet les plateformes à dévoiler les grands critères de ce tri. Sur Mym, où être vu, c’est être payé, il y a un vrai enjeu. Et le petit « etc. » du communiqué de l'autorité rappelle que la liste n’est pas close.
Pour y voir clair, l'ARCOM a adressé à Mym, le 14 octobre, une demande d'informations. Il s'agit d'une sorte de questionnaire officiel, auquel la plateforme doit répondre sous quinze jours, soit aux alentours du 29 octobre. Rien n'est tranché pour autant, puisque l'enquête doit justement établir si les soupçons sont fondés. Mais l'exercice n'est pas facultatif. Le DSA prévoit deux niveaux d'amende, jusqu'à 1 % du chiffre d'affaires mondial si la plateforme ne répond pas, ou de façon incomplète ou trompeuse, et jusqu'à 6 % si un manquement est avéré. On parle de plafonds, pas des montants automatiques. L'ARCOM, elle, promet de continuer à exiger des plateformes plus de transparence et une vraie protection de leurs utilisateurs, notamment des enfants.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 19, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 19, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, October 19, 2026.
From India’s artificial intelligence (AI) opportunity to how a Bengaluru hospital is paying doctors for recovery, not procedures, here are the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
India's next tech edge according to CTOs
India’s technology industry has long relied on talent, cost efficiency and scale. But as artificial intelligence makes advanced tools more accessible, these advantages alone may no longer be enough to differentiate companies.
The next edge, according to technology leaders at TechSparks 2026, will come from how effectively companies use AI to solve specific problems, understand customers and build products that are difficult to replicate.
Read more
Funding News
Even Healthcare raises $50M in Series B round
Bengaluru-based managed care company Even Healthcare has raised $50 million in a Series B round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures. Alpha Wave also participated in the round.
According to the company, the round values it at three times its valuation 18 months ago and brings its total funding to more than $120 million.
The money will go towards five new Even hospitals in Bengaluru over the next six months, beginning with Indiranagar. The company runs two hospitals in the city at present.
The Pant Project bags Rs 109 Cr to accelerate retail expansion
The Pant Project, a premium menswear label specialising in trousers and other bottomwear, has raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments.
Existing investor Sorin Investments also participated, alongside family offices and angel investors including Anisha Saraf, B&K Securities, MGA Ventures and B2V Ventures. The company has also secured venture debt from Alteria Capital, with IndigoEdge advising on the equity transaction.
Founded by brothers Dhruv and Udit Toshniwal, The Pant Project began as a digital-first business focused on fit, fabric performance and comfort for Indian men. Its products include Malai Pants and Inklock No Fade Black Jeans, and it sells through its website, Myntra, Amazon and physical stores.
Other News
AngelBot AI launches TeamSync to secure enterprise knowledge with AI-powered search
AngelBot AI has launched TeamSync, an AI-native platform designed to help enterprises securely search, manage and extract insights from fragmented documents and information repositories.
The platform combines natural-language document interaction, semantic search and permissions-aware AI, with citations and audit trails to support reliable information access. Its capabilities also include metadata extraction, electronic signatures, contract lifecycle management and eDiscovery.
Targeting mid-sized and large enterprises across regulated and document-intensive sectors, TeamSync offers subscription-based software, platform licensing and implementation services. The launch builds on AngelBot AI’s document management work, including IMIR, which has received recognition from the Indian Air Force.
VETO launches sports carnival, offers 300+ hours of subscription-free live sports
VETO, India’s subscription-free OTT platform, has launched the VETO Sports Carnival, offering more than 300 hours of live sports streaming across cricket, football, weightlifting and tennis during October and November.
The line-up includes an international ODI tri-series, Test matches, the IWF World Senior Championships, SAFF Championship, Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs and Davis Cup Finals.
The initiative expands VETO’s live sports portfolio as it seeks to make international sporting events accessible to Indian audiences without a subscription fee. The platform also offers 60+ live TV channels across 12 languages and more than 10 content genres.
Yes Madam revenue hits Rs 402 Cr annualised run rate, grows 3.9x in two years
At-home beauty and wellness platform Yes Madam has reported a 3.9-fold increase in revenue and 3.5-fold growth in Net Transaction Value (NTV) between Q2 FY25 and Q2 FY27. The company’s annualised revenue run rate reached Rs 402 crore, while its NTV run rate stood at Rs 836 crore.
In Q2 FY27, revenue rose 69% year-on-year to Rs 79.4 crore, while NTV grew 75% to Rs 165.8 crore.
Founded in 2016, Yes Madam operates across more than 55 cities with a network of 10,000-plus service professionals. The company plans to expand services, strengthen its network and invest in technology.
So/Facet raises Rs 10 Cr seed funding led by Sauce to build lab-grown diamond jewellery brand
So/Facet, a premium lab-grown diamond jewellery brand founded by former Unilever executives Aarushi Agrawal Naulakha and Abhishek Naulakha, has raised Rs10 crore in a seed funding round led by Sauce.
The company will use the capital for brand building, design, technology, hiring and an omnichannel retail expansion. Set to launch online in November 2026, So/Facet plans to open more than 30 premium stores over three years.
The brand aims to position lab-grown diamonds as expressions of personal style rather than jewellery reserved for traditional milestones. Its six launch collections feature IGI-certified diamonds and contemporary, in-house designs.
Guttify targets Tier II markets in three states, eyes 5x growth in annual recurring revenue
Gut-health startup Guttify plans to expand into select Tier II markets across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Punjab through pilot initiatives in FY27, targeting fivefold growth in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
The company has served over 30,000 consumers and reported 67% quarter-on-quarter growth. Its Rs 399 DIY Gut Scan Kit sold approximately 15,000 units between January and August 2026, with around half of buyers subsequently purchasing other products.
Guttify plans to expand its portfolio with products including Poopie, a fibre-based constipation-support product, and RISE, a morning greens blend, while strengthening personalised recommendations, consumer education and expert guidance.
As You Asked raises Rs 45 lakh pre-seed funding to expand children’s nutrition products
As You Asked, a nutrition startup focused on children aged 2–12, has raised Rs 45 lakh in an equity-funded pre-seed round backed by ISB D-Labs and angel investors. The company will use the funds to support its market launch, product development, manufacturing and distribution.
Its planned portfolio includes daily nutrition powders, hydration mixes and micronutrient gummies without added sugars. The startup has engaged more than 100 parents, conducted over 200 child taste tests and run an early pilot involving 200-plus customers to inform its product development. It aims to make everyday nutrition simpler, accessible and easier for families to incorporate into daily routines.
(The copy will be updated through the day)

articles.title: Siemens Software Center Vulnerability Exploited in ClickFix Malware Attacks
articles.text:
Siemens revealed on Monday that threat actors have exploited a vulnerability in Siemens Software Center as part of a malware campaign.
Siemens Software Center handles the download, installation, activation and updating of software that customers have bought, and it can also be used to start free trials.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-110936, exists because the program doesn’t properly restrict the locations it searches for DLL files. An authenticated local attacker could plant a malicious DLL in one of those folders and have their code executed with the same privileges as Software Center.
Siemens disclosed the flaw on October 15 in an advisory that assigned it a CVSS v4 score of 8.4. Two days later, the company updated the advisory to tell customers that version 4.0.9.8 resolves the issue.
Users who already have the application installed will receive the fix automatically the next time they launch it.
The advisory didn’t mention in-the-wild exploitation until Monday, when Siemens added a link to a new blog post describing the attacks.
The attackers paired a legitimate copy of the Siemens program, which carried a valid digital signature, with malicious DLL files they supplied themselves. When the program started, it loaded the attacker-provided files from its own folder.
Siemens noted that version 3.5.8.7, the newest release at the time, did not validate these helper files before loading them.
The company said its software was not tampered with, and that the malicious package was not spread through Siemens’ distribution channels.
“No Siemens system, product or update channel was breached to our knowledge,” the company said.
Siemens is sharing threat intelligence with authorities and EDR providers. Its blog post lists indicators of compromise (IoCs), as well as signs that a computer may have been infected.
Because the Siemens file used in the attacks is legitimate, the company recommends that defenders focus on suspicious behavior and the folders associated with the malware instead of relying on file hashes.
Huntress researcher Jose Oregon has been credited with reporting the vulnerability to Siemens.
Siemens links the attacks to the Romulus ClickFix operation
Siemens has linked the attacks to Romulus, a multi-platform ClickFix campaign. ClickFix attacks rely on fake prompts, such as bogus CAPTCHA checks, that instruct users to paste and execute malicious commands on their own devices.
Last week, Forescout published research on Romulus, a ClickFix delivery platform that can serve several different malware payloads. The security firm found the platform running on several servers, including the one Siemens identified as the distribution server for the malicious bundle containing its software.
Forescout saw the platform deliver the LegionLoader malware, as well as a trojanized installer that leveraged a legitimate Stardock application for DLL side-loading.
The researchers could not determine who runs Romulus. They said it could be a private tool, a service sold to cybercriminals, an affiliate program, or software copied by different threat actors.
Huntress described the same Stardock-based package in a late-September report on a campaign that used rogue ChatGPT Custom GPTs to lure users to ClickFix pages. In those attacks, signed programs from Canon and later Stardock were abused to side-load malicious code that ultimately deployed a RAT.
Huntress responded to at least 40 incidents linked to the campaign, and said it believes signed programs from other vendors are probably being misused as well.
Siemens Software Center is not mentioned in the Huntress or Forescout reports. However, the overlapping infrastructure and the similar side-loading approach suggest the Siemens program may have been added to the same toolkit.
Related: Siemens Says Desigo CC Files Flagged as Malware by Security Engines

articles.title: WordPress SEO plugin Rank Math compromised to backdoor websites
articles.text:
Some downloads of the Rank Math PRO WordPress plugin from the vendor’s official website carried malware that planted hidden backdoors in a supply-chain attack last week.
According to the vendor, a limited number of users who downloaded version 3.0.123 of the plugin between October 15 at 20:02 UTC and October 16 at 07:12 UTC received compromised versions that could compromise their websites upon activation.
“The affected plugin files contained malware that could compromise your website if the plugin was activated,” Rank Math warned.
“We immediately removed the affected files and released a clean version, Rank Math PRO v3.0.124.”
Users who installed and activated the trojanized version during this 11-hour window should treat their websites as compromised and follow the clean-up procedures in the advisory from the vendor.
Rank Math PRO is a WordPress search engine optimization (SEO) plugin that helps websites improve visibility in search results. It is the paid version of the free variant that is active on more than 4 million websites.
Sensitive material exposed
An advisory from the vendor highlights that only the PRO version was compromised and the free version of Rank Math SEO from WordPress.org remained unaffected.
Rank Math says that the malware establishes persistent access, communicates with ‘rank1cdn[.]com,’ and recreates hidden backdoors when someone visits the infected website.
The vendor warns that users installing the compromised version of Rank Math PRO expose database credentials, API keys, and other secrets accessible to the web server.
While researching the attack, BleepingComputer discovered a PHP malware sample on VirusTotal named 'cache-preloader-fff033 (1).php' that appears to be connected to the Rank Math compromise.
Although this file was not mentioned in the Rank Math or Wordfence advisories, BleepingComputer found it contained the same indicators of compromise (IoCs) included in Rank Math's alert:
- xmmqhn' XOR obfuscation key
- the '_np5pvf754c' WordPress database entry
- the '#ms6v46' cron job marker
- code for creating administrator accounts using the 'wpsupport_' username prefix and '@wp-mail.net' email addresses
The malware appears to act as a first-stage deployment script that creates the 'wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php' backdoor mentioned in Rank Math's advisory.
The PHP script also includes the ability to execute commands, modify WordPress databases, and steal AWS, Cloudflare, Google Cloud, Azure credentials, SSH keys, and other sensitive information.
While these IoCs indicate it is connected to the same threat actor as the Rank Math attack, BleepingComputer could not confirm whether it was distributed through the compromised plugin.
Cleanup recommendations
Website administrators who suspect a compromise should restore website files and the database from a clean backup, run security scans, and rotate all passwords, keys, and salts.
For websites without a safe backup to restore from, Rank Math recommends manual cleanup, noting that deactivating or updating the plugin after a compromise will not remove the threat.
Cleanup requires deleting the entire plugin folder and malicious database entries before investigating additional backdoors, unauthorized administrator accounts, altered files, scheduled tasks, and possible changes outside WordPress.
It is also recommended to block all outbound connections to the attacker's rank1cdn[.]com domain.
Users who installed but never activated the plugin should now delete it, download the clean 3.0.124 version, and then scan their sites.
BleepingComputer contacted Rank Math for details on the number of potentially affected sites and the initial attack vector but had received no response by the time of publication.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

articles.title: Las mejores ofertas de MediaMarkt durante su Hazte un Renove en tecnología, hoy 19 de octubre
articles.text:
MediaMarkt está celebrando su nueva campaña Hazte un Renove con ofertas muy atractivas en dispositivos tecnológicos. Hay de todo, desde móviles de gama alta hasta televisores, discos duros e incluso freidoras de aire. Por ello, en este artículo vamos a repasar los cinco mejores chollos que están ahora mismo disponibles.
- Seagate Expansion por 179,99 euros, un disco duro que tiene capacidad de 5 TB.
- Marshall emberton II por 89 euros, un altavoz Bluetooth con diseño retro.
- Google Pixel 11 Pro por 1.044,05 euros, uno de los mejores móviles de la marca.
- Ninja Crispi por 129 euros, una freidora de aire con dos recipientes de cristal.
- Haier S80G por 369 euros, un televisor QLED de 55 pulgadas.
Marshall emberton II
Seagate Expansion
En una época en la que tanto la memoria RAM como los discos duros (y SSD) han subido de precio, se agradece encontrar ofertas como la del Seagate Expansión que ha bajado hasta los 179,99 euros. Se trata de un disco duro portátil que tiene capacidad de 5 TB, lo que permite guardar muchísimas fotos, vídeos y archivos en general en un dispositivo con un formato muy compacto.
Seagate Expansion (5 TB)
Marshall emberton II
MediaMarkt también tiene de oferta el Marshall Emberton II por un precio de 89 euros, un altavoz Bluetooth que destaca por su particular diseño retro, un signo distintivo de la marca. Su batería ofrece una autonomía teórica de más de 30 horas, tiene un formato bastante pequeño y es resistente tanto al agua como al polvo (IP67).
Marshall emberton II
Google Pixel 11 Pro
Aunque no es el mejor precio que hemos visto hasta la fecha, MediaMarkt tiene un buen descuento en el Google Pixel 11 Pro, que ahora se puede comprar por 1.044,05 euros. Este precio sale únicamente si iniciamos sesión en la tienda. Se trata de un móvil de gama alta con un tamaño compacto de 6,3 pulgadas, ofrece un buen rendimiento y cuenta con un excelente apartado fotográfico.
Google Pixel 11 Pro (256 GB)
Ninja Crispi
Si aún no tienes una freidora de aire y buscas un modelo compacto que te permita preparar muchas recetas, MediaMarkt tiene la Ninja Crispi por 129 euros. Se trata de un modelo que incluye dos recipientes de cristal de 3,8 y 1,4 litros, ideales para ver cómo se cocinan los alimentos y extraerlos en su punto. Ofrece temperaturas de hasta 185 ºC y permite asar, dorar y mantener la comida caliente.
Haier S80G
Por último, la tienda también tiene de oferta la Haier S80G, una smart TV que con el descuento se queda por 369 euros. Incorpora un panel con tecnología QLED que tiene una diagonal de 55 pulgadas, su sistema operativo es Google TV, ofrece una tasa de refresco de hasta 120 Hz a través de software y sus altavoces son compatibles con Dolby Audio.
Haier S80G (55 pulgadas)

articles.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 Expands beyond Text to Support Code, Images, Video, and Audio
articles.text:
Based on Gemma 4 and released under the Apache 2.0 license, Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 is a compact, open-weight, multimodal embedding model designed to make semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) more efficient while optimizing performance for on-device deployment.
Designed to run on consumer hardware such as mobile devices and laptops, EmbeddingGemma 2 delivers low-latency semantic representations for on-device applications, like search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), classification, and clustering.
Thanks to its multimodal capabilities, EmbeddingGemma 2 supports a wide range of retrieval tasks, including finding relevant documents, screenshots, and recordings in response to a query, searching source code using natural language, and retrieving video content based on textual descriptions.
EmbeddingGemma 2's key feature, Google says, is its ability to represent text, code, images, video, and audio in a unified 768-dimensional embedding space. This enables developers to build retrieval systems that search across different media types without maintaining separate, incompatible embedding spaces for different media types.
Despite coming from different modalities, the embeddings generated by EmbeddingGemma 2 occupy the same dimensional space and can be compared on their semantic similarity.
The model allows developers to load only the encoders required for their applications, scaling from 270 million parameters for text and code to 740 million for full multimodal support. According to Google, the model "significantly outperforms EmbeddingGemma 1 on code search and technical retrieval, making it ideal for local codebase indexing and agentic code search".
EmbeddingGemma 2 supports Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), which allows embeddings to be truncated into shorter, unit-length vectors, reducing storage requirements. For example, storing a million 768-dimensional vectors at bfloat16 precision takes roughly 1.5 GB of memory, while truncating them to 128 dimensions requires just 250 MB, bringing a sixfold reduction. However, this implies a retrieval quality trade-off. Google therefore recommends using truncation only when storage or search speed require it. At 128 dimensions, the model retains approximately 90% of quality with text, but performance drops to around 75% for image, video, and speech retrieval.
Commenting on the announcement, Reddit user Distinct-Target7503 highlighted the model's multimodal capabilities while questioning the extent of its improvements for text-only tasks:
The impressive thing about this one is that it can embedd images and audio in a shared semantic space, but for text only it is not a massive improvement.
Meanwhile, Reddit user Open-Adhesiveness-86 cautioned developers about the importance of using the model correctly:
Two things that bit me on the first embeddinggemma and probably still apply: the task prefixes aren't optional, indexing docs with the query prefix instead of "title: none | text: " noticeably hurt recall. And if you truncate for MRL, slice first then L2-normalize the shorter vector, normalizing at 768 and then cutting gives you off-norm vectors.
EmbeddingGemma was introduced last year with a focus on "offline and privacy-sensitive scenarios, such as searching across personal files locally, running mobile RAG pipelines with Gemma 3n, or building domain-specific chatbots". EmbeddingGemma 2 is available on Hugging Face.

articles.title: Premier Mac tactile en vue : Apple envoie ses invitations pour le 28 octobre (MacBook Pro OLED) — Frandroid
articles.text:
Apple a officialisé ce lundi 19 octobre le rendez-vous que les rumeurs annonçaient depuis plus d’une semaine. La marque invite la presse le mercredi 28 octobre à Los Angeles, loin de son siège de Cupertino. Quelques journalistes français ont reçu l’invitation, dont Nicolas Lellouche de Numerama. Apple confirme donc une date et un lieu. Elle n’a par contre annoncé aucun produit.
Le lieu sort des habitudes. Apple présente d’ordinaire ses nouveautés à l’Apple Park, son campus en forme d’anneau à Cupertino. Elle a d’ailleurs déjà quitté la Californie ce mois-ci : son premier événement d’octobre, baptisé « Welcome home », s’est tenu le 13 octobre à New York. Apple y a lancé l’écran connecté HomeView, le HomePod mini 2 et une nouvelle Apple TV 4K.
    Pour aller plus loin
Toutes les annonces Apple « Welcome home » : Apple HomeView, Apple TV 4K (2026) et HomePod mini 2
            
Le carton d’invitation affiche le slogan « Pro and tell ». Greg Joswiak, vice-président senior chargé du marketing mondial d’Apple, l’a repris sur X avec une courte vidéo et ce message : « Can’t wait to pro and tell next week ». La formule vient de « show and tell », un exercice des écoles américaines où un élève présente un objet à sa classe. En remplaçant « show » par « pro », Apple ne laisse pas beaucoup de suspense sur la gamme concernée (le MacBook Pro, donc).
Le slogan laisse aussi penser que la machine s’appellera bien MacBook Pro. Le nom « MacBook Ultra » circulait pourtant dans les rumeurs.
Le MacBook Pro tactile en tête d’affiche
Apple n’a rien confirmé, mais Mark Gurman, journaliste de Bloomberg, a détaillé le programme probable dès le 8 octobre. En tête, on trouverait des MacBook Pro de 14 et 16 pouces avec un écran OLED tactile. L’OLED, déjà présent sur les iPhone et l’iPad Pro, allume chaque pixel séparément, ce qui donne des noirs plus profonds. Les MacBook Pro bénéficient néanmoins du Mini LED, dont les performances ne sont pas si loin du côté du taux de contraste.
Surtout, Apple vendrait pour la première fois un Mac tactile. La marque a longtemps refusé de mettre macOS sur un écran qu’on touche du doigt.
Ces PC portables auraient aussi droit à la Dynamic Island, la pastille noire interactive en haut de l’écran des iPhone. Ils seraient enfin nettement plus légers que les modèles actuels, avec un châssis plus fin. Ce serait la plus grosse refonte de la gamme depuis des années.
Les puces, elles, ne changeraient pas de génération. Ces MacBook Pro garderaient les M5 Pro et M5 Max, les puces maison d’Apple qui regroupent le processeur et la partie graphique. La puce M6, déjà dans le Mac mini, irait à l’iMac et à un MacBook Pro 14 pouces d’entrée de gamme, qui garderaient leur look actuel.
L’iPad mini serait aussi de la partie, avec un écran OLED, des haut-parleurs revus et une caméra FaceTime déplacée. Au total, Apple présenterait quatre nouveaux Mac et un iPad.
Toujours selon les rumeurs, ces produits arriveraient en magasin dès le vendredi 6 novembre. Apple ne donnera la liste officielle que sur scène. La présentation commencera le mercredi 28 octobre à 10 heures, heure de Los Angeles, soit 18 heures à Paris.

articles.title: Cheaper fibre fees don't spark Nigerian infrastructure investment
articles.text:
Nigeria’s states take widely different approaches to the cost of laying fibre-optic cables. Some have waived Right of Way (RoW) fees; others charge the ₦145-per-metre benchmark, while Ogun State charges up to ₦6,600 ($4.84) per metre. Yet these differences do not neatly explain where fibre infrastructure has been built, raising questions about what else drives investment.
Administrative reforms and project-specific concessions may help offset high fees, but there is little evidence that they do so systematically. The Lagos State Infrastructure Maintenance and Regulatory Agency (LASIMRA) describes itself as a one-stop regulator for utility infrastructure, and the state has announced an online permitting system to streamline approvals for fibre, masts and towers. However, the announcement does not establish whether the system has reduced processing times or costs or removed requirements such as environmental approvals.
Ogun has also reportedly waived RoW charges for a specific 250-kilometre MainOne deployment, but that historical concession does not establish that similar incentives are generally available today. There is no verified evidence of a telecom-specific tax-break programme that explains the substantial fibre networks in these high-fee states. Without access to operators’ permits, concession agreements and investment decisions, it remains unclear whether incentives offset the charges or whether companies invest despite them.
Data from the Nigerian Communications Commission’s (NCC) Ease of Doing Business portal, published in July 2026, shows that Ogun has 4,246.48 kilometres of deployed fibre, while Kano and Rivers, which charge ₦2,754 (2.02) and ₦2,256(1.65) per metre respectively, have 4,616.71 kilometres and 4,616.01 kilometres. Delta, with a rate of ₦2,706 ($1.98) per metre, has 4,202.62 kilometres.
RoW charges are only one component of deployment costs. Trenching and duct installation also depend on ground conditions, water crossings, construction methods and access to existing infrastructure. The NCC portal’s fee and deployment indicators do not provide route-level construction costs. Broader evidence establishes why this matters: the World Bank identifies civil works as the dominant component of certain broadband deployments, accounting for up to 80% of costs in some cases.
At the other end of the spectrum, Ebonyi, which charges a ₦145 benchmark, has just 586.92 kilometres of fibre. Bayelsa, at ₦850 ($0.62) per metre, has a length of 656.87 kilometres. Jigawa and Zamfara, both of which have waived the fee, have 970.10 kilometres and 1,100.98 kilometres, respectively.
The disparity raises a critical question about closing Nigeria’s connectivity gaps: what will persuade operators to invest in places they have largely overlooked? Lower fees may reduce deployment costs, but they do not necessarily make a project commercially viable. Understanding what drives investment is essential to ensuring that these reforms extend broadband to underserved communities, rather than simply lowering costs in places where operators already intend to build.
High fees, low deployment
Sango-Ota, a major town in Ogun State. Image source: Femi Adedesin-Kuti
Ogun presents a particularly striking case. Its ₦6,600 ($4.84) per metre fee is more than 45 times the ₦145 ($0.11) benchmark. A hypothetical 10-kilometre deployment would attract ₦66 million ($48,387) in RoW charges alone, compared with ₦1.45 million ($1,063) at the benchmark rate.
Despite this high charge, Ogun has more than 4,200 kilometres of deployed fibre. Kano and Rivers also have more than 4,600 kilometres each, despite charging substantially above the benchmark. These existing networks indicate that operators have built significant infrastructure in high-fee jurisdictions, driven by commercial markets, strategic transport corridors, enterprise customers, and existing telecoms infrastructure.
The comparison with low-fee states raises the opposite question. Ebonyi’s 586.92 kilometres of fibre and Bayelsa’s 656.87 kilometres are substantially below the footprints in Ogun, Kano, and Rivers. Jigawa and Zamfara also have fewer than 1,200 kilometres despite waiving RoW charges. A waiver removes one cost from a deployment project, but it does not guarantee that expected revenue will justify construction, equipment, maintenance, and security costs where demand is limited.
The picture is not uniformly unfavourable to states that have reduced or eliminated their fees. Kaduna, which has waived RoW charges, has 4,339.85 kilometres of fibre, putting it among Nigeria’s leading states for deployment. Anambra, another zero-fee state, has 2,547.34 kilometres, while Niger has 3,383.43 kilometres.
These examples matter because they show that a zero-fee policy and a substantial fibre footprint can coexist. However, total fibre figures reflect accumulated infrastructure over time rather than recent policy impacts. A state with a large network may have attracted investment before reducing its fees, while a state with a smaller network may have introduced a waiver recently and has yet to see its full effect.
Lagos exposes a separate pricing problem
Lagos and the Federal Capital Territory complicate the argument that high right-of-way (RoW) fees necessarily deter investment. The NCC portal lists Lagos’s RoW charge at ₦850 ($0.62) per metre and the FCT’s at ₦950 ($0.70). Yet Lagos has 11,586.70 kilometres of fibre, while the FCT has 6,973.13 kilometres. Together, they account for 18,559.83 kilometres, or 18.35% of Nigeria’s reported 101,148.36-kilometre fibre network.
Their sizeable networks reflect the concentration of businesses, financial institutions, government agencies, data centres and other major connectivity users in both locations. But Lagos also exposes a problem beyond its fees: inconsistent published rates. While the NCC portal lists ₦850 ($0.62) per metre, the Lagos State Infrastructure Maintenance and Regulatory Agency (LASIMRA) lists ₦1,500 ($1.10) per metre for fibre. It also publishes a ₦50,000 ($36.66) application fee and an administrative and project-management charge equivalent to 15% of permit fees.
For operators, the discrepancy makes expansion costs harder to predict. A 10-kilometre fibre route would attract a base charge of ₦8.5 million ($6,232) at the NCC-listed rate, compared with ₦15 million ($11,000) at LASIMRA’s rate—a difference of ₦6.5 million ($4,765) before additional charges. If LASIMRA’s 15% administrative and project-management fee applies to the base fibre permit charge, it would add ₦2.25 million ($1,650). Including the ₦50,000 ($36.66) application fee, the total would reach ₦17.3 million ($12,683) before construction costs. This is an illustrative calculation, not a confirmed invoice; operators need clarity on which schedule applies.
The NCC acknowledges that rates may differ and directs operators to confirm the applicable charges with LASIMRA before making payments. “Charges may vary depending on project location and scope. Operators are advised to engage the Lagos State Infrastructure Maintenance and Regulatory Agency (LASIMRA) for updated rates and guidelines,” the commission says on its website.
The problem extends beyond the amount operators pay to the uncertainty surrounding their costs. Higher upfront fees tie up capital that could fund other deployment needs, while inconsistent rates make it harder to budget for projects and assess their commercial viability.
Lagos’s extensive fibre network shows that substantial infrastructure can coexist with high charges, but it does not establish that those charges do not affect future investment. Operators must still weigh the full cost of deployment against expected demand, particularly on less profitable routes. Clear, consistently applied fees could reduce uncertainty and improve the prospects of projects that might otherwise struggle to make commercial sense.
Fibre kilometres are not capital expenditure
The length of a fibre network offers a useful measure of deployment, but it is not a direct measure of investment. Costs vary with route conditions, excavation and road reinstatement, equipment, network design, and the extent to which operators can use existing infrastructure. A longer network does not necessarily mean more capital was invested, just as a shorter one does not automatically indicate weaker investment.
Determining whether lower RoW fees attract investment requires data that links policy changes to actual deployment. The NCC and state governments should publish annual figures on new fibre laid, along with the dates of fee changes, permit applications, approval times and operators’ state-level capital expenditure. Such data would help distinguish the effect of lower fees from other factors influencing where operators build.
A commissioner in a northern state, who requested anonymity because of concerns about the upcoming general elections, said little had changed since the state adopted a ₦145-per-metre fee. The commissioner also pointed to Nasarawa, which has waived the charge but, in the commissioner’s assessment, has yet to see an improvement in infrastructure deployment. He did not provide specific figures for operator permit applications submitted before and after the adoption of the ₦145 fee.
These accounts suggest that lower fees alone may not be enough to spur investment, although assessing their effect requires time-series data on deployment and capital expenditure.
Anambra State, meanwhile, views its zero-fee policy as a long-term investment in connectivity rather than an immediate revenue driver.
“Anambra’s zero-RoW-fee policy is a strategic investment in expanding broadband infrastructure, improving connectivity and accelerating digital inclusion,” Chukwuemeka Fred Agbata Jnr., managing director and chief executive of the Anambra State ICT Agency, told TechCabal. “We see it as an enabler of long-term digital growth, with continued efforts to deepen infrastructure deployment across the state.”
Move beyond assuming cheaper fees automatically produce more fibre. Ogun, Kano, and Rivers maintain substantial networks despite high charges, while Ebonyi, Bayelsa, and Jigawa have comparatively little infrastructure despite lower fees. High fees do not halt expansion where strong commercial demand exists, just as waivers cannot single-handedly make an unviable market profitable.
For state governments, the real test is whether lower fees are followed by faster approvals, newly laid fibre, greater capital investment, and expanded connectivity beyond major urban centres. Until states systematically track and report new construction following policy changes, fee reductions remain an input into investment policy—not proof that investment has actually increased.
South Africa’s spam calls reached 17.5 billion in the first half of 2026. Now, the government wants companies to prove they have checked who they call before they press send.
The National Consumer Commission (NCC), South Africa’s consumer watchdog, launched a National Opt-Out Registry on Wednesday that will allow consumers to pre-emptively block unwanted direct marketing.
The registry is part of a sweeping government effort to tackle South Africa’s growing spam-call problem. Marketers will have to register with the system and cleanse their lists every month before running campaigns. Fintechs, banks, telcos, insurers, retailers and other digital businesses will need to build consumer opt-outs into their marketing systems.
Truecaller’s 2026 South Africa Spam Report found that there were 17.5 billion spam calls between January and June, 25.2% higher than the same period in 2025. Spam short message service (SMS) messages also jumped 58.9% to 3.7 billion
The numbers help explain why the NCC is moving beyond asking consumers to ignore or block unwanted messages and is instead imposing obligations on the companies that send them.
Parks Tau, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, said the growing sophistication of spam and scams required a stronger regulatory response.
“South Africans are becoming more alert, but alertness alone cannot substitute for a proper regulatory backstop,” Tau said at the launch. “Scam and marketing networks are becoming more sophisticated, using spoofing and artificial intelligence to reach consumers.”
The registry gives effect to Section 11 of the Consumer Protection Act, which gives consumers the right to block unwanted direct marketing communication. Tau believes the issue relates to data and privacy, as more companies rely on personal information to reach potential customers.
“Section 14 of our Constitution guarantees everyone the right to privacy. A person’s phone number, email address and time are not raw material to be harvested and traded without their consent,” he said.
For companies, however, the challenge will be translating that principle into their existing marketing systems.
The NCC said direct marketers have been able to register on the registry since September 15 and have until December 2026 to complete their registration. They will then have five months, from December to April 2027, to cleanse their marketing lists and prepare to interface with the system at no cost.
From May 2027, registered consumers will be able to pre-emptively block direct marketers from contacting them.
The registry means companies will have to account for it before launching campaigns, potentially requiring changes to customer databases, campaign-management tools, and internal compliance processes.
“This is a momentous occasion for consumers who have for years been flooded with unwanted direct marketing,” Hardin Ratshisusu, the NCC’s Acting Commissioner, said. “The National Opt-Out Registry will promote responsible direct marketing, ensuring consumers are protected from unwanted direct marketing through spam calls, texts, e-mails and other electronic communication.”
The NCC said the phased rollout will give businesses time to prepare and that it will publish further guidance while running a consumer education programme.

articles.title: Reseller says $470,000 worth of Nvidia RTX 5090s went missing at São Paulo airport
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: Thanks to the unprecedented boom in AI server and data center projects, Nvidia's most powerful GPUs have become extremely hard to come by. If a story out of Brazil is accurate, specialized thieves may now be targeting these components at specific points during shipment.
Oderço Distribuidora is a Brazilian hardware distributor that has been in business for more than 38 years, about 18 of them importing computer hardware. According to a recent message from company president Oderço Matos, the company has lost an undisclosed number of GeForce RTX 5090 cards after two pallets went "missing" at São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport.
Matos said the company has never been through anything like this. Oderço was expecting to receive pallets full of Zotac GeForce RTX 5090 cards, worth R$2.5 million (around $470,000), but the goods never reached the company, and no one has offered an explanation so far.
The company now wants to understand what happened, and how a cargo of such valuable consumer electronics can disappear inside an international airport without leaving any trace. São Paulo/Guarulhos is the main airport serving the city of São Paulo, the largest in Brazil and, by most measures, in Latin America, and one of the 50 busiest in the world by passenger traffic.
He added that the company decided to go public after receiving no explanation from public authorities or the airport itself. There is also no video footage of the pallets being moved. Oderço is looking for "answers" about the disappearance, but also hopes whoever is responsible will eventually let the company get its GPUs back.
Airport officials are reportedly unwilling to cooperate, either with the press or with Oderço. Brazilian media have received no answer about the incident, while the Brazilian Federal Police and Federal Revenue Service have yet to issue an official statement.
Technically, no one has officially confirmed that the goods were stolen. Oderço, for its part, has not provided specific details or tracking information on the Zotac cards.
Although not designed to run in data centers or accelerate AI workloads, GeForce RTX 5090 cards are now among the most sought-after pieces of computer hardware ever. Individual GPUs are selling for thousands of dollars, and recent rumors claimed the model would soon disappear from the market. Nvidia has since said the RTX 5090 is still being manufactured, but the cards are now even more expensive than they were a few days ago. I guess thieves have taken note.

articles.title: Google Traduction : la grande refonte de l'interface arrive enfin sur Android
articles.text:
Google Traduction s’offre un lifting important sur Android. Repérée sur plusieurs smartphones tournant sous la version 10.39.34.99 de l’application, la nouvelle interface évolue pour se rapprocher des standards graphiques Material 3 Expressive que l’on retrouve sur d’autres services de la marque.
Une nouvelle barre de navigation et plus de place pour saisir le texte
La barre de navigation en bas de l’interface adopte désormais un positionnement similaire à celui que l’on trouve déjà dans Google Photos ou Google Lens, par exemple. On remarque également que le champ de texte au centre est bien plus grand que sur la version précédente de l’interface.
L’ancien design à gauche, le premier redesign au milieu et le nouveau design à droite. – Source : Android Authority
Le bouton à trois points qui regroupait auparavant le sélecteur de modèle de traduction et l’option d’écriture manuscrite disparaît également. Cette dernière fonctionnalité bascule directement à l’intérieur de la boîte de texte, placée juste à côté d’une icône de microphone (légèrement modifiée elle aussi). Enfin, l’option pour coller le texte se trouve désormais sur la gauche.
Quelques compromis inévitables
En revanche, l’agrandissement important de la zone de saisie du texte laisse malheureusement trop peu de place pour afficher les raccourcis contextuels, comme celui de l’entraînement du jour ou de la reprise rapide d’une conversation. Les autres sections de l’application comme les onglets Traduction instantanée, Appareil photo et Entraînement, ne subissent pas de modifications majeures.
Source : Android Authority
À lire : Google Traduction veut faire le ménage dans nos hésitations orales
Côté graphique, on retrouve une cohérence des couleurs et des nouveaux éléments avec le style Material 3 Expressive de Google. Le déploiement de cette nouvelle version de Google Traduction se poursuit au compte-gouttes, ce qui signifie que vous devriez le voir arriver sur vos smartphones et tablettes Android dans les semaines à venir, si ce n’est pas déjà le cas.

articles.title: Plex : des pirates peuvent miner des cryptos avec votre serveur s'il n'est pas à jour
articles.text:
Plex : des pirates peuvent miner des cryptos avec votre serveur s'il n'est pas à jour
Des serveurs Plex d'utilisateurs sont activement exploités à leur insu pour miner de la crytomonnaie. Il y a heureusement une solution simple pour l'empêcher.
Le 1ᵉʳ septembre dernier, Plex déployait une "importante mise à jour de sécurité" pour Plex Media Server (1.43.3) et Plex Desktop (1.115.0). Alors, la société derrière la solution d'hébergement et de diffusion multimédia à domicile ne précisait pas contre quoi exactement cette rustine devait protéger. Depuis le 17 octobre, on en sait plus et il est urgent de mettre à jour si ce n'est pas déjà fait.
Une faille de sécurité de Plex déjà corrigée
Depuis quelques jours, des attaques avérées montrent que des pirates utilisent les failles de sécurité concernées sur des serveurs obsolètes afin de s'y infiltrer sans besoin de s'identifier. Une fois la prise de contrôle terminée, sans que l'utilisateur n'en ait conscience, ils utilisent alors l'installation pour miner de la cryptomonnaie.
Des outils comme le récent Plex2Shell et le plus connu XMRig sont utilisés. Si votre serveur Plex n'est pas à jour et que votre machine commence à chauffer et à souffrir de sérieuses lenteurs, il peut s'agir d'indices clairs que votre installation a été infiltrée.
Pour protéger son serveur Plex et son installation, deux solutions existent.
La première est d'aller vérifier manuellement que le serveur (et Plex Desktop) est à jour depuis les paramètres du logiciel, qu'il soit installé directement sur un ordinateur, un NAS ou via Docker, puis de télécharger et d'installer la mouture la plus récente proposée. Ce 19 octobre, il s'agit de la version 1.43.4.
Sinon, cela peut être un moment opportun pour tester une solution alternative, comme l'open source et gratuite Jellyfin.
