articles.title: ECOVACS DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone robot vacuum mop review - sets a new cleaning standard - Tech Guide
articles.text:
VERDICT
The Ecovacs DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone has established a new standard for robot vacuum mops. It's an investment in the cleanliness and hygiene of your home.
PROS
- Easy to set up and get started
- Excellent suction
- Next-level mopping
- Can be left alone for weeks
CONS
- Expensive for some
- Did leave dust behind after crossing threshold
- 
		
				
			VERDICT
Robot vacuum mops have come a long way with Ecovacs leading the way with its DEEBOT range and the X12S OmniCyclone has taken cleaning and convenience to another level.
Tech Guide has been testing the Ecovacs Robotics DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone since shortly after it was unveiled at the IFA Show in Berlin in September.
Ecovacs has packed in plenty of features and upgrades into the X12S which has a new level of power that makes it an effective cleaner so you can get on with other things.
At our place we placed the X12S OmniCyclone station in the corner of our main living area.
This action alone speaks volumes about the look and design of the OmniCyclone station which has a sleek look with silver brushed metal accents.
Ecovacs has even thought to tint the clear dustbin to disguise the collected dust but still make it easy see how much dust is inside when you get closer.
The unit is 38cm wide and 49cm long which is a relatively small footprint for a device as powerful as this.
Set-up is simple through the Ecovacs app and the first step is connecting the robot to your wireless network and running any firmware upgrades.
What the robot needed to do next is map your home. It went off and scanned our floor plan on its own which is then shown in the app.
The AIVI 3D 4.0 technology did a great job creating the map but also is always on the lookout for any obstacles and steers around them.
The OmniCyclone Station is where the robot charges and includes a clean water tank and a tank where the dirty water will be transferred.
It’s also where the dust is transferred from the robot into the dustbin which can be easily emptied cleanly and conveniently into your garbage.
Now at our place, our floor is mainly tiles with a couple of carpeted rooms and a rug.
There is also a laundry and a small powder room, which have slightly higher thresholds the robot easily got up and over.
We did notice a couple of times the force of getting up and over the threshold left some dust behind.
Usually it picks this up on its way out but there was one occasion where we had to clean it ourselves.
The X12S OmniCyclone robot has a side brush, an anti-tangle main brush, along with an antibacterial filter and a roller that extends to reach in closer to skirting boards and under cabinets.
The OZMO ROLLER 3.0 has improved downward pressure (4000 Pa) and higher-speed (260 RPM) scrubbing which means stains don’t stand a chance.
And the roller lifts by 1.5cm and a smart roller cover clicks into place when it moves from hard floors to stay clear of carpets to them dry and avoid cross-contamination.
The unit also has 27,000 Pa blast suction which offers 53AW of suction power.
Now we know how powerful this suction is.
At IFA in Berlin we saw the X12S suck a 25kg ball up a tube so it had no issue vacuuming dust and debris off the hard floors and carpet at our place.
X12S also has FocusJet Stain technology which can pre-treat messes with extra water through the front jets shift more stubborn stains.
This needs to be enabled in the settings and includes a way to control exactly where in your home you would prefer a no-spray zone to protect furniture and other surfaces.
We left this on and it was remarkable how it could identify these areas and soak them ahead of a thorough clean with the roller.
We normally move chairs and clear the floor when we deploy the robot but the X12S OmniCyclone can find its way in and around your furniture quite deftly.
Through a combination of its side brushes and true edge extreme edge cleaning, the X12S did a tremendous job in getting into those hard-to-reach places as well as under and around furniture.
The X12S did a great job controlling water flow so there was never any residual water. It just left dry clean floors in its wake.
In terms of cleaning quality, the X12S has set a new standard.
The robots of the past were good at maintaining a level of cleanliness but the X12S really gets to work to get through the dirt and dust and stains effectively and leave you with a spotless home.
Our tiles were clean and shiny and it was easy to see just where the robot had traversed our carpets with the suction leaving definitive tracks just like a powerful stick vac would.
The robot would regularly return to the station to clean the roller and to transfer dirty water and replace it with clean water.
At the same time it was also recharging its battery to reduce interruptions and create more efficiency.
X12S can restore 13 per cent of the battery in just 3 minutes.
The DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone is a complete cleaning solution that does a great job with your carpets and hard floors without you having to lift a finger.
It is really easy to maintain and can run on its own for weeks at a time.
The unit is priced at $2,999 which is an investment – it’s an investment in your time.
It means you get your time back instead of spending it vacuuming and mopping your floors.
VERDICT
The Ecovacs DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone has established a new standard for robot vacuum mops. It’s an investment in the cleanliness and hygiene of your home.

articles.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
articles.text:
NestJS, the TypeScript framework for building server-side Node.js applications, has released version 12, a major release that moves its core packages to ESM, adds first-class Standard Schema validation, rebuilds the CLI and introduces an official observability SDK. It follows April's roadmap, and creator Kamil Myśliwiec's announcement on X has passed 1,100 likes and 66,000 views.
The ESM change is the headline, largely because it asks so little of existing teams. Core packages now ship as ESM, but CommonJS applications keep working through Node.js require(esm) support, which is why v12 requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. nest new now asks whether to generate a CJS or ESM project, with ESM projects defaulting to Vitest and oxlint, while Rspack replaces webpack as the monorepo bundler. Developer Anton Chapala's preview benchmarks found no meaningful startup or memory gains from ESM, concluding it "is a massive cleanup of tooling and configuration debt" rather than a performance upgrade.
Day-to-day ergonomics change most around validation. Route decorators such as @Body(), @Query() and @Param() accept a schema option taking any Standard Schema compatible object, so Zod, Valibot and ArkType work without third-party wrappers once the new pipe is registered.
class-validator remains the documented default. Blogger iiaku argued that building on a spec rather than on Zod directly "keeps the choice in my hands while removing the boilerplate", though a commenter on ByteIota's preview coverage noted that types must still be annotated by hand because Nest continues to rely on legacy TypeScript decorators.
The most debated addition is @nestjs/observe, which hooks into Nest's own lifecycle through a new instrument option instead of patching the HTTP server, reporting traces in terms of controllers and providers. APM vendor Scout Monitoring acknowledged the richer context but warned the SDK is "NestJS-only", lacks cross-stack correlation out of the box and risks "vendor lock-in at the framework level". A new nest deploy command, forwarding to the Mau platform, points the same way towards first-party services.
The NestJS Observe dashboard, source: Trilon
Upgrading from v11 means installing the latest CLI with npm i -g @nestjs/cli@latest and running nest upgrade, which moves every @nestjs/* package to v12, bumps TypeScript to v6 and applies mechanical changes such as the GraphQL Playground to GraphiQL switch and the NATS v3 client swap.
It deliberately does not convert projects to ESM, Vitest or oxlint. The migration guide covers the rest, including lifecycle hook ordering and Joi v18.
One GitHub issue prompted docs noting AWS Lambda runtimes need --experimental-require-module, while others report path aliases breaking under ESM and Fastify middleware exceptions hanging. The follow-up v12.1 has since added built-in cookies, CSRF protection and security headers.
NestJS is an open-source, MIT-licensed framework for building efficient and scalable server-side applications with TypeScript. It combines an Angular-inspired module and dependency injection architecture with Express and Fastify support, and has more than 76,000 stars on GitHub.

articles.title: Raz-de-marée ou coup de com' ? L'incroyable rupture de stock de l'iPhone Duo
articles.text:
Vous aviez soigneusement économisé pour glisser la toute dernière révolution technologique sous le sapin de Noël, à savoir l’iPhone Duo, le tout premier smartphone pliant d’Apple ? Il va peut-être falloir préparer une enveloppe avec un mot d’excuse, ou réfléchir activement à un plan de secours.
La semaine dernière, Apple a officiellement ouvert les précommandes de son petit bijou. Si l’on se doutait que les fans seraient au rendez-vous, l’engouement général a pris des proportions impressionnantes.
La firme de Cupertino n’a d’ailleurs pas caché son enthousiasme. Lors d’une déclaration accordée à la chaîne CNBC, Apple a qualifié cette ferveur initiale d’« absolument extraordinaire ».
Mais ce succès fulgurant a un prix, et ce sont les consommateurs qui vont en faire les frais. Aux États-Unis, les délais d’expédition s’allongent à vue d’œil pour quiconque passe commande aujourd’hui. Si vous espériez frimer avec votre téléphone pliant pendant les repas de fin d’année, c’est raté. Les dates de livraison pour les nouvelles précommandes ont d’ores et déjà glissé jusqu’en janvier 2027.
Un succès à nuancer tout de même
Il faut bien sûr toujours prendre avec un grain de sable ce genre de déclarations. Comme nous ne disposons d’aucun chiffre, ni les stocks qui étaient disponibles au départ, ni le niveau d’engagement que visait Apple, la marque peut très bien trouver que cela dépasse ses propres attentes, sans que ces attentes ne soient particulièrement impressionnantes dans l’absolu pour un observateur extérieur. De même, il n’est pas exclu que la communication en forme de bombage de torse puisse servir à calmer les fans déçus. Mieux vaut tourner une difficulté logistique en victoire plutôt qu’en échec.
Conscient de la frustration générée par ces délais à rallonge, Apple a assuré travailler d’arrache-pied pour expédier son nouveau produit vedette le plus rapidement possible et continue d’accepter les commandes en ligne.
On peut tout de même reconnaître que l’organisation est plutôt transparente. Les acheteurs de la première heure pourront récupérer leur commande en boutique dès le 23 octobre. Pour la vague suivante, les réceptions s’étaleront entre les mois de novembre et décembre, cela est déjà entendu.
Quant aux retardataires laissés sur le carreau ? Il reste un petit espoir. L’Apple Store en ligne suggère aux clients de revérifier les disponibilités pour un retrait en magasin à partir du 24 octobre. Attention toutefois : la firme de Cupertino n’a pas garanti que ses boutiques physiques disposeraient de stocks en libre-service.
Enfin, la solution viendra peut-être des distributeurs tiers. Des enseignes comme La Fnac, Boulanger ou Carrefour affichent encore la possibilité de précommander pour le 23 octobre. Une dernière fenêtre de tir qui risque, elle aussi, de se refermer très vite.

articles.title: Son fils montre “le vieux tableau du salon” à l'IA Gemini : la toile achetée une bouchée de pain part à 220 000 €
articles.text:
Son fils montre “le vieux tableau du salon” à l'IA Gemini : la toile achetée une bouchée de pain part à 220 000 €
Soixante ans durant, un portrait déniché dans une friperie new-yorkaise a trôné au-dessus d'un canapé familial sans que personne ne sache qui l'avait peint. Il a suffi d'un cliché soumis à l'IA de Google pour remonter jusqu'à un maître écossais, puis jusqu'à une salle des ventes d'Édimbourg.
En 1966, Helene Plotkin, jeune professeure d'art diplômée en histoire de l'art, cherche de quoi habiller son nouvel appartement à White Plains, en lisière de New York. Dans une boutique de seconde main, un portrait la happe : une femme en noir, alanguie dans un fauteuil rouge vif, des éclats orangés jetés à la brosse. Elle le paie moins de 100 dollars. La signature est illisible, et une étiquette au dos parle d'un "Portrait of Miss Don Wauchope". La toile survivra aux parties de ballon de ses fils dans le salon.
	
Je n'y ai jamais, jamais pensé. J'adorais ce tableau, c'est tout.
Gemini remonte la piste de F.C.B. Cadell
En décembre 2025, son fils Barry photographie l'œuvre et la confie à Gemini. D'après le New York Times, l'assistant relève les accents orangés, le fond lilas et le chic Art déco, autant de traits "indubitablement" propres à Francis Campbell Boileau Cadell (1883-1937). Ce Coloriste écossais, formé à Paris, admirait Matisse. L'IA déchiffre la signature, invite à scruter le dos du châssis et souffle même deux noms d'experts chez Lyon & Turnbull : Nick Curnow et Alice Strang.
Les archives révèlent ensuite une vente chez Christie's, à Londres, en 1966, pour 21 livres. C'était quelques mois à peine avant que la toile n'échoue outre-Atlantique, par un chemin resté mystérieux.
Une erreur corrigée, puis 189 200 livres aux enchères
Les spécialistes confirment l'attribution et rectifient un point : Gemini voyait dans la modèle Bethia Hamilton Don Wauchope, dont le nom figure au verso. Le turban vert désigne en réalité May Easter, muse rousse de Cadell, déjà peinte dans Pink and Gold. Rebaptisée Interior: The Lady in Black et datée du milieu des années 1920, l'œuvre a été adjugée 189 200 livres frais compris, soit environ 254 000 dollars et quelque 220 000 euros, le 4 juin 2026 lors de la vente Scottish Paintings & Sculpture. Elle était estimée entre 150 000 et 200 000 livres, et c'est un acheteur privé qui l'a emportée.
	
Cette histoire montre que l'IA peut vous mettre sur la voie, mais rien ne vaut une véritable expertise.
Âgée de 88 ans et installée en Floride, Helene Plotkin destine la somme à ses fils. Elle garde un vœu : que ses petits-enfants croisent un jour "le tableau de Mamie" aux cimaises d'un musée.

Banking
South Africa wants all ATMs to become unbranded
South Africa is not trying to kill cash. It is trying to make using it cheaper.
The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) wants the country’s more than 30,000 automated teller machines (ATMs) to become a shared, unbranded network. Small withdrawals, deposits, and balance enquiries would be free below a set limit, regardless of which bank owns the machine.
What happened? A pilot starts in January 2027. By March, the central bank wants to create a national cash utility, then begin folding cash centres run by companies such as SBV and Fidelity into that system by mid-year. The first white-label ATMs are expected before the end of 2027.
Explain like I’m new here: Today, each bank runs its own ATM network, cash centres, and logistics. That means duplicated machines, vehicles, routes, and vaults, all moving physical money around. SARB wants to pool much of that infrastructure and make ATMs work more like a national utility.
The economics explain the urgency. South Africa has about R180.65 billion ($10.9 billion) in cash in circulation, according to the SARB. The broader annual economic cost of using cash—including fees, travel, time, and crime-related losses—is estimated at nearly R90 billion ($5.5 billion). Cash accounts for about 56% of consumer transactions in South Africa, according to a Reserve Bank-commissioned study using 2024 as its base year, even as digital payment alternatives expanded.
Between the lines: Fewer cash transactions do not automatically make ATMs cheaper to run. The machines, guards, cash vans, and vaults still cost money. When those costs are spread across fewer transactions, each withdrawal costs more. Rural and low-income areas are usually the first places where banks cut machines.
A shared network flips that model. Banks stop duplicating the same infrastructure, while the central bank can place ATMs where access is most needed.
What to watch: The difficult part will be getting banks to surrender some control over machines they currently brand, price, and use to keep customers in their banking networks. If the model works, South Africa will not have fewer ATMs. But it will have fewer reasons for every bank to have its own.

Capital Market
Banque du Caire may raise IPO stake to 45%
Egypt may make one of its biggest upcoming listings even bigger.
Banque Misr is considering selling up to 45% of Banque du Caire, Egypt’s sixth-largest commercial bank by assets, in its upcoming initial public offering (IPO), up from the 30% announced on October 11. Investment banks working on the deal recommended the bigger sale after roadshows drew strong investor interest globally.
Here’s a simple back-of-napkin maths: At Banque du Caire’s reported valuation of EGP 80 billion–EGP 80.5 billion ($1.5 billion–$1.51 billion), according to local publication Asharq Business, a 45% stake would be worth between EGP 36 billion–EGP 36.2 billion ($670 million–$674 million), compared with EGP 24 billion–EGP 24.2 billion ($447 million–$451 million) for 30%.
Those figures assume the shares sell at the reported valuation. Bloomberg reported on Sunday that the bank was seeking up to EGP 24.25 billion ($454 million) from a 30% sale and could increase the stake to 45%, depending on demand. The larger offer would take Egypt past that target, becoming the country’s largest listing in years.
Catch up: This IPO has been a decade in the making. Egypt first announced plans to float 20% of Banque du Caire in March 2016. The bank’s shares were provisionally listed on the Egyptian Exchange in 2017, but the sale was delayed. Another attempt in 2020 was shelved after COVID-19 hit global markets.
Another important detail: Banque du Caire will not receive the money. The IPO entirely consists of existing shares owned by Banque Misr, its state-owned shareholder. Selling 45% puts about 6.86 billion shares into investors’ hands compared with 4.58 billion under the current plan. Trading is expected to begin in November.
Between the lines: Going bigger does more than raise extra cash for the state. It leaves more Banque du Caire shares available for investors to trade after the IPO, which could help make the stock more liquid. More importantly, increasing the sale because investors asked for more would signal that foreign appetite for Egypt’s privatisation programme is returning.
Zoom out: Egypt’s stock exchange already has a strong line-up for Q4. MNT-Halan, the country’s first fintech unicorn, would begin trading on October 20, after its floated shares were at least three times oversubscribed. The planned listing aims to raise $150 million, with wide retail investors’ participation expected. With Banque du Caire taking over the following month, there’s a lot of excitement in Egypt right now.

Telecoms
Vodacom keeps control of Safaricom amid ongoing court case
In June, Vodacom, one of Africa’s largest telecom companies, bought a majority stake in Safaricom, the operator of M-PESA. Four months later, a Kenyan court said it should undo the sale. Now, the shares remain in Vodacom’s custody as the legal battle over who gets to keep them moves to the next round.
What happened? On October 13, Kenya’s Court of Appeal ordered that the current position around the Safaricom shares and the $1.9 billion purchase price remain unchanged while it fast-tracks the appeal. That means Vodacom remains the registered holder of the 15% stake it bought from the Kenyan government.
Explain like I’m new here: Vodacom bought 15% of Safaricom from the Kenyan government, plus another effective 5% from Vodafone, its subsidiary, taking its stake from 35% to a majority of 55%. However, the deal ran into legal trouble.
Critics, including broadcaster Tony Gachoka and academic Frederick Ogola, challenged the sale, arguing that the government had not properly involved the public in the decision. The court froze it in March, then unfroze it in June. In September, the High Court declared the transaction unconstitutional and ordered the stake returned to the Kenyan government, throwing a spanner in the state’s plan to finance projects from those proceeds.
What’s the state of Safaricom’s ownership? Because Vodacom remains the registered holder of the shares, it can continue exercising the rights attached to its majority stake, including voting as a shareholder and participating in decisions that require shareholder approval. If the High Court judgment survives the appeal, Vodacom would lose the 15% stake it bought from the government and fall back to roughly 40%.
Don’t miss Moonshot 2026 for anything in the world!
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Join us on October 28 & 29, 2026. Get your ticket.
Regulation
Ghana is changing how it collects VAT from foreign digital services
Ghana is looking to increase revenue, and taxing customers on the foreign digital services they use—such as Netflix, YouTube, and WhatsApp—is one strategy.
On October 15, the country launched Real-Time VAT (RTVAT) that lets the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), the country’s taxman, collect value-added tax (VAT) on qualifying digital services when customers pay foreign providers through Ghana-issued cards, mobile money accounts, and other digital payment channels.
The system applies to non-resident companies selling electronic services to customers in Ghana, including streaming platforms, cloud storage providers, software subscriptions, online advertising, and digital marketplaces.
Explain like I’m new here: This didn’t start today. Ghana has required foreign digital service providers to register for VAT since 2022. The GRA created an online registration and filing system for non-resident e-commerce businesses, requiring them to declare their Ghanaian sales and remit the taxes they collect.
However, Ghana cannot send a tax officer to a provider’s office monthly to check whether the right VAT was paid. Under RTVAT, when a Ghanaian customer pays for an eligible foreign digital service using a Ghana-issued card, mobile money account, or wallet, the payment provider can identify the transaction, withhold the applicable tax, and send it to the GRA.
Why is Ghana doing this? The GRA said that as of October 14, about 92 non-resident digital service providers were registered on the tax collection portal, while about 100 others either failed to collect the required taxes or haven’t remitted them. The authority previously estimated that an automated collection system could raise more than GH¢2.5 billion ($213 million) annually, compared with roughly GH¢515 million ($44 million) a year it currently collects.
What changes for users? If your Netflix bill already includes Ghanaian taxes, the GRA said RTVAT should not make you pay them twice. However, if a foreign provider previously didn’t collect the required tax, your final bill could now rise by 20%.
Zoom out: Banks, mobile money operators, payment service providers and other licenced payment processors handling these transactions must integrate with the RTVAT system. They must now correctly identify taxable transactions, collect and remit the right amount, and reverse the tax when refunds or chargebacks happen.

articles.title: Nvidia says the RTX 5090 isn't discontinued, but most listings are over $9,300
articles.text:
Why it matters: Reports of the RTX 5090's death may have been exaggerated. That's according to Nvidia, which recently confirmed that the flagship consumer card was still in production. However, that denial doesn't seem to line up with Nvidia's own US marketplace, where the RTX 5090 is conspicuously absent.
Prolific leaker MEGAsizeGPU last week wrote that Nvidia had "confirmed" the GB202 chip used in the RTX 5090 would no longer be used in new RTX 5090 cards. Instead, future supplies of the GPU would be used exclusively for RTX Pro Blackwell-based models.
 – MEGAsizeGPU (@Zed__Wang) October 10, 2026
Another leaker, Hongxing2020, said Nvidia would replace the RTX 5090 with a new RTX 5080 variant packing 24GB of VRAM.
Now, 4Gamers reports that Nvidia has denied the reports at an RTX Spark launch party event in Taipei, Taiwan.
Jeff Fisher, Nvidia's senior vice president of personal computing, talked about CUDA and how there would be no AI market today without it.
"The supply chain (capacity) is indeed somewhat constrained, but NVIDIA is fully committed to bringing products to market. Although there are other variants of the RTX 5090 chip, it has not been discontinued, and Nvidia will continue shipping, which is very important," Fisher said, according to the machine-translated site.
That all sounds pretty definitive, but it's at odds with Nvidia's official US marketplace. The option to see RTX 5090 cards has been removed completely, with the RTX 5080 sitting at the top of the list.
There are some RTX 5090 cards available on Newegg. The majority are over $9,300, with the most expensive model priced at $10,899. Amazon has just one, priced at $11,565. It ships from Germany in 2 to 3 weeks. There are almost none sitting on shelves in brick-and-mortar stores, either.
As for the RTX 5080 24GB, or Super, as it might be called, there are rumors it will launch next year. It's long been assumed that the Super series has been canceled, but there have been claims that it could land next year – or even sooner.
With the RTX 6000 series not expected until 2028 and rival AMD's RDNA 5 cards tipped to get here in late 2027, perhaps Nvidia will launch an RTX 5080 Super at some point, though we can only hazard a guess at its price.
As we all know, the situation comes down to the massive demand for AI products and the fact Nvidia makes a lot more money from these expensive professional and enterprise cards. Despite Fisher's claims, it wouldn't be a surprise to learn that the RTX 5090 is effectively dead.

articles.title: Aproveite: Nintendo Switch 2 entra em oferta relâmpago no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Aproveite: Nintendo Switch 2 entra em oferta relâmpago no Mercado Livre
Switch 2 com proposta multiuso e acesso a jogos exclusivos da Nintendo recebe raro desconto de 15% no Pix, mas promoção acaba ao meio-dia de hoje!
O Switch 2 está saindo por apenas R$ 3.814 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O mais recente console da Nintendo, que possui uma proposta de múltiplo uso e acesso a jogos exclusivos, recebe desconto de 15% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.499.
Embora não seja o menor preço histórico, esta é uma rara chance de adquirir o console por um preço menor, mas corra (mesmo!): a oferta relâmpago acaba ao meio-dia desta segunda-feira (19).
O destaque do Switch 2 é sua proposta como console híbrido. Assim como seu antecessor, o sistema mais vendido da Nintendo, ele pode ser usado conectado à TV por meio da dock, como portátil com os Joy-Cons conectados, ou como semiportátil apoiado sobre uma mesa.
Sua tela LCD de 7,9″, usada nos modos portátil e semiportátil, conta com resolução Full HD e taxa de 120 fps. Quando ligado à dock, o sistema suporta 4K a 60 fps ou 120 fps em 1080p e 2K, com HDR10 em TVs compatíveis, oferecendo uma experiência gamer fluida.
O hardware interno inclui um chip Nvidia T239 customizado, 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento expansível com cartões microSD especiais. Os Joy-Cons podem ser usados como um mouse quando apoiados em uma superfície, e a dock traz uma porta Ethernet nativa para conexões de rede mais estáveis.
O Switch 2 suporta boa parte da biblioteca do Switch original, e tem acesso a inúmeros games de franquias exclusivas da Nintendo, como Mario, The Legend of Zelda, Pokémon, Donkey Kong e Metroid, indisponíveis em sistemas concorrentes.
Sua bateria de 5.200 mAh resiste a até 6 horas de uso, segundo a fabricante. A dock é capaz de carregar o sistema quando usado como console de mesa, sem interromper a jogatina.
O Switch 2 (apenas R$ 3.814 no Pix) tem acesso ao Nintendo Switch Online, serviço que oferece jogos em rede e benefícios exclusivos para assinantes, como games clássicos de sistemas legados da companhia centenária de Quioto.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Tesla y SpaceX integrarían sus tecnologías de IA en una fusión que se anunciaría antes de diciembre de 2026
articles.text:
Barclays anticipa que Tesla y SpaceX, ambas lideradas por Elon Musk, podrían anunciar una fusión antes de que se celebre la junta general anual del fabricante de vehículos eléctricos, prevista como fecha límite para el 6 de diciembre de 2026.
Según los analistas encabezados por Dan Levy, el valor real de la operación no estaría tanto en las sinergias financieras como en la integración vertical de las tecnologías de inteligencia artificial de ambas compañías.
Por qué cobra fuerza la fusión entre Tesla y SpaceX
La posibilidad de que Tesla y SpaceX terminen fusionadas dejó de ser una especulación aislada para convertirse en un escenario que gana adeptos entre inversores y analistas.
“La posibilidad de una fusión entre Tesla y SpaceX se ha convertido cada vez más en la expectativa generalizada”, escribieron los analistas de Barclays en una nota dirigida a sus clientes.
El equipo liderado por Dan Levy planteó, sin embargo, un matiz sobre los tiempos del anuncio: “Aunque es posible que el momento del anuncio de la fusión entre TSLA y SPCX se retrase hasta finales de octubre o, tal vez, incluso hasta principios de noviembre, creemos que ese retraso podría complicar cada vez más la aprobación de la fusión en el marco de la junta general anual”.
Esa expectativa se intensificó después de que SpaceX completara este año una oferta pública inicial récord, un hito que reavivó las conjeturas sobre el futuro corporativo conjunto de ambas firmas.
Bloomberg News había informado en enero que SpaceX contempló en su momento una fusión con Tesla antes de optar finalmente por adquirir xAI, la startup de inteligencia artificial fundada por Musk.
Los vínculos comerciales que ya unen a ambas compañías
Más allá de la especulación bursátil, Tesla y SpaceX sostienen desde hace tiempo una red de relaciones comerciales que se superponen, además de compartir a Musk como director ejecutivo.
SpaceX ha comprado camionetas Tesla Cybertruck por un monto que supera los USD 100 millones, mientras que xAI figura entre los principales clientes de las baterías a escala industrial que produce Tesla.
A esa relación se suma Terafab, un proyecto conjunto de fabricación de chips orientado a producir semiconductores para los vehículos eléctricos de Tesla, sus robotaxis y los robots Optimus, además de un chip diseñado específicamente para los satélites orbitales de inteligencia artificial de SpaceX.
Musk se refirió públicamente a ese nivel de convergencia durante una conferencia de resultados reciente, en la que señaló que Tesla se solapa “en tantos frentes con SpaceX”.
En el plano bursátil, las acciones de Tesla se mantuvieron prácticamente sin cambios en las operaciones fuera de horario a las 17:00 horas en Nueva York tras conocerse el análisis de Barclays, mientras que los títulos de SpaceX registraron un ligero descenso.
Qué obstáculos podrían frenar la aprobación de la fusión
El principal escollo para concretar el acuerdo, según Barclays, pasaría por los votos de los accionistas, ya que tanto los de Tesla como los de SpaceX tendrían que dar su visto bueno a la operación.
“Aproximadamente el 11% del total de votos en circulación en la Junta General Anual de Tesla de 2025 correspondían a ‘votos no emitidos por intermediarios’, que en la práctica se contabilizan como votos ‘en contra’, y sospechamos que Tesla intentará aumentar la participación de los accionistas en una posible votación sobre la fusión con SpaceX”, escribieron los analistas de la entidad.
Ese porcentaje de abstenciones técnicas explica, en parte, por qué Barclays considera que cualquier demora en el anuncio formal de la fusión jugaría en contra de sus posibilidades de aprobación dentro del plazo que marca la junta anual de diciembre.

articles.title: British payments unicorn Zilch invests €91 million in larger London headquarters amid continued growth | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Zilch, the British intelligent payments unicorn with 6 million customers, has today announced it is committing €91 million (£77 million) to double its London office capacity with a move to a significantly larger headquarters in Victoria.
This comes off the back of a €150 million debt and equity raise back in November in 2025 – as covered by EU-Startups.
The move will see Zilch take over floors four and five of 40 Grosvenor Place, a 33,160sq ft space that can accommodate more than 400 employees. The investment will go towards a 10-year lease as the business continues to scale its operations and plans to create more jobs in the UK.
Philip Belamant, co-founder and CEO of Zilch, says: “It has been a transformational year for the business with a number of significant milestones, and our customers moving beyond £8 billion of spend across every region in the UK.
“As we continue to expand rapidly, our new headquarters reflect the scale of our ambition and the momentum behind our growth. This is an important investment in Zilch’s future, giving our team an incredible base to attract exceptional talent at home and beyond. We are proud to be investing further in the UK as we enter the next phase of growth.”
Zilch’s headquarters investment comes amid financing activity across European consumer credit and payments in 2026.
According to EU-Startups’ coverage, fellow UK companies Primer raised €86.2 million to develop its AI-powered payments infrastructure, Vuelo secured €64 million for its travel financing platform, and Plend obtained a credit facility of up to €58.3 million.
Elsewhere, Barcelona-based ID Finance secured €545 million in debt and equity to expand its Plazo consumer finance platform, while Madrid-based BCAS raised €30 million for flexible education financing.
Together with the €83 million secured by London-based Sokin and Manchester-based Ryft’s €23 million Series B, these announcements represent approximately €889.5 million in disclosed financing and credit facilities during 2026.
This data paints the FinTech sector, especially the UK FinTech sector, to be a rich and highly active ecosystem – providing context for Zilch’s competition and growth.
City Minister Rt Hon Lucy Rigby KC MP adds: “This is a major milestone for Zilch and it’s brilliant to see their continued success. The UK is a FinTech powerhouse and I’m committed to backing the sector to thrive and grow.”
Founded in 2018, Zilch is an intelligent payments platform, combining debit, credit, instalments, earned wage access, credit building, deals and rewards.
The new headquarters is the latest announcement in a period of growth for Zilch, including the acquisition of Fjord Bank (announced back in January 2026), which is expected to complete in the first half of 2027 and will lay the foundation of its European expansion, a multi-year strategic partnership with Visa and becoming Arsenal FC’s Official Way to Pay.

articles.title: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock
Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models, on both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints, where the model is available.
Whether you call Claude through Boto3 and the bedrock-runtime APIs or through the Messages API and the bedrock-mantle endpoint, you can now receive schema-compliant JSON responses that conform to a defined structure. You no longer need custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing.
Practical applications
With structured outputs for Claude on Amazon Bedrock, you can automate reliable, schema-compliant tasks across industries. Examples include extracting every required field from financial earnings reports and compliance documents, parsing clinical notes into Electronic Health Records (EHR), and enriching product catalogs with consistent, validated results. You can also analyze contracts for key terms, parties, and obligations, or power intelligent support ticket routing where intents, sentiments, and entities always match your application’s data model.
What changes with structured outputs on Amazon Bedrock
Structured outputs use constrained decoding to enforce your JSON schema during token generation, not after the fact. The model doesn’t produce tokens that would violate your schema. This changes output formatting from probabilistic to deterministic.
Two complementary mechanisms are now available on both Amazon Bedrock endpoints:
| Feature | Purpose | Use case | 
| JSON Schema output format | Control the model’s response structure | Data extraction, report generation, API responses | 
| Strict tool use | Validate tool parameters against schemas | Agentic workflows, function calling, multi-step automation | 
What this means for you
Each response is a valid JSON, so you no longer encounter JSON.parse() errors or parsing exceptions. Responses are also type safe: field types are enforced, and required fields are always present. Because outputs always conform to your schema, you don’t need retries to handle schema violations, making your integration more reliable. Structured outputs also constrains responses to only the fields your schema defines, which reduces output token count and can lower inference costs for high-volume workloads. These properties make structured outputs production ready, so you can deploy at scale without additional schema-validation code.
Supported models and availability
Structured outputs works with batch inference, so you can process large volumes of requests asynchronously while still receiving schema-compliant outputs. On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, it also works with cross-Region inference, so you can use it across AWS Regions without additional setup. If you need responses in real time, you can stream structured responses as typed events.
How it works
When you make a request with a JSON schema, here’s what happens behind the scenes:
- Schema validation – Amazon Bedrock validates your JSON schema against the supported JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 subset.
- Grammar compilation – For new schemas, Amazon Bedrock compiles a grammar artifact (the first request might take slightly longer).
- Caching – Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours, making subsequent requests faster.
- Constrained generation – The model generates tokens that produce valid JSON matching your schema.
Performance considerations
For performance, the first request with a new schema might take longer because Amazon Bedrock compiles a grammar artifact before generation begins. After that initial compilation, subsequent requests using the same schema run with minimal overhead because the compiled grammar is cached. This cache is scoped to your account and lasts for 24 hours from first access. Changing the structure of your JSON schema invalidates the cache and triggers a fresh compilation, while changing only the name or description fields leaves the cached grammar intact.
Getting started: Structured outputs with the InvokeModel API (bedrock-runtime)
The InvokeModel API takes the Anthropic-native request body, so the schema goes in output_config.format as a JSON object rather than a JSON string. The following example shows how to extract the structured lead data from a customer email using boto3 with an Anthropic Claude model:
Python

The response conforms to your schema. No additional validation is required.
For additional API usage examples, including the Messages API, see the accompanying sample notebook.
Strict tool use for agentic workflows
Amazon Bedrock Mantle is designed for agentic applications with server-side tools, background inference, and stateful conversations. With strict tool use on the bedrock-mantle endpoint, you can now guarantee that tool parameters match your input schema exactly. The following example shows how to define a tool with strict schema enforcement:
Setting strict: true constrains the model’s tool input to match your schema exactly. The location field is always a string, and the unit field is always either celsius or fahrenheit. The model can’t add fields outside your schema, so the tool input contains only what your schema specifies.
This is especially valuable for agentic use cases on Amazon Bedrock Mantle, where models orchestrate multi-step workflows with server-side tools like web search and code interpreter.
Top use cases for Claude structured outputs
Structured outputs reduce error-handling complexity the most in three common patterns:
- Data extraction: Extract fields from invoices, contracts, email, and transcripts into JSON that always matches your schema, ready to load into databases or customer relationship management (CRM) systems.
- Reliable agent tool calls: Validate tool arguments against their schemas at generation time, so multi-step agent workflows run without failures from malformed input.
- Classification at scale: Classify tickets, leads, or content by intent, priority, and sentiment for routing, moderation, and evaluation.
Claude Haiku 5.5 reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads such as summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests. The following example shows how to classify and route incoming data using the Invoke API and Haiku 5.5:
Requirements and best practices
To use structured outputs effectively on Amazon Bedrock, follow these guidelines:
- Set additionalProperties: false on all objects: This is required for structured outputs to work. Without it, your schema won’t be accepted.
- Use descriptive field names and descriptions: Models use property names and descriptions to understand what data to extract. Clear names like customer_email outperform generic names like field1.
- Use enum for constrained values: When a field has a limited set of valid values, use enum to constrain options.
- Start basic, then add complexity: Begin with the minimum required fields and add complexity incrementally. Basic schemas compile faster, are easier to debug, and keep your request payload lean because the schema counts toward the Converse API payload size.
- Reuse schemas to benefit from caching: Structure your application to reuse schemas across requests. The 24-hour grammar cache improves performance for repeated queries.
- Check the stop reason in every response: Two scenarios can produce non-conforming responses: refusals (when the model declines for safety reasons) and token limits (when max_tokens is reached before completing). Handle both cases in your code.
- Test with realistic data before deployment: Validate your schemas against production-representative inputs. Edge cases in real data often reveal schema design issues.
For additional best practices and schema design recommendations, see Structured outputs in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
Supported JSON Schema features
- All basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null.
- enum (strings, numbers, booleans, or nulls only).
- const, anyOf, allOf (with limitations).
- $ref, $def, and definitions (internal references only).
- String formats: date-time, time, date, duration, email, hostname, uri, ipv4, ipv6, uuid.
- Array minItems (only values 0 and 1).
Not supported
These keywords are accepted by the API but are not enforced during generation. A request that includes them returns a successful response, and the model can still return values that violate them. Validate these constraints in your application rather than relying on the schema to enforce them.
- Recursive schemas.
- External $ref references.
- Numerical constraints (minimum, maximum, multipleOf).
- String constraints (minLength, maxLength).
- additionalProperties set to anything other than false.
Conclusion
Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock provides the reliability that production AI applications require. It is available now on both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints. By combining JSON Schema output format and strict tool use, you can build data pipelines that need no additional validation. You can also create reliable agentic workflows and production AI applications without custom parsing or retry logic.
Structured outputs for Claude on Amazon Bedrock is now generally available. To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation and explore our sample notebook.
What workflows could validated, schema-compliant JSON improve in your organization? Share your feedback and questions in the comments.

articles.title: Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests
articles.text:
Arm claims AGI CPU delivers double the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in independent analysis — new CPU evaluation methodology developed by Arm evaluates agentic AI performance across seven workloads
AGI CPU delivers a 20% average per-chip performance lead
Arm announced last week that its AGI CPU, the company's data center CPU for agentic AI workloads, delivers twice the performance per rack as AMD EPYC 9755, calculated from chip performance and server-power assumptions measured across seven workloads. The claim stems from modeled rack results from tests aligned with Arm’s new CPU evaluation methodology, developed with support from Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI.
The results — verified in an Arm-commissioned independent analysis by Signal65 — do not establish the AGI CPU as the overall leader for agentic AI, as they apply to the selected processors, workloads, and configuration. They also use the specific Arm-developed evaluation methodology that Arm says should be the new standard for assessing performance. However, other chipmakers like AMD and Intel make performance claims based on different benchmarks. So, how is Agentic AI evolving CPU performance benchmarks, what does Arm propose to measure, and how do the different approaches compare?
Arm’s new CPU evaluation methodology
Agentic AI is changing the role of CPUs in modern AI data centers, requiring them to handle complex, multi-step workflows. Beyond inference, which the accelerator handles, AI agents execute tools, retrieve data, and maintain state within isolated environments, acting like virtual users. The CPU handles these critical surrounding workloads, from running those tools and serving database or API requests to preparing data and coordinating work for accelerators.
As these workloads scale rapidly with agentic capabilities, it becomes increasingly important to gauge CPU performance not just by how many agents can run concurrently, but also by how much useful work gets done. Arm argues that CPU performance is increasingly defined by how much useful work a system can sustain while staying responsive. Supporting more agents simultaneously offers limited benefit if their executions throttle or accelerators have to sit idle waiting for the CPU. Power, cooling, and physical space also limit how much hardware operators can deploy, extending the performance question to the rack.
Arm’s proposed methodology for evaluating CPU performance, developed with support from Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI, centers on representative agent workloads, repeatable CPU measurements, and validation against end-to-end task outcomes. In practical terms, the methodology identifies the tools and services an agent uses, measures their CPU performance under controlled conditions, and checks whether improvements help the agent complete its task. For example, a database test can establish how quickly a system handles transactions. An end-to-end evaluation would then examine whether faster database access actually improves the workflow that depends on it.
Executing the second aspect of the methodology, making these comparisons repeatable, presents another challenge, as an agent might choose different commands or take a different route through a task each time it runs. Model inference and remote services also introduce delays. Arm proposes replaying recorded agent actions to separate CPU performance from this variability, allowing different systems to execute a consistent sequence of work. Its whitepaper sets out a framework for selecting and interpreting these measurements, leaving the industry to develop an agreed benchmark suite and scoring approach.
To evaluate the CPU work described in its framework, Arm ran seven workloads — spanning tooling, agentic workflows, and reasoning/planning, plus Sandbench, which measures sandbox-creation overhead for agent execution — on its AGI CPU and AMD’s EPYC 9755. The tests combine established server applications with benchmarks focused on agent workflows.
| Workloads and breakdowns |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Workload | What it represents | Metric | 
| MySQL | Transactional database behind agent tools | Transactions per second | 
| NGINX | Web and API request handling | Requests per second | 
| Milvus | Vector search for retrieval | Queries per second | 
| Terminal-Bench 2 | 72 agent task types in sandboxed containers, 128 copies at once | Task completion time | 
| SWE-bench replay | Software-engineering agent workflow, 259 tasks | Tasks per minute | 
| fastText | CPU word-representation training | Words per second | 
| vLLM CPU overhead | CPU serving overhead with model compute bypassed | Requests per second | 
The vLLM result measures the CPU work around model execution, not GPU inference throughput. Similarly, the report’s “reasoning/planning” category groups supporting CPU workloads and does not assess how intelligently a model reasons.
ARM AGI CPU vs AMD EPYC 9755
For the tests, Arm used two AGI CPU configurations because of hardware availability: a 128-core chip at 2.8 GHz with DDR5-7200 for Terminal-Bench 2 and SWE-bench replay, and a 136-core chip at 3.2 GHz with DDR5-8000 for the other five workloads. The AMD comparison used one socket of the 128-core EPYC 9755 with DDR5-6400. Both platforms ran the same benchmark scripts but used different software environments. Arm used custom Linux 7.1.3 builds, with Ubuntu 24.04 for most tests and Ubuntu 26.04 for SWE-bench, while AMD’s main recorded configuration used Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux 6.8, with settings varying by test.
At the chip level, Arm’s AGI CPU won the majority of comparisons when compared to its AMD counterpart in five of the seven tests. With the EPYC 9755 as the baseline, Arm led by 9% on Terminal-Bench, 13% on SWE-bench, and 97% on fastText, but lagged by 12% and 5% in MySQL and Milvus throughput, respectively. On average, the AGI CPU led by 20% (1.20x) per-chip advantage, calculated across the seven normalized performance ratios.
| Results |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Workload | Measured per-chip performance vs EPYC 9755 | Modeled per-rack performance vs EPYC 9755 | 
| MySQL | 0.88x | 1.43x | 
| NGINX | 1.20x | 1.95x | 
| Terminal-Bench 2 | 1.09x | 1.93x | 
| SWE-bench replay | 1.13x | 2.00x | 
| Milvus | 0.95x | 1.54x | 
| vLLM CPU overhead | 1.16x | 1.88x | 
| fastText | 1.97x | 3.19x | 
| Arithmetic average | 1.20x | 1.99x | 
At the rack level, Arm’s modeled performance averages 1.99x AMD’s, with a lead in all seven workloads. The model uses rated server-power estimates of 950 W for the 128-core Arm configuration, 1,050 W for the 136-core version, and 1,700 W for AMD, including memory and other system components. After reserving about 8% of a 24 kW rack budget for networking and power distribution, this leaves room for 23 or 21 Arm servers versus 13 AMD servers.
For SWE-bench, the 2.00x per rack result was obtained by multiplying the roughly 1.13x chip result by 23/13. The larger gain comes from fitting more servers into the same power budget. Furthermore, these projections use modeled whole-server power, not throughput measurements from two fully populated racks.
Arm’s model also gives the AMD servers about twice as much RAM: roughly 2 TB against 1 TB for Arm. It allocates 4 GB per hardware thread, with each AMD core supporting two threads while each Arm core supports one. This puts the memory-power allowance at 336 W for AMD and 192 W for Arm. Signal65 also calculated what happens when memory is allocated per physical core. In this setup, AMD’s memory and power allowance falls, and Arm’s average modeled rack advantage drops from 1.99x to approximately 1.81x. The usefulness of the 2 TB AMD configuration depends on how much memory the workloads actually need, as SMT does not inherently require twice the memory.
To verify the findings, Signal65 remotely observed Arm’s test runs and examined the original logs, result files, scripts, and configuration records. A separate review team rebuilt the calculations with its own code and reproduced all seven results within 0.5%. However, Signal65 did not run a separate hardware rerun in its own lab. In addition, Signal65 could independently confirm BIOS and memory settings for only the EPYC 9965 system. These settings were unavailable for independent verification on the Arm and EPYC 9755 systems. Along with the software differences, these gaps slightly affect the certainty with which the results can be attributed to the processors themselves.
Arm’s approach vs AMD and Nvidia
While Arm believes its methodology should be the standard, it does not hold a monopoly on how the industry evaluates agentic CPU performance. For example, AMD promotes agents per watt, dollar, and rack. Footnotes on its EPYC 9006 page identify available CPU threads as a proxy for agent capacity, with actual throughput depending on the workload and system. Its separate workload analysis models a 100 kW rack and claims 2.37× performance for EPYC 9965 over Nvidia's Vera, using a geometric mean across six infrastructure workloads.
Nvidia, on the other hand, emphasizes Vera’s single-thread performance and memory bandwidth, and says a 256-CPU rack supports more than 22,500 concurrent CPU environments. These numbers describe different things and do not directly imply any specific advantage. Methodologies vary across manufacturers by workload, power assumptions, and aggregation methods, making direct CPU comparisons complex. The current comparison is against AMD's fifth-generation “Turin” processor with 128 cores. The company launched its latest sixth-generation EPYC 9006 “Venice” family this year, dedicated to agentic AI.
Etiido Uko is a news contributor for Tom's Hardware covering the latest updates in big tech and the PC industry. He is a mechanical engineer and senior technical writer with over nine years of experience in documentation and reporting. He is deeply passionate about all things engineering and technology, and is an expert in gadgets, manufacturing, robotics, automotive, and aerospace.

articles.title: AMD's Ryzen 7 7700X doesn't ship with a cooler — this $209 setup fixes that
articles.text:
AMD’s Ryzen 7 7700X, is 'hands down the best processor on the market for most people' — now it's dropped to $209 with a free 240mm AIO cooler
This 5-star CPU boasts 8 cores, 16 threads, and up to 5.4GHz boost
The AMD Ryzen 7 700X impressed us during our testing, with our components expert John calling it "hands down the best processor on the market for most people." If you’re building or upgrading to AMD’s AM5 platform, this CPU delivers a fast eight-core chip and the cooler to run it for well under the original asking price.
Now, the AMD Ryzen 7 700X is $239 (was $399) at Newegg with a free Cooler Master Elite Liquid 240mm AIO. But I've found a way to bring that down to $209 when you buy two $100 Newegg gift cards, with the site giving away a bonus $30 free with each purchase ($15 per card).
• Best for: gamers and everyday power users building a new AM5 system who want strong performance without paying for a Ryzen 9.
• Why we like it: eight Zen 4 cores with boost clocks up to 5.4GHz, PCIe 5.0 and DDR5 support, and a free 240mm liquid cooler, which matters because the 7700X doesn’t ship with one.
• What to know: To use this CPU, you need an AM5 motherboard and DDR5 memory.
An eight-core, 16-thread Zen 4 desktop processor for Socket AM5, with a 4.5GHz base clock, up to 5.4GHz boost, 32MB of L3 cache, and a 105W TDP. No cooler is included in the box, but Newegg is currently adding a Cooler Master Elite Liquid 240mm AIO free with purchase. For the full discount, get two Newegg gift cards for a bonus $30.
Why we recommend it
In our Ryzen 7 7700X review, we praised its outstanding performance and accessible price, calling it the processor most people should buy. At $209 with a free AIO, though, the chip is a much easier sell than at launch, and the bundled cooler removes one of the extra costs we flagged.
Price Context & Historical Value
By stacking two Newegg gift cards alongside the existing discount, you're saving $190 off the $399 list price. That's not the lowest ever price. But what makes this deal stand out is the free 240mm AIO cooler, which you’d otherwise have to buy separately. If you’re ready to build on AM5 now, it’s a strong time to buy.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the AMD Ryzen 7 7700X if... you’re building a new AM5 gaming or general-use PC, you want eight fast cores without paying Ryzen 9 prices, or you need a cooler anyway and like the idea of getting a 240mm AIO thrown in.
❌ Skip the AMD Ryzen 7 7700X if... you’re on an older AM4 or DDR4 system and don’t want to replace your motherboard and memory, you do heavy professional rendering that would benefit from more cores, or your case can’t fit a 240mm radiator.
