articles.title: IEEE Report Highlights How Members Are Engineering for Public Good
articles.text:
Advancing technology for the benefit of humanity isn’t just the tagline for IEEE’s mission as a public charity. It’s something that the organization’s more than 500,000 members strive to do all the time. IEEE’s recently released 2025 Social Impact Report showcases a variety of programs volunteers worked on to increase public awareness of technology’s impact on society, many of which The Institute covered.
Here is a selection of the programs from the report, with links to our related articles:
- Shaping trustworthy digital experiences for children online. An IEEE collaboration with Indonesian policymakers led to a new regulation to protect children, a first of its kind in the region. The advanced frameworks used for the design of Internet platforms and systems are based on the IEEE 2089-2021 and 2089.1-2024 standards. The IEEE 2089-2021 Standard for an Age-Appropriate Digital Services Framework Based on the 5Rights Principles for Children provides practical steps to qualify online products and services. The follow-up, the IEEE 2089.1-2024 Standard for Online Age Verification, provides a framework for designing, specifying, evaluating, and deploying age-verification systems. You can learn more about the two standards in “IEEE Makes Strides to Improve Online Safety for Kids.”
- Catalyzing humanitarian outreach. Last year IEEE launched its Mobile Outreach Vehicle (MOVE) program in India. The vehicle brings educational resources to communities and can provide communication and technology support to relief workers and survivors during emergencies. In 2024, for example, MOVE helped survivors of Hurricanes Helene and Milton in the Southeastern United States. When the vehicles are not deployed, IEEE MOVE remains engaged in outreach efforts, participating in 25 STEM educational events such as one in San Diego in 2023.
- Preserving Tech History. The IEEE Global Museum, developed by the IEEE History Center, presents traveling exhibits to educate the public about the history of technology and its impact on society. In “IEEE’s Global Museum Brings Engineering History to You,” you can learn about current exhibits “Unseen Signals: E. Howard Armstrong’s Radio Revolution” and “Microchips That Shook the World.”
- EPICS in IEEE. This program provides nonprofit organizations with technology solutions while broadening undergraduate students’ hands-on experiences. Last year US $290,000 was awarded to a record-breaking number of service projects around the world. Among the 48 projects was one in which a student team in Macedonia created IoT-driven sensing and display devices to help measure and promote awareness of pollution and air-quality issues in the capital city of Skopje.
- IEEE TryEngineering. This initiative inspires preuniversity students to pursue technology and engineering careers. It awarded US $70,379 in grants to 58 programs around the world. One is its TryEngineering Summer Institute, a nine-day summer sleepaway camp for students ages 13 to 17. More than 310 students participated last year, learning about aerospace and artificial intelligence.
- IEEE–Eta Kappa Nu. IEEE-HKN has more than 260 collegiate chapters worldwide and more than 200,000 members. The honor society encourages and recognizes excellence in education, professional practice, and meritorious work within IEEE’s designated fields of interest. IEEE-HKN members last year contributed 110,442 volunteer hours to universities and communities, and they held 827 service and outreach events and 137 STEM outreach activities. Last year IEEE and HKN celebrated the 15th anniversary of their merger.
- IEEE Connecting the Unconnected Challenge. This annual global competition solicits innovative solutions from startups, grassroots organizations, universities, and others working to bridge the digital divide. The Institute wrote about last year’s winners. They included a solar-powered community broadband network in Tanzania, a low-cost method for accessing the Internet that uses FM radio and a short message service, and a strategy for utilizing India’s rural broadband infrastructure to deliver medical services to people living in isolated, tribal, and other underserved regions.
- Supporting Sustainable Climate Efforts. IEEE helps foster the exchange of technical knowledge and information to develop technologies for a sustainable climate. “IEEE Plays a Pivotal Role in Climate Mitigation Talks” reported how the organization enhanced its standing as a trusted, neutral authority on the role of technology in climate change mitigation and adaptation. Leaders, including 2023 IEEE President Saifur Rahman, showcased tech solutions at COP30 and the International Symposium on Achieving a Sustainable Climate. Also, “IEEE Young Professionals Talked Sustainability Tech at Climate Week NYC” reported on the group’s activities during the 2024 Climate Week NY, the largest annual climate event, featuring more than 600 activities throughout New York City.
Engineering: A force for good
“The IEEE global community of more than 500,000 members and volunteers demonstrates what is possible when expertise is mobilized for the public good,” Sophia Muirhead, IEEE executive director and chief operating officer, said in a news release about the Social Impact Report. “Technology has the power to expand opportunity, strengthen communities and improve lives, and IEEE’s mission is to ensure that this power is used responsibly, ethically, and in service of humanity. The 2025 report shows how IEEE members and volunteers are advancing solutions that make a real difference in people’s lives around the world.”
Engagement research shows that members increasingly cited “giving back to my profession and the world community” as a reason for joining IEEE and renewing their membership, IEEE President Mary Ellen Randall said in her September column about the report.
“Humanitarian programs are not only meaningful,” she wrote. “They also are magnetic. They attract younger engineers, keep them engaged, and help them build a professional identity rooted in purpose and impact.
“IEEE has the opportunity to become the world’s leading convening force for developing interdisciplinary technology solutions to solve humanity’s most important challenges. Our future relevance will be defined not only by the technologies we advance but also by the problems we choose to help solve.”
- Reclaiming Social Engineering for Good ›
- IEEE President’s Note: Technology for Social Good ›
- What “Social Good” Means to Engineers ›
Kathy Pretz is editor in chief for The Institute, which covers all aspects of IEEE, its members, and the technology they're involved in. She has a bachelor's degree in applied communication from Rider University, in Lawrenceville, N.J., and holds a master's degree in corporate and public communication from Monmouth University, in West Long Branch, N.J.

articles.title: He comprobado todo lo que Google sabe de mi vida y esto es lo que guarda
articles.text: Un empleado de la Casa de la Historia pasa junto a una imagen de un ojo que refleja el logo de Google, en una exposición que aborda el miedo y la vigilancia en Alemania. Todos hemos escuchado alguna vez eso de que Google lo sabe todo de nosotros. Pero realmente no fui consciente de cuánto de verdad tiene esa afirmación hasta que decidí hacer una prueba: entrar en mi cuenta y revisar, uno por uno, los lugares que he visitado, las búsquedas que he hecho, los vídeos que he visto, los dispositivos desde los que he iniciado sesión y la información asociada a mis fotos. Seguir leyendo

articles.title: Spielt dein Chef auch Karla Kolumna auf Linkedin?
articles.text:
Linkedin: Warum Ankündigungsposts floppen und was die erste Zeile damit zu tun hat
Seit acht Jahren postet Céline Flores Willers mindestens dreimal pro Woche auf Linkedin, ohne Pause. Ihre Community dort umfasst heute 230.000 Follower. Daraus hat sie das Beratungsunternehmen The People Branding Company gegründet, die für Firmen wie Beiersdorf und Hugo Boss arbeitet.
Im Podcast t3n Arbeit in Progress gibt sie Einblicke, auf welche KPIs sie für ihren Linkedin-Account achtet, welche Inhalte tendenziell schlechter funktionieren und ob sie damit rechnet, dass Linkedin von einer anderen Plattform abgelöst wird. Das Interview ist gekürzt, die vollständige Fassung gibt es in der verlinkten Podcast-Folge.
t3n: In der Tech-Bubble springen viele auf Themen wie Unternehmertum und digitale Trends. Du hast dich durchgesetzt. Gibt es einen bestimmten Trick oder etwas, worauf du besonders achten musst?
Céline Flores Willers: Mit 230.000 Followern gehört mein Linkedin-Account in der deutschsprachigen Region zu den reichweitenstärksten. Für mich kommt es vor allem auf Konsistenz über viele Jahre hinweg an. Das gilt nicht nur für das Thema, sondern auch für die Frequenz. In den letzten acht Jahren gab es keinen einzigen Monat, in dem ich nicht gepostet habe. Hätte ich mir zwischendurch eine Pause oder ein kleines Sabbatical genehmigt, hätte ich so eine Community nicht aufgebaut. Ich glaube, der größte Schlüssel ist, einfach dranzubleiben.
t3n: Lass uns auf die KPIs schauen. Welche trackst du bei deinem eigenen Linkedin-Profil regelmäßig?
Für mein eigenes Profil schaue ich mir zwei Dinge an. Das eine ist der Follower-Growth, das andere sind die Impressions, also die Reichweite pro Posting. Das sind meine Top-KPIs.
t3n: Und warum?
Ich optimiere mein Profil auf Reichweite. Mein Ziel ist es, meine Bekanntheit in der deutschen Wirtschaft zu steigern, soweit sie digital auf Linkedin stattfindet. Dort will ich eine möglichst hohe Durchdringung erreichen. Jeder auf der Dmexco, auf der Bits & Pretzels, auf irgendeinem Wirtschaftskongress oder einer Wirtschaftsmesse wie der Hannover Messe soll sagen: Ja, Céline Flores Willers, die kenne ich, die steht für Unternehmertum in Deutschland. Das ist mein wichtigster KPI, und deshalb sind die Impressions wichtiger.
Wir haben wiederum Kunden, bei denen es um etwas anderes geht. Ein Beispiel ist eine Cybersecurity-Beratung, super nischig. Sie will ganz bestimmte Kunden und ganz bestimmte Accounts gewinnen. Dafür ist es viel wichtiger, dass sie mit den 500 richtigen Leuten und Entscheidern aus ihrer Branche vernetzt ist, die in den richtigen Positionen sitzen: mit den CTOs, mit den Cybersecurity-Leads. Diese Firma geht nicht auf Masse. Wir gehen mit ihr ganz gezielt auf diese Leads und Kontakte zu. Hier kommt wieder das Ziel ins Spiel. Nicht für jeden ist derselbe KPI relevant. Wer aber auf Reichweite maximiert, schaut auf Impressions und Follower.
t3n: Und was machst du, wenn deine Posts mal nicht performen, hast du konkrete Strategien, wie du deine Posts änderst?
Wir haben tatsächlich gerade eine große KI-Analyse über meinen Account laufen lassen. Wir wollten herausfinden, was die gut performenden Posts ausmacht und was die schlecht performenden. Ankündigungsposts performen immer schlecht, auch auf meinem Profil. Deshalb versuchen wir grundsätzlich, diese Posts inhaltlich aufzuhängen. Nimm die Dmexco als Beispiel. Ich schreibe nicht: „Ich bin nächste Woche auf der Dmexco.“ Ich schreibe zum Beispiel: „Es gibt diesen einen Trend in B2B, Marketing und Sales, den jede Company 2027 beachten muss.“ Ich komme also über den Inhalt, das ist dann die Hook. Erst hinten im Post sage ich, dass es um die Dmexco geht.
Das ist ein notwendiger Tipp an die Entscheider und C-Levels, die hier zuhören. Ich sehe so viele CEOs, die verhalten sich wie Karla Kolumna da draußen. Sie sagen nur, auf welchem Event sie sind. Das ist rein anlassbezogene, eventgetriebene Kommunikation. Ihr Aufhänger ist „Ich war auf dem Event“. Dabei sollte der Aufhänger das Thema sein, um das es eigentlich geht.
t3n: Deine Hauptkapazität steckst du weiterhin in Linkedin. Macht dir diese Abhängigkeit mitunter Angst oder Druck?
Nein, gar nicht. Ich sehe nichts, was sich auch nur anbahnt, um Linkedin in den nächsten Jahren zu ersetzen. Ich kenne kein Business-Social-Medium, bei dem ich sehe: Da entsteht etwas. Und wir schauen uns das ständig an. Es hängt ja nicht nur mein Account an der Plattform. Ich habe ein Unternehmen mit 30 Mitarbeitenden gegründet, da hängen Menschenleben und Familienleben dran. Natürlich haben wir alles auf dem Schirm, was in diesem Bereich passiert. Aber ich kann sagen: Wir haben in den letzten acht Jahren nichts gesehen. Ich sehe nichts kommen, was Linkedin ablösen kann. Deshalb schlafe ich ganz ruhig. Ich würde auch sagen: Es lohnt sich nach wie vor, stark in Linkedin zu investieren.
Podcast t3n Arbeit in Progress anhören
Ihr könnt den Podcast t3n Arbeit in Progress bequem in der Podcast-App eurer Wahl abonnieren. In der Regel findet ihr den Podcast einfach über die Eingabe „t3n Arbeit in Progress“ in der Suche. Ansonsten könnt ihr auch den RSS-Feed manuell in der App eingeben.

articles.title: Khosla Ventures doubles down on Even Healthcare to challenge India's hospital economics | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Even Healthcare has raised $50 million in a funding round led by Khosla Ventures, as the Indian startup seeks to change how hospitals in the world’s most populous country make money and how doctors are rewarded.
The all-equity Series B round also saw participation from Alpha Wave and valued it at $300 million, triple its valuation 18 months ago, according to Even. The latest funding brings Even’s total capital raised to more than $120 million.
Hospitals in India typically earn more when patients undergo additional tests, procedures, or longer stays, even when they may not need them. Even wants to change that by focusing on patient care rather than pushing unnecessary treatments that drive up medical bills.
That approach has continued to appeal to Khosla Ventures, which has invested in Even since its seed round in 2021. The Silicon Valley venture firm is doubling down as Even moves to build and operate hospitals of its own, giving it greater control over patient care and costs.
Vinod Khosla, founder of Khosla Ventures, said Even’s approach goes beyond fixing individual parts of a fragmented healthcare system by bringing financing, technology, and care delivery together. The goal, he said in a prepared statement, is to reward better health outcomes rather than greater use of healthcare services.
“The clinical and economic results so far give us conviction that this can become an important new model for healthcare in India and beyond,” Khosla said.
Initially, Even relied on partner hospitals to treat its members, but Mayank Banerjee, who founded the startup in 2021 with Matilde Giglio and Alessandro Ialongo, said in an interview that the startup began questioning that model after finding that patients had undergone tests or been recommended surgeries it considered unnecessary.
“We think patients are getting not only a bad experience, but insurers are getting a bad economic deal. And as a result, we decided to fix it by building our own hospitals,” Banerjee told TechCrunch.
Even has since opened two hospitals in Bengaluru, both of which reached operational profitability, excluding depreciation, within a year of opening, Banerjee stated. The startup plans to open five more hospitals in the southern Indian city over the next six months, funded by its latest round.
Banerjee told TechCrunch that Even leases hospital buildings on 20-year agreements and spends on fitting them out and buying medical equipment.
Unlike hospitals where doctors may have financial incentives to recommend more procedures, Even pays its doctors fixed salaries — not tying their compensation to the number of tests or surgeries they perform, though Banerjee said doctors can earn bonuses based on patient-reported clinical outcomes.
The same principle extends to hospital management, whose compensation is not linked to the number of procedures performed, Banerjee told TechCrunch. Managers, he said, receive salaries and company-wide incentives, while marketing teams focus on bringing in patients instead of the revenue those patients generate. Moreover, every employee, including doctors and other hospital staff, receives equity in Even. The idea is to give employees a stake in the startup’s long-term performance, not to reward them for generating more medical bills.
Most of Even’s revenue comes from patients paying for treatment, Banerjee said. The startup also generates revenue through its relationships with insurers. It is also working with insurer partners on a model that could compensate it for hospitalizations it helps prevent, not simply for providing more treatment.
Banerjee told TechCrunch that Even tracks how patients recover after treatment using established medical scoring systems. In the case of knee replacements, for instance, it uses the Oxford Knee Score to measure pain and mobility. The startup publishes results on its website, alongside figures from other healthcare systems for comparison.
Even says its hospitals have an unplanned readmission rate of less than 1%, compared with an industry benchmark of 8% to 15%. Furthermore, it claims patients spend 40% less time in the hospital and that its approach has saved insurers more than ₹500 million (about $5.27 million).
Jai Sajnani, a partner at Khosla Ventures, told TechCrunch that the early performance of Even’s hospitals was a key reason the firm led the round. “We look forward to helping the Even team put quality care within reach of every family in Bengaluru and across India,” he said.
Even is still losing money, though. The startup posted a net loss of ₹902 million (about $9.50 million) in fiscal 2025, nearly 25% more than the previous year, on revenue of ₹272 million (about $2.86 million), regulatory filings show.
In August, Even also laid off about 350 employees, according to Indian startup news website Entrackr. Banerjee acknowledged the restructuring and called it a difficult decision. He said the affected employees received severance, extended health insurance, and accelerated equity vesting.
Even currently employs about 650 people, including around 300 doctors full-time. The startup has about 250,000 members and has recorded more than 750,000 patient interactions since its launch in 2021, including consultations, diagnostic tests, and surgeries, Banerjee said.
Banerjee told TechCrunch that Even could turn profitable within months if it stopped spending on expansion, but the startup is choosing to grow instead. He declined to say when the startup expects to become profitable.
“Right now, we’re investing in growth and serving more patients,” Banerjee said.

articles.title: Germany Wants to Lead the World in Industrial AI: How NVIDIA Will Help
articles.text:
In the cavernous hall of Kraftwerk, a former power station in Berlin, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang sat down to discuss Germany’s AI roadmap, and in particular, the industrial applications of AI.
Huang opened by tracing NVIDIA’s longstanding relationship with German industry, beginning with gaming systems, workstations and automotive design in the early 2000s and leading to today’s partnerships in autonomous vehicle development and digital twins for manufacturing.
The conversation focused on how Germany can make the most of the AI revolution by playing to its strengths in manufacturing and automotive — and by encouraging AI adoption across the country’s ecosystem of small and medium-sized companies.
Earlier in the day, as part of the Invest in Germany Summit, Chancellor Merz, the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy and the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space signed a Joint Declaration of Intent with NVIDIA.
The German federal government’s aim is to merge traditional German engineering and manufacturing expertise with cutting-edge research and AI technology. The declaration sets out an agreement to work on a joint initiative with NVIDIA to advance cutting edge AI models for physical AI.
Formalizing and expanding NVIDIA’s collaboration with Germany’s federal government and its “Industry 4.0 Platform,” which is comprised of representatives from politics, industry, research and trade associations, helps achieve the government’s stated goal to “systematically bring industrial AI into widespread use and to establish a state-of-the-art industrial AI ecosystem in Europe.”
Germany’s Ambition to Integrate AI With Industry
Merz and Huang dug into industrial AI and how NVIDIA can help Germany lead the way. The German Chancellor first laid out his government’s ambition.
“We are fully committed to be one of the most advanced places in the world, not just in the European Union, but in the world to work with AI, to integrate AI into our industry,” Merz said. “I’m really optimistic that we will be one of the leading, if not the leading, country in the world in terms of the spread of AI for all the companies — our manufacturers, machinery, automotive industry and suppliers of the automotive industry. I think this is a great opportunity.”
Merz called out the leaders of the small and medium businesses — the Mittelstand — in the audience.
“The biggest advantage we have in Germany is our so-called Mittelstand,” Merz said. “Please open your doors for AI to make use of your data. This is a real secret and a real advantage for Germany to make use of all the data which is already available in our companies.”
Huang agreed, and praised Germany’s world-class expertise in manufacturing companies both large and small, as well as its math and science excellence. That national expertise and knowledge is what sets the German economy apart, he said, and AI will only amplify it.
“That knowledge belongs to you,” Huang said. “It cannot be replaced. AI can only augment your capability, it will not replace your capability. Take advantage of the technology. It’s a new instrument.”
Germany’s expertise with physical technologies is a differentiator, Huang and Merz agreed, and a powerful accelerator for the German economy when AI is included.
“If we are successful in bringing these two aspects and parts of the business of the future together,” Merz said. “I’m really very optimistic that Germany can be one of the most successful economies in the world.”
Huang described AI’s impact across virtually every industry as a new industrial revolution.
“This industrial revolution is so mighty, so powerful,” Huang said. “In the Chancellor’s words, you are re-engineering Germany. This is your chance to do it well.”
Merz envisioned a regular reunion with Huang to assess the progress Germany is making with AI.
“I would like to see him regularly, let’s say at least once a year, and discuss the progress we made,” Merz said, “And see a guy sitting in my office being extremely happy about Germany as a place to invest.”
NVIDIA’s Investments in Germany
Huang also announced new investments in four German startups, part of a nearly $10 billion commitment by NVIDIA to support companies, universities, research institutions and more across Europe.
NVIDIA has been investing across Germany’s startup ecosystem, supporting leading technology companies including n8n, Neura Robotics and Black Forest Labs.
Today, Huang announced new planned investments in Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace.
Agile Robots, a Munich-based robotics company, builds AI-powered robots, from robotic arms to its Agile ONE humanoid, for manufacturing, logistics and healthcare.
Avelios Medical, a Munich-based healthcare technology startup, develops an AI-native hospital information system that serves as the core system of record for clinical and administrative workflows, integrating AI directly into hospital operations to free up doctors and nurses to deliver better patient care.
Mirelo, a German startup, develops AI models that generate sound effects, speech and music for video, helping creators and production teams produce high-quality audio that perfectly matches their visuals on screen.
Reflex Aerospace, a Berlin-based space scaleup, designs and builds high-performance satellites ready for launch in about 12 months instead of years.
Siemens and NVIDIA Advance Autonomous Manufacturing; Record-Breaking Quantum Simulation
Earlier in the day, Siemens announced it’s partnering with NVIDIA to advance AI-driven, autonomous factories. Siemens showcased new AI solutions at its Erlangen factory, advancing its role as a global blueprint for autonomous manufacturing. Fully virtual production ramp-up reduces engineering effort by up to 85%, while agent-based production planning enables more adaptive manufacturing and cost savings of up to 20%.
NVIDIA researchers used JUPITER, Europe’s largest supercomputer at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, to run a record-breaking simulation of a fault-tolerant quantum computer. The 104-qubit simulation is the largest and most detailed of its kind to date.

articles.title: Mecka AI recruits growth hackers behind “IRL sidequest” app Thirdspace
articles.text:
Toronto- and New York City-based Mecka AI, which aims to supply the training data necessary to deploy robots in the real world, has completed its second acquisition to date.
The buzzy AI startup announced today that it bought Ottawa’s Thirdspace, a popular social mobile app that Mecka described as a mix between BeReal, Instagram, and Snapchat. Thirdspace bills itself as a venue for “[in real life] side quests with friends.” The news comes shortly after Mecka revealed it had closed $60 million USD ($86 million CAD) in Series B funding from Sequoia Capital, Nvidia, Microsoft, Qualcomm, and Samsung, among others.
“They’ve captured this lightning in the bottle of what it takes to get viral.”
Launched last year by former Carleton University students Cedric Osagie and Eshan Betrabet, Thirdspace allows users to take and post photos of themselves doing fun things and invites friends to join. The images are only briefly viewable—once others have accepted the invite, they’ll get a location to join in and capture a pic together.
In an exclusive interview with BetaKit, Osagie said the goal was to build a fun, spontaneous way to encourage lonely university students to connect more in person. The idea has taken off: in less than two years, Thirdspace has amassed upwards of 20,000 downloads, 60 million views, and has been tripling its monthly active users on the back of $100,000 CAD in angel funding.
In an interview with BetaKit, Mecka special projects lead Mark Grinev said Thirdspace’s “small but mighty team” was “the most important piece,” noting that Mecka was drawn to the playbook that Osagie and Betrabet deployed to grow Thirdspace.
Both firms declined to disclose the acquisition price. The cash-and-stock deal, which closed a few weeks ago around the same time as Mecka’s recent $60-million USD Series B round, is effectively an acquihire, similar in nature to Mecka’s purchase of Vancouver-based Docula earlier this year.
While Thirdspace will remain operational going forward, Osagie and Betrabet have ceased working on it and have joined Mecka as heads of mobile capture and to expand the reach of its home capture app and lead its efforts “across all things mobile.”
“They’re exceptional growth hackers and thinkers, and they’ve captured this lightning in the bottle of what it takes to get viral,” Grinev said. “That is crucial because scaling the mobile app is imperative to hit these big goals of ours.”
RELATED: Mecka AI reveals $60-million USD Series B round backed by Sequoia, Nvidia
Mecka is betting that egocentric, or first-person video will help robots learn faster and scale more efficiently. Demand for this type of data—which, unlike the text, images, and video required to train large language models, cannot be scraped from the internet—is booming. The approximately 80-person startup has built hardware with sensors to capture video and the computer vision and multimodal models to turn it into usable robot training fodder for multiple frontier robotics labs and Big Tech firms.
While Mecka has already collected millions of hours worth of egocentric video from hundreds of thousands of individuals, that is still far from enough to train real-world robots, Grinev said. Given this, Mecka has set an ambitious video target for the end of 2027: 100 million hours of footage. Getting there will require millions of people to download its app, strap their phones to their heads, and collect and submit footage of themselves completing various tasks, he said.
Mecka is betting that Osagie and Betrabet can deploy some of the same strategies they used at Thirdspace to help the company get there, including their ability to leverage user-generated content and find and run with the right viral formats to fuel organic growth.
“This is actually the first team I’ve seen in the robotics realm that is growth-hacking their app like a traditional consumer product, which I think gives incredible advantages,” Osagie said.
RELATED: Mecka AI acquires Docula as it builds the data layer for robotics
While TechCrunch first reported last month that Mecka was raising a new round at a valuation of about $500 million, Grinev declined to share how Mecka’s all-equity, all-primary capital Series B financing valued the two-year-old startup, which has now raised $120 million USD.
Grinev said that Mecka, which claimed to have surpassed a $100-million USD run-rate in June and expects to hit $300 million by the end of this year, raised so much in close succession because it sees a big opportunity and requires a lot of capital to sustain its pace.
Mecka intends to use its Series B capital to grow its teams across Toronto and New York and expand to San Francisco. It also plans to use the funds to finance its compute and storage costs, fund payouts for the folks capturing data, and support its tech development plans.
Grinev acknowledged that the AI talent wars have become “quite intense.” While Mecka does not have any other acquihires planned at the moment, he said he would not be surprised to see the company pursue more such deals in the future.
Feature image courtesy Mecka AI.

articles.title: N'achetez pas de smartphone sur Leboncoin, Vinted ou eBay après le 17 octobre
articles.text:
Des vitrines brisées, des boutiques saccagées et des individus qui repartent les bras chargés de marchandises. Les scènes de pillage se sont multipliées le samedi 17 octobre 2026 en France, en marge des manifestations contre la vie chère et les conditions d’études. Les commerces de téléphonie et d’électronique n’ont pas été épargnés parmi les 1 500 commerces touchés, avec plusieurs boutiques saccagées de SFR à Paris, Orange à Rennes, la Fnac à Nantes ou encore l’Apple Store de Lille et de Bordeaux.
Les annonces de smartphones dérobés à prix cassé pourraient se retrouver ces prochains jours en vente sur eBay, Leboncoin, Vinted ou d’autres plateformes. Mieux vaut ne pas les acheter.
Un smartphone volé peut être bloqué après votre achat
Un vêtement dérobé peut facilement changer de mains sans que son propriétaire puisse le retrouver. Pour un smartphone, c’est une autre histoire : plusieurs dispositifs permettent de bloquer son utilisation, en coupant son accès aux réseaux mobiles ou en verrouillant directement l’appareil.
Les opérateurs peuvent bloquer un téléphone grâce à son IMEI, un identifiant à 15 chiffres. Changer de carte SIM ne suffit donc pas à retrouver du réseau : c’est le téléphone lui-même qui est visé. Ce blocage n’est toutefois pas immédiat. Selon l’Arcep, il intervient dans les quatre jours ouvrés suivant la réception, par l’opérateur, de la déclaration officielle de vol transmise par la police ou la gendarmerie.
Un smartphone dérobé pendant le week-end du 17 octobre peut donc encore fonctionner lors d’une remise en main propre en début de semaine, puis perdre son accès après l’achat.
Au blocage du réseau mobile peuvent également s’ajouter des protections qui verrouillent l’appareil lui-même. Une vidéo relayée le 18 octobre par le compte Chino montre ainsi un iPhone issu des poillages de l’Apple Sotre Lillois affichant un message sans ambiguïté : « Veuillez retourner l’appareil à l’Apple Lille ». L’écran indique que le téléphone a été désactivé, visiblement par l’administrateur des appareils.
« Veuillez retourner l’appareil à l’Apple Lille. » L’écran précise que le téléphone a été désactivé, qu’il est en cours de géolocalisation et que les autorités vont être averties. Ce verrouillage de l’appareil est distinct du blocage de l’accès au réseau par les opérateurs.
L’avocat Alexandre Archambault met justement en garde sur X contre les « bonnes affaires LeBonCoin » qui pourraient suivre ces pillages. Si certains téléphones sont déjà bloqués, d’autres peuvent encore fonctionner au moment de la vente et le devenir seulement après l’achat.
Parmi les appareils volés samedi 17 ou dimanche 18 octobre, certains peuvent encore fonctionner lors d’une remise en main propre en ce début de semaine, puis perdre leur accès au réseau quelques jours après l’achat, voire au-delà selon la date de transmission du signalement à l’opérateur.
Avant de payer, une vérification prend quelques secondes. Composez *#06# sur le téléphone pour afficher son IMEI, comparez-le avec celui imprimé sur la boîte et demandez la facture au vendeur. Un appareil neuf, encore emballé, vendu bien sous son prix et sans facture doit vous alerter.
Que faire si le smartphone acheté se retrouve bloqué ?
Acheter un téléphone en sachant qu’il a été volé constitue un recel. Cependant, l’acheteur de bonne foi, qui ignorait l’origine du smartphone, n’est pas automatiquement un receleur.
En cas de doute, vous devez conserver l’annonce et vos échanges avec le vendeur, qui serviront à prouver votre bonne foi. Toutefois, être de bonne foi ne vous garantit pas de garder le téléphone, que son propriétaire peut réclamer pendant trois ans après le vol.
Signalez ensuite la situation à la plateforme et demandez le remboursement au vendeur par écrit. Pour un achat effectué auprès d’un particulier via le paiement de la plateforme, les délais de signalement diffèrent :
- Sur Leboncoin, vous disposez de trois jours à compter de la confirmation de réception du colis pour déclarer un problème de conformité.
- Sur Vinted, vous avez deux jours calendaires après la notification indiquant que la commande aurait dû être livrée pour sélectionner « J’ai un problème » dans la conversation. Ne validez pas « Tout est OK » si vous constatez une anomalie.
- Sur eBay, la Garantie client prévoit généralement 30 jours calendaires après la date de livraison estimée ou réelle, selon ses conditions, pour demander un retour pour objet non conforme.
Un blocage peut apparaître après l’expiration de ces délais, notamment sur Leboncoin et Vinted. Contactez malgré tout l’assistance pour signaler la vente d’un appareil volé, sans considérer le remboursement comme acquis.
Si l’appareil vous a été vendu en dissimulant son origine, rendez-vous au commissariat ou à la gendarmerie pour déposer plainte, avec les justificatifs de votre achat.
Les réponses des plateformes
Numerama a contacté Leboncoin, Vinted et eBay au sujet de ces potentielles reventes de smartphones volés via leurs plateformes, après les pillages du 17 octobre.
Vinted nous indique avoir renforcé « le contrôle des annonces suspectes » depuis ce week-end. Ses équipes ont, selon la plateforme, agi pour « identifier et supprimer les annonces susceptibles de concerner des biens volés ». Vinted rappelle que ces ventes sont interdites et que les infractions peuvent entraîner le bannissement définitif des comptes concernés. L’entreprise assure également collaborer avec les forces de l’ordre et les autorités françaises.
De son côté, eBay indique ne pas pouvoir confirmer « une hausse des annonces pouvant faire suite à des vols ayant eu lieu ce week-end » à ce stade. La plateforme explique utiliser « des outils technologiques pour détecter les comportements suspects », complétés par des contrôles manuels et l’examen des signalements. « Dès lors que les forces de l’ordre nous confirment qu’un objet a été volé, nous procédons immédiatement au retrait de l’annonce », assure eBay. Les sanctions peuvent aller jusqu’à la suspension définitive du compte du vendeur.
Nous mettrons à jour cet article avec les réponses des autres plateformes lorsque nous les recevrons.

articles.title: Microsoft: October Windows Server updates break Exchange sign-in, mail flow
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed that this month's Windows Server security updates are causing OWA sign-in and mail delivery issues on some Exchange Server systems.
In a new Windows release health dashboard update over the weekend, Microsoft said users may have trouble accessing email or signing in to Outlook after installing the latest updates on systems running Windows Server 2019 and later.
In some cases, affected customers are also reportedly seeing Exchange Server OWA failing with a "MapiExceptionMdbOffline: Unable to make connection to the server. (hr=0x80004005, ec=1142)" error and Event ID 1006 in the application log.
"After installing the October 2026 Windows security update [..], some on-premises Exchange servers might experience issues accessing or sending email. Users might be unable to sign in to Outlook on the web (OWA), or email messages sent from Outlook might remain in the Outbox and not be delivered. Additionally, Exchange might experience issues accessing mailboxes during mailbox replication," it said.
"The October 2026 update introduced a default limit on the amount of memory used by Endpoint Mapper when handling Endpoint Lookup calls. For workloads such as Exchange Server, the default limit of 512 simultaneous Endpoint Lookup calls might not be sufficient under heavy load. Administrators can use this registry setting to increase the maximum number of simultaneous Endpoint Lookup calls, which increases the amount of memory that Endpoint Mapper can use."
However, Microsoft says these known issues aren't linked to the October 2026 Exchange server security updates and urges customers not to uninstall them.
"Issues reported are not related to installation of October 2026 security updates for Exchange Server. This is not a 'known issue' related to October 2026 Exchange update. Any version of Exchange that runs on impacted versions of Windows could be impacted," Microsoft added in a separate blog describing the issues.
"Not all Exchange servers will be impacted by installation of those updates equally; the severity and speed of impact varies based on Exchange server load. Some servers might never see a problem."
While it works on a fix, Microsoft also shared a temporary workaround that should resolve these issues by modifying a registry key on affected Exchange Server systems.
To do that, you have to run the following command from an elevated Command Prompt on the Exchange Server and then reboot the device:
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc" /v EpmapSavedContextCap /t REG_DWORD /d 65536 /f
After the system restarts, customers should monitor the Exchange environment and raise the Endpoint Mapper memory limit if it reoccurs.
In July. Microsoft also announced that it will stop shipping extended security updates for Exchange 2016 and 2019 this month after a 6-month extension announced in April 2026 to the original Extended Security Update (ESU) program.

Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
articles.text:
Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of East Anglia
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.
- Share:
Scientists have discovered a surprising ability of light that allows it to develop spinning patterns as it moves through empty space, without relying on special lenses, mirrors, or materials. The finding reveals that light possesses a hidden geometric structure that can influence its behavior in ways researchers previously thought were difficult to achieve.
The discovery comes from an international team led by researchers at the University of East Anglia (UEA) in the United Kingdom, working with scientists in South Africa. Their experiments demonstrate that carefully prepared light can be controlled through its own internal geometry, offering a new approach to manipulating how light spins and twists.
The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how different properties of light interact. They could eventually lead to more sensitive medical tests, faster and more secure communications, and advanced quantum technologies that use light to transmit and protect information.
Why the Direction of Light's Spin Matters
One of the most intriguing aspects of the discovery involves chirality, a scientific term describing the difference between left-handed and right-handed structures.
Human hands provide a familiar example. Although they are mirror images of each other, a left hand cannot be perfectly superimposed on a right hand. Many molecules have a similar property, including compounds used in medicines. Two versions of the same molecule can have nearly identical chemical structures yet produce very different effects in the body.
Scientists can distinguish these molecular forms by studying how they interact with light that has a particular rotational behavior. Traditionally, producing and controlling such light has often involved specialized materials, carefully designed surfaces, or powerful lenses that focus beams extremely tightly.
The research demonstrates that appropriately prepared light can develop this behavior naturally as it travels, without requiring those additional optical components.
"Our work shows that light can naturally develop this handed behavior all on its own," said Dr. Kayn Forbes from UEA's School of Chemistry, Pharmacy and Pharmacology.
"You just have to prepare it in the right way.
"Most people think of light as traveling in straight lines. But scientists can also create structured light -- light whose brightness, shape, and direction are carefully arranged.
"One extreme example is light that twists as it travels, forming a corkscrew shape known as an optical vortex. Each twist can carry information, making this kind of light valuable for high-speed internet, secure communications, and advanced sensors.
"Light can also spin as it travels, depending on how it is polarized. This spin can be left-handed or right-handed -- another form of chirality."
Scientists Discover How Light Develops a Hidden Spin
Light can exhibit different kinds of rotational behavior. An optical vortex, for example, has a wave pattern that twists around its direction of travel, much like a corkscrew. Light also has a property known as polarization, which describes how its electric field oscillates. Certain polarization patterns produce a form of rotation called spin.
Physicists have long studied the relationship between these two properties. However, the interactions responsible for the newly observed effect were generally considered extremely weak and difficult to detect without specialized experimental conditions.
The researchers found that the situation changes when a beam of light is prepared in a particular balanced configuration.
Under those conditions, the beam can initially have no spin, yet distinct regions with spinning behavior emerge as it travels through free space. The effect does not require the light to pass through engineered materials or additional optical devices.
"It starts off with no spin at all," explained MSc student Light Mkhumbuza, who carried out key experiments. "But as the beam travels forward, spinning regions appear and separate out -- almost as if the spin was hiding and then revealed itself."
Rather than creating spin through an external optical component, the researchers demonstrated how the beam's existing internal structure can determine where spinning regions develop during propagation.
The Hidden Geometry That Controls Light
To explain this unexpected behavior, the researchers turned to topology, a mathematical field concerned with properties that remain unchanged when objects are continuously stretched, bent, or reshaped.
Dr. Isaac Nape, from the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa, offered a simple way to understand the concept.
"To explain it, imagine a mug and a doughnut," he said. "You can morph one into the other without tearing it, because they both have one hole. That hole is a topological feature."
The researchers found that structured light possesses its own topological characteristics, encoded in the arrangement of its polarization.
This underlying pattern acts like a mathematical fingerprint. Even as the light beam changes shape while traveling, its topological structure remains, influencing how different regions of the beam evolve.
As a result, the arrangement of the light itself can determine where its left-handed and right-handed spinning patterns become visible.
The discovery gives scientists a way to guide this behavior by designing the beam's initial structure, rather than depending on specialized materials to produce the desired effect.
"This gives us a completely new tuning knob for light. By adjusting its topology, we can decide how and where chirality appears," said Dr. Nape.
Potential Breakthroughs in Medicine and Communications
The ability to control light through its geometry could eventually make several important optical technologies simpler, more affordable, and more versatile.
One particularly promising application involves medical diagnostics and pharmaceutical research. Because many biologically important molecules have left-handed and right-handed forms, carefully structured light could help scientists identify these differences with greater sensitivity. Such tools could be valuable for evaluating drug safety and detecting biological markers associated with disease.
The same principles could support smaller optical sensors capable of identifying chemicals or biological substances without requiring large, sophisticated laboratory instruments.
Communications technology could also benefit. By encoding information into different twisting and spinning patterns, researchers may be able to increase the amount of data carried by individual light beams. This could contribute to faster optical communications, improved information security, and future quantum networks.
Other potential uses include manipulating microscopic particles, cells, and molecules with light, as well as developing more resilient quantum systems. Topological properties may help protect delicate quantum information against certain forms of noise and interference.
"The implications are wide-ranging," said Dr. Forbes. "This work could lead to simpler and more sensitive medical tests, especially in drug development.
"It could also be used to pack more information into laser beams -- boosting data capacity for communications, including future quantum networks.
"And because the effect doesn't rely on fragile materials or precision-engineered surfaces, it could be easier and cheaper to use in real-world technologies.
"This research could lay the foundations for a new generation of light-based technologies, by showing that light's behavior can be controlled using its own internal geometry," he added.
These applications remain possibilities for future development, but the underlying discovery provides researchers with another way to design and control the behavior of light.
A Hidden Property of Light Finally Revealed
For decades, scientists have relied on increasingly sophisticated optical equipment to produce and manipulate unusual forms of light. The findings suggest that some of these behaviors can instead arise from carefully designed structures already encoded within a light beam.
By showing how topology governs the emergence of spinning regions during propagation, the team has revealed a previously underappreciated connection between light's geometry and its physical behavior.
The discovery also illustrates how much remains to be learned about something as familiar and extensively studied as light.
"For something so familiar, light is proving to be far richer, stranger and more powerful than anyone imagined," said Dr. Forbes.
"And astonishingly, this new behavior has been there all along -- just waiting to be seen."
The research, 'Topological Control of Chirality and Spin with Structured Light', was published in the journal Light: Science & Applications.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of East Anglia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Light Mkhumbuza, Pedro Ornelas, Angela Dudley, Isaac Nape, Kayn A. Forbes. Topological control of chirality and spin with structured light. Light: Science, 2026; 15 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41377-026-02278-6

articles.title: Permis de conduire valable 15 ans : la France va dire adieu au permis à vie
articles.text:
Plus que quelques mois. La France, comme une grande partie des États membres de l’Union européenne, n’a plus que quelques mois pour mettre en place la réforme votée le 21 octobre 2025. Celle-ci instaure une nécessité de renouveler son permis de conduire tous les 15 ans. Adoptée à 339 voix pour et 240 voix contre, la directive (UE) 2025/2205 datée du 22 octobre 2025 signe la fin du permis à vie dans les États qui le proposent, France en tête.
Le délai légal pour la mise en place de cette directive est fixé à trois ans après la signature. Concrètement, cela revient à dire que la mesure doit être appliquée en France avant le 21 octobre 2028. Il reste moins de deux ans au gouvernement pour engager ce changement. La France n’est d’ailleurs pas la seule à prendre son temps : ils ne seraient que cinq États, sur les vingt-deux à avoir officiellement franchi le pas (Italie, Danemark, Pays-Bas, Finlande et Portugal).
Que prévoit le texte ?
Le texte européen voté l’an dernier prévoit qu’un contrôle médical doit être effectué tous les quinze ans afin de renouveler la validité du permis de conduire pour une nouvelle période de quinze ans. C’est un cadre légal minimum, c’est-à-dire que chaque État membre est libre de durcir les règles.
Le seul durcissement évoqué par la directive européenne concerne les conducteurs de plus de 65 ans. Le Parlement européen précise que les pays de l’UE peuvent réduire la durée de validité du permis pour les conducteurs âgés de 65 ans ou plus, afin de les soumettre à des contrôles médicaux plus fréquents ou à des cours de remise à niveau. Un rapport de l’Assemblée nationale sur cette directive évoque dans le même sens une « visite médicale obligatoire tous les 15 ans puis tous les 5 ans après 65 ans ».
En ce qui concerne les chauffeurs de bus et de poids lourds, la règle reste inchangée. Elle prévoit, comme aujourd’hui, un renouvellement sous contrôle tous les cinq ans.
Examen médical ou auto-évaluation ?
Si la directive européenne prévoit bien une date butoir pour la mise en œuvre, la méthode de contrôle et de renouvellement reste à l’appréciation des États. Ainsi, contrairement à ce qui a pu être dit par ailleurs, l’examen médical obligatoire tous les 15 ans n’est pas la seule option sur la table.
Le texte européen prévoit une autre solution, moins contraignante : l’auto-évaluation. C’est l’alinéa 3 de l’article 11 du texte. Il s’agirait, pour l’heure, d’un système basé sur une déclaration sur l’honneur confirmant son aptitude à prendre le volant (après une éventuelle série de tests à faire chez soi). Ce second cas de figure est d’ailleurs celui qui est préconisé par les eurodéputés français dans une résolution déposée cette année.

articles.title: Ne jetez pas votre vieux smartphone : cette application gratuite le transforme en baladeur audio HD — Frandroid
articles.text:
Iida Piano, une petite société japonaise a mis en ligne le 18 octobre le site de reTONE. Le but de cette application est transformer nos vieux smartphones en lecteurs musicaux, de l’écran d’accueil jusqu’à l’écran de verrouillage. Atout de taille, elle accepte des téléphones sous Android 4.0, une version sortie en 2011.
La France a de quoi faire. En 2019, une étude de l’AFNUM, la fédération des industriels du numérique, menée avec l’ADEME, estimait qu’entre 22 et 45 millions de smartphones encore fonctionnels dormaient dans les tiroirs des Français.
Une fois installée, reTONE peut prendre la place de l’écran d’accueil d’Android. Le téléphone s’allume alors directement sur la bibliothèque musicale et l’écran de verrouillage affiche la pochette en plein écran. Un mode « DAP silencieux » (DAP pour digital audio player, le nom anglais des baladeurs audio) coupe notifications, sonneries et alarmes, puis remet les volumes d’origine quand on le désactive.
reTONE ne passera pas par le Play Store. Il faudra télécharger le fichier APK sur le site officiel et l’installer à la main. Pas besoin d’accès root ni de ROM personnalisée, et une désinstallation suffit pour retrouver le téléphone tel qu’il était. Iida Piano promet aussi zéro publicité, aucune collecte de données et des fonctions réseau désactivées par défaut.
Un moteur audio qui court-circuite Android
L’essentiel du travail se fait dans le moteur audio maison. Il lit le MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC, l’ALAC et l’AIFF en haute résolution, ainsi que le DSD (le format des SACD, du DSD64 au DSD256), même quand le lecteur d’origine du téléphone ne prend pas en charge ces formats. D’après les essais d’Iida Piano, un téléphone de 2012 équipé d’un processeur double cœur lit du 24 bits/192 kHz et du DSD64 sans broncher.
Android a par ailleurs l’habitude de convertir le son à sa façon, souvent vers 48 kHz, alors qu’un morceau tiré d’un CD est en 44,1 kHz. Quand cette conversion est inévitable, reTONE la fait lui-même, une seule fois, avec un filtre qui préserve le signal jusqu’à 20 kHz, la limite de l’oreille humaine.
Avec un DAC USB, l’application envoie le son directement, y compris sur de vieux téléphones dont Android ne gérait pas ces DAC.
Est-ce que ça fera d’un Xperia de 2012 un baladeur haut de gamme ? Pas vraiment, car le son dépend toujours des circuits audio du téléphone. L’application fait aussi l’impasse sur l’égaliseur, la normalisation du volume et les services de streaming.
Le DAC USB exige en plus un port compatible OTG, c’est-à-dire capable d’alimenter un accessoire. Les téléphones à puce Intel Atom, comme certains vieux Zenfone d’Asus, sont exclus, puisque seuls les processeurs ARM sont pris en charge.
Iida Piano prévient aussi que ces vieux téléphones ne reçoivent plus de mises à jour de sécurité. Mieux vaut donc limiter leur connexion au réseau et vérifier que la batterie ne chauffe pas et ne gonfle pas.
Comme le note Clubic, la référence du genre, USB Audio Player PRO, est payante. Une aolternative gratuite est donc très intéressante. reTONE n’a pas encore de date de sortie. Iida Piano la présentera le 7 novembre au salon du casque d’automne de Tokyo, et prévoit de recruter des testeurs avant la version publique.

articles.title: Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM
Multi-turn agentic workloads build on accumulated context as an agent reasons, invokes tools, and incorporates earlier results. With each new turn, the client resends the conversation history, including system instructions, prior prompts, tool results, and model responses, causing the growing context to be processed repeatedly. In Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation, each request is split across specialized nodes: the prefill node processes the prompt and builds its key-value (KV) cache, then the decode node retrieves those KV blocks and generates the response.
Conventional disaggregated serving, however, only transfers KV cache in one direction: from prefill to decode node. This one-directional flow creates two inefficiencies for multi-turn workloads. First, after generating a response, the decode node holds KV cache entries for both the prompt and the newly generated tokens. When processing the next turn, the prefill node cannot retrieve those entries, so it must recompute the KV projections for the previous response tokens. Second, the decode node maintains the session state while the prefill nodes don’t, increasing the probability of cache eviction for active sessions on the prefill nodes. On a full cache miss, the prefill node must recompute KV projections for the entire conversation history, including system instructions, prior user requests, tool results, and model-generated responses. As the conversation grows, this redundant work consumes more accelerator capacity and increases time to first token (TTFT).
When you build conversational assistants and agentic applications, longer interaction histories can increase latency and consume accelerator capacity through repeated prefill computation. In this post, we show how bi-directional KV cache transfer lets prefill and decode nodes reuse previously computed context across turns, which improves accelerator utilization and helps applications sustain responsive TTFT as conversations grow.
In our multi-turn benchmarks on a 1P1D deployment using Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) P5en instances, bi-directional KV transfer reduced TTFT by up to 1.6x for Qwen3-32B and up to 3.3x for zai-org/GLM-5-FP8 (see the Performance data section). Results vary with workload and configuration. The instances are connected with AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (AWS EFA), a low-latency remote direct memory access (RDMA) network used across servers in AWS. On supported instance types, AWS EFA supports GPUDirect RDMA and Neuron Direct RDMA to move KV blocks directly between GPU or AWS Trainium device memory on the prefill and decode nodes.
We originally built and validated the feature on AWS Trainium instance clusters connected with EFA and contributed it to vLLM as an accelerator-agnostic capability. The results presented here are from an Amazon EC2 P5en GPU cluster with EFA, showing that the benefits also carry over to GPUs. This post explains the bi-directional KV transfer architecture, router metadata flow, KV-block retention and recompute controls, performance results, and how to reproduce the benchmark.
Bi-directional KV transfer
Bi-directional KV transfer is a mechanism in which a decode node returns previously computed KV to a prefill node on subsequent turns of a conversation. This avoids recomputing shared context on the prefill node and is governed by a configurable KV recompute threshold. It mitigates both computational-redundancy scenarios described earlier. To make it work, the KV must survive past the turn that produced it and travel in the reverse direction, coordinated by a KV-cache-aware router.
NIXL KV connector enhancements for bi-directional transfer
We extended the NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library (NIXL) KV connector to let prefill nodes consume remote KV blocks, similar to how decode nodes already consume KV blocks that the prefill node provides. This is not a trivial change, because the two node types are architecturally different: prefill nodes compute KV representations for new prompt tokens and can provide complete prompt KV blocks. Decode nodes lack the capability (or efficiency) to generate complete KV representations and can only serve previously cached KV blocks. As a result, prefill and decode nodes still carry their own roles and logic for computing the metadata of remote and local KV blocks. The actual KV transfer mechanism (a NIXL READ), however, is common to both the P->D and D->P directions.
The following diagram first shows the existing flow in blue. The router sends the request to prefill node, prefill node computes the prompt KV and returns its block metadata, and the router forwards the request and metadata to decode node for the standard P→D NIXL READ. The numbered red path illustrates the bi-directional KV transfer additions: (1) decode node retains eligible KV blocks after generation, (2) returns their metadata in the streaming response, and (3) the router caches that metadata for the next prefill request. Prefill node then (4) checks the remotely reusable KV after it applies local cache matches, (5) queues an asynchronous receive when the reusable token count meets the threshold, and (6) performs a D→P NIXL READ before computing the remaining suffix.
KV-cache-aware router
vLLM includes connector-side support for bi-directional KV transfer, while coordinating KV reuse across conversation turns requires a KV-cache-aware router. vLLM GitHub provides an example proxy that implements the flow used in this post which can be adapted for your environment.
The KV-cache-aware router is a lightweight, stateful control-plane component between the client, prefill, and decode nodes. It maintains an in-memory mapping from the client-provided conversation_id to decode’s kv_transfer_params. The router stores only block-location metadata, not KV tensors, and obtains that metadata from the response stream rather than separately querying decode node.
The following diagram shows how the router manages KV metadata across conversation turns. On the first turn, the cache lookup misses and the request follows the standard P→D flow. The router then saves decode’s metadata from the response stream. On later turns, the router retrieves that metadata using the conversation_id so prefill can reuse KV from decode. It then refreshes the metadata after generation for the next turn.
Block retention TTL
Normally a decode instance frees a request’s blocks as soon as generation finishes. Under bi-directional KV transfer mode, it holds them for a configurable lifetime (decoder_kv_blocks_ttl, default 480 seconds) and publishes their location and expiry. The conversation’s KV, both prompt prefix and generated response, then stays available for the next turn. For a turn that arrives before the time to live (TTL) expires, prefill node reuses the KV. One that arrives later falls back to normal prefill. Because this TTL is fixed and not renewed, tune it to the expected time between turns to balance KV reuse against accelerator-memory usage. A natural next improvement is to extend the heartbeat-renewed lease to the decode side. A decode instance could then reclaim blocks as soon as a conversation goes idle rather than at the end of a fixed timer.
KV recompute threshold
KV reuse isn’t always faster than local recomputation. For a short reusable prefix, interconnect and coordination overhead can exceed the time needed to recompute the tokens. The kv_recompute_threshold setting, which defaults to 64 tokens, controls this decision. Prefill node recomputes when the token count to compute is below the threshold and pulls KV from decode node when it is at or above the threshold. Deployments can tune this value based on model computation time, KV size, and interconnect performance.
Performance data
For evaluation, we used Qwen3-32B and GLM-5-FP8 models on a 1P1D deployment using Amazon EC2 P5en instances connected with EFA. To emulate scenarios in which the prefill node has evicted its local cache or the router selects a different prefill node that does not have the conversation’s KV blocks, we disabled prefix caching on prefill node with --no-enable-prefix-caching.
Across both the models, turning on bi-directional KV transfer reduces prefill computation on multi-turn conversations, and the benefit typically grows with prompt length. With the feature OFF, the prefill instance recomputes the entire grown context each turn, so TTFT rises steeply. Qwen3-32B climbs from 158 ms at 2k to 778 ms at 24k, and GLM-5-FP8 from 500 ms at 2k to 2,334 ms at 20k. With it ON, the decode instance’s retained KV is reused instead of recomputed, keeping TTFT far flatter. Qwen3-32B rises only from 122 ms to 460 ms over the same range (about a 1.6x reduction at the longest prompt), while GLM-5-FP8 rises from 358 ms to 702 ms and runs up to 3.3x below the recompute path at long prompts. The prefill-duration breakdown explains why.
Bi-directional transfer adds a small KV-transfer time (about 30 ms to 130 ms for Qwen3-32B; about 29 ms to 110 ms for GLM-5-FP8), but the prefill compute it removes far outweighs that KV-transfer time. As a result, the total prefill duration with transfer ON (Qwen3-32B: 128 ms to 414 ms; GLM-5-FP8: 316 ms to 541 ms) stays well below the recompute-only path (Qwen3-32B: 153 ms to 744 ms; GLM-5-FP8: 500 ms to 2,331 ms). The larger GLM-5-FP8 model shows a bigger absolute and relative gap, since its higher per-token recompute time makes KV reuse pay off even more as models and contexts scale.
Qwen3-32B
The following chart plots TTFT against prompt length for Qwen3-32B, comparing bi-directional KV transfer ON versus OFF.
The next chart breaks the prefill duration for the same runs into its recompute and KV-transfer components.
Together the charts show TTFT staying nearly flat with the feature ON while the OFF path climbs steeply as context grows, because the small KV-transfer time is far outweighed by the recompute it removes.
zai-org/GLM-5-FP8
The same two views follow for GLM-5-FP8. The first plots TTFT against prompt length with the feature ON versus OFF.
The second breaks the prefill duration into its recompute and KV-transfer components.
GLM-5-FP8 shows a much larger gap than Qwen3-32B, up to about 3.3x lower TTFT at long prompts, because its higher per-token recompute time makes KV reuse pay off even more as context length grows.
How to run benchmark
To reproduce our 1P1D benchmark configuration, one prefill node and one decode node, using Amazon EC2 P5en instances with EFA, follow the step-by-step instructions in the Reproducing our results guide. The guide covers environment setup, launching the vLLM prefill and decode servers, running the benchmark, and collecting results. The feature can run on other supported configurations, but performance results will vary depending on the hardware, model, workload, and network configuration.
Conclusion
In this post, we showed how bi-directional KV cache transfer can reduce TTFT as an agent’s conversation history grows. In P-D disaggregated deployments, the feature lets prefill node reuse KV blocks retained by decode node across turns, reducing repeated computation. Configurable block-retention and recompute thresholds determine when reuse occurs. On a 1P1D deployment using Amazon EC2 P5en instances connected with EFA, at the longest prompt lengths tested, we observed TTFT reductions of 1.6x for Qwen3-32B and 3.3x for zai-org/GLM-5-FP8. Results depend on the workload and deployment configuration. To implement this in your environment, use vLLM v0.21.0 or later with NixlConnector, enable bidirectional_kv_xfer on both prefill and decode servers, use a kv-cache-aware router, and follow the GitHub reproduction guide.
Related resources

- Prefill-Decode (P-D) disaggregated serving
- Benchmark KV Cache Offloading with Multi-Turn Conversations

We thank the vLLM community for their support in maintaining this feature.

Thanks, Nilay. Great to be with you.
